feature: Screen reader mode
detail: Opt-in mode that replaces the boxed terminal UI with plain linear labeled text readable by VoiceOver or NVDA; supports full conversation, approvals and review.

feature: Enable screen reader mode per session (--ax-screen-reader flag)
detail: Launch flag turns the mode on for one session; flag beats env var, which beats the setting.

feature: Enable screen reader mode via CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER env var
detail: Set to 1 in a shell to cover sessions started from it; 0 keeps the mode off even if the setting is true. Set on the remote machine over SSH.

feature: Enable screen reader mode for all sessions (axScreenReader setting)
detail: User-level setting turning the mode on everywhere, including the VS Code integrated terminal.

feature: Startup confirmation line for screen reader mode
detail: First printed line states the mode is on and via flag, env or settings.

feature: Project settings cannot enable screen reader mode
detail: Project .claude settings files and their env values are ignored for this mode; a startup line says so.

feature: Screen reader startup pause (CLAUDE_AX_STARTUP_QUIET_MS)
detail: Waits 3 seconds after the confirmation line before drawing the prompt; any key ends it; the env var changes the length. Needs v2.1.217+.

feature: Cursor pre-park delay (CLAUDE_AX_PREPARK_MS)
detail: Optional env var holding the cursor at line start for set milliseconds before writing changed lines in screen reader mode. Needs v2.1.233+.

feature: Screen magnifier cursor (CLAUDE_CODE_ACCESSIBILITY)
detail: Setting 1 keeps a visible terminal cursor that follows the input caret and, v2.1.218+, the highlighted menu row, for magnifiers like macOS Zoom.

feature: Reduced motion setting (prefersReducedMotion)
detail: When true, spinners, shimmer and other animations are reduced or removed.

feature: Colorblind-friendly themes (dark-daltonized, light-daltonized)
detail: Selectable through the theme setting or the /theme command.

feature: Terminal bell when waiting (preferredNotifChannel terminal_bell)
detail: Outside screen reader mode, rings the terminal bell when Claude is waiting on you.

feature: Screen reader output: flat text, no chrome or color-only cues
detail: No box-drawing, static progress text, no redraw of unchanged content; tables read as header: value sentences; diffs shown line by line with plus/minus.

feature: Screen reader transcript labels
detail: Each message is prefixed with a searchable label: you, claude, thinking, tool, tool error, error, warning, Permission Required, Cost.

feature: Announced deletions in text editing
detail: Deleting words or lines via Ctrl+W, Alt+D, Option+Delete, Ctrl+U, Cmd+Backspace or Ctrl+K announces the deleted text.

feature: Permission mode change announcement on Shift+Tab
detail: Cycling modes announces the new mode (e.g. plan mode on, accept edits on) once; mode changes via commands such as /plan are not announced.

feature: Jump between turns with OSC 133 markers
detail: Terminal jump-to-previous-prompt keys (iTerm2, VS Code terminal, Windows Terminal via scrollToMark, Kitty, Ghostty) move between turns; not in macOS Terminal or WezTerm.

feature: Numbered-list menus and permission prompts in screen reader mode
detail: Arrow-key menus become numbered lists answered by typing a number; Escape cancels where allowed; /effort slider becomes a numbered list too.

feature: Typed y/n answers for yes-no prompts
detail: Yes/no prompts ask for y, n, yes or no typed with Enter instead of a menu.

feature: Terminal bell notifications in screen reader mode
detail: Bell rings when a reply finishes, a prompt needs an answer, or a tool that ran over 5 seconds ends.

feature: Cost summary announced at exit
detail: Screen reader mode prints a Cost: summary on exit if the account shows costs, not per turn.

feature: VS Code extension announces conversation activity to screen readers
detail: On v2.1.236+, the extension chat panel announces activity without any setting.

feature: Known limits: no auto-detect, attach uses alternate screen
detail: Mode does not auto-start when a screen reader runs; attaching to background sessions uses alternate screen without scrollback (exit with Left Arrow or Ctrl+Z); -p mode unchanged.

feature: Managed settings overriding local config
detail: Org policy delivered via admin console, MDM or file takes precedence over developer settings, covering tools, commands, servers and network destinations.

feature: API provider choice for Claude Code
detail: Teams/Enterprise seats, Claude Console pay-as-you-go, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform or Microsoft Foundry, each affecting billing, auth and compliance.

feature: Features needing a claude.ai account
detail: Cloud sessions, cloud scheduled tasks, Code Review, Remote Control and the Chrome extension do not work with Console API keys or cloud-provider credentials alone.

feature: Server-managed settings via admin console
detail: Fetched at startup and refreshed hourly; highest-priority delivery; can also come from a self-hosted Claude apps gateway for Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry setups.

feature: Plist and registry managed policy
detail: macOS plist and Windows HKLM registry deliver tamper-resistant policy; HKCU registry is a low-priority convenience only.

feature: File-based managed settings
detail: managed-settings.json at OS-specific paths on macOS, Linux/WSL and Windows.

feature: Managed settings precedence and merge rules
detail: Managed beats user/project except security exceptions; permission arrays merge so devs can extend but not remove; fallbackModel, availableModels, modelPicker are replaced.

feature: WSL inherits Windows settings (wslInheritsWindowsSettings)
detail: Admin-only setting extending Windows registry and Program Files policy to WSL sessions.

feature: WSL sessions in Claude Code Desktop
detail: Desktop can run Code sessions in a WSL 2 distro; disabled by default on managed devices, enabled with disableWslSessions=false under HKLM (Desktop v1.19367.0+).

feature: Permission rules (allow/deny) enforcement
detail: Managed permissions.allow and permissions.deny rules for tools and commands.

feature: Permission lockdown
detail: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly makes managed settings the sole source of rules; permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode disables skip-permissions.

feature: Starting permission mode and disabling auto mode
detail: permissions.defaultMode sets the starting mode; permissions.disableAutoMode removes auto mode.

feature: Sandboxing controls
detail: sandbox.enabled and network allowedDomains give OS-level file and network isolation; needed because denying WebFetch does not stop curl via Bash.

feature: Managed policy CLAUDE.md
detail: Org-wide guidance file at the managed path; guidance, not a client-enforced rule.

feature: MCP server control
detail: allowedMcpServers, deniedMcpServers, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, managedMcpServers or managed-mcp.json restrict or deploy MCP servers.

feature: Plugin marketplace control
detail: strictKnownMarketplaces, blockedMarketplaces, disableSideloadFlags, disableCommandPluginSources, pluginSuggestionMarketplaces restrict plugin sources and sideloading.

feature: Customization lockdown (strictPluginOnlyCustomization)
detail: Blocks skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from user/project sources; locking skills also stops claude.ai skill sync.

feature: Disable claude.ai skills and plugins sync
detail: syncClaudeAiSkills and syncClaudeAiPlugins false stop loading what devs enable on claude.ai; turning Skills off for the org stops sync and (v2.1.273+) removes synced ones.

feature: Hook restrictions
detail: allowManagedHooksOnly and allowedHttpHookUrls restrict which hooks and HTTP hook URLs run.

feature: Login method enforcement (forceLoginMethod)
detail: Restricts login method across VS Code, Agent SDK, setup-token and install-github-app; terminal interactive screen not blocked by claudeai/console value.

feature: Login organization enforcement (forceLoginOrgUUID)
detail: Restricts claude.ai logins to your org in terminal, VS Code and Agent SDK; not applied to Console or gateway sign-in.

feature: Credentials blocked by login enforcement keys
detail: With either key set, sessions using ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or apiKeyHelper are blocked at startup.

feature: Provider restrictions (allowedProviders)
detail: Limits API providers per machine; unlisted provider sessions refused at startup, login and next API contact. Needs v2.1.285+.

feature: Disable agent view (disableAgentView)
detail: Turns off claude agents, --bg, /background and the on-demand supervisor.

feature: Corporate launcher (processWrapper)
detail: Prefixes the background-agent supervisor, workers and other background processes with a required launcher instead of disabling agent view.

feature: Model restrictions (availableModels, enforceAvailableModels)
detail: Filters the model picker; enforce also constrains the auto-selected default.

feature: Effort cap (maxEffortLevel)
detail: Caps effort level for all models or per model on any provider.

feature: Version floor and required version range
detail: minimumVersion blocks auto-update below a floor; requiredMinimumVersion/requiredMaximumVersion refuse to start outside the range.

feature: Telemetry opt-out
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 via managed env turns off usage metrics, error reports and surveys.

feature: Organization model restrictions (server-side)
detail: Enterprise admins disable individual models from org admin settings, enforced server-side; not for Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry.

feature: Organization default model
detail: Admin sets which model new sessions start on; members can switch unless an override is enabled.

feature: Organization effort limits
detail: Admins cap effort levels per role, enforced server-side.

feature: Cloud environments page and default environment
detail: Owners create org-shared cloud environments (network access, env vars, setup script) and pick the default at claude.ai admin settings.

feature: Connected GitHub accounts admin page
detail: Owners see GitHub orgs/accounts linked via the Claude GitHub App (shared by Claude Code, Claude Tag, Claude Security); can link or unlink; Admin role cannot open it.

feature: Limit which GitHub accounts can be linked
detail: Allow-list orgs or names and turn on Only allowed accounts can be linked; existing links keep working until unlinked; unlinking stops Code Review on those repos.

feature: Compliance API activity for GitHub link events
detail: Enterprise activity types record GitHub app installation linked and unlinked.

feature: Usage visibility options
detail: OpenTelemetry export, analytics dashboard, programmatic reporting APIs and spend controls, with availability differing between Teams/Enterprise and Console.

feature: Spend report for per-user usage
detail: Teams/Enterprise per-user usage and spend come from the spend report in analytics settings, not the dashboard.

feature: Zero Data Retention
detail: Nothing stored after request completes; for qualified Enterprise accounts.

feature: HIPAA-ready configuration
detail: For HIPAA-enabled Enterprise orgs some local-mode features are off or off by default; gateway sessions are ineligible.

feature: No training on code or prompts
detail: On Team, Enterprise, API and cloud provider plans Anthropic does not train on code or prompts.

feature: Verify managed settings via /status
detail: Status tab Setting sources line names the winning managed source.

feature: Login troubleshooting commands
detail: /logout then /login to switch accounts; claude update if enterprise auth option is missing; seat lacking Claude Code access shows a not-added message.

feature: Advisor tool (second stronger model consultation)
detail: Claude consults a stronger advisor model with the full transcript before committing to an approach, when stuck, or before finishing; runs server-side.

feature: Enable advisor via /advisor command
detail: Picker or direct model argument sets and saves advisorModel; also works in -p mode, Agent SDK, desktop app and Remote Control (v2.1.260+); /advisor off disables.

feature: advisorModel setting
detail: Persistent default advisor model in settings file.

feature: --advisor launch flag
detail: Sets advisor for one session; errors at launch if unsupported, unaccepted or disallowed, and starts without advisor in background sessions.

feature: Advisor pairing rules
detail: Advisor must rank at or above the main model; aliases fable, opus, sonnet or full IDs; Haiku 4.5 can call but not act as advisor; subagents inherit it.

feature: Fable advisor needs usage credits consent
detail: Where Fable bills to usage credits, one-time consent via /model fable is required before Fable can be the advisor.

feature: Advisor transcript status lines
detail: Shows Advising with model name, then Reviewed, Declined or Unavailable with error code; Ctrl+O reads guidance.

feature: Advisor usage billing
detail: Advisor tokens bill at advisor rates on API plans and count toward limits on subscriptions; Fable advisor bills to usage credits where applicable; counted in /usage.

feature: Advisor does not break prompt cache
detail: Toggling advisor mid-session keeps the main cache intact; advisor reads the full transcript uncached each call.

feature: Advisor provider and gateway requirements
detail: Needs Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS or Claude Models on Google Cloud (v2.1.300+); not Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry; needs feature-flag fetch.

feature: Disable advisor entirely (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL)
detail: Env var removes /advisor and ignores advisorModel and the flag.

feature: Advisor vs opusplan vs subagents vs /model
detail: Documented alternatives for second opinions: opusplan uses stronger model in plan mode, subagents with model set, or switching main model.

feature: Agent teams (lead plus teammates)
detail: Multiple Claude Code sessions coordinated by a lead; teammates have own context, message each other and can be messaged directly.

feature: Enable agent teams (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS)
detail: Disabled by default; set env var to 1; also makes named subagents launch as teammates; not spawned in -p mode; set 0 to turn off.

feature: Agent panel for teammates
detail: Panel below prompt: arrows select, Enter opens transcript and messaging, Esc clears or interrupts; idle rows hide after 30 s and more than three idle collapse into a counted row.

feature: Teammate display mode: in-process
detail: All teammates run in the main terminal, works in any terminal.

feature: Teammate display mode: split panes (tmux or iTerm2)
detail: Each teammate in its own pane via teammateMode auto, tmux or iterm2, or --teammate-mode flag; needs tmux or iTerm2 with it2 CLI and Python API.

feature: Choose teammate models
detail: Model picked from spawn prompt, subagent definition, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, then lead model; _FORCE=1 overrides; availableModels allowlist substitutes blocked models.

feature: Teammate effort inheritance
detail: Teammate on lead's model inherits lead effort level (split-pane from v2.1.186).

feature: Plan-first teammates with plan approval
detail: Teammate spawned while lead is in plan mode plans first, then requests approval; auto-approved unless its mode was changed, then lead reviews.

feature: Message and stop teammates directly
detail: Enter opens a teammate to message it; x stops it; Ctrl+T toggles task list; /compact, /clear, /rewind confirm and act on lead; /model and /fast do not run from teammate view.

feature: Shared task list with dependencies
detail: Tasks pending, in progress, completed or blocked; lead assigns or teammates self-claim with file locking; dependents auto-unblock.

feature: Graceful teammate shutdown
detail: Ask by name; lead sends a request the teammate may approve or reject; team directories cleaned up at session end.

feature: Team quality-gate hooks
detail: TeammateIdle, TaskCreated and TaskCompleted hooks can exit 2 to send feedback and block.

feature: Subagent definitions as teammates
detail: Reuse a subagent type; tools, model, effort, autoCompactWindow (v2.1.296+) and body apply, with differences by display mode; skills not applied.

feature: Teammate permissions follow the lead
detail: No per-teammate modes at spawn; starts in lead mode (dontAsk becomes Manual); prompts surface in lead; Shift+Tab cycles a teammate; flag propagation differs for split panes.

feature: Inter-agent messaging safeguards
detail: Messages are marked as from another session and cannot grant approval; auto-mode classifier reviews SendMessage content and treats relayed approvals as untrusted.

feature: Team mailbox, config and task storage
detail: Mailboxes and config under ~/.claude/teams, tasks under ~/.claude/tasks kept per cleanupPeriodDays; one team per session.

feature: Teammate prompt cache TTL (subagentPromptCacheTtl)
detail: In-process teammate cache holds 5 minutes by default; setting 1h extends it at a higher write rate.

feature: Agent team limitations
detail: No resume or rewind of in-process teammates, no nested teams, lead fixed, no background subagents from teammates, status can lag, slow shutdown.

feature: Five ways to run work in parallel
detail: Subagents, agent view, agent teams, dynamic workflows and projects, differing by who coordinates and where work runs.

feature: Projects (threads in cloud or via Remote Control)
detail: One ongoing conversation at claude.ai/code or desktop where Claude starts parallel threads in cloud or on your computer via Remote Control, with project instructions.

feature: Dynamic workflows
detail: Script that runs many subagents and cross-checks results for audits, large migrations or cross-checked research; listed with /workflows.

feature: Cross-session messaging
detail: Claude can list and message your other sessions on this machine, other machines or the cloud.

feature: /batch skill
detail: Splits one large change into 5 to 30 worktree-isolated subagents.

feature: Background bash commands
detail: Run one shell command without blocking the conversation.

feature: Forked subagent (/subtask) and /fork
detail: Subagent inheriting full conversation via /subtask; /fork copies the session into a background session; with agent view off /fork is the subagent command.

feature: Cloud scheduled tasks
detail: Run a session on a schedule in the cloud.

feature: Check running work: claude agents, /agents, /tasks, /workflows
detail: claude agents opens agent view; /agents points to subagent file locations; /tasks lists background items; /workflows lists runs and phases.

feature: Worktrees for parallel sessions
detail: Separate git checkout per session; agent view sessions auto-move to their own worktree before editing.

feature: Agent view (claude agents)
detail: One terminal screen listing all background sessions grouped by state, with an input to dispatch new ones; sessions keep running without a terminal.

feature: Dispatch a background session from agent view
detail: Typing a prompt starts a new session, auto-named by a Haiku-class model; each prompt is its own session; prompts under four characters are rejected.

feature: Session states and icons
detail: Working, Needs input, Idle, Completed, Failed, Stopped with distinct icons; shape shows running, exited or looping.

feature: Peek panel and inline reply
detail: Space opens a panel with the latest output or pending question; reply inline, ! sends Bash, /stop stops; /model, /effort, /rename, /usage run instantly on working sessions.

feature: Attach and detach from a session
detail: Enter or right-arrow attaches to the full session with a recap; left-arrow, /exit or Ctrl+Z detach; detaching never stops it; attached sessions render fullscreen.

feature: Background an open session with left arrow or /bg
detail: Pressing left on an empty prompt or /background moves the current conversation into agent view; carries over bash commands, subagents and loops, but monitors stop.

feature: Footer hint and waiting count for background agents
detail: Regular sessions show a left-arrow hint, then counts like 2 agents waiting or 2 done; hidden in screen reader mode, no colour change under reduced motion.

feature: Open agent view by default setting
detail: /config Open agents view by default (defaultToAgentsView) makes bare claude open agent view.

feature: Leave-arrow shortcut toggle (leftArrowOpensAgents)
detail: Setting in /config disables the left-arrow shortcut for foreground sessions.

feature: Scope agent view to a project (--cwd)
detail: Narrows the list to sessions started under one directory, including worktrees.

feature: Row summaries by Haiku-class model
detail: One-line status or question per row, refreshed every 15s from output and rewritten by a model at turn end and mid-turn; costs a short request billed normally.

feature: Pull request status label on rows
detail: Rows show #N (or !N for GitLab) linked to the PR, coloured yellow, green, purple or grey by status; several PRs show a count.

feature: Group, pin, reorder and rename sessions
detail: Groups Ready for review, Needs input, Working, Completed; Ctrl+S groups by directory; Ctrl+T pins (keeps process alive); Shift+arrows reorder; Ctrl+R renames; Alt+arrows jump groups.

feature: Stop and delete sessions in agent view
detail: Ctrl+X stops, second press deletes (also whole group); transcript stays resumable and worktree is removed with uncommitted changes.

feature: Bring back past session with /resume
detail: Bare /resume in dispatch input lists the repo's past sessions including deleted ones and resumes one as a background session.

feature: Filter sessions (a:, s:, n:, o:, PR number or URL)
detail: Dispatch input filters by agent, state, name or first prompt, result text, PR/MR number or URL; combinable.

feature: Agent view keyboard shortcuts
detail: Navigation, Space peek, Alt+1..9 attach, Tab subagent browse, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+G external editor, Ctrl+Y restore cleared text, Ctrl+Enter dispatch and attach, ? help; rebindable in keybindings.json.

feature: Dispatch with subagent, repo, command or PR mentions
detail: First word or @name runs a custom subagent as main agent; @repo targets a repo or worktree; /skill dispatches a skill; # or URL selects an existing PR session.

feature: Run shell command as background job (! prefix or --exec)
detail: Runs a command in a PTY job shown as a row, no model involved; output kept in memory and cleared about five minutes after exit.

feature: Paste images and long text into dispatch
detail: Images can be pasted with a task; text over 800 characters or three lines collapses to a placeholder.

feature: Voice dictation in agent view
detail: Hold-to-record dictation works in the peek reply and dispatch inputs.

feature: /fork copies session to background
detail: Copies the conversation, model, permission mode, effort and added dirs into a new background session, optionally with a prompt; copy works in its own worktree.

feature: Dispatch from shell (claude --bg, --agent, --name, --resume)
detail: Starts a background session directly; supports --agent, --name, --model, --resume (same ID or copy) and --fork-session; rejects -p; asks for workspace trust.

feature: Worktree isolation for background sessions
detail: Sessions move into a git worktree under .claude/worktrees before editing; commit, push to own branch and draft PR happen automatically, never main or force push; worktree.bgIsolation none disables.

feature: Non-git isolation via WorktreeCreate hook
detail: Other version control systems can isolate edits through a WorktreeCreate hook.

feature: Set model, effort and fast mode for dispatched sessions
detail: /model, /effort (low to max) and /fast typed in dispatch input apply to next sessions; ultracode only via claude agents --effort.

feature: Dispatch defaults flags
detail: claude agents accepts --permission-mode, --model, --effort, --agent, --restricted, and dangerous-skip-permissions flags with disclaimer.

feature: Permission mode inheritance for background sessions
detail: Backgrounded sessions keep their mode; dispatched ones use directory defaultMode, else originating session mode, never more permissive than project settings allow.

feature: Settings, plugin and MCP flags for agent view
detail: --settings, --setting-sources, --add-dir, --plugin-dir, --mcp-config, --strict-mcp-config pass through to dispatched sessions.

feature: Session shell commands (attach, logs, stop, respawn, rm)
detail: claude attach/logs accept ID or name; stop/kill; respawn one or --all; rm removes a row, with --discard-unpushed and --force-remove-worktree retries.

feature: claude agents --json for scripts
detail: Prints sessions with id, state, status, waitingFor, name; --all includes completed; supported way to read state.

feature: Supervisor background service
detail: A supervisor hosts sessions across terminal closes and updates; stops idle unattended processes after about an hour; claude daemon status, logs and stop --any commands.

feature: Sleep and shutdown recovery for sessions
detail: Sessions survive sleep; after shutdown they show failed (within 48h) or stopped and resume from saved conversation on reply or attach.

feature: Notifications when background session needs input or finishes
detail: Sends terminal notification through preferredNotifChannel and fires Notification hook types agent_needs_input and agent_completed.

feature: Disable agent view (disableAgentView, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW)
detail: Turns off background agents entirely; admins can enforce via managed settings.

feature: Session kind in /status
detail: Shows background job attached, unattended, or interactive.

feature: Agent view macOS permission prompts
detail: Background host needs separate Files and Folders or Local Network permissions on macOS.

feature: Agent view limits
detail: Research preview; consumes subscription quota per session, runs locally and stops on shutdown.

feature: Needs-input handling for MCP and GitHub app commands
detail: /mcp list and /install-github-app need an attached terminal; unattended sessions show a Needs input row.

feature: Cross-session message approval row
detail: A session holding a cross-session message awaiting approval shows who sent it on its Needs input row.

feature: Claude Code analytics dashboard (Teams/Enterprise)
detail: claude.ai/analytics/claude-code shows usage metrics, contribution metrics, leaderboard and CSV export; viewable by Admins and Owners.

feature: Usage metrics: accepted lines, accept rate, active users, sessions
detail: Dashboard counts lines accepted via Edit/Write, suggestion accept rate, daily active users and sessions.

feature: Contribution metrics with GitHub integration
detail: Counts merged PRs and lines written with Claude Code; needs Owner role, Claude GitHub app, analytics and GitHub toggles; not with ZDR or GitHub Enterprise Server.

feature: Analytics charts: PRs per user, PRs breakdown, lines toggle
detail: Charts for total PRs per user and PRs with Claude Code versus all, switchable to lines of code.

feature: Contributor leaderboard and CSV export
detail: Top 10 users by PRs or lines with Claude Code; Export all users downloads all contributors as CSV.

feature: PR attribution and claude-code-assisted label
detail: Merged PRs matched to sessions from 21 days before to 2 days after merge, with generated files excluded and heavily rewritten code (over 20%) not attributed; PRs labelled claude-code-assisted.

feature: Enterprise Analytics API
detail: Per-user engagement, usage and cost reports across Claude surfaces via read:analytics key created by Primary Owner; not on Teams.

feature: Spend report export
detail: Organization analytics export listing token usage and estimated credit spend per user and per model.

feature: Console analytics dashboard for API customers
detail: platform.claude.com/claude-code shows accepted lines, accept rate, active users, sessions and daily spend; needs UsageView permission; no GitHub contribution metrics.

feature: Console team insights table
detail: Per-member spend and lines accepted over a chosen range (default 30 days), keyed by API key name or email.

feature: Claude Code Analytics API
detail: Programmatic daily per-user metrics using an Admin API key.

feature: Auto mode classifier no-charge server-side checks
detail: Server-side classifier checks actions in auto mode at no charge on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team; elsewhere Claude Code's own classifier requests count toward token usage.

feature: Classifier not eligible notice and response
detail: Notice holds the first checked action; Enter continues with billed classifier (gateway ack lasts 24h), Esc or Ctrl+C cancels; -p prints to stderr and stream-json emits a warning.

feature: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0 setting
detail: Temporary env var forcing Claude Code's own classifier requests and suppressing the notice, for gateways that cannot pass the checks.

feature: Auto mode server status in /status
detail: Auto mode server row shows Enabled or Disabled depending on whether server checks decide actions.

feature: Gateway requirements for server checks
detail: Gateway must forward anthropic-beta header and safeguards field unchanged and keep safeguard_results in responses.

feature: Artifacts published from Claude Code sessions
detail: Claude turns session work into a live interactive web page at a private claude.ai URL that updates in place; Claude may publish on its own or on request.

feature: Artifact use cases
detail: Annotated PR walkthroughs, dashboards, side-by-side options, investigation timelines, link-sharing instead of pasting, and status boards.

feature: Artifact reopen shortcut and session pill
detail: Ctrl+] reopens the latest artifact; a pill below the prompt shows its name or count and opens the /artifacts list in fullscreen.

feature: Control browser auto-open (CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_AUTO_OPEN)
detail: Set to 0 to stop the browser opening on publish; Remote Control prompts do not open a tab on the host.

feature: Permission prompts before publishing
detail: Asks in plan mode, when capabilities are declared, public artifacts, scheduled-task turns, unreadable files and some edits; auto mode uses classifier review.

feature: Update artifact in place with versions
detail: Republish to the same URL; each publish is a version and the Share control picks which version viewers see; other sessions need the URL or /artifacts attach.

feature: One-step artifact edits toggle (CLAUDE_CODE_ARTIFACT_PUBLISH_EDITS)
detail: Setting 0 disables small file changes bundled into a publish; requires relaunch.

feature: /artifacts list
detail: Lists owned and shared artifacts, current session first; Enter open or attach, o open, c copy link, d permanently delete (not in cloud sessions).

feature: Artifact sharing: private, organization, shared folder, public
detail: New artifacts are private; Team/Enterprise can share with specific people or the org or via folder; public links need no sign-in and are off until an Owner enables them.

feature: Artifact gallery
detail: claude.ai/code/artifacts lists every artifact you created; header shows author for org viewers or an unverified-content label for outsiders.

feature: Deep links to artifact tabs and sections
detail: Claude can supply links with anchors like #overview to specific views.

feature: Artifact editor role
detail: On Team/Enterprise, sharing dialog lets viewers be promoted to editors who republish through Claude; stale publishes are refused and merged.

feature: Read an artifact shared with you
detail: Claude reads another's artifact as a summary (injection-safe) and saves full source locally; approvals needed in several cases such as other-org public artifacts and plan mode.

feature: Comments on shared artifacts
detail: Org viewers comment on the page; Send to Claude or @claude activates a thread for Claude to read, reply or resolve (v2.1.221+); public-link viewers cannot see or add comments.

feature: Claude auto-replies to artifact comments
detail: Session watches published artifacts and replies to activated comments per permission mode (v2.1.228+); capped at 60 per hour; pause with Ctrl+C, /tasks or Ctrl+X Ctrl+K twice; watch limit 25.

feature: Artifact live data via MCP connectors
detail: Pages call claude.ai MCP connectors on each view using the viewer's own account, with viewer permission ask, caching and refresh; not local MCP servers; needs v2.1.209+.

feature: Connector tool-name validation on publish
detail: Publish checks declared tool names against available connector tools and refuses when none match (v2.1.265+).

feature: Artifact file downloads capability
detail: Pages offer a download button (CSV, PNG) through a per-account downloads capability; script or link downloads are blocked by the viewer.

feature: Artifact build patterns: diff tour, compare, tune, copy-as-prompt
detail: Documented prompt patterns including interactive sliders and an export control that pastes a result back into the session.

feature: Built-in design skill and project design tokens
detail: Artifacts use a built-in design skill and prefer a design system recorded in CLAUDE.md; typefaces load from Google Fonts or inlined data URIs.

feature: Artifact templates (Design, Docs, Sheets, Whiteboards, Data)
detail: Account templates usable from Claude Code; admins can toggle templates and roles; Docs and Sheets need the Claude Docs connector.

feature: /design command for Claude Design canvas
detail: Drafts UI mockups as artboards on a canvas artifact; editable in desktop browser with PNG or PDF export per artboard (v2.1.265+).

feature: Claude Docs via connector
detail: Documents for other people go to Claude Docs connector (claude.ai Claude Docs in /mcp); files such as docx or README stay local on request.

feature: Artifact page constraints
detail: Single static HTML/HTM/MD page under strict CSP, UTF-8, 16 MiB max, Google Fonts and five CDNs only, no backend, no network-share sources.

feature: Artifact availability requirements
detail: Needs claude.ai sign-in on Anthropic API; not on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, API key or gateway sessions; not with CMEK, HIPAA or ZDR; CLI or desktop v1.13576.0+; off in -p and SDK.

feature: Disable artifacts (enableArtifact, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT, deny rule)
detail: Users can turn off via /config, settings, env var or Artifact deny rule; project settings can disable but not re-enable.

feature: Admin toggle for artifacts and role scoping
detail: Owners enable or disable artifacts org-wide; Enterprise RBAC can scope the Artifacts permission per role.

feature: Admin toggle: Enable artifact connectors
detail: Separate switch for connector calls from artifacts in Claude Code and claude.ai conversations.

feature: Admin toggle: External sharing for artifacts
detail: Off by default; turning off blocks existing public links without changing audiences.

feature: Artifact retention policy
detail: Enterprise sets separate retention periods for private and shared artifacts under Data and privacy.

feature: Artifact audit via Compliance API activity feed
detail: Enterprise can see who published, shared or deleted artifacts.

feature: Compliance API list, read and delete artifacts
detail: Endpoints to list artifacts, fetch a version's content and delete an artifact.

feature: Network allowlist for artifact viewer
detail: Viewer loads from *.claudeusercontent.com; optional Google Fonts hosts and five CDN hosts for libraries.

feature: Browser login on first launch
detail: Running claude opens a browser to sign in; c copies the URL, a pasted code can be entered at the prompt, and Login successful confirms.

feature: Accepted account types for Claude Code
detail: Pro, Max or Ultra subscription, Team or Enterprise seat, Claude Console, cloud providers (Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry), Claude apps gateway, and Enterprise Admin Console sign-in.
plans: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise, Console

feature: 3rd-party platform setup wizard at login
detail: Login prompt option launching an interactive wizard for Bedrock and Agent Platform.

feature: Corporate SSO via Claude apps gateway
detail: Self-hosted gateway signs developers in via IdP using /login or VS Code; gateway token is the only credential.

feature: Enterprise Admin Console sign-in (claude auth login)
detail: Owner-enabled sign-in where user selects their organization in the browser.

feature: /logout and re-authenticate
detail: Logging out resets first-launch setup state so login and setup run again.

feature: Skip login via ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or earlier claude auth login
detail: Approved API key or prior sign-in (including dev container volume) bypasses prompt; v2.1.290+ stops always prompting.

feature: Multiple accounts with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
detail: Separate config dirs keep separate settings, history and logins; keyless Console sign-ins are not isolated.

feature: Team onboarding: subscribe, invite, log in
detail: Teams and Enterprise: subscribe, invite from admin dashboard, members log in with claude.ai accounts.

feature: Console roles: Claude Code vs Developer
detail: Claude Code role can only create Claude Code API keys; Developer can create any key; invite via Members page or SSO.

feature: Keyless Console sign-in (Anthropic profile)
detail: Sign in to Console without creating an API key (recommended) or create an API key (legacy); stored as a profile, undone with /logout; v2.1.242+.

feature: Prevent keyless sign-in on managed machines
detail: Deploy forceLoginOrgUUID with Console org ID; developers need a role that can create keys.

feature: Restrict login to an organization (forceLoginOrgUUID)
detail: Managed key rejects claude.ai logins to other orgs and exits at startup; may be an array; setup-token and install-github-app enforce method only.

feature: Restrict login method (forceLoginMethod)
detail: Values claudeai, console or gateway pre-select or require a sign-in method across login paths (v2.1.212+).

feature: Restrict API providers (allowedProviders)
detail: Managed list of permitted services (e.g. anthropic, bedrock, customEndpoint); others refused at startup and next request; v2.1.285+.

feature: Credential storage locations
detail: macOS Keychain with 0600 file fallback, Linux and Windows .credentials.json; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR changes location and Keychain entry.

feature: apiKeyHelper credential script
detail: Setting runs a script returning an API key; warns after 10s and fails with an error after three attempts; applies to CLI, VS Code, SDK, Actions but not Desktop or cloud.

feature: Login expiry check (claude auth status --text)
detail: Shows a Sign-in ends window (v2.1.318+); -p runs warn on stderr within 10 days.

feature: Login expiry warning and /login renew
detail: Startup warning three days before expiry; after expiry requests fail or use other credentials; /status shows Login Expired; Remote Control and background sessions stall.

feature: Authentication precedence order
detail: Cloud provider, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, apiKeyHelper, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, profiles, then subscription OAuth; gateway session outranks all; /status shows the active one.

feature: Use custom API key toggle in /config
detail: Appears while ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set to remember approve or decline; -p always uses the key.

feature: Anthropic profiles and Workload Identity Federation
detail: Named profile or federation variables supply credentials (oidc_federation or user_oauth); not read in bare mode, Desktop or cloud; disables claude.ai connectors and /schedule.

feature: claude setup-token long-lived token
detail: Prints a one-year OAuth token for CI as CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN; needs a paid plan, cannot do Remote Control or claude.ai connectors; not read in bare mode.

feature: Cloud sessions always use subscription credentials
detail: API key or token set in a cloud environment does not override the subscription.

feature: Sign in with Amazon Bedrock wizard (/setup-bedrock)
detail: Login option 3rd-party platform then Amazon Bedrock, or /setup-bedrock later; picks AWS profile, Bedrock API key, access keys or environment credentials, region, verifies and pins models, saves to user settings.

feature: Bedrock one-time use-case form and Organizations call
detail: Per-account form to enable Anthropic models; AWS Organizations can submit once from the management account via PutUseCaseForModelAccess.

feature: AWS credential methods for Bedrock
detail: aws configure, exported access keys, SSO profile, aws login console credentials (up to 12h) or Bedrock API key (AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK); EC2/ECS role credentials work via default chain.

feature: AWS credential cache and resolve timeout
detail: Resolved chain cached until 5 minutes before expiry or 1 hour; 60s resolve timeout; CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_AWS_CRED_CACHE and CLAUDE_CODE_AWS_CHAIN_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS tune it.

feature: awsAuthRefresh and awsCredentialExport settings
detail: awsAuthRefresh runs a refresh command (e.g. aws sso login) only when credentials are expired; awsCredentialExport returns JSON credentials for cross-account setups.

feature: Enable Bedrock via CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK and region resolution
detail: Region resolved from AWS_REGION, AWS_DEFAULT_REGION, profile, then us-east-1; /status shows it; optional small-fast-model region and custom endpoint URL.

feature: Bedrock limitations: /logout unavailable, no WebSearch tool
detail: Authentication is via AWS credentials so /logout is hidden, and the WebSearch tool is not available on Bedrock.

feature: Pin Bedrock model versions
detail: Set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS/SONNET/HAIKU_MODEL or ANTHROPIC_MODEL (IDs or application inference profile ARNs); unpinned aliases use built-in defaults that can lag.

feature: Bedrock default models and background-task model
detail: Defaults are Opus 5.5 primary and Sonnet 4.5 small/fast; background tasks use Sonnet unless Haiku is pinned or a primary model is selected.

feature: Prompt caching controls on Bedrock
detail: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING turns it off; ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H requests one-hour TTL at higher write cost; availability varies by region.

feature: modelOverrides map versions to inference profile ARNs
detail: Exposes several versions per family in /model, each routed to its own application inference profile ARN.

feature: Startup model checks and pin update prompt
detail: Verifies models are accessible, offers to update stale pins, falls back for the session with a notice; refusals remembered up to a day (CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MODEL_ACCESS_MEMORY).

feature: enforceAvailableModels on Bedrock
detail: Managed allowlist limits startup checks to listed profile IDs (v2.1.287+).

feature: Mid-session model disabled fallback
detail: Switches to another model with a notice, or a configured fallback chain; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MODEL_ACCESS_FALLBACK makes requests fail instead; /model then s picks a session-only model.

feature: Cross-region inference prefixes and ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX
detail: Prefix chosen by region (us-gov, us, eu, apac, global); override values us, eu, apac, jp, au, global; GovCloud always us-gov.

feature: Bedrock IAM policy requirements
detail: Needs InvokeModel, streaming, ListInferenceProfiles, GetInferenceProfile and Marketplace permissions; missing GetInferenceProfile adds a retry round-trip.

feature: 1M token context window on Bedrock
detail: Fable, Sonnet 5+ and Opus 4.7+ default to 1M on Invoke and Mantle; Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 need [1m]; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT keeps 200K.

feature: Bedrock service tiers
detail: ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_SERVICE_TIER set to default, flex or priority sends a tier header on Invoke requests; not for Mantle or gateway.

feature: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
detail: Content filtering via guardrail headers in ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS or a Claude apps gateway; blocked responses end with the configured message.

feature: Mantle endpoint for Claude on Bedrock
detail: Native Anthropic-shape endpoint via CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE with anthropic.-prefixed model IDs; needs bedrock-mantle IAM actions; /status shows Amazon Bedrock (Mantle).

feature: Run Mantle alongside Invoke API
detail: Setting both provider vars routes Mantle-format IDs to Mantle and others to Invoke; availableModels lists Mantle IDs in /model.

feature: Mantle through a gateway (CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_MANTLE_AUTH)
detail: Skips client-side SigV4 signing when a gateway injects credentials and sets ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_MANTLE_BASE_URL.

feature: Bedrock troubleshooting notes
detail: Covers awsAuthRefresh loops behind VPNs, CA store use for AWS calls, gateways rewriting event-stream content-type, zero /context counts before v2.1.196, and Mantle 403/400 errors.

feature: Auto mode classifier replaces routine permission prompts
detail: A classifier reviews each tool call and blocks irreversible, destructive or out-of-environment actions so routine work runs without prompts. By default it trusts only the working directory and the repo's configured remotes; deny and ask rules run before it.

feature: Ask rules as a human checkpoint for push and PR commands
detail: Adding permissions.ask rules such as for git push or gh pr create forces a prompt even in auto mode. Commands phrased differently (git -C dir push) do not match, so a PreToolUse hook is needed for full-text inspection.

feature: Permission deny rules block before the classifier
detail: permissions.deny blocks a matching action before the classifier runs; neither the classifier nor user intent can override it. A boundary stated only in conversation can be lost to context compaction.

feature: Classifier reads CLAUDE.md instructions
detail: The classifier reads the same CLAUDE.md content Claude loads, so a rule like never force push steers both Claude and the classifier.

feature: autoMode settings block scopes: user, managed, --settings flag
detail: autoMode is read from ~/.claude/settings.json, managed settings, or inline --settings/Agent SDK JSON, never from project .claude/settings files so a repo cannot inject its own allow rules. Entries from scopes are merged; developers can add but not remove managed entries.

feature: autoMode.environment trusted infrastructure entries
detail: Prose entries name trusted orgs, buckets, domains and services, covering context slots (organization, cloud, secrets, network, host containment), trust slots (repos, source control, internal domains, buckets, services, package registry) and sensitivity slots. The literal $defaults keeps built-in entries.

feature: autoMode hard_deny, soft_deny and allow rule lists
detail: hard_deny blocks even when the user asks, soft_deny blocks but yields to explicit user intent or allow exceptions, allow overrides soft denials. Explicit, specific user requests clear soft blocks; vague requests do not.

feature: /auto-mode-setup drafts classifier environment entries
detail: Scans CLAUDE.md, README, config, git remotes, permissions and recent session commands (plus two optional scans of shell history and home-directory repos) and drafts autoMode entries; you accept or discard the whole draft, saved to ~/.claude/settings.json. Offers to remove permission rules that auto mode ignores.
plans: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise, Console API key

feature: Prompt to run /auto-mode-setup after repeated blocks
detail: After several blocks with no environment entries, a dialog offers to run the setup; Don't show again stops the offer, and a skillOverrides entry set to off disables the command and the offer.

feature: /permissions Auto mode tab
detail: Lets you view and edit classifier rules and environment entries in the CLI; managed or flag-provided entries are read-only. Not available in the desktop app.

feature: Suspend broad shell allow rules; classifyAllShell
detail: Auto mode drops broad allow rules like Bash(*) but keeps narrow ones; autoMode.classifyAllShell true sends every Bash/PowerShell command through the classifier, including in plan mode, at the cost of slower approvals.

feature: claude auto-mode defaults, config, critique and reset
detail: Subcommands print built-in rules (with --label prefix filter), print the effective merged rules, get AI feedback on custom rules for ambiguity or redundancy, and remove the user autoMode section (confirmation, --yes to skip).

feature: Recently blocked tab to approve denied actions
detail: In /permissions, press r to approve a blocked action so Claude retries it, Enter to approve for later or take back an approval, Esc to apply, Ctrl+C twice to discard. Approval adds no rule and the retry can be blocked again.

feature: PermissionDenied hook captures blocked inputs
detail: A hook receives the exact input of auto mode denials for programmatic handling; denial notices name the matched rule category in brackets.

feature: Policy-category denials (destructive, unauthorized access, oversight, communicat
detail: The server-side classifier can block with broad categories; fix by naming the action and target in chat, adding a trusted destination to environment, or writing an allow entry.

feature: Automatic checkpoints before each prompt
detail: Every prompt that starts a turn snapshots Claude's file edits. The 100 most recent checkpoints keep snapshots, and checkpoints are saved with the conversation so rewind works after resuming.

feature: Checkpoint snapshot retention and cleanupPeriodDays
detail: Session file snapshots are swept by default about 30 days after the last save; rewinding past that can fail with No files were restored. cleanupPeriodDays extends retention.

feature: /rewind and /undo command, double Esc shortcut
detail: Opens the rewind menu listing prior prompts; double Esc with an empty input does the same (from NORMAL mode in vim mode). With text in the input, double Esc clears it and saves it to history.

feature: Rewind: restore code and conversation
detail: Reverts both files and conversation to the chosen prompt; the original prompt returns to the input box for editing or re-sending.

feature: Rewind: restore conversation only
detail: Rewinds the chat to a message while keeping current code. Rewound messages can reappear if you exit before sending another prompt.

feature: Rewind: restore code only
detail: Reverts file changes while keeping the conversation; both code options appear only when the checkpoint has tracked file changes.

feature: Summarize from here / up to here
detail: Compresses the conversation after or before a chosen point into a summary to free context, leaving a Summarized conversation marker; files are unchanged and originals remain in the transcript. You can type guidance for the summary.

feature: Rewind past /clear to previous session
detail: After /clear in the same process, the rewind menu adds a top entry to resume the prior session until you exit or resume another.

feature: Checkpoint limitations: bash, subagents, external edits, links
detail: Files changed only by Bash, subagent edits (except foreground forked skills), outside edits, other sessions, and symlinked or hard-linked files are not restored; mid-turn typed messages show No code restore. Git remains the permanent history.

feature: /branch and --continue --fork-session to branch a session
detail: Alternative to summarizing: branch off to try another approach while keeping the original session intact.

feature: New terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto mode
detail: Interactive sessions default to auto mode, with auto compaction and subagent delegation; default model is Opus at medium effort on most plans and providers.

feature: Permission modes: Manual, auto, bypassPermissions, dontAsk
detail: Manual asks for every edit/command; auto uses the classifier; bypassPermissions approves all not covered by deny/ask (for disposable containers); dontAsk refuses anything not pre-approved. Shift+Tab cycles modes; --permission-mode sets it at launch.

feature: Auto mode pause after repeated blocks
detail: After three blocks in a row or twenty total, auto mode pauses and asks again; in non-interactive -p runs a block denies that one action and the run continues.

feature: Hooks: command, HTTP, MCP tool, prompt and agent handlers
detail: Hooks run at points in the agent loop (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart). Command, http and mcp_tool hooks are deterministic; prompt/agent hooks use a model. onFailure block stops the action if the hook crashes.

feature: Stop hook enforces a check before finishing
detail: A Stop hook that exits with code 2 sends stderr back to Claude and keeps it working; after eight consecutive blocks the turn ends, adjustable with CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP.

feature: /goal condition checked by a separate model
detail: Sets a completion condition that another model evaluates after each turn, sending Claude back to work until met; useful for long background runs.

feature: /code-review in a fresh subagent
detail: Reviews the current diff in a subagent that never saw the conversation, so it is not biased by the code's reasoning.

feature: /verify builds and runs the app to check results
detail: After Claude says it is done, /verify has it build and run the app and inspect the outcome, catching issues tests and typechecks miss.

feature: CLAUDE.md project instructions and CLAUDE.local.md
detail: CLAUDE.md loads into every session; keep it short (guidance under 200 lines). Personal preferences go in a gitignored CLAUDE.local.md.

feature: /init generates a starter CLAUDE.md
detail: Creates an initial instructions file from the codebase to be pruned afterward.

feature: /doctor and /doctor prompt-audit
detail: /doctor suggests cuts for instructions Claude can infer; prompt-audit flags instructions written for older models, pointing to missing files, or contradicting each other.

feature: /context all confirms loaded instructions
detail: Shows what context, including CLAUDE.md, was loaded into the session.

feature: Path-scoped rules in .claude/rules with paths filter
detail: Rule files with a paths glob list load only when Claude works on matching files.

feature: Skills at .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md
detail: Reusable team procedures; only name and description sit in context until the skill is needed. disable-model-invocation true makes a skill user-invoked only via slash command.

feature: MCP servers via claude mcp add and /mcp
detail: Add remote or local MCP servers from the shell; they appear under /mcp where individual servers can be disabled to save context.

feature: Code intelligence plugins for typed languages
detail: Plugins that let Claude jump to definitions instead of reading many files.

feature: @ file references, pasted images, piped input
detail: Type @ and a path to include a file, paste screenshots into the prompt, or pipe command output into claude -p.

feature: /effort levels low, medium, high, xhigh, max
detail: Controls how long Claude thinks; Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku default to medium. ultrathink in a single prompt requests deeper reasoning for one turn.

feature: /model switching including Fable
detail: Switch models in session, e.g. /model fable; Opus is the default, Sonnet cheaper for routine work, Haiku suited to simple subagent jobs.

feature: Subagents: Explore, forks, background, custom agents
detail: Claude delegates broad searches to Explore, forks side tasks, runs subagents in the background by default; custom agents in .claude/agents can set model and restrict tools (e.g. read-only reviewer).

feature: /usage breakdown by skill, subagent, plugin and MCP server
detail: Shows where usage goes and flags patterns such as long context or frequent cache misses above 10%.

feature: Prompt cache duration by auth type
detail: About one hour on a subscription versus five minutes on API key, cloud provider or usage credits; idle long sessions get compacted before expiry.

feature: /clear, /clear <name>, /compact with focus
detail: /clear starts fresh (optionally naming the session left behind); /compact summarizes with a focus instruction.

feature: Esc interrupts Claude mid-action
detail: Stops the current action while keeping work done so far so you can redirect.

feature: /btw side questions
detail: Answers a quick question without adding it to the conversation history.

feature: /rename, --resume by name, --continue
detail: Name a session and resume it later with claude --resume <name>, checkpoints included; --continue resumes the latest.

feature: Headless claude -p with --bare, --allowedTools, --max-turns, --max-budget-usd
detail: Runs once and exits for CI and scripts; --bare skips hooks, skills, plugins, MCP and CLAUDE.md and ignores claude.ai login; --output-format json or stream-json; --permission-mode dontAsk or auto.

feature: /loop repeats a prompt on an interval
detail: Re-runs a prompt every set interval inside the open session, each run another turn of the same conversation.

feature: /schedule cloud scheduled tasks (routines)
detail: Cloud tasks that run on a timer while the laptop is closed, with optional GitHub-event or API triggers; need claude.ai login. Advised to protect main with an unbypassable branch rule.

feature: Parallel sessions with git worktrees (claude -w)
detail: Each session gets its own checkout; the desktop app runs several side by side and cloud sessions run remotely. .worktreeinclude copies listed gitignored files, worktree.symlinkDirectories links large dirs, empty worktrees auto-clean.

feature: /batch splits a large change into 5-30 worktree units
detail: Shows a plan, then each unit gets its own worktree and opens a PR or reports status.

feature: claude agents background overview screen
detail: One screen for everything running in the background on the machine.

feature: /sandbox OS-level filesystem and network confinement
detail: Confines shell commands on macOS, Linux and WSL2, honoring Read deny and WebFetch domain rules; strict sandbox mode in the Overrides tab disables retrying outside the sandbox.

feature: Permission rule scopes: local, user, repo, managed
detail: settings.local.json and user settings are personal; repo settings.json applies to everyone after trust dialog acceptance; managed settings (admin console, MDM, file) cannot be overridden.

feature: /fewer-permission-prompts builds an allowlist
detail: Scans recent transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP calls and adds them to the project allowlist.

feature: Plan mode via Shift+Tab
detail: Cycling to plan mode makes Claude research and propose changes without editing source files; review before approving.

feature: @directory/ mentions
detail: Mentioning a directory with @ lets Claude analyze its contents, e.g. find components missing tests.

feature: Stop hook desktop notification on task completion
detail: A configured Stop hook can send a desktop notification when a long task finishes.

feature: /team-onboarding generates a teammate setup guide
detail: Scans your recent sessions, commands and MCP servers in a project and produces a guide a new teammate can paste as their first message to replicate your setup.

feature: Terminal install in about two minutes, no IDE extension required
detail: Claude Code installs as a terminal command and works after a single /init without an IDE plugin.

feature: Quickstart and common workflows guides
detail: Official starter pages for installing, first tasks, and discoverable features.

feature: Channels: push events into a running session
detail: A channel is an MCP server delivered as a plugin that pushes messages, alerts and webhooks into the open Claude Code session; can be two-way. Events only arrive while the session is open; terminal shows inbound message and a tool-call confirmation but not the reply text.
plans: Pro, Max, Ultra; Team/Enterprise need admin enablement; Console API key; not Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry

feature: Telegram channel plugin
detail: Create a bot in BotFather, install the telegram plugin, set the token with /telegram:configure, start with --channels, pair with a code via /telegram:access pair, then lock to an allowlist policy. Requires Bun.

feature: Discord channel plugin
detail: Needs a Discord bot with Message Content Intent and permissions to view channels, send/thread messages, read history, attach files, add reactions; configure with /discord:configure, DM to pair, then allowlist access.

feature: iMessage channel plugin (macOS)
detail: Reads the Messages database directly and replies via AppleScript; needs Full Disk Access and an Automation prompt, no bot token. Texting yourself works immediately; other senders are added with /imessage:access allow by phone or Apple ID email.

feature: Fakechat demo channel
detail: A localhost chat UI at port 8787 for trying the channel flow with no external service or authentication.

feature: --channels flag opts channels into a session
detail: Servers must be named in --channels (space-separated list) to push messages; presence in .mcp.json is insufficient. Flag is unlisted in --help during preview; --dangerously-load-development-channels tests custom channels.

feature: Channel sender allowlist and pairing
detail: Direct messages reach the session only from allowlisted senders, bootstrapped by pairing code; anyone allowed can also approve or deny tool use if the channel relays permission prompts.

feature: Permission relay for remote approval
detail: Channel servers declaring the capability can forward permission prompts so you approve or deny remotely; otherwise an unattended session pauses at a prompt. In -p mode, tools needing terminal input are disabled.

feature: channelsEnabled and allowedChannelPlugins managed settings
detail: Owners enable channels in Organization settings > Claude Code > Channels or via managed settings; blocked by default on Team/Enterprise, allowed by default for Console without managed settings. allowedChannelPlugins replaces the Anthropic allowlist (marketplace and plugin pairs).

feature: Webhook receiver via a custom channel
detail: CI, error tracker or deploy webhooks can arrive in a session that already has your files and context.

feature: Comparison: cloud sessions, Claude in Slack, MCP, Remote Control
detail: Cloud sessions run in a fresh sandbox cloned from GitHub; Slack @Claude spawns a cloud session; Remote Control lets claude.ai or the mobile app drive a local session; standard MCP only answers on-demand queries.

feature: Build custom channels as MCP servers (one-way or two-way)
detail: A channel declares the claude/channel capability, emits notifications with content and optional meta attributes over stdio, and optionally exposes a reply tool. Events queue and are delivered together on the next turn; no delivery acknowledgement.

feature: Webhook receiver channel for CI and alerts
detail: A local HTTP listener turns POSTed payloads into channel events inside the running session, so CI failures or monitoring alerts reach Claude with project context.

feature: Sender gating to prevent prompt injection via channels
detail: Channels should check the sender identity (not room) against an allowlist before emitting events; an ungated channel is an injection vector.

feature: Permission relay: approve tool use from chat with yes/no and ID
detail: A channel can receive permission prompts in parallel with the terminal dialog and reply yes or no with a five-letter request ID; first answer wins. Covers tool-use approvals only, not project trust or MCP consent dialogs.

feature: Relayed prompt sanitization and credential masking
detail: Relayed descriptions and input previews are sanitized, whitespace-folded and capped near 3,500 characters (middle elided), and recognizable provider credential tokens are replaced with a redaction marker; unprefixed secrets are not masked.

feature: Packaging channels as plugins and allowlist rules
detail: Channels ship as plugins installed with /plugin install and enabled with --channels; only claude-plugins-official channels are default-approved, others need the development flag (interactive only) or an org allowedChannelPlugins entry. The development flag is ignored with -p or the Agent SDK.

feature: Claude Code browser automation through Claude in Chrome
detail: Connects the CLI or VS Code extension to the Chrome extension so Claude opens tabs in a visible window, shares your logged-in state, and pauses for logins or CAPTCHAs. Tabs are grouped per session and closed on /clear.
plans: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise (direct Anthropic plan)

feature: Chrome capabilities: debug, verify design, test, extract, automate
detail: Reads console errors and DOM state, verifies UI against a Figma mock, tests forms and flows, works in authenticated apps (Docs, Gmail, Notion), extracts data to local files, fills forms, uploads files, and records GIFs.

feature: Supported browsers and platform limits
detail: Works with Chrome and Edge, and detected in Brave, Arc, Vivaldi and Opera; not supported in WSL or via Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry; requires /login (API key or setup-token auth keeps it off). Extension version 1.0.36 or later.

feature: Chrome availability with HIPAA and zero data retention
detail: For HIPAA Enterprise orgs it is off by default and an Owner can enable it in Organization settings (BAA does not cover third-party site data); with ZDR it is unavailable in Claude Code.

feature: claude --chrome flag and /chrome command
detail: Launch with --chrome; /chrome shows status, manages permissions, reconnects the extension, chooses which connected browser to use, and toggles Enabled by default (shared between CLI and VS Code).

feature: Install extension prompt and startup dialog
detail: When the extension is missing, a once-per-session prompt offers Install extension (guided setup), Not now, or Don't ask again; a startup dialog on detection sets Enabled by default yes or no. Managed MCP policies can suppress the prompt.

feature: VS Code @browser and Enabled by default switch
detail: In VS Code, type @browser or turn on Enabled by default (v2.1.287+ connects at session start); permission prompts appear as cards in chat with an option to allow the site. Always-on browser tools raise context usage.

feature: Per-site permissions and allow-all-for-session
detail: Claude Code asks before browser actions with a dialog offering to allow all actions on a site for the session; in auto mode the classifier's approval can skip the extension's per-site check unless deny rules apply.

feature: Browser tools in plan mode prompt first
detail: Recording a GIF or opening a new tab in plan mode prompts for permission, as do tabs_context calls with createIfEmpty and batch calls containing those actions.

feature: File upload to web pages
detail: Attaches local files to page upload fields in local or remote sessions; limited to 10 MB total, needs Read permission, refuses multi-hard-linked files and credential-named files (.env, .pem, .key, .ssh).

feature: Record GIF of browser interactions and save screenshots
detail: Claude can record a browser flow as a GIF (captures everything visible, including account details) and save screenshots to disk, reporting the path.

feature: Multi-site workflows and Google Docs drafting
detail: Claude works across tabs, e.g. reading a calendar then researching attendees, or typing a draft directly into a Google Doc without API connectors.

feature: Project settings cannot enable Chrome
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_CFC in project settings is ignored with a warning so a checked-out repo cannot connect Claude to your browser.

feature: Chrome troubleshooting: reconnect, org mismatch, native host
detail: /chrome Reconnect extension fixes idle service worker drops; the extension must be signed in to the same claude.ai org as Claude Code (/status shows it); a native messaging host file is installed per browser; logging out of the extension loses its shortcuts and scheduled tasks; network needs bridge.claudeusercontent.com.

feature: Computer use for native macOS apps
detail: Referenced as the option for tasks that cannot be done in a browser.

feature: Claude apps gateway: self-hosted YAML-configured gateway for Claude Code
detail: One gateway.yaml (started with claude gateway --config) defines listener, OIDC sign-in, sessions, Postgres store, inference upstreams, model routing, managed policies and telemetry; validated against a schema at boot.

feature: Gateway SSO via OIDC with email-domain and group restrictions
detail: Developers sign in through the org identity provider; sign-in can be limited by allowed email domains and IdP groups, custom claim paths for email and groups, userinfo fallback, PKCE, custom scopes, clock-skew tolerance and extra auth params.

feature: Gateway Google Workspace group lookup
detail: For Google as IdP, groups are fetched via the Admin SDK Directory API using a service account with delegation, so group emails drive sign-in and policy matching.

feature: Certificate (private_key_jwt) client authentication to the IdP
detail: Gateway can authenticate to the IdP token endpoint with a signed JWT from a certificate instead of a client secret (e.g. Entra); supports rotation by uploading the new cert first.

feature: Gateway IdP requests via forward proxy and proxy-only egress
detail: oidc.use_proxy routes IdP calls through HTTPS_PROXY; CLAUDE_GATEWAY_PROXY_IS_EGRESS_BOUNDARY hands hostnames to the proxy for locked-down networks, with an SSRF guard otherwise.

feature: Gateway session token lifetime and secret rotation
detail: Gateway-minted bearer tokens default to one hour with silent refresh when the IdP issues refresh tokens; jwt_secret accepts an array so secrets can be rotated.

feature: Gateway PostgreSQL store for device grants and rate limits
detail: Requires a Postgres URL; the gateway migrates its schema at boot and exposes pool size, connect timeout and readiness grace settings.

feature: Gateway secret expansion from env vars and files
detail: Secrets in the config are referenced as ${VAR} or ${file:/path} and resolved at boot instead of being written inline.

feature: Gateway listener, public URL, TLS and trusted proxies
detail: Configure bind host/port, required public https URL, optional TLS cert/key, and trusted proxy CIDRs for real client IP in rate limiting and audit.

feature: Ordered upstream list with failover
detail: Gateway forwards inference to the first upstream that serves the model and fails over on 5xx, 429, 401, 403, 404 or timeout; other 4xx are returned. Same provider can repeat with distinct names (regions, accounts, provisioned throughput).

feature: Upstream providers: Anthropic API, Bedrock, Mantle, Claude Platform on AWS, Goog
detail: Supported inference backends with their own auth (API key, OAuth bearer, workload identity federation, AWS credential chain, Azure AD, Google ADC) and endpoint overrides for FIPS, VPC or Private Service Connect.

feature: Per-user identity headers to a proxy upstream
detail: forward_user_identity adds developer email and subject headers so a proxy you run can attribute spend; a per-user 429 is returned instead of failing over.

feature: Amazon Bedrock guardrails on gateway traffic
detail: A guardrail id and version can be applied to every Bedrock request; input_tagging (last_message, user_messages, all_messages, all_messages_and_system) controls tagged text; tool results, images and PDFs are not covered.

feature: Guardrail trace logging
detail: guardrail_trace true writes guardrail.trace audit events with filter details but without matched text; Bedrock trace data is stripped from replies.

feature: Bedrock assume_role and per-developer AWS cost attribution
detail: Gateway assumes a role (possibly in another account) for short-lived credentials; session_name email or sub gives each developer their own AWS session for billing attribution.

feature: Per-team upstreams via groups lists
detail: Each upstream can list IdP groups so only those developers reach a given AWS account or Google project; open upstreams go last; developers in no listed group get a 400.

feature: Static headers on upstream requests
detail: headers: adds fixed headers to requests for one upstream for proxy routing; reserved names (authorization, x-api-key, host, anthropic-*, x-amz-*) are refused.

feature: Custom model IDs restricted to specific upstreams
detail: A models entry with an upstream_model map pins a custom id to named upstreams (e.g. an isolated account), maps provisioned-throughput ARNs, or Foundry deployment names.

feature: Gateway upstream error mapping and auto-compact token
detail: Gateway returns upstream status with generic or capability_rejected messages for cloud providers (e.g. prompt_too_long) so Claude Code compacts automatically.

feature: Gateway login notice
detail: Up to 500-character notice shown before sign-in on the verification page and terminal sign-in screen (needs Claude Code 2.1.319+).

feature: Gateway per-developer spend limits and Admin API
detail: An admin block enables /v1/organizations/spend_limits with named read and write API keys, admin_groups for human admins, a custom blocked message on the 429 billing error, and configurable audit, spend and identity retention periods.

feature: Pooled group budgets and conflict ordering
detail: A group can share one monthly pooled budget on top of each member's cap; with several groups, budgets are tried by largest limit first or by an explicit priority list.

feature: Group cap resolution min or max
detail: When a developer is in several groups with caps, the gateway enforces the most restrictive (min, default) or least restrictive (max).

feature: Spend enforcement fail-open or fail-closed
detail: If Postgres is down, enforcement defaults to fail open so inference stays up; fail_closed_on_error blocks over-cap developers (and everyone if the store is unreachable).

feature: Contracted pricing and multiplier for the spend meter
detail: pricing.multiplier (greater than 0, up to 10) and per-upstream per-model rate overrides make caps and /effective reflect contract rates or an internal markup; web search stays at list price.

feature: Rates pushed to clients so /usage, status line and telemetry match
detail: The gateway serves pricing as the modelPricing managed setting so developers matched by a policy see contracted costs; a policy can opt out with an empty value.

feature: Admin-curated model list and built-in model toggle
detail: models block (id, label, description, per-upstream IDs) is served at /v1/models; auto_include_builtin_models false exposes only listed models; the fable alias needs an explicit (model name) entry in that case.

feature: Managed policies by IdP group or email domain
detail: Ordered policies matched by groups and/or email_domain, with a match-all catch-all as base; allow-lists replace, deny-lists and hooks union, env/modelOverrides/skillOverrides merge; served per-user with ETag caching.

feature: Layered policy mode applies every matching policy
detail: policy_mode layered applies all matching policies instead of first match, with caveats that combined rules can be looser than any single policy.

feature: Server-side model allowlist enforcement
detail: availableModels is enforced at /v1/messages so patched clients cannot bypass it; enforceAvailableModels makes the Default model resolve within the list; deniedModels and availableModelsMatch block specific models or versions.

feature: Gateway has no user directory or SCIM
detail: Authorization comes from IdP token claims; user lifecycle is managed in the IdP and group changes take effect at next token refresh; policy edits reach clients on an hourly poll.

feature: Policy key code vs cli (Claude Desktop Code tab coverage)
detail: Claude Code settings in a policy go under code (recommended) or cli (legacy; alias settings); code can also cover the Claude Desktop Code tab when a desktop block is present.

feature: Managed settings pushed through the gateway
detail: A policy carries a full managed-settings document: permissions (deny, bypass disable, managed-rules-only), env variables (e.g. DISABLE_UPDATES), org-wide hooks and managed remote MCP servers (http/sse).

feature: Security approval dialog for network-delivered settings
detail: Before applying hooks, proxy/base-URL env vars, shell-execution settings or weakened sandbox settings, the CLI asks the developer to approve; declining exits the session; non-interactive runs apply for that run only.

feature: 1M context in gateway terminal sessions
detail: Sessions signed in through /login use a 1M window for current Opus, Sonnet and Fable models, compacting near 967K tokens; auto-compact window can be lowered via policy env.

feature: One-hour prompt cache TTL via policy
detail: promptCacheTtl and subagentPromptCacheTtl in a policy request a one-hour cache instead of five minutes; fails if any upstream rejects the TTL, and one-hour writes cost more.

feature: Managed MCP servers delivered by policy
detail: managedMcpServers in a policy provides remote (http/sse) MCP servers to all matching developers alongside their own; entries are validated at boot.

feature: Claude Desktop connects to the gateway via bootstrapUrl
detail: Desktop's managed config points bootstrapUrl at the gateway, uses device-code sign-in and fetches settings; only policies with a desktop key (even empty) serve it.

feature: Settings derived for Claude Desktop from policy
detail: Gateway derives model list, disabled tools, egress allowlist and an OTLP endpoint with user identity for Desktop; policy desktop block can set keys directly (e.g. disable auto updates, banner, local dev MCP).

feature: Code settings applied in Desktop Code tab
detail: code-block settings apply in the Desktop Code tab when the policy has a desktop key, Desktop 2.9939.2+, client-side managed settings name the gateway and the machine reaches it over HTTPS on a private network; web search turns off in Cowork, Chat and Code tab.

feature: Desktop policy refresh timing and relaunch enforcement
detail: Desktop fetches policy at start and rechecks every 10 minutes; some settings need a Relaunch card and Desktop auto-restarts after 24 hours (relaunchEnforcementHours can shorten, 0 immediate).

feature: 1M context option in Claude Desktop model picker
detail: Desktop offers a 1M variant for eligible Opus, Sonnet and Fable models; modelPrefer1mContext starts new users on it; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT removes it.

feature: Precedence of gateway settings over MDM or local managed settings
detail: Gateway-delivered settings rank first; policies apply to every invocation including claude -p and Agent SDK, and signed-in sessions exit with an error if the gateway is unreachable at startup.

feature: Gateway telemetry relay via OTLP to your collectors
detail: CLI, Desktop and Cowork send metrics, logs and optional traces to the gateway which forwards to configured https destinations with per-signal opt-in (default metrics only); data never goes to Anthropic.

feature: Telemetry stamped with user identity and groups
detail: Exports carry user.id, user.email and user.groups (and enduser.sub for Desktop/Cowork) for per-developer cost attribution; custom resource_attributes labels can be added.

feature: Direct-to-collector telemetry via policy env
detail: A policy can set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and headers so sessions export straight to your collector, subject to checks and a developer approval dialog; signing out stops exports.

feature: Telemetry destination failure handling
detail: Gateway does not buffer or retry; after five consecutive failures it pauses forwarding in 30-second stretches, except payload-refusal statuses which just log warnings.

feature: Gateway IP allow/deny lists
