detail: access_control allow_cidrs and deny_cidrs restrict client addresses (deny first, default-deny when allow set); boot and runtime warnings flag public clients; health endpoints exempt.

feature: Gateway request size, header, URL, timeout and sign-in rate limits
detail: Configurable max body (32 MiB default), header and URL length caps, upstream time-to-first-byte (120 s default for Anthropic upstream), and per-IP limits on device authorization and code verification.

feature: Gateway load_test_mode
detail: Streams canned replies without calling a provider to load-test the gateway and database; must use an empty database and never on production gateways.

feature: Force gateway login with managed settings
detail: forceLoginMethod gateway plus forceLoginGatewayUrl in per-OS managed-settings.json route every developer's /login to the org gateway; parentSettingsBehavior merge keeps Desktop's egress allowlist working in embedded sessions.

feature: allowedProviders gateway lock
detail: Setting allowedProviders to gateway makes Claude Code refuse sessions that bypass the gateway via cloud provider variables or a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (needs 2.1.285+).

feature: Deploying client managed settings through MDM
detail: The managed-settings.json is deployed per device, typically via MDM; registry or plist policies replace the file rather than merging.

feature: Gateway log level and JSON log format env vars
detail: CLAUDE_GATEWAY_LOG_LEVEL (debug to error) and CLAUDE_GATEWAY_LOG_FORMAT=json control operational logs; audit events are always emitted.

feature: Claude Code cloud sessions
detail: Coding sessions run on cloud infrastructure and keep going after the laptop closes; they can be checked or steered from any device and count toward plan usage with no separate VM charge.
plans: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise (premium or Chat + Claude Code seats)

feature: Start a cloud session from browser, phone Code tab, Desktop or terminal
detail: Cloud sessions can be started at claude.ai/code, the Code tab of the mobile app, the Desktop environment selector (Cloud), or the CLI with --cloud; scheduled runs also execute as cloud sessions.

feature: Custom role permission for cloud sessions
detail: Where custom roles govern access, a role must include the cloud sessions permission before a member can start sessions on Anthropic infrastructure; owners add it under Organization settings > Roles.

feature: Cloud environments (network, env vars, setup scripts)
detail: Each cloud session runs in a saved environment controlling network access, environment variables and setup scripts; onboarding creates a Default environment with Limited network access.

feature: GitHub App connection for cloud sessions
detail: Authorize the Claude GitHub App during web onboarding to reach public repos and private repos where it is installed; required for Auto-fix and for project threads.

feature: /web-setup: connect GitHub using the local gh token
detail: Running /web-setup sends the local gh CLI token to the Claude account so cloud sessions can reach any repository that token can access, with or without the GitHub App.

feature: GitHub credentials stay outside the cloud VM
detail: In Anthropic-hosted environments GitHub credentials, signing keys and network secrets stay encrypted server-side and a proxy attaches them to requests; they never enter the VM.

feature: Cloud sessions unavailable under ZDR, HIPAA config or CMEK
detail: Organizations with Zero Data Retention, the HIPAA configuration, or customer-managed encryption keys cannot use /web-setup or cloud sessions.

feature: Quick setup toggle for Claude Code cloud onboarding
detail: An owner toggle (off by default) at Organization settings > Claude Code that enables /web-setup for members, skips the GitHub App install prompt and auto-creates the Default environment.

feature: claude --cloud: start a cloud session from the terminal
detail: Creates a new cloud session for the current repo and branch (clone from GitHub, so push first) with a live setup checklist and queued typed messages; runs in parallel for multiple tasks. --remote is a deprecated alias.

feature: Plan locally, then execute in the cloud
detail: Use plan mode in the CLI to agree an approach, commit the plan, then launch a cloud session to execute it autonomously.

feature: Upload a local repo bundle to the cloud (no GitHub required)
detail: If the repo has no remote or the GitHub App is missing, the repo is bundled (history plus uncommitted tracked changes, under 100 MB, with fallbacks to current branch or snapshot) and uploaded; CCR_FORCE_BUNDLE=1 forces it.

feature: Sensitive files excluded from repo bundle uploads
detail: On macOS, Linux and WSL, uncommitted edits to env files, tfvars, key files and git-filter-managed files are left out of uploads with a notice; native Windows uploads tracked changes as they are.

feature: Send follow-up messages to a running cloud session from the CLI
detail: claude -p "message" --cloud <session-id> queues a message into a session from any logged-in machine and exits; supports stdin, session URLs and --output-format json.

feature: Cloud sessions require an Anthropic account and org policy
detail: --cloud needs a claude.ai sign-in (not API key, Console, Bedrock or Vertex) and the organization's allow_remote_sessions policy enabled by an owner.

feature: Teleport a cloud session into the terminal
detail: claude --teleport (picker or ID), /teleport or /tp, /tasks then t, or Open in > Terminal pulls a cloud session and its branch local; requires clean git state, same repo, pushed branch and same account; terminal copy diverges from the cloud one.

feature: Send a local Desktop session to the cloud
detail: The Desktop app Code tab can push a local session to the cloud from its Open in menu, whereas the CLI hand-off is one-way (cloud to terminal only).

feature: Permission mode picker for cloud sessions
detail: Choose a permission mode from the mode dropdown at task creation and while running; the mode is kept when reopening after environment expiry or a self-hosted runner release.

feature: Changes card and diff view with inline comments
detail: After a push, the Changes card shows lines added/removed and opens a diff where you can leave inline line comments to send with your next message and compare against any branch instead of the base.

feature: Activity panel / session rail toggle
detail: The panel beside the chat (Changes etc.) can be shown from the Activity panel or Show session rail buttons or the title bar menu, and Changes can open as a pane in Desktop.

feature: Slash commands in cloud sessions take arguments
detail: Text-output built-in commands work; /model, /effort, /color and /rename take an argument instead of a picker; /fast toggles fast mode; /config opens settings in the browser; terminal-only commands like /plugin and /resume are unavailable.

feature: /compact, /context, /clear and auto-compaction in the cloud
detail: Summarize history with optional focus text, view context contents, or reset the conversation; auto-compaction triggers before the window fills, and the window can be changed with /autocompact or an env variable.

feature: Subagents and opt-in agent teams in the cloud
detail: Subagents in the repo .claude/agents load automatically; agent teams are off by default and enabled with an experimental environment variable.

feature: Plugin suggestion cards with Add and Manage
detail: Claude may show a card suggesting plugins for the task; Add turns the plugin on for the account permanently and Manage opens its claude.ai page to remove it.

feature: Disable plugin suggestions via permission deny rules
detail: Deny the SearchPlugins and SuggestPluginInstall tools in permissions to stop suggestions; ignored in repo settings when managed settings restrict permission rules.

feature: Take back a queued message
detail: A message sent while Claude is working queues; clicking the x on it returns the text to the box unless Claude has already read it.

feature: Share cloud sessions: Private/Team or Private/Public
detail: Team and Enterprise sessions are Private or Team visible (repo access verification on by default, display name shown, Slack sessions auto Team); Pro/Max/Ultra are Private or Public to any logged-in claude.ai user, verification off by default.

feature: Sharing settings: require repo access, hide name
detail: Individual accounts can require recipients to have repository access and hide their name in shared sessions, under Privacy or Claude Code > Sharing settings.

feature: Archive and unarchive cloud sessions
detail: Archive from the session menu to remove it from the sidebar; find it on the Archived tab at claude.ai/code/sessions and unarchive there. Archived sessions cannot accept new messages.

feature: Permanently delete a cloud session
detail: Delete from the sidebar, session menu or Archived tab, with a confirmation; it permanently removes the session and its data.

feature: Auto-fix pull requests
detail: Claude watches a PR and reacts to CI failures and review comments, pushing clear fixes, asking about ambiguous ones, and replying in threads labeled as Claude Code; enabled from the Changes card, /autofix-pr, mobile, or by pasting a PR URL. Merge conflicts are not detected.

feature: Cloud session network access controls
detail: Anthropic-hosted environments default to limited network access with a default domain allowlist and can disable it entirely; the Anthropic API remains reachable even with access off.

feature: Cloud session environment expiry and reopen
detail: Idle sessions are reclaimed; reopening provisions a fresh VM restoring conversation history but not running shell commands, subagents or session-scoped scheduled tasks and loops.

feature: Cloud session limitations: GitHub only, shared limits
detail: Clone and PR creation need GitHub (GitHub Enterprise Server on Team/Enterprise); other hosts only via local bundle without push-back; sessions share plan rate limits and have command and setup-script time limits.

feature: Self-hosted environments for cloud sessions
detail: Organizations can route cloud sessions to their own self-hosted runners, where isolation and git credentials are the deployment's job and network secrets are unavailable.

feature: Claude Code Projects: one coordinating conversation with parallel threads
detail: A project is a long-running conversation where Claude acts as coordinator, starting a cloud-session thread per task, routing follow-ups, and reporting back; threads run in parallel and can be steered from the phone.
plans: Pro, Max, Ultra (not Team or Enterprise yet)

feature: Projects gradual rollout and waitlist
detail: Projects appear in the claude.ai/code and desktop Code-tab sidebar (or under More) as the rollout reaches an account; others can join a waitlist. Accounts with existing chat or Cowork projects are reached later.

feature: New project dialog (name, goal, context)
detail: Only a name is required; optional one-line goal and context of GitHub repos, files, folders or Google Drive folders. If old claude.ai projects exist the button reads Get started and asks to upgrade or archive them first.

feature: Setup recommendations on first project turn
detail: On a first project Claude takes its own turn, may start an exploratory read-only thread and posts recommended repositories, scheduled tasks and threads that can each be toggled before Update setup.

feature: Continue in project from an existing session
detail: A cloud session (or a Remote Control local session) can be turned into a new project or folded into an existing one from its sidebar menu or a Set up project banner; blocked for local sessions when Require trusted devices is on.

feature: GitHub setup for projects: App install, org owner approval, SSO
detail: Project threads need github.com repos with push access and the Claude GitHub App installed (org owner approval required); SAML SSO orgs must be authorized; the dialog names missing steps and offers Check again.

feature: Claude routes messages: answer, new thread, or existing thread
detail: Quick questions are answered in place, new work becomes or joins a thread, unrelated tasks in one message become separate threads; users can override routing in plain language.

feature: Suggested threads list
detail: Claude can propose threads instead of starting them; an arrow starts one and a button starts all.

feature: Thread pull request behavior with auto-fix
detail: Cloud threads branch from the default branch, open a PR when asked or for concrete fixes, then watch it with auto-fix on, pushing CI fixes, addressing comments and replying when ready.

feature: Project Overview pane with thread states
detail: A pane groups threads into Ready for review, Waiting on you, Working, Landing, Idle and Resolved (resolved manually, by Claude, or after a week idle; reopenable); a Threads button shows a dot when input is needed.

feature: Project Library and Scheduled tasks views
detail: Library holds added files and folders plus files threads produce; Scheduled tasks lists the cloud scheduled tasks Claude set up from the project.

feature: Desktop project notifications
detail: By default notifies when Claude posts in the conversation, a thread errors or needs input (not while viewing); a per-project Notifications menu adds per-turn notifications or turns them off.

feature: Open and steer a single thread
detail: Opening a thread shows its messages and status, lets you message it directly, answer its permission prompts and interrupt it with Stop; project-conversation follow-ups only reach it if Claude matches them.

feature: Project coordinator and thread model and effort
detail: Project settings set separate model and effort for the coordinator and for threads; new projects default to Opus (high effort for threads, low for conversation), and one task or running thread can use a different model.

feature: Automatic context management in projects
detail: Threads auto-compact and the conversation works from recent messages, recent threads and project memory so a project can run indefinitely; a thread that overflows shows a ran-out-of-context message and may continue in a fresh session.

feature: Tune project behavior in natural language
detail: Tell Claude how many threads to run, whether to propose before starting, update frequency, when to open PRs or use smaller models; preferences are saved to project memory but are not hard caps.

feature: Auto mode for project threads and in-thread approvals
detail: Threads run in auto mode when the model supports it; approval prompts appear inside the thread and only that thread, not the project conversation, can answer them; repo permission rules are not applied.

feature: Run a project thread on your own computer (Work locally)
detail: A thread can run in a local folder via Remote Control (Claude Code v2.1.280+, desktop toggle or claude remote-control with optional --spawn worktree), chosen from the + menu and allowed on a card with Allow once and optional Worktree; it uses local files, MCP, hooks and permissions and pauses when the computer sleeps.

feature: Use this computer from your phone and claude.ai / Keep awake
detail: Settings > Code toggles to expose local folders to Remote Control, plus Keep this computer awake for Remote Control so local project threads keep running.

feature: Project memory (auto memory files)
detail: Claude keeps notes about requirements, decisions and pitfalls as files with a MEMORY.md index that every cloud thread reads; ask it to remember or forget, and read, edit or delete in Project settings > Memory.

feature: Project instructions (16,000 characters)
detail: A standing brief sent to every new thread and the coordinator, up to 16,000 characters, set in Project settings > Memory or by asking Claude to change it.

feature: Project repositories and per-thread repo adding
detail: Added repos are cloned into every thread with CLAUDE.md loaded; threads can self-add other repos from the same GitHub owner, scoped to that thread; a project can have no repo and deliver files to the Library.

feature: Project file and folder uploads and limits
detail: Upload up to 1,000 files and 2 GB per batch, single file up to 480 MB; folders skip hidden files and node_modules, max 10 folders plus Google Drive folders; uploads are copies replaced via Replace; threads read them under /mnt/project-files.

feature: What cloud threads inherit from repositories
detail: CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules and repo skills, agents and commands load; .mcp.json servers, repo-enabled plugins, settings permission rules, hooks and env do not; older threads and dot-named repos skip repo skills.

feature: Connectors, plugins and skills in project threads
detail: Threads use all claude.ai account connectors and account-enabled skills; plugins are added in Project settings > Plugins; a thread's + menu Connectors toggle removes one from that thread and saves it as the account default; the coordinator itself has no connectors.

feature: Project settings: General, Environment, Plugins, Usage, Memory
detail: Settings cover name, icon and goal, coordinator/thread model and effort, instructions, repos, cloud environment, plugins, usage by thread and model, memory, auto-continue, restart Claude, and pause/archive/delete; changes affect new threads only.

feature: Auto-continue when usage limits reset
detail: On by default: a thread or project conversation stopped at the 5-hour or weekly limit continues itself at reset; a project-wide setting can turn it off.

feature: Pause, archive and delete a project
detail: Pause halts everything until Resume; Archive hides the project and its threads and stops scheduled tasks (Unarchive from Projects page); Delete permanently removes threads, memory and files but not GitHub branches or PRs.

feature: Project usage, cost and 500 threads/day cap
detail: Projects draw on the same plan limits and only exceed them with usage credits; a hard limit of 500 new threads per day applies, and the Usage panel shows tokens by thread and model; watched PRs can wake idle threads.

feature: Project limitations: single-user, no sharing, no org controls
detail: A project belongs to one user with no sharing of project or thread transcripts, no org-level controls in beta, no moving threads between projects or merging projects, and no CLI, IDE or Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry availability.

feature: Restart Claude when the project conversation is silent
detail: A banner or Project settings > General row restarts the coordinator when replies stop arriving; an in-progress reply is lost but threads are unaffected.

feature: Claude Tag compared with Projects
detail: Claude Tag is team Slack Claude on Team and Enterprise where everyone in a channel steers shared work; Projects are single-user on Pro, Max and Ultra with the user's own GitHub and connectors.

feature: CLAUDE.md project and global instruction files
detail: Markdown instructions loaded every session from the project and from ~/.claude; AGENTS.md can be read in place of CLAUDE.md, and CLAUDE.local.md holds private project preferences.

feature: .claude/rules topic files with optional path gating
detail: Instruction files split by topic; rules with a paths frontmatter load only when a matching file is touched, others load at start. Available per project and globally.

feature: settings.json and settings.local.json with precedence
detail: Enforced permissions, hooks, env vars and model defaults at project, local-personal, global and managed levels; single-value keys take the highest ranked file and lists merge; most edits apply mid-session.

feature: Managed settings override all local settings
detail: Organization-deployed managed-settings.json or server-managed settings outrank every settings file and flag except narrow exceptions; a cached remote-settings.json refreshes at startup and hourly.

feature: .mcp.json project MCP servers and tool search
detail: Team-shared MCP servers load after approval at session start, with tool schemas deferred and loaded on demand; personal servers live in ~/.claude.json.

feature: .worktreeinclude for git worktrees
detail: Lists gitignored files (gitignore syntax) to copy into new worktrees created by --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool or subagent worktree isolation.

feature: Skills (SKILL.md) invoked by /name or auto-matching
detail: Skill folders with supporting files, usable by user and Claude by default; frontmatter such as disable-model-invocation and user-invocable restrict who can call it; many other frontmatter fields (model, effort, context, hooks, paths, allowed-tools) exist.

feature: Custom slash commands in .claude/commands
detail: A single Markdown file becomes a /command; superseded by skills for anything needing bundled references or scripts.

feature: Output styles (.claude/output-styles)
detail: Markdown files adjusting how Claude works or responds, selected with /output-style, /config or the outputStyle setting; project style wins over same-named global; read at startup.

feature: Custom subagents (.claude/agents)
detail: Markdown files with name and description define subagents with own prompt, tools, model, permission mode, memory, hooks, isolation and more, each running in its own context window.

feature: Dynamic workflows (.claude/workflows/*.js)
detail: Scripts that spawn and coordinate many subagents, written by Claude and saved from /workflows; each saved workflow runs as a /name command when workflows are on.

feature: Persistent subagent memory (project and user scope)
detail: Subagents with memory set to project or user keep their own MEMORY.md index (first 200 lines, 25KB loaded) while auto memory is on.

feature: Auto memory per project
detail: Claude saves notes about your role, corrections, decisions and references in per-project topic files indexed by MEMORY.md (first 200 lines or 25KB loaded at start); you can edit or delete them and the sweep never deletes them.

feature: Custom keybindings (~/.claude/keybindings.json)
detail: Rebind interactive CLI shortcuts via /keybindings; the file hot-reloads and some shortcuts are reserved.

feature: Custom color themes and /theme
detail: JSON themes with a built-in base preset plus color-token overrides, created via /theme, hot-reloaded and stored as a custom theme preference.

feature: ~/.claude.json global config and /config
detail: Holds account details, per-project trust decisions, personal MCP servers and UI toggles; written when changing options in /config or trusting a folder.

feature: Installed and synced plugins
detail: Plugins from marketplaces live under ~/.claude/plugins; plugins and skills synced from a claude.ai account download there and removed ones go to a recoverable .trash until swept; command-source plugins need v2.1.229+.

feature: Local transcript retention (cleanupPeriodDays)
detail: Transcripts, subagent logs, tool results, file snapshots, plans, debug logs, pastes and uploads are deleted after a configurable age (default 30, minimum 1); managed settings can set it and desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays limits Desktop/Cowork transcripts.

feature: Checkpoint restore via file-history snapshots
detail: Pre-edit snapshots of changed files for the 100 most recent checkpoints enable rewind and restore of past sessions.

feature: Session scratchpad directory
detail: A per-session temp directory Claude uses for intermediate files without permission prompts; available only with claude.ai sign-in, Anthropic API and enableArtifact not false; removed with the transcript or OS cleanup.

feature: Prompt history recall and Ctrl+R search
detail: history.jsonl stores typed prompts for up-arrow recall, Ctrl+R history search and ! shell-command completion; kept until deleted (trimmed by age under HIPAA).

feature: /usage totals and /insights reports
detail: Cached token and cost counts back /usage; /insights writes an HTML usage report and cached analysis to usage-data.

feature: /feedback bundles and Claude-drafted feedback
detail: On third-party providers or without Anthropic credentials, /feedback writes redacted transcript archives to send to an account team; Claude can queue up to 10 drafted feedback items to review.

feature: claude purge: delete a project's local data
detail: Removes a project's transcripts, auto memory, tasks, debug, file-history, matching prompt history and config entry; supports --dry-run, --yes, --all and -i, confirms before deleting; formerly claude project purge.

feature: Skip transcript persistence options
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY or --no-session-persistence with -p (and persistSession false in the TypeScript SDK) prevent writing transcripts; transcripts are otherwise plaintext, so deny rules on credential files are advised.

feature: Remote Control attachments saved locally
detail: Files and phone photos attached from web or mobile to a Remote Control session are saved under ~/.claude/uploads, while cloud-session attachments stay in the cloud environment.

feature: Background sessions and task lists state
detail: Task lists written by task tools and background session state (jobs and daemon) persist locally; MCP tasks that run on the server can be resumed.

feature: Mods Claude writes during a session
detail: Mods that Claude created for its own interface are stored per session under dev-mods.

feature: /release-notes cached changelog and /debug logs
detail: The changelog is cached and refreshed in the background for /release-notes; --debug or /debug writes per-session debug logs; /heapdump snapshots contain credentials and must be deleted manually.

feature: Claude apps gateway (self-hosted, built into claude binary)
detail: A self-hosted service run with claude gateway --config that sits between Claude Code/Desktop clients and Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, Foundry or the Anthropic API, with SSO sign-in, per-group policy and telemetry; requires v2.1.195+.

feature: Gateway SSO sign-in with OIDC device flow
detail: Developers sign in via browser with a corporate OIDC IdP (Okta, Entra, Google Workspace, Keycloak, Dex etc.) and get short-lived tokens without API keys or a claude.ai account; SAML and LDAP are unsupported; /logout clears the credential.

feature: Per-IdP-group model access and managed settings
detail: Groups map to model allowlists, managed settings policies and upstreams; model access is enforced server-side (disallowed models return 400) and the /model picker is filtered.

feature: Gateway delivers managed settings (replaces admin-console settings)
detail: Gateway sessions fetch settings from the gateway's managed block hourly instead of claude.ai server-managed settings; sessions exit at startup if the gateway is unreachable after about 10 seconds.

feature: Gateway OTLP telemetry fan-out
detail: OTLP/HTTP metrics with token counts, model, user identity and latency go to configured destinations, with logs and traces opt-in per destination; the gateway stores no prompt or completion content; gRPC unsupported.

feature: Multi-upstream routing and failover through the gateway
detail: Clients speak the Messages API while the gateway translates per upstream (Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, Foundry, Anthropic API) and fails over; model catalogs translate automatically.

feature: Gateway private-network and TLS fingerprint pinning guards
detail: Claude Code only logs in to a gateway on private addresses (or admin-declared public blocks via gatewayInternalNetworks) and pins the TLS certificate on first connect with a trust prompt that shows a fingerprint; rotations re-prompt.

feature: forceLoginMethod and forceLoginGatewayUrl settings
detail: Managed (or user, v2.1.295+) settings that open /login on the Cloud gateway screen with the URL prefilled; sessions using API keys or helpers exit at startup on managed machines; CI has no service-token flow.

feature: Claude Desktop connection to the gateway
detail: Desktop uses a bootstrapUrl in its managed configuration and a policy desktop overlay (gateway v2.1.203+), sends all tab traffic through the gateway, and signs in separately from the CLI; parentSettingsBehavior merge delivers the egress allowlist to embedded sessions.

feature: allowManaged*Only locks to restrict parent settings
detail: Five locks (permission rules, MCP servers, hooks, sandbox domains, read paths) plus allowlists limit what a host process like Desktop, an SDK app or IDE can add; some keys such as availableModels and allowedProviders still need to be set in the winning source.

feature: Gateway availability and limitations
detail: Works: 1M context, prompt caching, 1-hour cache TTL opt-in, auto mode on eligible models, spend limits. Not available: server-side web search, Remote Control, /design-sync, flag-dependent features like /import, SAML, multi-tenant, Windows server, Helm chart.

feature: Gateway admin UI for spend limits
detail: In Claude Desktop 4.23118.0+ connected to the gateway, members of admin groups can manage spend limits; all other gateway configuration stays in YAML.

feature: Gateway protocol reference endpoint (/protocol)
detail: A running gateway serves its protocol documentation (SSO, inference, managed settings, model discovery, telemetry) at GET /protocol; breaking changes are announced but compatibility is not guaranteed.

feature: Gateway data plane sends nothing to Anthropic
detail: Telemetry, audit logs, managed settings and IdP identity stay in the customer's infrastructure unless the Anthropic API is a configured upstream; deprovisioned users lose access within the session TTL (one hour default).

feature: Gateway spend limits per user, group or organization
detail: Admins cap spend by day, week or month for a user (OIDC sub), IdP group or the whole org via an admin API; effective cap is user override, then most restrictive group (or least with group_limit_mode max), then org default; over-cap requests get a 429.

feature: Spend-limits admin API with read/write keys and audit trail
detail: Endpoints under /v1/organizations/spend_limits to list, create/replace, get, delete caps, view effective spend per principal and an audit of mutations; authenticated by write/read API keys or admin-group bearer tokens.

feature: Spend-limit blocked message and reset behavior
detail: Blocked developers see the reset date (UTC daily, Monday weekly, first of month) plus an admin-set custom message and a retry-after header; a zero cap blocks everything and has no reset.

feature: Gateway spend metering and pricing overrides
detail: Usage is priced from list or admin override rates times a multiplier, with unknown models at a fallback tier and aborted streams billed by estimate; amounts are estimates, not invoices.

feature: Fail-open or fail-closed enforcement on database outage
detail: If the Postgres store is unreachable enforcement proceeds by default; fail_closed_on_error returns a spend limit unavailable 429 instead.

feature: Spend limit warnings and /usage Spend bar in Claude Code
detail: Developers get warnings past 75% and 95% of a cap, a Spend limit bar in /usage with dollars spent and reset time, a status-line spend field, and a Spend (UTC) readout when no cap applies; needs recent client and server versions.

feature: Spend data retention and per-person erasure
detail: Spend counters kept 13 months, audit 365 days, identity (email, name, groups) 90 days after last activity by default; a person's identity row can be deleted directly for offboarding or DSAR.

feature: Claude Code via Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)
detail: Run Claude Code against the Anthropic-operated API reached through a Google Cloud project using Application Default Credentials or a service account key, with roles/claude.user IAM, a workspace ID and Marketplace billing; needs v2.1.307+.

feature: Google Cloud (Anthropic managed) provider env variables and /status check
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_GOOGLE_CLOUD, project, workspace ID, location (default global), base URL and skip-auth variables configure the provider; /status or claude auth status --text confirms it; team rollout via managed settings.

feature: Pin model versions for team deployments
detail: Set default opus, sonnet, fable and haiku model env variables so a Claude Code update does not move a whole team to a newer model at once.

feature: Features unavailable on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)
detail: Fast mode, Remote Control, cloud sessions, claude.ai MCP connectors, Channels, /design-sync, /import and server-managed settings do not work with this provider.

feature: Claude Code on Claude Platform on AWS
detail: Points Claude Code at an Anthropic-operated workspace via AWS Marketplace billing, authenticating with SigV4 AWS credentials or a workspace API key; creates a separate Anthropic organization tied to the AWS account.

feature: AWS credential refresh via awsAuthRefresh and /login
detail: awsAuthRefresh re-runs an SSO login command on expiry or at startup, and /login > 3rd-party platform > Claude Platform on AWS refreshes credentials without restarting; /login does not sign in to claude.ai here.

feature: Claude Platform on AWS env configuration and routing
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS, workspace ID, region and optional base URL select the provider (opt-in; Bedrock and Foundry take precedence); the banner and /status show Claude Platform on AWS.

feature: Prompt caching 1-hour TTL option
detail: Prompt caching is automatic with a 5-minute TTL; ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H requests a 1-hour TTL at a higher write rate, and TTLs can be chosen separately for main and side requests.

feature: Agent SDK and corporate proxy support on AWS provider
detail: The Agent SDK reads the same provider variables, and a proxy or LLM gateway can be set via base URL with an option to skip client signing when the gateway adds SigV4 headers.

feature: Gateway deployment on Google Cloud (Cloud Run or GKE)
detail: Worked example running the gateway on Cloud Run or GKE with Cloud SQL Postgres (private IP), Secret Manager, Artifact Registry and a service account for Agent Platform; provided as an example, not a supported production deployment.

feature: Google Workspace as gateway IdP with google_groups lookup
detail: Google id_tokens carry no groups, so oidc.google_groups resolves groups via the Admin SDK Directory API with domain-wide delegation; otherwise policies match on email domain.

feature: Gateway trusted_proxies and internal load balancer fronting
detail: The gateway honors X-Forwarded-For only from listed proxy ranges so rate limits and audit logs record developer IPs; the public URL must resolve privately via internal Application Load Balancer, internal GKE Ingress or private DNS.

feature: Gateway Terraform and setup.sh reference assets for GCP
detail: Example repository assets provide an idempotent gcloud provisioner, Terraform, a sample gateway.yaml and a distroless Dockerfile for the Cloud Run track.

feature: Gateway deployment on AWS (ECS Fargate or EKS)
detail: Worked example with Bedrock via IAM role, RDS Postgres (TLS enforced), Secrets Manager, ECR and an internal ALB; example only, not a supported production deployment; Claude Platform on AWS can replace or accompany Bedrock.

feature: Gateway per-developer AWS cost attribution via assume_role
detail: With assume_role and session_name email the gateway assumes a Bedrock role per developer per hour so AWS billing shows spend per developer (needs v2.1.281+); roles can live in another account.

feature: Per-team cost attribution with application inference profiles
detail: One tagged Bedrock inference profile per team and model, mapped to team model ids and pinned to IdP groups; developers may get a multi-team group and choose the billing team per session with --model.

feature: Gateway telemetry relay to OpenTelemetry collectors
detail: telemetry.forward_to pushes exporter settings to connected clients and forwards OTLP to listed destinations per signal (metrics default, logs and traces opt-in), with user identity and group attributes; clients show a security approval dialog for pushed settings.

feature: Gateway health endpoints, audit logs and streaming keepalive
detail: /readyz checks the store, /healthz is an alternative, audit events are JSON on stderr for CloudWatch, and the gateway sends SSE pings about every 15 seconds on quiet streams (v2.1.229+) so load balancers do not cut them.

feature: Microsoft Entra ID and Okta as gateway IdP
detail: Okta uses userinfo fallback and groups scope; Entra uses issuer v2.0, group object IDs or App Roles via groups_claim roles; Google, Keycloak, Dex also supported.

feature: Gateway container image and Kubernetes/Cloud Run deployment
detail: Self-built image around the pinned, signature-verified native Linux claude binary (glibc or musl), run as claude gateway with a read-only config; deploys as a stateless Deployment on Kubernetes or Cloud Run (min 1 instance), not Lambda or Cloud Functions.

feature: Gateway has no license fee and does not block direct access
detail: No separate per-seat cost beyond inference and compute; the gateway does not stop developers using their own provider credentials, so network egress policy must close that path (which also breaks the WebFetch safety check unless skipWebFetchPreflight is set).

feature: Gateway sign-in rate limits for large rollouts
detail: Per client IP defaults of 30 sign-in starts and 10 code submissions per 10 minutes can be raised through rate_limits for NAT/VPN fleets; Claude Code shows a limiting-sign-in message when reached.

feature: Gateway audit events and operational log formats
detail: JSON audit events (sign-ins, denials, inference, managed settings served, spend blocked, admin changes, guardrail traces) plus operational logs with debug/info/warn/error levels and an optional JSON format (v2.1.319+).

feature: Gateway outage behavior and readiness grace
detail: During a database outage existing sessions keep serving inference but new sign-ins fail; store.readiness_grace_seconds keeps replicas ready through failovers; an IdP outage only blocks new logins until the TTL expires.

feature: Gateway concurrency limit, timeouts and first-byte deadline
detail: Each replica sends 256 upstream requests at once by default (adjustable); clients can set CLAUDE_STREAM_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS (v2.1.307+), API_TIMEOUT_MS and CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS to handle slow or long-thinking streams.

feature: Gateway JWT secret rotation and session revocation
detail: Rotate in stages by prepending a new secret to the array; replacing it outright signs out every session, and there is no per-session revocation (deprovision in the IdP instead).

feature: Gateway Postgres store, pooling, upgrades and graceful drain
detail: Postgres holds device grants, rate limits, spend, spend limits, audit and identity; connection pool sizing per replica, self-migrating append-only schema, safe rollback, and a SIGTERM drain window (25s default, configurable) for in-flight streams.

feature: Gateway security model and SSRF guard
detail: Device grant (RFC 8628) with PKCE to the IdP, same-origin and rate-limited verification page, 8-character user codes, and an SSRF guard blocking metadata and loopback addresses for operator-set URLs.

feature: Gateway compliance posture and client-side telemetry controls
detail: The gateway sends nothing to Anthropic unless it is an upstream; CLI analytics and error reporting are off while signed in, ratings are not uploaded, transcript sharing writes locally, and DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DISABLE_UPDATES and nonessential-traffic flags tighten pre-login and update traffic.

feature: Plugin marketplace controls for gateway fleets
detail: The official marketplace is fetched directly from developer machines on first start; strictKnownMarketplaces, blockedMarketplaces or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL prevent it.

feature: Gateway sign-in error handling and messages
detail: Documented Claude Code errors for gateway login: not signed in, API key conflicts, private-network and proxy checks, TLS pin changes, 431 oversized group headers, group-not-allowed 400, expired sessions and settings-load failures.

feature: Gateway IdP refresh tokens and deprovisioning tradeoff
detail: Refresh tokens (offline_access) allow silent renewal and revoke access when a user is disabled; without them users re-login every ttl_hours, so admins can raise ttl at the cost of slower deprovisioning.

feature: Gateway support reporting and version display
detail: Gateway version shows on the landing page and x-cc-gateway-version header; support asks for stderr, redacted config, and a debug file via claude --debug-file from the developer.

feature: Claude Security plugin: multi-agent vulnerability scan
detail: Plugin that scans a repo inside a Claude Code session: maps architecture, builds a threat model, hunts for flaws and independently verifies each finding before reporting.
plans: Paid plan, API, or third-party provider

feature: /claude-security command and menu
detail: One command opens a menu with three jobs: scan codebase, scan changes, suggest patches; jobs can also be requested as arguments or in plain language.

feature: Scan the whole codebase or a focused area
detail: After reading the repo it offers the whole repository or a focused scope; answering I don't know picks a size-based default.

feature: Scan only changes: branch diff, PR or single commit
detail: Scans committed changes only (branch diff, one of your open PRs, or a commit); needs git; PR listing needs gh signed in and permitted.

feature: Scan effort levels low, medium, high
detail: Low skips architecture map and threat model; medium is default; high hunts more in the same code. Verification is identical at all levels.

feature: Scan results directory with report, JSONL, SARIF, revision stamp
detail: Each scan writes a timestamped folder with a markdown report, machine-readable JSONL, SARIF 2.1.0 (CWE-classified) and a revision stamp; it has its own .gitignore which you delete to commit it.

feature: Independent verifier agents filter findings
detail: Findings appear only after verifier agents analyze them; scans are nondeterministic so repeat runs can surface different findings.

feature: Suggest patches for chosen findings
detail: Pick findings and get one F<n>.patch plus a note each, drafted in a scratch copy of the repo against committed code; stale findings are skipped.

feature: Patch review by independent agent and test run
detail: A separate agent runs project tests and reads the diff; a patch is written only if it fixes the one finding, adds no vulnerability and keeps behavior; otherwise a note explains.

feature: Patches never applied automatically
detail: User applies with git apply or asks Claude to apply and open a PR; one patch per pull request recommended; note flags patches with no tests.

feature: Runs on session model and any provider
detail: No separate key; agents use the session model (change with /model), some steps use the sonnet alias; works on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry with pinned versions advised.

feature: Prerequisites: Python 3.9, Git, OS support
detail: Needs python3 3.9+ on PATH, Linux/macOS/Windows, git for change scans and patches; Pro plan must enable Dynamic workflows in /config.

feature: Install, update and uninstall the plugin
detail: Install via /plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official (or desktop/VS Code plugin install); auto-updates by default; uninstall from /plugin or claude plugin uninstall.

feature: Auto mode recommended for scans
detail: Works best in auto mode so agents proceed without permission prompts; scan needs Claude Code left open and asks confirmation before running.

feature: Automatic model fallback on Fable safeguards flag
detail: When Fable cyber classifiers flag a scan request, Claude Code re-runs it on an Opus model; on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry it may end in a refusal.

feature: Scans count toward usage; managed Claude Security product on Enterprise
detail: Plugin scans consume plan usage; a separate managed Claude Security service monitors connected repos and can use Mythos, Enterprise only.

feature: Layered security tooling: guidance plugin, /security-review, Code Review
detail: Docs position the plugin as the deep on-demand scan beside the in-session security guidance plugin, single-pass /security-review, PR Code Review and managed scanning.

feature: Python missing warning in /claude-security menu
detail: Menu warns when python3 is absent or older than 3.9 and names the version found.

feature: Claude Tag: tag @Claude in Slack channels
detail: Anyone in a Slack channel can mention @Claude to hand it work; it replies in the thread, posts a progress checklist and the exchange stays visible to the channel.

feature: Claude Tag plan availability
detail: Only Team and Enterprise on Anthropic first-party service; not on Free, Pro, Max, Ultra or third-party deployments; requires pairing a Slack workspace with the Claude org.

feature: Claude Tag admin setup: pair Slack, set spend limit, launch
detail: Owner opens claude.ai admin settings, sends @Claude connect in Slack for a pairing code, enters it, sets monthly spend limit, adds Claude to channels and launches; no per-user setup.

feature: Claude Tag usage-based billing and spend limit
detail: No per-seat charge; channel, thread and group DM work draws from an Owner-funded usage balance capped by a per-period spend limit, with a per-channel usage breakdown in admin settings.

feature: Claude Tag one-to-one DM billed to member's own seat
detail: A DM from a member with a connected Claude account runs on that account and seat limits (needs Claude Code seat or Enterprise Cowork/usage Chat seat); unconnected members can bill the org for a limited time.

feature: Claude Tag: restrict who can use Claude
detail: By default anyone in the paired Slack workspace can use it; an Owner can limit to Claude org members or, on Enterprise, to specific roles; Slack users need no Claude seat for channels.

feature: Claude Tag: allow or disable direct messages
detail: An Owner can turn off DMs to Claude for the whole organization.

feature: Claude Tag works in channels, threads, group DMs and DMs
detail: Interact by writing in a Slack channel, thread or DM; mention @Claude in a channel to guarantee it picks up the message.

feature: Claude Tag ephemeral sandbox per conversation
detail: Tasks run in a sandbox created when a conversation starts, holding code and files, discarded when idle; not on the user's computer.

feature: Claude Tag connectors, plugins and skills scoped by admin
detail: Owner or Claude Tag admin configures connectors, plugins and skills for all of Slack, one workspace or one channel; Tag starts with no access to external systems.

feature: Claude Tag: personal connectors in channels
detail: Members can allow Claude to use their own claude.ai connectors for their own requests inside a channel.

feature: Claude Tag GitHub App for bug fixes and draft PRs
detail: Admin grants repositories to the Claude GitHub App; a bug reported in a channel can come back as a draft pull request.

feature: Claude Tag: Configure link and access query
detail: Ask @Claude what it can access from the channel, or click Configure in a reply footer (signed-in org users) to see the channel's connections; org-shared channels have no Configure link.

feature: Claude Tag use cases: triage, docs answers, data questions, monitors
detail: Documented uses include intake triage, doc answers, warehouse queries with charts, monitor/alert watching, project status digests, approval chasing, threads to docs/tickets, personal digests.

feature: Claude Tag scheduled jobs, channel watching and triggers
detail: Can run scheduled dashboard checks, standing digests, follow-ups and investigate alerts as they arrive.

feature: Claude Tag channel memory
detail: Memory follows places: channel memory and what is shared across the workspace, with rules on who can see what.

feature: Claude Tag security model and audit trails
detail: Admin-governed access per channel, credentials storage, audit trails and network requirements are covered in a dedicated security page.

feature: Claude Tag admin docs: choose model, commands, glossary, rollout
detail: Docs list admin areas (before install, setup, roll out, customize, operate) and user areas (commands, control when Tag responds, group DMs, routines, choose the model).

feature: claude: interactive session with optional initial prompt
detail: Start a terminal session, optionally with a first prompt.

feature: claude -p print mode and piped input
detail: Runs one query non-interactively and exits; accepts piped stdin content.

feature: claude -c / -r: continue or resume sessions
detail: Continue most recent conversation in the directory, or resume by session ID or name.

feature: claude update, install [version], doctor
detail: Update the CLI, install or reinstall the native binary (specific version, stable or latest), and print read-only install/settings diagnostics.

feature: claude auth login, logout, status
detail: Sign in (email prefill, SSO, or Console API billing), sign out, and show auth status as JSON or text with exit code.

feature: claude setup-token long-lived OAuth token
detail: Generates a long-lived token for CI and scripts; needs a Claude subscription; printed not saved.

feature: claude gateway self-hosted Claude apps gateway
detail: Admins run a gateway giving SSO and policy in front of Claude Code on Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry; needs a gateway.yaml.

feature: claude agents: agent view of background sessions
detail: Opens a view to monitor and dispatch parallel background sessions; filters by directory, JSON output, default permission mode/model/effort/agent.

feature: Background session commands: attach, logs, respawn, stop, rm
detail: Attach to, read logs of, restart (one or all), stop, or remove background sessions; transcripts remain resumable.

feature: --bg and --exec background jobs
detail: Start a session as a background agent and return, or run a shell command as a PTY-backed background job.

feature: claude daemon: logs, run, status, stop
detail: Control the background-session supervisor: follow its log, run in foreground, show state, stop it (optionally keeping workers).

feature: claude auto-mode defaults and reset
detail: Print the auto mode classifier rules (optionally filtered by label, with your settings applied) or restore defaults.

feature: claude import: bring config from other coding agents
detail: Interactive session that imports configuration from other agents into Claude Code; supports dry-run; not on third-party providers.

feature: claude mcp login/logout and MCP management
detail: Configure MCP servers and run or clear an MCP server's OAuth flow from the shell, including claude.ai connectors and no-browser mode over SSH.

feature: claude plugin: manage plugins
detail: Install and manage plugins from the shell (alias plugins).

feature: claude purge: delete local project state
detail: Removes transcripts, task lists, debug logs, edit history, prompt history and project entry; has dry-run, yes, interactive and all-projects options.

feature: claude remote-control server
detail: Starts a Remote Control server so sessions can be driven from claude.ai or the Claude app; sessions can be resumed after stopping.

feature: claude self-hosted-runner
detail: Registers a machine or container as a self-hosted environment hosting Claude Code cloud sessions, with setup, doctor and on-demand orchestrator subcommands.

feature: claude ultrareview non-interactive
detail: Runs ultrareview, prints findings, JSON option, 45-minute default timeout, optional posting to a GitHub PR as one comment.

feature: Mistyped subcommand suggestion
detail: Closest match is suggested and nothing starts.

feature: --add-dir extra working directories
detail: Grants read/edit access to more directories; persistable via settings; not most config discovery.

feature: --advisor: server-side advisor tool model
detail: Enables the advisor tool for the session with fable, opus, sonnet or a model ID.

feature: --agent and --agents custom subagents
detail: Pick an agent for the session or define subagents inline as JSON (or a file with -p).

feature: --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --tools
detail: Allow tools without prompting, deny or remove tools by rule, or restrict the built-in tool set.

feature: --permission-mode and bypass flags
detail: Start in default/manual, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk or bypassPermissions; --dangerously-skip-permissions equals bypass; allow flag adds bypass to the Shift+Tab cycle.

feature: --permission-prompt-tool and --permission-prompts
detail: Route print-mode permission prompts to an MCP tool or host, or deny them when nobody can answer.

feature: --append-system-prompt(-file) and --system-prompt(-file)
detail: Append to or replace the system prompt from text or file; can be combined; snapshot flag controls whether a resumed conversation reuses the recorded prompt.

feature: --append-subagent-system-prompt(-file)
detail: Adds text to every subagent system prompt in print mode.

feature: --autocompact window
detail: Sets the auto-compact window for a session without saving.

feature: --ax-screen-reader accessible output
detail: Flat text output without decorative borders or animations for screen readers; forces classic renderer.

feature: --bare minimal mode
detail: Skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP, memory and CLAUDE.md for faster scripted calls.

feature: --safe-mode troubleshooting start
detail: Starts with all customizations disabled (CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP, memory) while auth, model, tools and permissions work.

feature: --restricted mode for evaluation harnesses
detail: Removes command-running tools and WebFetch, confines file tools to working dirs, loads only managed settings, refuses bypass and cloud sessions.

feature: --channels (research preview)
detail: Listen to MCP server channel notifications from plugins in a session; needs claude.ai or Console auth; development channels flag bypasses allowlist.

feature: --chrome / --no-chrome
detail: Enable or disable Chrome browser integration for web automation and testing.

feature: --cloud: start or message a cloud session
detail: Create a cloud session from a task, or queue a follow-up into an existing session; --remote is a deprecated alias.

feature: --teleport: resume cloud session locally
detail: Pulls a cloud session into the local terminal.

feature: --desktop: open Claude Desktop on directory
detail: Opens the desktop app on the current directory (with continue/resume to open a session); macOS and x64 Windows, subscription sign-in.

feature: --remote-control / --rc and session name prefix
detail: Start an interactive session also controllable from claude.ai or the app, with optional name and auto-name prefix.

feature: --debug, --debug-file, --verbose
detail: Debug logging with category filters, log to file, and verbose turn-by-turn output.

feature: --disable-slash-commands
detail: Disables all skills and commands for the session.

feature: --effort levels
detail: Session effort low, medium, high, xhigh, max or ultracode depending on model.

feature: --model and --fallback-model
detail: Set the model by alias (sonnet, opus, haiku, fable) or ID; fallback chain used when the primary is overloaded or retired.

feature: --fork-session, --from-pr, --name, --session-id
detail: Fork when resuming, filter sessions linked to a PR (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket), name sessions, or pin a UUID session ID.

feature: --worktree and --tmux
detail: Run in an isolated git worktree (optionally from a PR/MR) and create a tmux or iTerm2 pane session for it.

feature: --teammate-mode for agent teams
detail: Display agent team teammates in-process, auto, tmux or iterm2.

feature: --ide: auto-connect to IDE
detail: Connects to the IDE on startup when exactly one is available.

feature: --init, --init-only, --maintenance setup hooks
detail: Run setup hooks with init or maintenance matcher (print mode), or run setup and SessionStart hooks then exit.

feature: Print-mode output and input formats
detail: text, json or stream-json output; stream-json input; partial messages, hook events, subagent text forwarding, prompt suggestions and user message replay options.

feature: --json-schema structured output
detail: Returns validated JSON matching a schema after the agent finishes (print mode).

feature: --max-budget-usd and --max-turns
detail: Stop a print-mode run at an estimated spend or agentic turn count; spend includes subagents.

feature: --mcp-config and --strict-mcp-config
detail: Load MCP servers from files or strings, waiting for them in print mode; strict skips other configured servers.

feature: --plugin-dir and --plugin-url
detail: Load plugins from a directory, zip, folder of plugins or URL for one session.

feature: --settings and --setting-sources
detail: Supply settings JSON (file up to 2 MiB or inline) and choose user, project, local sources.

feature: --no-session-persistence
detail: Print mode only: sessions are not saved or resumable.

feature: --betas headers (API key users)
detail: Include beta headers in API requests.

feature: --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections
detail: Moves per-user context into first user message to improve prompt-cache reuse across users.

feature: --environment, --ref, --metadata, --correlation-id
detail: Create a cloud session on a self-hosted environment, base checkout on a ref, label it, and pass a correlation ID to the spawn-runner hook.

feature: --version / -v
detail: Prints the version number.

feature: Dynamic system prompt boundary marker
detail: A marker line in a replacement prompt splits static cached text from per-run context.

feature: Cloud environments for cloud sessions
detail: Each cloud session runs in an environment with configurable network access, env variables, network secrets and a setup script; used by desktop, mobile, claude.ai/code, CLI --cloud, scheduled tasks and Claude Tag.
plans: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise (premium or Chat+Claude Code seats)

feature: Default environment auto-created at onboarding
detail: Pro/Max/Ultra get Default automatically; Team/Enterprise see a create form unless an Owner enabled Quick setup; Default has Limited network and no variables or script.

feature: Environment selector and per-surface choice
detail: Pick the environment under the message box; Owner org default fills the selection; project threads use the project's environment; CLI uses /remote-env pick or fallbacks.

feature: Add, edit and archive environments
detail: Create/edit via the selector dialog; archiving hides it from new sessions (running ones continue); Anthropic-hosted environments cannot be deleted; self-hosted ones can by an Owner.

feature: Edit the cloud environment of a running session
detail: Use the caret after the session title and choose Edit cloud environment.

feature: Environment variables in .env format
detail: KEY=value lines readable by any command in the session; applied at creation and VM restore; OTEL_* withheld; visible to everyone using the environment so not for secrets.

feature: Network secrets via agent proxy
detail: Store an API key on an Anthropic-hosted environment; the proxy attaches it to requests for listed hosts so the session never sees it; Bearer/token/username-password types, wildcard hosts for admins.

feature: Network secrets limits: never for GitHub, Anthropic API, registries, setup scrip
detail: Secrets are not attached to GitHub, api.anthropic.com, major package registries, setup script requests or telemetry; unavailable on self-hosted environments or with customer-managed keys.

feature: Network secrets: non-admin shorter form on Team/Enterprise
detail: Members without an org admin role add one secret per host (no wildcard) as Token or Username and password; Owners manage shared environments' secrets.

feature: /remote-env sets default cloud environment for CLI
detail: Picker saves remote.defaultEnvironmentId in user settings; does not start sessions or edit environments.

feature: Organization-shared environments
detail: Owners create or share environments visible to all members under Organization, with read-only summary; Owner sets the org default environment in admin settings.

feature: Claude Tag channel environment
detail: Tag channels use only org-level (shared or self-hosted) environments, set as org default or pinned per channel; an Owner can add toolchains via setup script.

feature: Network access levels None, Limited, Full
detail: None blocks outbound; Limited allows default allowlist plus listed domains; Full allows any domain; GitHub proxy, MCP connectors and secret hosts still reachable; live changes apply within about a minute.

feature: Limited network: Allow package managers and allowed domains list
detail: Checkbox includes default registries; list one domain per line with *. wildcard; no org-wide allowlist or server-managed setting; trusted/custom legacy levels map to Limited.

feature: Default allowed domains list
detail: Allowlist covers Anthropic, GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, container registries, cloud platforms, major language package managers, Linux mirrors, dev tools, monitoring, CDNs, schema hosts and MCP domains.

feature: MCP connectors work regardless of allowed domains
detail: Connector traffic goes through Anthropic servers so hosts need not be allowlisted; turning off unneeded connectors limits tool reach.

feature: GitHub proxy keeps credentials outside the VM
detail: All GitHub operations in hosted environments go through a proxy: scoped git credentials, REST substitution, no branch deletion or tag pushes, only attached repos, GraphQL and gh pr/issue blocked.

feature: Security proxy for outbound traffic
detail: Hosted sessions' internet traffic passes through an HTTP/HTTPS proxy for malicious-request protection and rate limiting.

feature: Built-in GitHub tools in cloud sessions
detail: Read issues, list PRs, fetch diffs and post comments without setup; GH_TOKEN reads as proxy-injected unless set; gh CLI REST works.

feature: Fresh Ubuntu 24.04 VM per session with preinstalled toolchains
detail: x86_64 VM with repo cloned; Python, Node 20/21/22, Ruby, PHP, Java, Go, Rust, C/C++, Docker, Postgres 16, Redis 7, Chrome for Testing, utilities; check-tools command reports versions.

feature: What carries over from local setup to cloud sessions
detail: Repo CLAUDE.md, settings hooks/permissions, .mcp.json, rules, skills, agents, commands and server-managed settings carry over; user-level config, repo-declared plugins, local MCP and SSO do not.

feature: Personal preferences via setup script writing ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
detail: Write user instructions into the cloud VM from a setup script on your own environment; verify with /context.

feature: Setup scripts run as root before Claude starts
detail: Bash script up to 64 KB typed or loaded from file; must exit zero, finish within about five minutes, needs network for installs, runs before env variables are set.

feature: Environment caching of setup script results
detail: Filesystem snapshot reused by later sessions when setup finishes in under about five minutes; rebuilt on script/host change or after about seven days; running processes are not kept.

feature: SessionStart hooks for dependency install in cloud
detail: Repo hook can install packages; use CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE to scope to cloud; not run for multi-repo sessions or project threads; adds startup latency.

feature: Session link trailer in commits and PRs
detail: Cloud commits carry a Claude-Session trailer and PR bodies the session URL; attribution.sessionUrl=false removes them; session ID readable from an env variable.

feature: Start Postgres, Redis and Docker services in session
detail: Ask Claude to start preinstalled services or docker compose; images pulled in setup script are cached, containers are not.

feature: Cloud VM resource limits
detail: About 4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM, 30 GB disk; heavy workloads advised to use Remote Control or self-hosted environments.

feature: Cloud time limits: commands, hooks, idle VM
detail: Foreground command default 2 min up to 10, then moved to background up to 30 more minutes; SessionStart hooks 600 s; idle VMs pause after minutes and may be reclaimed; timeouts raisable by env vars.

feature: Self-hosted environments option
detail: Cloud sessions from every surface can route to a self-hosted environment on org infrastructure, with own network boundary and git credentials, no network secrets.

feature: Remote Control vs cloud environment
detail: Remote Control connects web/mobile to a session on your own machine using its network and files instead of a cloud environment.

feature: Custom base image not supported
detail: Customize via setup script or run own containers with docker compose; replacing the base image entirely is not supported yet.

feature: Code Mode: Claude writes JavaScript making many tool calls
detail: Experimental mode where Claude runs one JS program that runs commands in parallel and chains results; user sees tool calls, not code. Off by default, may be removed.

feature: View Code Mode code in transcript viewer (Ctrl+O)
detail: Each program appears as a collapsed Code row in the transcript viewer.

feature: Enable Code Mode via CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE
detail: Set to 1 in shell or user settings (ignored in project settings), confirm on first use; 0 turns it off; sessions can only be resumed with it on.

feature: Code Mode requirements
detail: Needs v2.1.323+, subscription or Console account, native build, terminal session, supported models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku 5.5, Fable 5.2); not on gateways/Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, HIPAA or zero retention orgs, VS Code, desktop or cloud.

feature: Code Mode limitations
detail: Resume terminal-only; auto mode reviews code not each call; foreground code stops at ten minutes; no Remote Control, Claude in Chrome or computer use; cannot move to Desktop or background.

feature: Code Mode permission checks: deny/ask rules, hooks, auto mode classifier
detail: Each tool call goes through deny/ask rules and PreToolUse hooks; auto mode classifier reviews the code before it runs; other modes prompt per call.

feature: Approve each piece of Code Mode code with an ask rule on REPL
detail: Add an ask rule for REPL to read and approve code before it runs.

feature: Answer permission prompt during code: No stops or refuses call
detail: Answering No or Esc stops the code; No with a comment refuses that call and lets code continue.

feature: Sandbox applies to shell commands in Code Mode, strict sandbox
detail: Sandbox covers shell commands only; JS and file/web/MCP calls run outside; strict sandbox mode keeps commands sandboxed.

feature: Background Code Mode code up to two hours
detail: In auto or bypass mode code can continue in the background while you chat, up to two hours; stop with Esc or /tasks then x.

feature: PostToolUse hook to check or redact Code Mode output
detail: Hook matching REPL can read result/stdout/stderr and return updatedToolOutput to redact; blocking and error cases need a redacted copy.

feature: Block Code Mode organization-wide via managed settings
detail: Admin sets the env variable to 0 in managed settings; cannot be forced on from managed settings.

feature: Code Mode with agent teams
detail: Needs v2.1.326+; teammates use Code Mode in in-process display mode, not in split panes.

feature: Code Mode troubleshooting messages
detail: Status line explains why Code Mode did not start (provider, API key helper, model, telemetry, plugin, mod, org policy); countdown prompt auto-blocks unattended requests.

feature: Hook failure behavior onFailure block or continue
detail: From v2.1.329 a call from code runs by default after a hook failure; hooks can set onFailure block or continue.

feature: Code Review billed on token usage credits
detail: No flat per-review price; billed to the organization via usage credits separate from plan usage, even on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry setups; cost scales with review level and change size.

feature: Review runs setting: once, every push, manual
detail: Per repo: once after PR creation (open/reopen/ready), after every push (default for added repos), or manual via @claude review.

feature: @claude review and @claude review always comment commands
detail: review runs one review; review always subscribes the PR to push-triggered reviews; drafts and fork PRs skip automatic reviews.

feature: Pilot cost estimate using Average cost column
detail: Admin settings table shows average cost per repository; multiply by PR count (and pushes) to estimate monthly spend.

feature: Code Review monthly spend limit
detail: Org-wide limit for the Code Review service set on the usage admin page; reviews skip when that limit, org limit or credits balance runs out, with a PR comment naming the cause.

feature: Code Review analytics dashboard
detail: Page showing PRs reviewed, month cost, auto-resolved feedback, findings by severity and per-repo breakdown with estimated list-price cost.

feature: Customize Code Review with CLAUDE.md
detail: Review reads root and parent-directory CLAUDE.md files of changed files as context; violations become findings at fitting severity.

feature: REVIEW.md review-only instructions
detail: Root REVIEW.md tells reviews what to flag, severity and what to skip; subdirectory REVIEW.md files add checks on protected branches; read by the service but not by local /code-review.

feature: REVIEW.md: recalibrate severity, cap nits, skip paths, add checks, require evide
detail: Freeform Markdown can redefine Important, cap Nit comments, exclude generated files or CI-enforced issues, add team rules and demand file:line evidence.

feature: Subdirectory REVIEW.md ignored in test, vendor, generated, example dirs
detail: Folders named like tests, fixtures, examples, generated, vendor or node_modules never apply their REVIEW.md; remaining subdirectory files share a 150,000 byte limit.

feature: Include other files in REVIEW.md with @file lines
detail: Root REVIEW.md can pull in up to eight root-level files on a protected branch; one level only; 150,000 bytes combined and 64 markdown links limit.

feature: Include a skill's SKILL.md in REVIEW.md
detail: An @.claude/skills/<folder>/SKILL.md line includes the skill body only (no frontmatter, commands, args or supporting files), max 30,000 bytes and eight skill lines; skills are not run.

feature: REVIEW.md read from protected base or default branch
detail: Never read from the PR itself; protected default branch honors severity lowering, exclusions and nit caps; unprotected setups read less or nothing; classic rule vs ruleset counts differ.

feature: /code-review local review command (alias /review)
detail: Reviews current branch for correctness bugs (plus cleanups depending on model/effort); runs as a background subagent in a terminal and reports findings in the conversation; works on any plan.

feature: /code-review targets: PR, branch, range, commit, path
detail: Review the current branch plus uncommitted changes by default, or a PR number, branch comparison, commit range, single commit, or file/directory path.

feature: /code-review --fix applies findings
detail: Asks Claude to apply findings to the working tree via the permission mode; background fix edits sit outside checkpoints so /rewind may not undo them.

feature: /code-review --comment posts to GitHub PR or GitLab MR
detail: Posts findings as inline comments on a GitHub PR or a single note on a GitLab merge request via glab; prints in terminal if glab is missing.

feature: /code-review effort levels and remembered level
detail: low reports high-confidence findings only, medium to max broaden coverage; last typed level is reused across sessions; ultra neither uses nor updates it.

feature: /code-review --max-findings
detail: Limit findings to n, all, or default (32 in the findings tool); the value is remembered across later reviews except in -p runs.

feature: Findings list in host apps via ReportFindings
detail: Desktop and other hosts show findings as a list with file location, one-line summary, category tag and later fixed/skipped/no-change status.

feature: /code-review reads CLAUDE.md, not REVIEW.md
detail: Local review follows CLAUDE.md including in -p runs; REVIEW.md only configures the managed service.

feature: Run /code-review in foreground
detail: Use -p or Agent SDK, disable background tasks via env var, or rerun while one is in progress.

feature: Claude can start /code-review itself or via scheduled task
detail: Triggered by plain-language request or a session-scoped scheduled task; a skillOverrides entry can make it user-invocable only.

feature: /code-review ultra: cloud ultrareview
detail: Deeper cloud review of branch vs default branch plus uncommitted changes, optional base branch, free-text note, --fix on return and --post to a GitHub PR; needs claude.ai auth.

feature: Ultrareview unavailable on third-party, ZDR, HIPAA or CMEK orgs
detail: Not available on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, with Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configuration or customer-managed keys; falls back to a local review (CMEK cannot run it).

feature: Replace or extend the bundled code-review skill
detail: A project or personal skill named code-review overrides it while /review keeps the bundled one; /simplify and /verify are neighboring commands.

feature: Code Review managed service on GitHub pull requests
detail: Owner enables per repo; Claude posts inline comments, a summary and a Claude Code Review check run; never approves, blocks or fails a check.

feature: Finding severity: Important, Nit, Pre-existing
detail: Red Important bug to fix before merge, yellow Nit minor, purple Pre-existing bug not introduced by the PR; collapsed Why this was flagged shows reasoning.

feature: Respond to findings: resolve, fix, reply
detail: Resolve a thread to dismiss; pushing a fix lets next review auto-resolve; replies are read by the next review; branch protection may require resolution.

feature: Check run details table and annotations
detail: Details link lists findings by severity; unposted line findings appear as annotations in Files changed; run concludes neutral or skipped.

feature: Earlier result kept after no-change pushes
detail: On empty commits or clean rebases with no open Important findings, review is skipped or not repeated; Re-run or @claude review forces one.

feature: Read severity counts from check run in CI
detail: Last line of Details holds JSON counts (nit, normal, pre_existing) parsable with gh and jq to gate merges; missing line means no verdict.

feature: Ways to request a review: open, ready, push, Re-run, retry
detail: Reviews start on open/ready/push per Review runs setting, via comment, via Re-run after failure, or an automatic single retry for interrupted sessions.

feature: @claude review comment commands: once, always, stop, off, pause
detail: review/once run a single review; always subscribes to pushes; stop/off/pause unsubscribes; needs write permission, top-level comment, first line, open PR.

feature: Later reviews focus on changes and post fewer nits
detail: Re-reviews cover what changed and note unposted counts; @claude review does a full re-review.

feature: Drafts and fork PRs need manual review commands
detail: Automatic reviews skip drafts and forks; comment commands work (write access to base repo); always on a fork does not subscribe to pushes; Re-run does nothing on forks.

feature: Code Review alongside Claude Code GitHub Action
detail: @claude review also triggers the Action in interactive mode with default phrase; set a different trigger_phrase to separate them.

feature: Code Review: Allow code review admin switch
detail: Owners turn Code Review on or off org-wide in Admin settings > Claude Code; turning it off stops new reviews everywhere but keeps the repo list.

feature: Code Review: connect GitHub and install Claude GitHub App
detail: Setup links a GitHub account (github.com or Enterprise Server), installs the Claude GitHub App on chosen repos and links the install to the Claude org; reviews run on Anthropic infrastructure with no workflow files.

feature: Code Review: add repositories one at a time
detail: Owners add repos from an Add a repository dialog; needs write access to each repo from the connected GitHub account; unlisted repos need the app granted access.

feature: Code Review: cover a whole GitHub organization
detail: Setting Review runs on an organization row covers every repo the app can reach including future ones; needs org-owner GitHub account, github.com, and a monthly spend limit; overrides individual repo settings.

feature: Code Review: review level Quick, Standard, Deep
detail: Org default level (Standard by default) with per-repo override; Quick is cheapest and fastest, Deep most thorough and costly; applies to new reviews.

feature: Code Review: when reviews run (once, every push, manual)
detail: Per-repo setting: once after PR open/ready, after every push (auto-resolves fixed threads), or manual by @claude review; new repos default to every push.

feature: Code Review: @claude review always subscribes a PR to pushes
detail: Developers comment @claude review always to get a review on each later push of that PR, even in Manual repos; not for drafts or forks.

feature: Code Review: @claude review comment command
detail: Anyone with write access comments @claude review to start a review, including on drafts and fork PRs that automatic reviews skip.

feature: Code Review: tip comments toggle
detail: Show tips on pull requests (on by default) makes Claude explain why no review started: Manual mode, fork PR, commenter without write access, or unlinked GitHub org.

feature: Code Review: remove or turn off a repository or org
detail: Per-repo Code review switch, Remove repository (frees it for another org), or Off on an org row; a repo under whole-org coverage can only be switched off.

feature: Code Review: developers customize with REVIEW.md and CLAUDE.md
detail: Developers without Owner role can change what reviews flag by committing REVIEW.md and CLAUDE.md; reviews they request bill to the org.

feature: Code Review: draft and fork PRs skipped by automatic reviews
detail: Automatic reviews never run on drafts or fork PRs regardless of the run setting.

feature: Code Review: Claude Code Review check run
detail: Each review posts a check run named Claude Code Review on the PR; a test PR verifies setup.

feature: Code Review check run states
detail: Titles show queued, in progress, found no issues, issues found, skipped no new changes, not repeated while earlier findings open, failed, timed out, or declined.

feature: Code Review budget-skipped reviews
detail: When the monthly Code Review cap, usage credits or remaining budget are insufficient, review is skipped with a warning comment and sometimes a declined check; commenting @claude review after restoring budget reruns.

feature: Code Review retrigger by comment or Re-run
detail: Failed or timed-out reviews can be restarted by a top-level @claude review comment or the GitHub Re-run button (not for forks); interrupted sessions retry once automatically.

feature: Code Review findings shown outside inline comments
detail: Findings not accepted inline appear in check run Details severity table, Files changed annotations, whole-file comments, or an Additional findings section in the review body.

feature: Code Review REVIEW.md safeguards
