feature: managed-settings.json file deployment
detail: A JSON file in a system directory (macOS /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode, Linux/WSL /etc/claude-code, Windows C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode) enforces policy; /status shows 'Enterprise managed settings (file)'.

feature: Four managed delivery mechanisms
detail: Server-managed (claude.ai console or gateway, polled hourly), MDM/OS policy (macOS profile or HKLM registry, checked every 30 min), file-based (reloaded on change), and HKCU registry fallback for Windows/WSL.

feature: MDM starter templates
detail: Example templates for Jamf, Iru, Intune and Group Policy exist in Anthropic's MDM examples repository.

feature: Different policy per group
detail: Deploy different files or profiles per group, or on Enterprise use per-group configuration in server-managed settings; a self-hosted gateway delivers per IdP group.

feature: HIPAA managed settings example
detail: A fuller managed-settings example covers sandboxing, network allowlist, credential protections and local data retention for the HIPAA configuration.

feature: Surfaces that read managed settings
detail: Terminal, VS Code and JetBrains extensions, desktop Code tab and Agent SDK sessions read managed settings; Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions need server-managed settings, self-hosted runners read the file in their image.

feature: Cowork sessions and managed policy
detail: Cowork never fetches server-managed settings; on the user's machine it reads local MDM/file policy, in a full VM sandbox (requireCoworkFullVmSandbox) or remote Cowork it has no device policy; claude.ai applies marketplace allow/block lists itself.

feature: Claude Tag sessions skip server-managed settings
detail: Claude Tag cloud sessions do not receive server-managed settings, are configured in Claude Tag admin settings, and read a runner-image file only on self-hosted environments.

feature: Policy update timing and approval dialogs
detail: Most changes reach running sessions without restart; server-managed changes to hooks or env vars wait for the developer to accept a dialog; requiredMinimumVersion blocks old binaries from starting but does not end running ones.

feature: Policy storage formats
detail: macOS profile in com.anthropic.claudecode domain, Windows HKLM/HKCU Settings value under SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode, symlinked files allowed with a status warning; legacy C:\ProgramData path is not read.

feature: managed-settings.d drop-in directory
detail: Per-team JSON files merge alphabetically after managed-settings.json: single values replaced, lists unioned, nested blocks merged, fallbackModel chain, marketplaces, managed MCP and modelPicker replaced whole.

feature: managedSourcesBehavior first-wins or merge
detail: Default uses only the highest-ranked managed source (remote, MDM, file, HKCU); merge (v2.1.242+) combines every admin source by key kind: lists union, locks strictest, allowlists from highest source.

feature: Cross-source managed keys
detail: Sandbox locks, MCP allow/deny locks, disableClaudeAiConnectors, sandbox binary paths, useAutoModeDuringPlan, syncClaudeAiSkills/Plugins, enableArtifact, maxEffortLevel cap, attribution opt-out, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh and per-variable env are read from every admin source.

feature: Login keys from MDM or file beat remote settings
detail: forceLoginOrgUUID, forceLoginMethod and gateway login keys are taken from the MDM policy or file rather than claude.ai console settings.

feature: policyHelper executable
detail: An executable named in MDM or file policy computes managed settings at startup; its output becomes the only managed settings and any schema violation stops startup.

feature: parentSettingsBehavior for embedding hosts
detail: Settings supplied by hosts like Claude Desktop, IDE extensions or SDK apps are ignored when an admin source exists unless set to merge, and then only restrictive values are kept.

feature: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly and Cowork folder access
detail: Makes managed settings the sole source of permission rules, which strips Cowork's folder allow rules; admins re-add Edit allow rules for connected folders in the managed source.

feature: Check policy with /status Setting sources and claude doctor
detail: /status labels the active source (remote, plist, HKLM, file, drop-ins, merged, HKCU, parent process, helper), lists Skipped sources (v2.1.242+); claude doctor lists dropped entries and the Organization policy line (v2.1.261+).

feature: Invalid managed entries are repaired or fail closed
detail: Unreadable restrictive keys (e.g. allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, disableAutoMode) read as their restrictive value; allowlists like allowedMcpServers, availableModels, strictKnownMarketplaces default to empty; sandbox is validated per field; unparseable documents stop startup.

feature: Managed-only keys list
detail: Keys honored only from managed sources include allowManagedHooksOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, blockedMarketplaces, strictKnownMarketplaces, channelsEnabled, allowedChannelPlugins, disableCommandPluginSources, disableSideloadFlags, pluginSuggestionMarketplaces, pluginTrustMessage and sandbox allowManaged locks.

feature: Channels enablement and channel plugin allowlist
detail: channelsEnabled turns channels on for the org and allowedChannelPlugins replaces Anthropic's default list of plugins allowed to push messages.

feature: Marketplace restrictions: strict and blocked lists
detail: strictKnownMarketplaces limits which marketplace sources users may add; blockedMarketplaces are checked before download; pluginSuggestionMarketplaces and pluginTrustMessage customize suggestions and trust warnings.

feature: disableSideloadFlags
detail: Rejects --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents and --mcp-config at startup (v2.1.193+); in cloud sessions the server-delivered MCP config is dropped instead.

feature: strictPluginOnlyCustomization
detail: Blocks skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from user and project sources; true locks all four or an array names which.

feature: Remote Control and cloud sessions org toggles
detail: On Team and Enterprise an Owner enables or disables Remote Control and cloud sessions org-wide in Claude Code admin settings; disabled Remote Control disconnects running sessions (v2.1.286+) within about an hour; disableRemoteControl works per device.

feature: Disable telemetry organization-wide
detail: Delivering DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 in managed env applies without an approval dialog but also stops analytics-dashboard data and feature-flag fetching for those developers.

feature: Developer limits on managed policy
detail: Local admins can edit managed files, server cache edits last until next fetch, other tools are not bound, and developers can add to allow lists unless the allowManaged*Only locks are set.

feature: WSL inherits Windows managed settings
detail: wslInheritsWindowsSettings makes WSL read the Windows policy chain before /etc/claude-code.

feature: Add an MCP server: claude mcp add
detail: Registers a hosted (--transport http) or local stdio server (command after --) with a chosen name; confirms and shows the file modified.

feature: claude mcp list status indicators
detail: Shows Connected, tools fetch failed, Needs authentication, Failed to connect, Connection error, Pending approval, Disabled for this project and Blocked by enterprise managed policy.

feature: /mcp panel inside a session
detail: Lists servers, shows tools, and lets users authenticate, reconnect, or disable a server without leaving the session.

feature: claude mcp remove
detail: Removes a server by name, with --scope to choose which copy when it exists in several scopes.

feature: MCP installation scopes: local, project, user
detail: Local (default) is private to you and one project in ~/.claude.json, project writes .mcp.json shared with the team, user applies to all your projects; scope is fixed at add time.

feature: Project .mcp.json shared with team with approval prompt
detail: Teammates who clone and start Claude Code are prompted to approve project servers; claude mcp reset-project-choices re-shows the prompt.

feature: Local stdio MCP servers (e.g. Playwright)
detail: Runs a program as a subprocess for local resources such as a browser; Playwright MCP needs Node 18+ and can drive other browsers via --browser.

feature: OAuth sign-in for hosted MCP servers
detail: Add the server URL, then /mcp > Authenticate opens a browser sign-in for services like Sentry, Linear or Notion; tokens-based servers use --header Authorization.

feature: claude mcp get for server details
detail: Shows scope, URL or command, and error detail such as HTTP status for a failing server; warns about hidden whitespace in config values.

feature: Connect MCP from other surfaces
detail: Desktop Code app uses a Connectors UI, VS Code has its own flow, cloud sessions load a committed .mcp.json (or claude.ai connectors inside projects), and claude.ai connectors load in the CLI when signed in; claude mcp add-from-claude-desktop imports Claude Desktop config on macOS/WSL.

feature: Anthropic Directory for finding MCP servers
detail: A browsable directory of connectors/servers referenced for discovery of servers to connect.

feature: MCP_TIMEOUT environment variable
detail: Raises the default 30-second MCP startup timeout (in ms), useful for slow first npx downloads.

feature: MCP --env flag and env field
detail: Pass API keys or variables to a server with --env KEY=value or the env field in .mcp.json when tools do not appear.

feature: Reference MCP resources with @ mentions
detail: MCP resources can be attached to prompts with @ mentions.

feature: Run MCP prompts as slash commands
detail: Prompts exposed by MCP servers appear in the / menu as commands.

feature: MCP servers consume context window
detail: Each connected server's tool names and instructions load into every session, so removing unused servers frees context.

feature: MCP troubleshooting guidance
detail: Covers no servers shown (wrong scope or config path), failed connections (curl and direct command checks), 404 endpoint messages, timeouts, duplicate names, empty tool lists, stale .mcp.json and OAuth browser failures.

feature: Claude Code sessions from the Claude phone app
detail: The iOS and Android Claude app is a client for Claude Code sessions, not a place where code runs; there is no separate mobile Code app. Sessions live in the app's Code tab.

feature: Get the app via /mobile, /ios, /android QR code
detail: Running /mobile, /ios or /android in a Claude Code session shows a QR code that opens the right app store for the phone. iPad uses the iOS app.

feature: Phone Code tab needs claude.ai account and same organization
detail: Cloud sessions and Remote Control need a claude.ai sign-in matching the one used for Claude Code; Console API keys and third-party providers like Bedrock cannot reach them.

feature: Code tab entry and claude.ai/code/new deep link
detail: Tap Code in the app to reach sessions, or open claude.ai/code/new on the phone to start a new Code session. The tab is hidden when the plan or org lacks the feature.

feature: Cloud sessions from phone
detail: Pick a repository and branch, describe a task and submit; it runs on Anthropic-managed cloud and continues after the phone is put away. Check progress, answer questions or steer from the app.

feature: Sessions persist across laptop and phone
detail: A task started on a laptop can be reviewed from the phone and vice versa.

feature: Watch a pull request and auto-fix CI from phone
detail: Tell Claude to watch a PR and fix CI failures or review comments as they arrive.

feature: Projects: coordinated parallel threads
detail: A project is a conversation where Claude coordinates parallel threads of work and reports which finished or need you; reachable from the phone.

feature: Remote Control from phone to local session
detail: Drive a Claude Code session running on your computer from the app; execution and files stay local. Start with claude remote-control or /remote-control, then scan the QR code or pick the session in the Code tab.

feature: Phone photo attachments reach local sessions
detail: In Remote Control, attached photos are seen directly by Claude and also saved under ~/.claude/uploads/ with the path given to Claude.

feature: Phone file attachments become @ references
detail: Non-photo files attached in the app are downloaded to the computer and passed to Claude as @ file references.

feature: Push notifications from Remote Control
detail: With Remote Control active Claude can push to the phone when a long task finishes or needs a decision; you can also ask in the prompt (e.g. notify me when tests finish). Two /config toggles control it.

feature: Dispatch notifications for spawned Code sessions
detail: Dispatch sends its own notification when a Code session it started finishes or needs approval.

feature: Dispatch: message a task to the Desktop app
detail: Message a task in the app and Dispatch decides how to run it on the Desktop app on your computer. Not available to new users; needs Pro, Max or Ultra, not Team or Enterprise.

feature: Computer must stay on for Remote Control and Dispatch
detail: These drive your own machine so it must stay on with Claude Code or Desktop running; a sleeping machine reconnects when back online. Cloud sessions and projects keep running with the laptop closed.

feature: Mobile limit: local-only commands unavailable
detail: Terminal-only commands such as /plugin and /resume do not work from the app; Remote Control docs list which commands do.

feature: Mobile permission modes
detail: Cloud sessions offer Accept edits, Plan and Auto; Remote Control sessions offer Manual, Accept edits, Plan and Auto. Bypass permissions cannot be selected from the app.

feature: Channels: Telegram, Discord, iMessage to a session
detail: Ask Claude something from chat apps while the work runs on your machine.

feature: Claude Code in Slack via @Claude
detail: Delegate coding tasks from a Slack workspace by mentioning @Claude.

feature: Claude Code on Microsoft Foundry
detail: Run Claude Code against Claude models deployed in Microsoft Foundry on Azure using CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY=1 plus the resource name or base URL. Needs an Azure subscription and deployment permissions.

feature: Foundry auth: API key
detail: Set ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY from the Endpoints and keys section of the Foundry resource.

feature: Foundry auth: Microsoft Entra ID
detail: With no key set, Claude Code uses the Azure SDK default credential chain (e.g. az login); identity needs Foundry User or Cognitive Services User role.

feature: Foundry auth: bearer token
detail: ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_AUTH_TOKEN is sent as a Bearer header on every request and takes precedence over API key and Entra chain.

feature: /logout unavailable on Foundry
detail: Authentication is handled by Azure credentials, so /logout does not work.

feature: Pin Foundry model versions per deployment
detail: Set ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS/SONNET/HAIKU_MODEL to deployment names; unpinned aliases may point to a model missing in the account, causing a switch to an older model or failure.

feature: Foundry background tasks default to the primary model
detail: Because not every account has a Haiku deployment, background work like title generation uses the main model unless Haiku is pinned.

feature: Foundry 1M context by default
detail: Fable models, Sonnet 5 and later and Opus 4.7 and later get the 1M window by default when the deployment name identifies the model; modelOverrides maps custom deployment names; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 keeps 200K.

feature: Prompt caching and 1-hour TTL on Foundry
detail: Prompt caching is automatic (5-minute default); ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 requests a 1-hour TTL, billed at a higher rate for cache writes.

feature: /status shows API provider
detail: Run /status to confirm provider shows Microsoft Foundry with the resource name or base URL; Foundry has no interactive setup wizard unlike Bedrock and Agent Platform.

feature: Foundry troubleshooting messages
detail: Token-chain failure means configure Entra or set the API key; repeated connection errors on the first prompt usually mean a placeholder resource name.

feature: CLAUDE.md persistent instructions
detail: Markdown files you write that load at the start of each session as context, scoped to managed policy, user, project or local; context, not enforced config.

feature: Auto memory
detail: Claude writes its own notes across sessions from corrections and preferences, in four types: user, feedback, project, reference; it skips what code or CLAUDE.md already says.

feature: CLAUDE.md scopes and locations
detail: Managed policy file (OS-specific path), ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, and ./CLAUDE.local.md for personal project notes, loaded broadest to most specific.

feature: CLAUDE.md loads from ancestors; subdirectories on demand
detail: Files in the working directory and above load at launch; subdirectory files load when Claude reads, writes or edits a file there. Files concatenate rather than override.

feature: /init generates a CLAUDE.md
detail: Analyzes the codebase and writes starting build, test and convention notes; suggests improvements if one exists. Imports Cursor and Copilot rules.

feature: /init interactive multi-phase flow (CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT)
detail: With the env var set to 1, /init asks which artifacts to set up (CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks), explores with a subagent and shows a proposal first; also reads AGENTS.md, Devin, Windsurf and Cline rules.

feature: @path imports in CLAUDE.md
detail: Import other files with @path (relative or absolute, up to four hops deep); skipped inside code spans; paths with spaces need backslash escapes.

feature: External import approval dialog
detail: First time a project memory file imports outside the working directory, a dialog lists the files; declining keeps them disabled. User-scope files are trusted, except in Cowork sessions where outside imports are skipped.

feature: Block HTML comments stripped from CLAUDE.md
detail: Block-level HTML comments are removed before injection so maintainer notes cost no tokens; they stay in code blocks and when the file is read directly.

feature: Load CLAUDE.md from --add-dir directories
detail: Set CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 to load CLAUDE.md, rules and local files from extra directories added with --add-dir.

feature: .claude/rules/ modular rules
detail: Markdown files under .claude/rules/ (recursive) are loaded at launch like project instructions; user-level rules in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to every project; symlinks supported.

feature: Path-scoped rules via paths frontmatter
detail: A rule with paths globs (list or comma string, brace expansion, 1,000-pattern budget) loads only when Claude reads, writes or edits matching files.

feature: Symlinked rules outside the project need approval
detail: A symlink pointing outside the working directory is treated as an external import and loads only after approval; network paths are never followed.

feature: Organization-wide managed CLAUDE.md
detail: IT deploys a managed CLAUDE.md (macOS, Linux/WSL, Windows paths) or sets claudeMd in managed settings; it cannot be excluded by users. Guidance only; enforce with managed settings.

feature: claudeMdExcludes setting
detail: Skip specific CLAUDE.md or rules files by absolute-path glob in any settings layer (arrays merge); cannot exclude the managed file.

feature: AGENTS.md read by default when no CLAUDE.md exists
detail: Claude reads AGENTS.md as project instructions if no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists in or above the working directory; requires v2.1.277 or later.

feature: Project instructions setting (instruction file mode)
detail: In /config choose claude-md-or-agents-md (default), claude-md-and-agents-md, claude-md, or managed-only (managed CLAUDE.md and auto memory only).

feature: AGENTS.md sharing via @AGENTS.md import or symlink
detail: Put @AGENTS.md in CLAUDE.md with Claude-specific lines below, or symlink; symlinks block Edit/Write through the link and are unreliable on Windows.

feature: /import and /init migrate other tools' instructions
detail: /init folds Cursor and Copilot rules into CLAUDE.md; /import brings another agent's instruction files, MCP servers, commands, subagents and skills.

feature: Auto memory on/off toggle
detail: On by default in local sessions; toggle in /memory (saves autoMemoryEnabled), per-project setting, or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1. Cannot be re-enabled in background or nested sessions.

feature: Auto memory storage and index limits
detail: Stored per repository at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ with a MEMORY.md index; first 200 lines or 25KB load each session, topic files read on demand; autoMemoryDirectory relocates it. Machine-local, shared across worktrees.

feature: Memory files exempt from transcript cleanup
detail: Memory files stay until edited or deleted even though old session transcripts are removed after cleanupPeriodDays.

feature: Memory timestamps and Saved/Recalled messages
detail: Memory writes with frontmatter get an ISO modified timestamp; the UI shows messages like Saved 2 memories or Recalled 2 memories.

feature: /memory command
detail: Lists CLAUDE.md, local and auto memory locations (including AGENTS.md read), toggles auto memory, opens the memory folder, and opens or creates files in your editor.

feature: Ask Claude to remember something
detail: Saying remember X saves to auto memory; asking to add it to CLAUDE.md writes there instead.

feature: Subagent persistent memory
detail: Subagents can keep their own auto memory directory via the memory field; main conversation memory is not loaded into subagents except forks.

feature: /context all lists loaded memory files
detail: Shows memory files loaded at launch; subdirectory files appear via a Loaded line when they load; /status and startup warn about oversized files.

feature: /doctor prompt-audit
detail: Audits CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules, skills, commands, subagents and output styles for outdated or conflicting content and proposes edits without applying; needs v2.1.283+ and the claude-api skill.

feature: /doctor trims checked-in CLAUDE.md
detail: The doctor checkup proposes cutting derivable content like directory layouts and dependency lists while keeping pitfalls and rationale.

feature: Instruction file size limits
detail: Target under 200 lines; files over 4 MiB are skipped; on-demand files truncate at 40,000 chars (200K window) or 150,000-200,000 (1M window).

feature: Instructions survive /compact
detail: Project-root CLAUDE.md is re-read and re-injected after compaction; nested files and path-scoped rules reload on demand; conversation-only instructions are lost.

feature: InstructionsLoaded hook
detail: A hook event that logs which CLAUDE.md and rules files load and why; does not fire for AGENTS.md read via the setting.

feature: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
detail: Open-standard Model Context Protocol servers give Claude access to issue trackers, monitoring, databases, designs and email so it can read and act on them directly.

feature: Anthropic Directory of reviewed connectors
detail: Reviewed connectors at claude.ai/directory use the same MCP infrastructure and can be added with claude mcp add.

feature: mcp-server-dev plugin to scaffold a server
detail: Install via /plugin and run /mcp-server-dev:build-mcp-server to get a remote HTTP or local stdio server scaffolded.

feature: Add remote HTTP MCP server
detail: claude mcp add --transport http name url, with optional --header; HTTP is the recommended transport; streamable-http accepted as alias in JSON.

feature: Add SSE MCP server (deprecated transport)
detail: --transport sse for SSE-only services; adding with http now tries HTTP first then falls back to SSE (v2.1.265+).

feature: Add local stdio MCP server
detail: claude mcp add name -- command args, with --env pairs; Claude Code sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR for the server and answers roots/list with granted working directories.

feature: Add WebSocket MCP server
detail: type ws via .mcp.json or add-json for servers that push events; header-only auth, no OAuth and not accepted by --transport.

feature: claude mcp add-json
detail: Add a server from a JSON config (also from stdin with - on v2.1.327+), with --scope and --client-secret options.

feature: Import MCP servers from Claude Desktop
detail: claude mcp add-from-claude-desktop opens a picker; works on macOS and WSL; names with spaces are rejected, duplicates get a numeric suffix.

feature: Manage servers: list, get, remove, reset-project-choices
detail: claude mcp list/get/remove; remove deletes stored OAuth tokens; reset-project-choices clears .mcp.json approvals; /mcp checks status in-session.

feature: MCP server status indicators
detail: list/get/ /mcp show Connected, Needs authentication, Failed (with detail), Pending approval, Rejected, Disabled for project, Blocked by managed policy, not configured, cached.

feature: Cached tool discovery for remote servers
detail: Remote servers used before can show cached status and connect on first tool call; needs v2.1.221+, off unless MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE=1 or rollout.

feature: MCP configuration warnings
detail: Warns on hidden whitespace in config values, same name in multiple scopes with different endpoints, reserved built-in names, and unset ${VAR} references.

feature: /mcp panel: tool counts and server menu
detail: Shows per-server tool count, flags servers with tools capability but no tools, and offers Reconnect, Disable and Clear authentication actions.

feature: Disable an MCP server without removing it
detail: Toggle off in /mcp; stored per project in disabledMcpServers (or enabledMcpServers for default-off built-ins like computer-use).

feature: MCP client runtimes v1 and v2
detail: v2 runtime (MCP SDK 2.0, protocol 2026-07-28) is used in many sessions; override with MCP_SDK_GENERATION and MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION.

feature: Dynamic tool updates via list_changed
detail: Interactive sessions refetch tools, prompts and resources on list_changed; -p and SDK refresh only tools; v2 holds an open notification stream with reopen limits.

feature: Automatic reconnection of dropped servers
detail: Five retries with exponential backoff; interactive shows pending then failed or still retrying (up to a day); -p/SDK retry in background; stdio servers need Reconnect.

feature: /mcp reconnect all
detail: Retries every failed or auth-needed server in an interactive session; needs v2.1.284+.

feature: Failed-connection retries and discovery retries
detail: HTTP/SSE first connections retry three times on transient errors; discovery requests (tools/list etc.) retry three times; auth and 4xx errors are not retried.

feature: Claude is told which server failed
detail: With tool search on, Claude is informed of failed servers and errors; without tool search it is not.

feature: Channels: MCP servers push messages into a session
detail: A server declaring claude/channel and enabled with --channels can push CI, alerts or chat messages for Claude to react to; v2 revision servers are not registered as channels.

feature: MCP config scopes: local, project, user
detail: --scope local (default, ~/.claude.json per project), project (.mcp.json shared via git) or user (all projects); precedence local, project, user, plugin, claude.ai.

feature: MCP timeouts: startup, per-server and idle
detail: MCP_TIMEOUT for startup, per-server timeout field (hard wall clock), MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT, and an idle timeout (5 min remote, 30 min stdio, CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT).

feature: Long MCP calls auto-move to background after 2 minutes
detail: Main-conversation calls over two minutes become background tasks visible in /tasks and stoppable; tunable with CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS and disable flags; not for subagents or IDE servers.

feature: MCP tasks that run on the server
detail: Servers using the MCP tasks extension run long jobs; footer shows a task count, /tasks can stop (x) or answer questions, remote tasks survive exit and resume; public beta, v2.1.304+.

feature: Make Claude wait for MCP task result
detail: Set CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS=0 or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MCP_TASK_BACKGROUND=1 so Claude waits; Esc or limits then cancel the task.

feature: MCP task status messages
detail: /tasks shows reconnecting, needs sign-in, did not reconnect within 300s, reconfigured transport, rejected id and outcome unknown states with remedies.

feature: Plugin-bundled MCP servers
detail: Plugins can bundle servers in .mcp.json or plugin.json that start on enable, support ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, appear in /mcp, and are named mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>.

feature: Environment variable expansion in .mcp.json
detail: ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} in command, args, env, url and headers; credential variables like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY read as empty in remote url/headers by design.

feature: GitHub MCP example with personal access token
detail: Add api.githubcopilot.com/mcp with a PAT header for PR review, issues and listing; example of verifying via /mcp.

feature: Database access via DBHub MCP example
detail: Example stdio server for querying Postgres with a read-only user.

feature: OAuth 2.0 for remote MCP servers via /mcp
detail: Authenticate in the browser from /mcp; tokens stored securely and refreshed; Clear authentication revokes; paste callback URL if redirect fails; 401/403 handling differs by header source.

feature: claude mcp login and logout
detail: Run a server's OAuth flow from the shell; detects no-browser (SSH) and prints the URL; --no-browser forces it; logout clears credentials.

feature: Fixed OAuth callback port and pre-registered client
detail: --callback-port and --client-id/--client-secret (masked prompt, MCP_CLIENT_SECRET for CI) support servers lacking dynamic client registration; CIMD supported.

feature: OAuth metadata override and scope pinning
detail: oauth.authServerMetadataUrl bypasses discovery; oauth.scopes pins requested scopes (offline_access appended if advertised); insufficient_scope prompts re-auth.

feature: headersHelper dynamic auth headers
detail: A command run at connect (10 s limit) returns JSON headers for Kerberos or short-lived tokens; re-runs on 401/403; gated by workspace trust; credential env vars stripped for repo-supplied helpers.

feature: OAuth behind an authenticating gateway or proxy
detail: Configured headers (not Authorization) are added to sign-in, refresh and revocation requests on the server origin; needs v2.1.299+.

feature: claude.ai connectors in Claude Code
detail: Connectors added at claude.ai/customize/connectors appear in /mcp automatically with claude.ai sign-in; admins only on Team and Enterprise; hidden connectors collapse under Show unused.
plans: All claude.ai plans; admin-only add on Team, Enterprise

feature: Claude Docs connector auto-provided
detail: Where available, /mcp lists claude.ai Claude Docs with no setup and Claude uses it for documents meant for others.

feature: Managed connector badge
detail: /mcp and /plugin mark connectors whose authentication the organization manages in claude.ai.

feature: Connector availability by auth method
detail: claude.ai connectors load only with a claude.ai subscription login, not with API key, auth token, apiKeyHelper, third-party providers, profiles or setup-token credentials.

feature: Session token rejected state for connectors
detail: /mcp shows session token rejected when claude.ai rejects the login token; fix with /login then reconnect.

feature: Anthropic-hosted connectors can't use local OAuth
detail: Microsoft 365, Gmail, Google Calendar and similar must be connected at claude.ai/customize/connectors rather than via claude mcp add.

feature: How connectors reach each session type
detail: Terminal/IDE/SDK fetch from claude.ai; cloud sessions get them from the host and proxy; desktop local and SSH sessions get them in-process.

feature: Organization per-tool controls on connectors: ask or blocked
detail: Admins can set connector tools to ask (prompt every call, even in auto/bypass modes) or blocked (hidden from Claude); desktop honors blocked only.

feature: Disable claude.ai connectors
detail: disableClaudeAiConnectors setting or ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false; deniedMcpServers blocks individual connectors; /mcp toggles per project.

feature: Use Claude Code as an MCP server
detail: claude mcp serve exposes Claude Code's tools over stdio to clients like Claude Desktop; client handles confirmations; background command output readable via backgroundOutputPath (v2.1.295+).

feature: MCP output limits
detail: Warning at 10,000 tokens, default cap 25,000 (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS), 50,000-character text spill to file, 16 MiB response cap, error text trimmed, per-tool anthropic/maxResultSizeChars up to 500,000.

feature: Images in MCP tool results
detail: PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP results are shown inline and original bytes saved under the session tool-results folder (v2.1.283+).

feature: Root-level schema combinators flattened
detail: Tool schemas with top-level anyOf/oneOf/allOf are flattened with a description hint; invalid or API-rejected schemas exclude the tool with an explanation.

feature: Tool names over 128 characters are skipped
detail: MCP tools whose full name exceeds 128 characters are left out to avoid API rejection.

feature: Tool requires user interaction annotation
detail: Server can mark a tool so every call prompts even in acceptEdits, auto and bypass modes, with no always-allow and no one-tap approval on Remote Control.

feature: Idempotent and read-only tool hints
detail: readOnlyHint tools run in parallel and idempotentHint lets Claude Code repeat a call pending when a connection closed.

feature: MCP elicitation dialogs (form and URL modes)
detail: Servers can ask for structured input mid-task; form mode shows fields, URL mode asks to open a link; Elicitation hook can auto-respond.

feature: Answer elicitation in cloud sessions
detail: Cloud sessions show a card with Submit, Open link/I'm done and Decline.

feature: MCP resources via @ mentions
detail: Type @ to reference server resources as @server:protocol://path; fuzzy search, multiple allowed, auto-attached; not in -p; ui:// MCP Apps resources excluded from lists.

feature: MCP tool search (deferred tool loading)
detail: On by default: only tool names and server instructions load at start, definitions on demand; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH values true, auto, auto:N, false; deny ToolSearch to disable; unsupported on Azure-hosted Foundry.

feature: Per-server and per-tool alwaysLoad
detail: alwaysLoad true exempts a server's tools from deferral (startup waits up to 5 s), false defers all; authors can set anthropic/alwaysLoad per tool.

feature: Description length limits
detail: Server instructions and upfront tool descriptions cut at 4,096 chars, tool-search descriptions at 16,384; CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH changes both.

feature: MCP prompts as slash commands
detail: Server prompts appear as /server:prompt (MCP) or /mcp__server__prompt with space-separated arguments; anthropic-skills server name reserved.

feature: Managed MCP configuration
detail: Admins deploy managed-mcp.json, managedMcpServers, and allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers; blocked servers are hidden or marked blocked by policy.

feature: Project .mcp.json approval and workspace trust
detail: Interactive sessions prompt before using .mcp.json servers; -p, SDK and some cloud sessions load without prompt; disabledMcpjsonServers, --strict-mcp-config and --setting-sources keep servers out.

feature: Per-server tool timeout and tool-call stdio shutdown
detail: Stdio servers get SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGKILL at 100 ms and 400 ms (Windows closes stdin then ends process tree).

feature: Model aliases: default, best, fable, sonnet, opus, haiku
detail: Aliases select the latest model per family without version numbers; best equals opus; default clears overrides. On the Anthropic API they resolve to Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5; Fable to Fable 5.2.

feature: Provider-specific alias resolution
detail: opus/sonnet/haiku resolve to older versions on Bedrock, Agent Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud (Anthropic managed) and Foundry (Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5 on Foundry).

feature: sonnet[1m] and opus[1m] aliases
detail: Request a 1M-token window; no effect where the model already has native 1M (Sonnet 5.x, Opus 4.7+).

feature: opusplan hybrid model
detail: Uses Opus in plan mode and Sonnet for execution; opusplan[1m] requests 1M; substitutes the newest allowed Opus under allowlists.

feature: Fable models for hardest, longest tasks
detail: Not default on any plan; select with /model fable (5.2) or by ID for 5.1/5; sustained autonomous sessions, more self-verification; saved Fable 5.1 moves to the fable alias on paid plans.

feature: Fable usage credits consent prompt
detail: Depending on plan and seat tier, Fable bills to usage credits; /model shows Requires usage credits and a consent prompt lets you continue or switch; prompt held per dialogExpiry (5 min) in remote or background sessions.

feature: /model switch with save or session-only
detail: /model with no argument opens a picker; Enter saves as default, s switches for this session only; /model name behaves like Enter; Enterprise also records the choice on the account.

feature: Ways to set the model and their priority
detail: /model, claude --model, ANTHROPIC_MODEL, settings model field, then ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL (v2.1.236+) for new sessions.

feature: Picker shows prices on Anthropic API
detail: /model rows display per-model prices when talking to the Anthropic API or a proxying gateway; none on third-party providers.

feature: PreModelSwitch hooks
detail: Hooks that run before a model switch and can block it or ask for confirmation.

feature: Model choice validated for SDK, apps and Remote Control
detail: setModel from the SDK or apps confirms the ID with the provider; Remote Control checks locally; typo warnings suggest the closest model name.

feature: Retirement and remap warnings
detail: Startup notice (and stderr in -p text mode) when the requested model is scheduled for retirement or auto-remapped, also for subagent frontmatter models.

feature: Resumed session keeps its saved model
detail: --resume and --continue restore the saved model except when alias variables, retired or restricted models, provider deployment IDs, haiku or opusplan settings apply.

feature: availableModels allowlist
detail: Managed settings restrict selectable models by family, version prefix or full ID across /model, --model, env vars, subagents, skills, advisor and background agents; blocked picks are rejected or replaced.

feature: enforceAvailableModels for the Default option
detail: With a non-empty allowlist, makes Default resolve to the first allowed model (v2.1.175+).

feature: deniedModels and availableModelsMatch exact
detail: Managed-only keys (v2.1.283+) block specific models or force each listed ID to permit only its own version; requiredMinimumVersion keeps older clients out.

feature: Allowlist surface coverage
detail: Server-managed settings and MDM files reach CLI, IDE, desktop, web, mobile, cloud, SDK and Cowork differently; Cowork on-device does not get server-managed settings; picker greying is convenience only.

feature: Organization model restrictions (admin console)
detail: Enterprise admins disable individual models org-wide or per role in claude.ai; Haiku cannot be disabled; changes apply within about a minute; Anthropic API and LLM gateways only.

feature: Organization default model
detail: Enterprise admins set a default model org-wide or per role, optionally overriding user choice; shown as Org default in /model (v2.1.196+).

feature: Organization effort limits and maxEffortLevel
detail: Enterprise admins cap effort per model per role; maxEffortLevel managed setting caps on any plan or provider; higher levels are not offered and requests run at the cap.

feature: Default model by account type
detail: Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise and API default to Opus 5.5; Bedrock, Agent Platform, Claude Platform on AWS default to Opus 5.5; Foundry to Sonnet 4.5; Fable never the default.

feature: Fallback model chains
detail: --fallback-model a,b or fallbackModel setting (max three) switch for the turn when the primary is overloaded or unavailable; applies to subagents and compaction; skipped entries outside allowlist or with smaller context.

feature: Automatic model fallback on safety flags
detail: Fable, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5 re-run cybersecurity- or biology-flagged requests on a fallback model (Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5) or end in refusal; session stays on the fallback until /model.

feature: Switch models when a message is flagged setting
detail: /config option or switchModelsOnFlag: Ask each time pauses to switch or edit the prompt; subagents fail rather than ask; mobile cloud sessions cannot edit and retry.

feature: claude --safe-mode to diagnose fallback triggers
detail: Starts with CLAUDE.md, skills, MCP servers and hooks disabled to see if customizations trip classifiers.

feature: Effort levels per model
detail: low, medium, high, xhigh, max on Fable and Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.x, Opus 4.7/4.8; Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 lack xhigh; unsupported levels fall back downward.

feature: /effort slider, flag and env resolution
detail: /effort (slider, level, auto, status), /model slider, --effort, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, per-model modelSettings; Enter saves, s is session-only; max applies to session only.

feature: Default effort per model
detail: Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium; Opus 4.7 to xhigh; others to high; org may set a default for its default model.

feature: Effort from Remote Control and skill or subagent frontmatter
detail: Phone or browser effort control applies to that session (v2.1.234+); effort frontmatter in skills and subagents overrides while they run.

feature: Ultracode toggle
detail: Setting that has Claude orchestrate dynamic workflows for substantive tasks at the current effort level; /effort ultracode, Tab toggle in slider, --effort ultracode (starts xhigh), or ultracode setting.

feature: ultrathink keyword for one-off deep reasoning
detail: Including ultrathink in a prompt requests deeper reasoning that turn and raises to xhigh (rainbow-highlighted) in terminal, VS Code and desktop Code tab local sessions; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRATHINK turns it off.

feature: Send no effort level (auto)
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=auto or unset lets the API default apply; /effort status reports it.

feature: Adaptive reasoning vs fixed thinking budget
detail: Newer models always use adaptive reasoning; Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 can revert with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING=1 and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS.

feature: Extended thinking toggle and display
detail: Option+T / Alt+T toggles; /config sets alwaysThinkingEnabled; MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0 disables; Ctrl+O shows reasoning; showThinkingSummaries setting; thinking tokens are billed.

feature: Thinking cannot be turned off on newest models
detail: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable models always think; toggle shows Thinking can't be turned off.

feature: 1M token context window support
detail: Fable, Sonnet 5+, Haiku 5.5 and Opus 4.7+ run 1M by default; Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 need [1m]: Opus 4.6 included on Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise; Sonnet 4.6 1M needs usage credits on every plan.
plans: Opus 4.6 1M: Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise; credits on Pro

feature: Turn off 1M context
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1 removes [1m] variants and treats models as 200K.

feature: Haiku 5.5 1M window and long-prompt pricing
detail: Haiku 5.5 has 1M on every plan; prompts over 100K tokens cost more per token; sessions auto-compact near 967K by default.

feature: Auto-compact window control
detail: /autocompact value (500k, 1M, auto), --autocompact flag, autoCompactWindow setting, CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW (min 100K, max model window); per-model saved values.

feature: Default auto-compact thresholds
detail: Compacts at the model limit except cloud sessions, 200K-boundary models, and native-1M models (about 967K); idleCompaction setting also compacts idle conversations.

feature: Correct context window for gateway or custom model ID
detail: Unrecognized IDs assume a window and warn; fix via update, modelOverrides, [1m] suffix or CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS.

feature: See current model in status line and /status
detail: Status line (if configured) and /status show the active model and account.

feature: Custom model option in /model picker
detail: ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION (+ _NAME, _DESCRIPTION) adds one entry; gateway model discovery via CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1; modelPicker setting reorders rows.

feature: Alias pin variables per family
detail: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE/OPUS/SONNET/HAIKU_MODEL set what aliases map to; CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL sets default for subagents, teammates and workflow agents; ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL is deprecated.

feature: Pin models for third-party deployments
detail: Set version-specific IDs per provider before rollout so aliases do not lag the newest release; add [1m] for Opus/Sonnet 4.6 on those providers.

feature: Pinned model display name, description and capabilities
detail: _NAME, _DESCRIPTION and _SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES (effort, xhigh_effort, max_effort, thinking, adaptive_thinking, interleaved_thinking) customize pinned rows on third-party providers.

feature: modelOverrides per version
detail: Settings map Anthropic model IDs to Bedrock ARNs, Agent Platform versions or Foundry deployments for governance, cost or regional routing; managed-source only when an allowlist is set.

feature: Prompt caching disable switches
detail: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING plus per-family variants for Haiku, Sonnet, Opus and Fable; TTL choosable for main conversation and subagents.

feature: Model alias version history
detail: Table of Claude Code versions at which fable, best, haiku, sonnet and opus aliases changed target models.

feature: Terminal CLI native installer
detail: Install script for macOS, Linux, WSL and Windows (PowerShell or CMD); the native install auto-updates in the background.

feature: Homebrew install with stable and latest casks
detail: Two casks: one follows a stable channel about a week behind, the other gets releases immediately; Homebrew installs do not auto-update.

feature: WinGet install
detail: Windows package-manager install; no auto-update, upgrade manually.

feature: Linux package-manager installs
detail: apt, dnf and apk installs are available for Debian, Fedora, RHEL and Alpine.

feature: Desktop app downloads and Linux beta
detail: Installers for macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon), Windows x64 and ARM64; Ubuntu or Debian via apt in beta.

feature: First-run login or API key use
detail: Claude Code prompts for login on first use; an approved ANTHROPIC_API_KEY skips the login prompt. Most surfaces need a Claude subscription or Console account.

feature: Claude Code in the terminal
detail: Full CLI agent that reads a codebase, edits files, runs commands and handles git from the command line.

feature: VS Code and Cursor extension
detail: Inline diffs, @-mentions, plan review and conversation history inside the editor; opens via Command Palette 'Open in New Tab'.

feature: JetBrains plugin
detail: Plugin for IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm and others with interactive diff viewing and selection sharing; requires the CLI installed separately.

feature: Desktop app Code tab
detail: Standalone app to review diffs visually, run several sessions side by side, schedule recurring tasks and start cloud sessions; paid subscription required.

feature: Claude Code on the web
detail: Run coding tasks in the browser with no local setup, in parallel, on repos not on your machine; also in the iOS and Android apps.

feature: Projects that coordinate parallel web sessions
detail: For larger bodies of work, a project lets Claude coordinate multiple parallel cloud sessions.

feature: Automate routine dev tasks
detail: Write tests, fix lint, resolve merge conflicts, update dependencies and draft release notes from a prompt.

feature: Git commits, branches and pull requests
detail: Stages changes, writes commit messages, creates branches and opens PRs directly.

feature: GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD
detail: Automate code review and issue triage in CI pipelines.

feature: GitHub Code Review on every PR
detail: Automatic code review on each pull request.

feature: MCP servers
detail: Connect external tools and data (Drive, Jira, Slack, custom) through the Model Context Protocol.

feature: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md instructions
detail: Project markdown read at every session start for standards and checklists; an existing AGENTS.md can be read in its place.

feature: Skills for repeatable workflows
detail: Package shareable workflows such as /review-pr or /deploy-staging.

feature: Hooks
detail: Shell commands that run before or after Claude Code actions, e.g. auto-format after edit or lint before commit.

feature: Parallel subagents with a lead agent
detail: A lead agent assigns subtasks to several agents and merges results.

feature: Background agents view
detail: Run several full sessions in parallel and watch them from one screen.

feature: Agent SDK
detail: Build custom agents on Claude Code's tools with control of orchestration, tool access and permissions.

feature: Dynamic workflows
detail: Orchestrate many subagents at once with workflows.

feature: Non-interactive CLI piping and scripting
detail: Pipe input into claude -p for one-shot analysis, CI translation or bulk review of changed files.

feature: Cloud scheduled tasks
detail: Formerly routines; run in the cloud while the computer is off, triggered by schedule, API call or GitHub event; created from web, Desktop or /schedule.

feature: Desktop scheduled tasks
detail: Recurring tasks run on your machine with local file and tool access.

feature: /loop repeats a prompt in a session
detail: Re-runs a prompt within a CLI session for quick polling.

feature: Remote Control
detail: Continue a local session from a phone or any browser.

feature: Dispatch tasks from phone to Desktop
detail: Message a task from the phone and open the Desktop session it creates.

feature: Teleport cloud session into terminal
detail: claude --teleport pulls a web or mobile session into the terminal; needs a claude.ai subscription.

feature: /desktop hands a terminal session to Desktop
detail: Continues the current session in the Desktop app for visual diff review; macOS and x64 Windows, claude.ai subscription.

feature: claude --cloud starts a cloud task from terminal
detail: Start locally then continue on mobile via the cloud.

feature: Channels from Telegram, Discord, iMessage or webhooks
detail: Push events from chat apps or your own webhooks into a session.

feature: Slack: @Claude turns bug reports into pull requests
detail: Mention Claude in Slack to route a task and get a PR back.

feature: Claude in Chrome for debugging live web apps
detail: Chrome integration to debug running web applications.

feature: Output styles
detail: Session-wide instructions that change Claude's role, tone and response format; five options including Default.

feature: Default output style
detail: No style instructions added; standard software-engineering prompt.

feature: Proactive output style
detail: Starts work immediately, assumes on routine decisions, skips plan mode unless asked, and asks before deleting data or changing shared systems.

feature: Concise output style
detail: Leads with the result, drops preamble and recaps, one to three sentences for simple questions; full length for errors and warnings. Needs v2.1.237+.

feature: Explanatory output style
detail: Adds Insight blocks in chat explaining why choices were made; not written to files.

feature: Learning output style
detail: Insight blocks plus leaves TODO(human) pieces for the user to write, then waits and reviews.

feature: /output-style command
detail: Switch or list styles; saved to local project settings; works non-interactively and via Remote Control (built-in only).

feature: Output style picker in /config
detail: Terminal menu to pick a style.

feature: VS Code Output styles menu
detail: Pick built-in or custom styles, and create a style file, from the slash menu.

feature: Desktop outputStyle setting
detail: Desktop sets style through the outputStyle field in settings files rather than a menu.

feature: Default output style across projects
detail: Set outputStyle in user settings; project settings take precedence. Value is case-sensitive.

feature: Switching style mid-session
detail: New style applies from the next message (v2.1.251+).

feature: Custom output style files
detail: Markdown files with frontmatter at user, project or managed-policy level; closest project directory wins on name clash.

feature: Custom style frontmatter options
detail: name, description, keep-coding-instructions (retain coding prompt) and force-for-plugin (plugin styles auto-apply).

feature: Plugins can ship output styles
detail: Plugins may include an output-styles directory.

feature: Output styles affect main chat and forks only
detail: Other subagents use their own system prompt; styles add input tokens (cached) and change output length.

feature: Permission modes overview
detail: Six modes set what Claude does without asking: default (manual), acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions; deny rules block in every mode.

feature: Manual (default) mode
detail: Asks before most edits, shell commands and network access; reads in working directories run freely.

feature: acceptEdits mode
detail: Auto-approves file edits and common filesystem commands (mkdir, touch, rm, rmdir, mv, cp, sed) in scope; protected paths and critical removals still prompt.

feature: Plan mode
detail: Claude researches and proposes changes without editing until a plan is approved; entered with Shift+Tab, /plan or --permission-mode plan.

feature: Plan approval options
detail: Choices: approve with auto mode, approve and manually review edits, or keep planning; Ctrl+G edits the plan; optional clear-context option; accepting titles the session.

feature: Auto mode with classifier
detail: A separate classifier model reviews actions and blocks escalation, unknown infrastructure or injected content; default start mode in terminal and VS Code since v2.1.283.

feature: Auto mode model requirements
detail: Needs supported models (e.g. Opus 4.6+, Sonnet 4.6+, Haiku 5.5, Fable); stricter list on Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry and gateway sessions.

feature: Auto mode fallback to prompting
detail: After 3 blocks in a row or 20 total, auto pauses and prompts; blocked actions appear in /permissions Recently blocked.

feature: Server-side classifier review
detail: Where rolled out the server reviews actions within model requests; CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0 forces local classifier requests.

feature: Choose classifier model
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL sets a different reviewer model (v2.1.302+); default is Sonnet 5; /status shows Auto mode server state.

feature: Auto mode default block list
detail: Blocks curl|bash, force push, prod deploys, IAM grants, secret leaks, destructive git resets, unreviewed PR merges, tunnels and similar; allows local edits and read-only requests.

feature: Trusted infrastructure for auto mode
detail: Admins list trusted repos, buckets and services in autoMode.environment; claude auto-mode defaults prints built-in rules.

feature: Boundaries and approvals stated in chat
detail: The classifier treats statements like 'don't push' as blocks and specific approvals as one-action clearances; compaction can lose them.

feature: First read outside working directories prompt
detail: One-time prompt with four answers; 'block from now on' sets blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories in user settings. Not shown in -p, SDK, background, VS Code panel or desktop.

feature: Block reads and writes outside working directories
detail: Settings refuse or prompt for access outside working directories in every mode, including bypass.

feature: Subagent checks in auto mode
detail: Classifier checks a subagent's task at spawn, each action while it runs and its results on return.

feature: Auto mode drops broad allow rules
detail: Entering auto drops blanket Bash(*), wildcard interpreters, Agent and Monitor allow rules; narrow rules stay and return on exit.

feature: dontAsk mode
detail: Denies anything that would prompt; only reads and pre-approved tools run; for locked-down CI; never in Shift+Tab cycle.

feature: bypassPermissions mode
detail: Disables prompts and checks for isolated containers; needs launch flag, warning dialog acceptance, refuses root, blockable by admins.

feature: Dangerous-skip warning dialog
detail: First bypass session asks acceptance, stored as skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt; declining exits.

feature: Restricted mode (--restricted)
detail: Refuses bypassPermissions and stops the classifier approving protected-path writes (v2.1.248+).

feature: Background sessions and bypass
detail: Background sessions honor bypass acceptance only from user or managed settings; otherwise start in Manual.

feature: Shift+Tab cycles permission modes
detail: Cycles default, acceptEdits, plan, then optional bypass and auto; status bar shows the active mode.

feature: Yes, and switch to auto mode on Bash prompt
detail: Bash permission prompts in Manual or acceptEdits add an option to approve and switch to auto.

feature: --permission-mode flag and defaultMode setting
detail: Choose start mode by flag (manual alias for default) or permissions.defaultMode; auto and bypass in project files are ignored.

feature: VS Code permission mode indicator
detail: Labels Manual, Edit automatically, Plan, Auto, Bypass; claudeCode.initialPermissionMode pins the start mode (not auto); bypass needs an extension toggle.

feature: Desktop mode selector
detail: Per-folder remembered mode; bypass needs a settings toggle on Pro, Max, Ultra and policy on Team and Enterprise; Cowork has separate modes.

feature: Web and mobile permission dropdown
detail: Cloud sessions offer Accept edits, Plan, Auto; Remote Control sessions offer Manual, Accept edits, Plan, Auto; mobile via + then Permission.

feature: claude remote-control --permission-mode
detail: Sets starting mode for a Remote Control local session; needs claude.ai sign-in, not API keys.

feature: Cloud sessions ignore dontAsk and bypass from settings
detail: Checked-in repo settings cannot start a cloud session in those modes.

feature: Non-interactive -p default is manual
detail: claude -p and SDK runs deny calls needing approval unless allow rules, auto mode or a prompt tool is given (v2.1.302+).

feature: Admin switches: disableAutoMode and disableBypassPermissionsMode
detail: Managed settings can remove auto mode or block bypass for an organization.

feature: HIPAA configuration permission defaults
detail: With HIPAA config, terminal and VS Code sessions start in auto on v2.1.326+; earlier versions started in default.

feature: Actions no mode auto-approves
detail: Ask rules, org ask connectors, AskUserQuestion, critical rm removals and cross-session safeguards always prompt or deny even in bypass.

feature: Protected paths
detail: Writes to .git, .vscode, .idea, .claude, shell rc files, .mcp.json etc. prompt in default and acceptEdits, go to the classifier in auto, are denied in dontAsk and allowed in bypass.

feature: Critical-path rm protection
detail: rm and rmdir on root, home, top-level dirs or working directory (and variable-glob forms) are not approved by allow rules or hooks.

feature: Mounted drive rm prompt
detail: Recursive rm on /Volumes, /media, /mnt style drives prompts; CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUNTED_DRIVE_RM_PROMPT=1 turns it off.

feature: Two-minute countdown on critical removals
detail: In auto and bypass terminal prompts, unanswered after 2 minutes denies; three timeouts then deny immediately; outside terminal they are denied.

feature: Env overrides for removal prompts
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_DANGEROUS_RM_TIMEOUT and CLAUDE_CODE_EVEN_MORE_DANGEROUSLY_SKIP_PERMISSIONS relax the removal prompt; startup notices confirm effect.

feature: PowerShell Remove-Item protections
detail: Remove-Item, rd, rmdir, del and erase on system paths or wildcards are denied in every mode; working-directory recursion follows the mode.

feature: Cross-session messaging safeguards
detail: isolatePeerMachines approval and crossSessionInbound hold apply even in bypass mode.

feature: Proxy support via HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY
detail: Honors standard proxy variables (lowercase too), basic auth in URL; no SOCKS support; loopback WebSockets bypass the proxy.

feature: CA certificate store selection
detail: Trusts bundled Mozilla CAs plus OS store by default; CLAUDE_CODE_CERT_STORE picks bundled, system or both.

feature: Custom CA via NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS
detail: Adds an enterprise CA file; warns when the file is only partly readable.

feature: mTLS client certificates
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_CERT, KEY and passphrase enable client auth; rotated files are re-read on connection errors or settings apply.

feature: Network settings in managed settings env
detail: All variables can go in settings.json env; cloud sessions ignore cert variables; Desktop managed sessions read them from managed settings only.

feature: Verify network configuration
detail: claude --debug logs cert loading; /status shows Proxy, mTLS and extra CA rows.

feature: Network settings for background agents
detail: Put proxy and cert variables in settings, not the shell, because a shared supervisor hosts background agents; processWrapper prefixes a corporate launcher.

feature: Streaming idle watchdogs
detail: Four timers abort stalled streams: first-byte, event-level, byte-level, body idle; tunable via CLAUDE_STREAM_* and API_TIMEOUT_MS variables.

feature: Network allowlist requirements
detail: Lists hosts to allow (Anthropic API, claude.ai auth, MCP proxy, downloads, npm, GitHub, Chrome bridge, artifact content, optional Datadog telemetry).

feature: Disable non-essential traffic
detail: DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DO_NOT_TRACK, DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC stop optional operational telemetry hosts.

feature: IP allowlisting and Chrome bridge routing
detail: Org IP allowlists need bridge.claudeusercontent.com routed through the same proxy egress for Claude in Chrome.

feature: Cloud provider and gateway routing
detail: Bedrock, Agent Platform, Foundry and Claude apps gateway sessions send model traffic to the provider or gateway; fast mode check still needs api.anthropic.com.

feature: OpenTelemetry export for usage monitoring
detail: Opt-in export of metrics, events and traces to your own backend via CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY and OTEL_* variables.

feature: Managed OTel settings pin the collector
detail: Managed env settings remove developer-set conflicting endpoints, protocols and credentials; repo settings cannot enable telemetry.

feature: OTel exporters
detail: Metrics via otlp, prometheus, console or none; logs via otlp, console or none; grpc, http/json or http/protobuf; interval variables.

feature: OTel mTLS and dynamic headers
detail: Client certs per protocol and otelHeadersHelper script for refreshed auth headers (29-minute default).

feature: Metrics cardinality controls
detail: Toggle session.id, version, account UUID, entrypoint, resource attributes and repository attributes on telemetry.

feature: Host name and ID attribution
detail: OTEL_RESOURCE_INCLUDE_HOST adds host.name and host.id to resources (v2.1.326+).

feature: Traces (beta)
detail: Span tracing linking each prompt to API requests and tool runs; needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA; TRACEPARENT passed to Bash subprocesses.

feature: Eight usage metrics
detail: Counters for sessions, lines changed, pull requests, commits, cost (USD), tokens, edit-tool decisions and active time.

feature: Telemetry event types
detail: Events for prompts, responses, tool results and decisions, API request/error/refusal, MCP connections, plugins, skills, hooks, compaction, subagents, auth, permission-mode changes and more.

feature: Content logging opt-ins
detail: Prompts, responses, tool details, tool content, raw API bodies and managed settings are redacted unless explicit OTEL_LOG_* variables are set.

feature: OTel data goes only to your collector
detail: Telemetry including user email stays at the configured endpoint, never Anthropic; content truncated at 60 KB by default.

feature: Retention sweep event
detail: Reports session transcript cleanup per cleanupPeriodDays (default 30 days) with counts and skip reasons (v2.1.227+).

feature: Managed settings resolved event
detail: Logs the sources and state of managed settings and policy helper at session start (v2.1.274+).

feature: Safety event (retired)
detail: claude_code.safety_event stopped sending in v2.1.312; use tool_decision events to see refused calls.

feature: Telemetry from cloud sessions and Claude Tag
detail: Set OTel variables in server-managed settings or the cloud environment; filter by ccr.session.id; Cowork is configured separately.

feature: Desktop SSH and Cowork telemetry
detail: Desktop Code tab reads managed settings for OTel; remote SSH sessions need host variables on the remote; Cowork has an admin console monitoring form.

feature: SIEM audit and cost monitoring guidance
detail: Map events to security questions, audit MCP activity, detect retry exhaustion and send events to a SIEM.

feature: Bedrock monitoring pointer
detail: Separate AWS guidance covers monitoring Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock.

feature: Tiered permission system per tool type
detail: Read-only tools run without asking inside working directories; Bash, file edits, WebFetch and WebSearch ask in Manual mode, with different 'don't ask again' scopes (per repo, per domain, until session end).

feature: Permission prompt: Yes, don't ask again saves a rule
detail: Approving permanently saves an allow rule to the repository's local settings file, applied to future sessions in that repo and its worktrees; file-edit approvals last only until the session ends.

feature: Add a comment when answering a permission prompt
detail: Press Tab on Yes or No to attach a note to Claude; Yes sends it after the result, No sends it as the denial reason. Not offered on WebFetch, browser or save-a-rule options.

feature: /permissions dialog
detail: Lists every allow, ask and deny rule with the settings file it comes from; changes apply from Claude's next tool call even mid-turn; includes an Auto mode tab for classifier rules.

feature: Allow, ask and deny rules with deny-first order
detail: Rules evaluate deny, then ask, then allow; the first match wins regardless of specificity, so a narrow allow cannot carve an exception from a broad deny.

feature: Bare-name deny removes a tool from Claude's context
detail: A deny rule naming only a tool hides it from Claude entirely; scoped deny rules leave the tool and block matching calls. EndConversation cannot be removed this way.

feature: Permission mode: default (Manual)
detail: Prompts before most edits, shell commands and network requests; labeled Manual in CLI, VS Code, JetBrains and desktop, with manual accepted as alias.

feature: Permission mode: acceptEdits
detail: Auto-accepts file edits and common filesystem commands (mkdir, touch, mv, cp) for paths in the working or additional directories.

feature: Permission mode: plan
detail: Claude explores with reads and read-only shell commands but does not edit source files; classifier-approved commands also run when auto mode is available.

feature: Permission mode: auto with background classifier
detail: Runs without routine prompts while a background classifier checks that shell commands and network requests match the user's request.

feature: Permission mode: dontAsk
detail: Auto-denies anything that would otherwise prompt; reads and pre-approved tools still run. AskUserQuestion and some other calls are denied even if allowed.

feature: Permission mode: bypassPermissions
detail: Skips prompts except for actions no mode auto-approves, including writes to .git and .claude; intended only for containers or VMs.

feature: Disable bypass and auto modes by setting
detail: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode and permissions.disableAutoMode set to disable lock those modes out; most useful in managed settings.

feature: denyInsteadOfPrompting setting
detail: When true in user or managed settings, calls that would wait on a prompt are denied so unattended sessions keep running, independent of the current mode.

feature: Permission rule syntax Tool and Tool(specifier)
detail: Rules name a tool alone or with a specifier such as a command, file path or domain; Bash(*) equals bare Bash.

feature: Deny/ask rules matching tool input parameters
detail: Tool(param:value) rules match a top-level scalar parameter such as Agent(model:opus) or Bash(run_in_background:true), with wildcard support; primary content fields like command or file_path cannot be matched this way.

feature: Bash wildcard patterns and :* suffix
detail: A * matches any text; a trailing ' *' also matches the bare command; the space before it matters (ls * vs ls*); Bash(ls:*) is an equivalent trailing form; startup warning for wildcard before the subcommand.

feature: Tool-name glob rules (mcp__*)
detail: Deny and ask accept globs in the tool-name position; allow globs only after a literal mcp__server__ prefix; unanchored allow globs are ignored.

feature: Compound command handling
detail: Commands split on &&, ||, ;, |, |& , & and newlines; every part must be allowed; deny/ask match any part including subshells; approving saves up to five separate rules.

feature: Wrapper stripping before Bash rule matching
detail: timeout, time, nice, nohup, stdbuf, command, builtin, noglob, bare xargs and known-safe env assignments are stripped so rules match the inner command; runners like npx, docker exec, devbox are not stripped.

feature: Exec wrappers and find actions always prompt
detail: watch, setsid, ionice, flock and find with -exec/-delete/-fprint cannot be approved by a prefix rule; only an exact no-wildcard rule or a PreToolUse hook avoids the prompt.

feature: Built-in read-only command set
detail: ls, cat, echo, pwd, head, tail, grep, find, wc, which, diff, stat, du, cd and read-only git run without prompts; not configurable except via ask/deny rules; several edge cases still prompt (globs with write flags, docker other daemon, ps e, UNC paths, unparseable or 10,000+ char commands).

feature: Redirect and tee target checks
detail: Output redirects, input redirects and tee destinations are checked against Edit/Read rules, protected paths and working directories; /dev/null, fd forms and here-docs are exempt.

feature: PowerShell permission rules
detail: Same shape as Bash rules; cmdlet aliases canonicalize (gci/ls/dir match Get-ChildItem), case-insensitive, AST-parsed with each subcommand of a compound checked.

feature: Read and Edit deny rules for files
detail: Read deny rules block file tools, @-mentions, pasted image paths, directory listings and IDE context for matching paths; they also block Edit/Write; claudeignore is not honored; Write/Glob/Grep path rules do not match, use Edit/Read.

feature: Gitignore-style path patterns with anchors
detail: //path is absolute, ~/path is home, /path anchors at the settings source, plain or ./path is relative; allow and deny differ on single-segment directory depth; ! negation carves out within the same source.

feature: Symlink-aware permission checks
detail: Allow needs both requested and resolved paths to match; deny matches either; writes to a symlink itself are refused; resolved targets outside working directories or in protected paths prompt.

feature: Network path read prompts (UNC and /net)
detail: Reads from UNC or /net automount paths always prompt, even against allow rules, hooks or auto mode; dontAsk denies; mapping a drive or mounting locally avoids it.

feature: WebFetch domain rules and wildcards
detail: WebFetch(domain:host) matches hostnames case-insensitively; *.example.com covers subdomains but not the apex; bare WebFetch vs domain:* differ in sandbox allowlist effect and artifact reads.

feature: MCP permission rules
detail: mcp__server, mcp__server__* or mcp__server__tool match server or single tool; allow rules take no specifier; plugin servers use plugin-scoped names; connector tools can be forced to ask by an organization even in bypass mode.

feature: Cowork shell and fetch covered by Bash/WebFetch deny rules
detail: Deny rules naming Bash or WebFetch also block Cowork's workspace bash and web_fetch tools; allow rules do not carry over.

feature: Agent(name) rules to allow or deny subagents
detail: Deny Agent(Explore), Agent(Plan) or a custom subagent name to disable specific subagents.

feature: Cd rules for the /cd command
detail: Bare Cd deny disables /cd; Cd(pattern) deny blocks targets; any Cd allow rule turns /cd into allowlist mode; only governs user-typed /cd.

feature: PreToolUse hooks extend permissions
detail: Hooks can deny, force a prompt or allow a call, but never override deny or ask rules; an exit-code-2 block beats allow rules; plan mode ignores hook allow for non-read-only calls.

feature: Mods and the built-in guard in permission precedence
detail: Installed mods handling tool.check answer after hooks; with managed settings or Team/Enterprise login a built-in guard keeps deny/ask/hook outcomes, without them a mod can approve more.

feature: Working directories: --add-dir, /add-dir, additionalDirectories
detail: Extend file access at startup, in-session or via settings; added directories follow normal rules; trust prompt for untrusted folders; only flag/command-added directories also load skills, commands, subagents and some settings.

feature: Block reads and writes outside working directories
detail: blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories and blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories make file tools refuse outside paths in every mode; writes key does not limit shell, MCP or hooks.

feature: /cd moves the session to another directory
detail: Keeps the conversation, loads the new directory's CLAUDE.md, settings, hooks, MCP servers, plugins and skills, prompts for workspace trust, and disconnects the old directory's servers.

feature: Sandboxing complements permissions
detail: Sandbox adds OS-level filesystem and network limits for Bash, PowerShell and Monitor; autoAllowBashIfSandboxed lets sandboxed commands run without prompting except content-scoped ask rules.

feature: Managed settings and allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly
detail: Admin-deployed managed settings cannot be overridden by user, project or CLI settings; the lock makes managed settings the only source of permission rules; a deny at any level cannot be allowed elsewhere.

feature: Workspace trust dialog gates project allow rules
detail: Project permissions.allow and additionalDirectories apply only after the trust dialog is accepted (repo-root keyed, home-dir trust is session-only); not shown in -p or SDK runs; untracked local settings apply without it.

feature: Safe-run options for unfamiliar repos in -p mode
detail: --setting-sources user, --bare, --settings disableAllHooks and disabledMcpjsonServers limit what a repository can run before trust.

feature: Claude Code CLI as full-feature surface
detail: Terminal surface with the full feature set, Agent SDK and scripting (CLI-only), third-party providers, and computer use on macOS.

feature: Claude Code in Desktop app
detail: Diff viewer, app preview, parallel sessions, managed setup and computer use; supports gateway providers and Google Cloud Agent Platform for enterprise.

feature: Claude Code in VS Code
detail: Extension with inline diffs, integrated terminal and file context; supports third-party providers.

feature: Claude Code in JetBrains IDEs
detail: Extension for IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm and others with diff viewer, selection sharing and a terminal session running the CLI.

feature: Claude Code on the web (cloud sessions)
detail: Anthropic-managed cloud sessions at claude.ai/code for long-running tasks that continue after you disconnect.

feature: Claude Code from the mobile apps
detail: Start and monitor cloud sessions from the Claude app, or steer local sessions through Remote Control.

feature: Shared config, memory and MCP across local surfaces
detail: Configuration, project memory and MCP servers are shared among the CLI, Desktop and IDE surfaces on the same project.

feature: Claude Code Chrome integration
detail: Controls the browser using your logged-in sessions for testing web apps, filling forms and automating sites without an API.

feature: GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD integrations
detail: Run Claude in CI pipelines for automated PR review, issue triage and scheduled maintenance.

feature: Code Review on every pull request
detail: Reviews each PR automatically to catch bugs before human review.

feature: Claude Code in Slack via @Claude
detail: Responds to @Claude mentions under your own account, running on Anthropic cloud with Claude Code on the web enabled, to turn bug reports into PRs.

feature: Claude Tag shared organization identity
detail: Runs @Claude as the organization's shared identity with admin-configured access instead of per-user Slack sessions.

feature: Dispatch from mobile to Desktop
detail: Message a task from the Claude mobile app to run on your paired Desktop; not available to new users.

feature: Remote Control of a running session
detail: Drive a session running on your machine (CLI, Desktop, VS Code) from claude.ai/code or the mobile app via claude remote-control or /remote-control.

feature: Channels push events into a session
detail: Push events from Telegram, Discord or your own server into a CLI session via channel plugins, e.g. for CI failures or chat messages.

feature: Self-hosted environments for cloud sessions
detail: Run cloud sessions on your organization's infrastructure via deployed runners so they stay inside your network.

feature: Scheduled tasks (CLI, Desktop, cloud routines)
detail: Recurring prompts on a chosen frequency, run locally in the CLI or Desktop or as cloud routines.

feature: Claude Code Projects coordinating cloud sessions
detail: One conversation where Claude coordinates many cloud sessions for a body of work and reports back.

feature: Computer use on macOS from CLI
detail: Let Claude open apps and control your screen on macOS.

feature: claude plugin eval command
detail: Runs a plugin's eval suite in isolated non-interactive sessions, scoring each case over multiple runs; needs Claude Code 2.1.269+ and git 2.31+; each run is a real model call counted against plan or API.

feature: claude plugin eval init generates cases
detail: Interactive session that reads the plugin, proposes prompts and graders, trial-runs them and writes case directories; --bare writes a blank template (used in CI).

feature: Eval no-plugin baseline and delta
detail: Each case runs with and without the plugin (default 3 runs per arm) and reports WITH, W/OUT and delta; --ablation none runs one arm; skill-fired graders are excluded from scoring in two-arm runs.

feature: Eval grader types
