detail: Six graders: regex, tool_used, tool_order, file_exists (free) and llm and baseline (judge model); weights and arm settings; targets include last message, trace, files, a file's contents and mock calls; no custom-code graders.

feature: Eval case files and frontmatter
detail: Cases are directories with prompt.md (tags, runs 1-50, model, max_turns default 10, timeout 300s, allowed_tools, append_system_prompt, EVAL_* env) and optional case.yaml with scaffold_script, history_file and add_dirs.

feature: Eval MCP server mocks
detail: Per-tool Markdown mocks (fixed or judge-model agent answers, input expect guards, error mode, fixtures) stand in for MCP servers; agent-mock answers can be recorded and replayed; --allow-real-servers or --mocks off use real servers.

feature: Eval run options and tool grants
detail: Options include --runs, --concurrency 1-8, --model, --judge-model, --threshold, --max-cost-usd, --case/--tag filters, --keep-temp, --eval-dir; non-read-only tools need --allow-tools and Bash grants run in the OS sandbox.

feature: Eval CI mode, exit codes and JSON result
detail: --json writes a versioned result, --trust-plugin skips the trust prompt, exit codes 0/1/2/130/143 signal pass, fail, partial (cost ceiling or auth) or interruption.

feature: Eval HTML report and private artifact publishing
detail: Self-contained report.html with verdict line, tiles and per-run grader verdicts; subscription users with artifacts get a private published copy, disabled by --no-publish and kept local for session-started runs.

feature: Eval runs isolated with plugin-directory trust prompt
detail: Each run gets a temp home and config with only the plugin loaded, case definitions hidden, Artifact tool off; first run asks to trust the plugin directory.

feature: Official plugin marketplace auto-added
detail: claude-plugins-official is added on first interactive terminal session, containing Anthropic-maintained plugins plus partner and other-author plugins; can be blocked by managed policy or an env var.

feature: Community plugin marketplace
detail: claude-community holds third-party plugins submitted to Anthropic; added manually with /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-community.

feature: Topic marketplaces and third-party marketplaces
detail: Other marketplaces (anthropics/skills, knowledge-work-plugins, authors' own repos) are added with /plugin marketplace add owner/repo and installed with plugin@marketplace; Anthropic does not review third-party ones.

feature: Deprecated claude-code-plugins marketplace
detail: The marketplace in anthropics/claude-code is deprecated in favor of claude-plugins-official; ralph-wiggum became ralph-loop and (model name) is retired.

feature: Discover plugins: /plugin Discover tab, install by name, web marketplace
detail: Browse and search plugins in the /plugin Discover tab, /plugin install <name>, or the Claude Marketplace web catalog showing install counts and Anthropic verified marks.

feature: Anthropic plugin directory on claude.ai syncs to Claude Code
detail: A plugin added from the claude.ai directory reaches Claude Code through account sync.

feature: Plugin install hint prompt from other CLIs
detail: A claude-code-hint tag on stderr from a third-party CLI triggers a one-time Plugin recommendation dialog (Yes install / No / No and never show hints); tag stripped from tool output; official-marketplace plugins only.

feature: Plugin hint prompt limits and opt-out
detail: One prompt per session, one per plugin ever, cap of 100 plugins, none in -p, subagent, hook, cloud, Remote Control or analytics-off sessions; 30 seconds with no answer counts as No.

feature: claude plugin init scaffolds a plugin
detail: Creates a skills-directory plugin under ~/.claude/skills with flags for description, author, --with skills/agents/hooks/mcp/lsp/output-style/channel starters and --force; loads next session as name@skills-dir.

feature: claude plugin install with scope, config and JSON
detail: Installs at user, project or local scope; --config sets userConfig options; --marketplace adds and installs in one step; command-source plugins show the command and ask for confirmation (-y or --accept-command sha256); --json prints a result object.

feature: claude plugin uninstall with keep-data and prune
detail: Removes a plugin from one scope; deletes its options, secrets and data directory when last scope, unless --keep-data; --prune also removes orphaned auto-installed dependencies.

feature: claude plugin enable and disable
detail: Toggle a plugin at a scope (auto-detected local, project, user); disable --all turns off every plugin; dependency rules block disabling a needed plugin; synced plugins use name@synced; a local-scope disable overrides a project-enabled plugin.

feature: claude plugin update including managed scope
detail: Updates to the latest marketplace version (loads next session or after /reload-plugins), by bare or qualified name; managed scope can be updated but not installed to; retries unfinished dependency installs.

feature: claude plugin list with JSON, available and data size
detail: Lists installed, session-only, skills-directory and claude.ai-synced plugins with version, scope and status; --json adds details, --available lists uninstalled marketplace plugins, --data-size measures saved data.

feature: claude plugin details shows inventory and token cost
detail: Prints a loaded plugin's skills, agents, hooks, MCP and LSP servers plus its always-on projected token cost and per-component estimates.

feature: claude plugin configure for userConfig options
detail: Shows a plugin's options and set/not set state without revealing sensitive values, or saves values piped as JSON with --values-stdin after type validation.

feature: claude plugin restore-set-aside
detail: Restores or discards (--discard) options and secrets set aside when an organization replaced a same-named marketplace.

feature: claude plugin prune removes orphaned dependencies
detail: Removes auto-installed dependencies no plugin needs, with --dry-run preview and -y to skip confirmation; never removes plugins you installed yourself.

feature: claude plugin tag creates release tags
detail: Creates an annotated git tag name--vversion after checking plugin.json and marketplace versions agree; supports --push, --dry-run, --force, custom message and remote.

feature: claude plugin test for mods
detail: Runs .test.ts and .test.tsx files for a mod (a plugin whose code registers event handlers) with no session, sign-in or network.

feature: claude plugin validate with strict, JSON and README advice
detail: Validates plugin or marketplace manifests and skill/agent/command files with exit codes 0/1/2; --strict treats warnings as errors; reports mod gating hooks, hosts and an advisory when README lacks an install line.

feature: claude plugin marketplace add from many source types
detail: Add a marketplace from GitHub owner/repo (with ref), SSH or HTTPS git URLs, a hosted marketplace.json URL, or a local directory or file, at user, project or local scope; --sparse limits monorepo checkout.

feature: Add a claude.ai-hosted marketplace with --claudeai
detail: Adds a marketplace hosted on the account (listed under From claude.ai) by name; it is tied to the account and cannot be shared through project settings.

feature: claude plugin marketplace list, remove and update
detail: List configured marketplaces (text or JSON); remove deletes cache and uninstalls its plugins from the last scope (warning); update refreshes one or all from source, following a pinned ref.

feature: /plugin panel and subcommands in session
detail: /plugin (aliases /plugins, /marketplace) opens tabs Discover, Installed, Marketplaces, Stats; subcommands list, install, manage, stats, enable, disable, uninstall, configure, validate, tag and marketplace add/list/update/remove; interactive sessions only.

feature: /reload-plugins applies plugin changes mid-session
detail: Reloads plugins, skills, agents, hooks and MCP/LSP servers and prints a summary; resolves missing dependencies; refuses cache-invalidating MCP changes unless --force; works in desktop, SDK and -p when typed directly, not over Remote Control.

feature: --plugin-dir and --plugin-url session-only plugins
detail: Load a plugin from a directory, .zip or URL for one session without installing; shows as name@inline and overrides an installed plugin of the same name; admins can block with disableSideloadFlags.

feature: Code intelligence plugins (LSP)
detail: Language server plugins for C/C++, C#, Go, Java, Kotlin, Liquid, Lua, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, Swift and TypeScript/JavaScript give Claude live diagnostics after edits; the user installs the server binary separately; not available in cloud sessions.

feature: LSP tool for symbol navigation
detail: A read-only LSP tool lets Claude look up definitions and references by symbol through the language server instead of text search.

feature: Diagnostics summary after edits (Ctrl+O to expand)
detail: After an edit the conversation shows 'Found N new diagnostic issues in M files'; Ctrl+O expands the issues; the /plugin Errors tab shows missing-binary errors.

feature: LSP plugin recommendation dialog
detail: When a language server binary is on PATH but its plugin isn't installed, a once-per-session dialog offers Yes install, Not now, Never for this plugin or Disable all; 30 seconds ignored counts, five ignores disable it; never shown in cloud sessions.

feature: Custom language server via .lsp.json plugin
detail: Languages without an official plugin can be connected by writing a plugin with an .lsp.json naming the server command and file extensions, loaded via --plugin-dir or a marketplace.

feature: Plugin skills as namespaced slash commands
detail: A plugin's skills/<dir>/SKILL.md runs as /plugin:dir, loaded by Claude when the description matches or invoked directly; extra skill directories via manifest; a root SKILL.md works as one skill; CLAUDE.md at plugin root is not loaded.

feature: Plugin commands (legacy format)
detail: Markdown files under commands/ become /plugin:file (subfolders add segments), or can be defined inline in the manifest; superseded by skills for new work.

feature: Plugin subagents
detail: Markdown files under agents/ define subagents named plugin:name (subfolders nest), invokable with @agent-plugin:name; frontmatter supports model, effort, maxTurns, tools, skills, memory, background, isolation worktree; permissionMode, hooks, mcpServers are ignored.

feature: Plugin hooks
detail: hooks/hooks.json registers lifecycle hooks (shell command, HTTP, MCP tool call, model prompt or subagent) when the plugin loads; receive CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, DATA and option env vars; same-name plugins register only one set; JavaScript hook modules make the plugin a mod.

feature: Plugin MCP servers
detail: Declared in .mcp.json or the manifest and shown in /mcp as plugin:plugin:server with tool names mcp__plugin_plugin_server__tool; unchanged servers keep connection on reload; stdio servers run in Claude Code and local Cowork but not claude.ai, remote https servers reach claude.ai as connectors.

feature: Packaged MCPB servers in plugins
detail: mcpServers can point at a .mcpb or .dxt bundle (path or https URL); bundle user_config settings are set via /plugin Configure or claude plugin install --config; a bundled server missing required settings does not start.

feature: Plugin LSP servers (.lsp.json)
detail: Maps server names to command, args and extensionToLanguage; one server per extension; invalid entries skip the whole file; stdout carries protocol only (64 KiB headers, 32 MiB body limit).

feature: Plugin executables in bin/
detail: Files in a plugin's bin/ directory are put on the shell PATH while enabled so Claude can run them by name, after the user's own PATH; claude.ai and Cowork do not install plugins with a top-level bin/.

feature: Plugin color themes and output styles
detail: Plugins can ship themes/<slug>.json appearing in /theme and output-styles/<name>.md appearing in /output-style as plugin:name; plugin themes are read-only and edits save as user copies.

feature: Plugin channels
detail: A channels manifest entry binds an MCP server so an outside system such as Telegram can message into a session, with its own userConfig (e.g. a sensitive bot token).

feature: Plugin background monitors
detail: monitors/monitors.json lists shell commands started in the background for the session whose output reaches Claude as notifications; run unsandboxed with full user permissions, only in interactive sessions, no user_config access, not stopped when plugin disabled.

feature: Plugin workflows
detail: workflows/ holds .js scripts with a meta block that orchestrate several subagents and run as /plugin:name.

feature: Plugin userConfig dialog with sensitive values
detail: Options declared in the manifest prompt in /plugin on install or enable (and /plugin configure, or a gear icon in VS Code); sensitive values are masked and stored in secure storage rather than settings.json.

feature: Plugin path variables and persistent data directory
detail: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT (per-version cache), CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA (survives updates at ~/.claude/plugins/data/id) and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR are substituted in components; Node dependencies auto-install for marketplace plugins.

feature: Create a private plugin marketplace (marketplace.json)
detail: A directory or git repo with .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (name, owner, plugins array) lets a team or org distribute plugins; can be private and an admin can require it on every machine.

feature: Marketplace plugin source types
detail: Entries can come from a relative path, GitHub repo, git-subdir of a monorepo, any git URL, an HTTPS zip archive, an npm package, or a command that produces a directory; git sources can be pinned to ref or sha.

feature: Local marketplace edits apply without version bump
detail: A marketplace added from a local directory reads plugin files in place, so edits load at next session or /reload-plugins; hosted marketplace users get cached copies instead.

feature: Reserved official marketplace names and submodule fetching
detail: Official marketplace names such as claude-plugins-official cannot be used by third parties; adding a marketplace fetches only git submodules that hold plugin files.

feature: Suggest plugins by relevance
detail: A marketplace can have Claude Code suggest one of its plugins when a session matches its relevance rules.

feature: Plugin structure: manifest, skills, agents, hooks, MCP
detail: A plugin is a directory with .claude-plugin/plugin.json (name required; description, version, author optional) plus skills/, commands/, agents/, hooks/hooks.json and .mcp.json; its skills and agents get the plugin-name prefix.

feature: Load a folder of plugins with --plugin-dir
detail: Pointing --plugin-dir at a folder loads each immediate subfolder with a manifest as a separate plugin; subfolders added or removed mid-session load or unload, held for /reload-plugins if it would invalidate the prompt cache.

feature: CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS environment variable
detail: Lists absolute plugin paths to load when a flag cannot be added; loaded in addition to --plugin-dir; cannot be set by project or local settings; managed settings can disable it.

feature: Skills-directory plugins load every session
detail: A folder in ~/.claude/skills (or a project's .claude/skills) with a .claude-plugin/plugin.json auto-loads as name@skills-dir with no install; a root SKILL.md is invoked as /name; admins can block it.

feature: plugin-dev plugin for authoring plugins
detail: Anthropic's plugin-dev plugin from the official marketplace adds skills and agents (e.g. /plugin-dev:create-plugin) that walk through designing, creating and validating a plugin.

feature: Share a plugin: send directory, own marketplace, or Anthropic directory
detail: Plugins can be shared as a directory or zip, listed in a team marketplace, or submitted for review to Anthropic's directory so they appear on claude.ai and in Cowork and reach Claude Code through account sync.

feature: Same plugin folder on claude.ai and Cowork with subset of components
detail: A plugin folder installs on claude.ai and Cowork too, but only some component types load there (e.g. top-level bin/ and stdio MCP servers are not supported).

feature: Plugin debugging tabs: /plugin Errors and Installed
detail: /plugin Installed tab shows found components; Errors tab lists load failures such as missing component paths; /mcp shows MCP server status.

feature: Plugin dependencies with semver ranges
detail: plugin.json dependencies array takes plugin names or objects with name, version range (^, ~, >=, =) and marketplace; constrained dependencies install at the highest matching git tag; pre-release versions need explicit opt-in.

feature: Bundle plugins for a team via dependency-only plugin
detail: A plugin with only a name and dependencies installs a curated set with one command; adding a dependency in a new version reaches users via marketplace auto-update or claude plugin update; admins can deploy via enabledPlugins in managed settings.

feature: Cross-marketplace dependency allowlist
detail: Dependencies from another marketplace install only if the root marketplace lists it in allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn, unless already installed and enabled at the same scope.

feature: Dependency resolution across multiple plugins
detail: Overlapping ranges resolve to the highest satisfying version, conflicting ranges fail the install, auto-update respects every installed plugin's range, and uninstalling the last constrainer releases the pin.

feature: Automatic dependency installs and local testing
detail: Missing dependencies install on install, /reload-plugins, auto-update, update and marketplace add; command-source dependencies are never auto-installed; local --plugin-dir copies satisfy dependencies; claude.ai-synced plugins count as met by same-name claude.ai plugins.

feature: Host a marketplace on GitHub, git host, URL or shared directory
detail: Marketplaces can be hosted on GitHub, GitLab/Bitbucket/GHES, a hosted marketplace.json URL (relative-path entries fail) or a shared filesystem; pin a branch or tag with #ref; project scope shares it with a repo's teammates.

feature: Hosted file download limits
detail: marketplace.json URLs are capped at 5 MiB and 10 s; archive zips at 256 MiB and 120 s with at most five https redirects and extraction caps (100,000 entries, 512 MiB per file, 1 GiB total, 50x ratio).

feature: Symlinks within a marketplace
detail: Plugin symlinks resolving inside the plugin stay relative, those to elsewhere in the marketplace are dereferenced into the cache, and those outside are skipped; Git LFS files arrive as pointers.

feature: Distribute plugins via Organization settings > Plugins & skills
detail: Admins sync a marketplace from the org's GitHub or GitLab connection on claude.ai without users' git credentials; repo must be private or internal, only some source types accepted, plugins with a top-level bin/ are rejected.

feature: Private marketplace access via user git credentials
detail: Claude Code runs non-interactive git with the user's SSH keys or credential helper (no token of its own); GitHub owner/repo probes SSH then falls back to HTTPS, CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS=1 forces HTTPS; archive sources need no git account.

feature: Marketplace background auto-update
detail: Off by default; users enable it per marketplace in /plugin Marketplaces or admins set autoUpdate in managed settings; private repos use credential helpers silently; CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE keeps the checkout on failure.

feature: Plugin versioning and release channels
detail: Users receive a new copy only when the computed version changes (plugin.json first, then entry); omit version to track commits; ref/sha pin a plugin; two marketplaces with different refs give stable and early-access channels.

feature: Rename or remove plugins with renames map and forceRemoveDeletedPlugins
detail: A renames map migrates users' enabled settings to new names or null; displayName changes the label safely; forceRemoveDeletedPlugins uninstalls removed plugins at session start and lists them under Needs attention.

feature: headers and headersHelper for archive downloads
detail: Entries or url-source marketplaces can send HTTP headers, or a helper command (max 500 chars, 10 s, JSON output) for short-lived tokens; users must accept the command when installing; blocked by disableCommandPluginSources; credential-like env vars are stripped.

feature: Command-source change re-acceptance
detail: Changing a command plugin source's command or mode stops background runs and requires each user to accept the new command via claude plugin update.

feature: Company rollout via managed settings and suggestions
detail: Admins use extraKnownMarketplaces, enabledPlugins, autoUpdate and strictKnownMarketplaces in managed settings; pluginSuggestionMarketplaces lets relevance-based plugin suggestions appear; marketplaces have no audience, deprecation or git-token fields.

feature: Install plugin from /plugin panel
detail: Slash command opens the plugin details pane to review contents and choose a scope before installing; no-name form opens the Discover tab with type-to-search.

feature: Plugin details pane: will install, last updated, context cost
detail: Shows commands, agents, skills, hooks and MCP/LSP servers added, last-updated date for official plugins, and per-turn and when-invoked token estimates.

feature: Install scopes: user, project, local
detail: User scope applies in every project on the machine, project scope enables for all repo collaborators via committed settings, local scope enables only for you in one repo; local overrides project overrides user.

feature: Install summary outcomes
detail: After install the summary says active now, active but bundled MCP server needs setup, reload needed (auto-runs reload, or pends if it would invalidate prompt cache), or load failed.

feature: Force plugin reload despite prompt-cache cost
detail: A reload-plugins command with a force flag activates a pending plugin at the cost of one uncached request.

feature: Confirm plugin via namespaced slash commands and list command
detail: Installed plugin skills appear as /plugin:skill; the Installed tab and the plugin list shell command show version, scope and status.

feature: Official marketplace auto-registered on first run
detail: The official Anthropic marketplace is added automatically on first interactive terminal start; the web marketplace Claude Code button copies the shell install command.

feature: Install plugins in desktop app Code tab
detail: The plus menu next to the prompt box offers Add plugins / Browse plugins / Manage plugins for local or SSH sessions, with scope choice of user, project or local.

feature: Manage plugins in VS Code
detail: Typing /plugins in the Claude Code panel opens Manage plugins with Plugins and Marketplaces tabs; install with a scope choice; changes apply to open sessions without restart.

feature: Cloud sessions do not load local or repo plugins
detail: Cloud sessions have no plugin browser and ignore plugins installed locally or enabled in repo settings; org-managed plugins are the route.

feature: JetBrains uses terminal plugin steps
detail: JetBrains plugin runs Claude Code in the IDE terminal so plugin install follows the terminal flow.

feature: Non-interactive runs cannot use /plugin
detail: In print/non-interactive mode the plugin panel is unavailable but already-installed plugins load; manage via shell commands.

feature: Agent SDK plugin loading
detail: Agent SDK apps load plugins through the SDK plugins option.

feature: Session-only plugin from directory flag
detail: Plugin authors can load an on-disk plugin for one session with a plugin-dir flag instead of installing.

feature: Plugins synced from claude.ai account
detail: Plugins turned on for your claude.ai account or by your organization sync into terminal sessions at start (and into Cowork sessions) as name@synced; plugins installed locally do not sync back.

feature: Install plugin from shell
detail: Shell install command installs without a session; user scope default, project/local via scope flag; loads next start or on reload; a yes flag accepts command-source prompts in scripts.

feature: Command-source plugin install confirmation
detail: Plugins that install via a marketplace-named command show that command and ask for acceptance first.

feature: Add marketplace from GitHub, git URL, local path or hosted JSON
detail: Marketplace add accepts owner/repo (optional #ref pin), any git clone URL, a local directory or file path, or an https marketplace.json URL; /plugin market is a shorthand.

feature: Add marketplace and install in one command
detail: Install with a marketplace flag adds an unknown marketplace (session asks confirmation, v2.1.275+; shell adds without confirmation, v2.1.292+) then installs.

feature: Private marketplace via local git credentials
detail: Private repos clone with existing HTTPS credential helpers or passphrase-less SSH keys with known hosts; never prompts; env var can force HTTPS for GitHub shorthand.

feature: Add marketplace from claude.ai
detail: Marketplaces listed by claude.ai (org library, own uploads) can be added by name from the Marketplaces tab or a claudeai flag (v2.1.273+); registered locally with a claudeai- prefix.

feature: Installed tab: enable, disable, favorite, filter
detail: Installed list supports type-to-filter, Space to toggle, f to favorite, Enter for details; disabled plugins collapse at the bottom; details offer disable/enable, update now, uninstall.

feature: Configure options and Configure for plugin settings
detail: Plugins with userConfig show Configure options; plugins with a bundled MCP server show Configure for that server's settings.

feature: Managed-scope plugins locked
detail: Plugins installed by organization managed settings show at Managed scope and cannot be enabled, disabled or uninstalled by the user.

feature: Auto-reload on closing plugin panel
detail: Closing /plugin with pending changes runs reload automatically unless it would invalidate the prompt cache.

feature: Manage synced plugins
detail: Synced plugins can be toggled in the Installed tab unless the org requires them; removal is done by turning the plugin off on claude.ai.

feature: Uninstall project-enabled plugin: disable for me or uninstall for everyone
detail: Prompt offers writing false to local settings or removing from shared project settings.

feature: Plugin details command shows always-on token cost
detail: A plugin details shell command reports tokens added to every session and per-component contributions.

feature: Not used recently section
detail: Installed tab groups self-installed plugins that were not used lately so users can prune context and startup cost.

feature: Plugin dependencies installed and enabled automatically
detail: Install and enable also act on declared dependencies at same scope; disable refuses if another enabled plugin needs it; auto-installed dependencies remain until a prune command.

feature: Manage plugins from shell: enable, disable, uninstall
detail: Shell commands mirror the panel with a scope flag; enable/disable act on the most specific listing scope, install/uninstall default to user.

feature: Plugin auto-update by marketplace
detail: Marketplaces with auto-update refresh after session start and update installed plugins; on for official and claude.ai marketplaces, off for community, third-party and local ones.

feature: Toggle marketplace auto-update
detail: Marketplaces tab menu turns auto-update on or off per marketplace.

feature: Update plugin now / update marketplace
detail: Update now per plugin, or Update marketplace to refresh listing and update its installed plugins; command-source or headersHelper plugins are updated individually; no update-all command.

feature: Manage marketplaces: list, update, remove
detail: Marketplaces tab and shell/session commands list, update or remove; removal uninstalls its plugins after confirmation.

feature: Plugin load stages: declared, fetched, loaded
detail: Plugins pass from settings declaration to on-disk fetch to loaded session; reload command applies changes made outside the panel.

feature: Background fetch of declared marketplaces
detail: Plugins load at start from cache without network; declared but missing marketplaces are cloned in background and plugins downloaded and reloaded.

feature: Plugin id origins: marketplace, inline, skills-dir, synced
detail: Each plugin id ends with its origin; inline (session flags/env/SDK), skills-dir (plugin folder under skills directories) and synced are reserved origin names.

feature: Skills-directory plugins
detail: A folder with a plugin manifest saved under user or project skills directory loads as a plugin, honoring defaultEnabled; project copy only loads from primary working directory root.

feature: Project plugin trust check and component limits
detail: Repo-shared plugins load only after workspace trust; their MCP servers need per-server approval, MCP bundles are skipped, and background monitors do not load.

feature: Managed settings can block skills-directory plugins
detail: Strict plugin-only customization or restrictive marketplace allowlists make admins skip skills-directory plugin folders silently; status command shows managed sources.

feature: Synced plugins sign-in requirements
detail: Terminal sync needs claude.ai login on v2.1.273+; skipped with token/API-key auth, disabled nonessential traffic, bare or safe mode, or setting sources excluding user.

feature: Turn off synced plugins
detail: Disable one synced plugin (saved as false in user settings), turn off all with syncClaudeAiPlugins false (moves to trash), or admin-required plugins cannot be disabled.

feature: Org-required synced plugins
detail: Plugins an org marks required load regardless and are labeled required by your org; disable is refused.

feature: Enabled plugins precedence across six sources
detail: enabledPlugins merges key by key from add-dir, user, project, local, flag and managed; managed true force-enables and false blocks.

feature: Add-dir settings need saved trust
detail: Plugins enabled in an added directory are skipped until workspace trust is saved there (v2.1.319+).

feature: Enabled in project but not installed
detail: Project-enabled plugins don't load until installed per clone; relative-path or seed-directory plugins can load without install.

feature: On-disk plugin layout and data directory
detail: Plugin files live under a plugins root (cache, data, marketplaces, mcpb, synced, trash); a persistent data dir survives updates and is deleted on last uninstall unless keep-data used.

feature: Component paths cannot escape plugin directory
detail: Paths outside the plugin root, escaping symlinks, and backslash paths on macOS/Linux are rejected.

feature: Previous plugin versions cleaned after 14 days
detail: Old version directories get an orphan marker and are removed 14 days later.

feature: Automatic Node dependency install for plugins
detail: Copied plugins get npm/Bun dependencies installed from lockfile only: registry packages, no scripts, no overrides, 60-second timeout; cannot be disabled.

feature: Plugin version computation and update detection
detail: Version comes from manifest, then marketplace entry, then source (commit SHA, archive digest, unknown); unchanged version means no update.

feature: Marketplace refresh before install
detail: name@marketplace installs refresh that marketplace first; bare-name session installs refresh only after a miss; falls back to cache with a not-refreshed notice.

feature: Auto-update timing and env switches
detail: After first message a random delay up to ten minutes precedes the pass; update/autoupdater/nonessential-traffic env vars disable it unless forced.

feature: Mid-session update path switching
detail: After an update hooks, MCP and LSP servers need reload to switch; monitors need a restart.

feature: Command-source plugins re-run
detail: Command-source plugins re-run the accepted command on install/update, once per session in background, and on missing version; changed output installs a new version and reloads.

feature: Plugin name conflict precedence
detail: Managed, session-only dir plugins, installed marketplace, skills-dir, then synced; shadowed plugins show not-loaded rows in Errors tab.

feature: Duplicate plugin names: only one set of hooks registers
detail: With same manifest name from two marketplaces only one copy's hooks and hooks module run; Errors tab names the holder (v2.1.296+).

feature: Disable session-only plugin via inline false
detail: Setting name@inline to false stops a flag-loaded plugin from shadowing others.

feature: Plugin manifest file (optional plugin.json)
detail: Optional manifest in the plugin's hidden config folder holds metadata, userConfig and inline component definitions; without it standard-layout components are auto-discovered.

feature: Manifest validation command
detail: A validate shell command checks a plugin dir, reporting passed, passed with warnings (strict flag makes warnings fail) or failed; also checks MCP entries (v2.1.281+).

feature: Manifest metadata fields
detail: Name (kebab-case, required), displayName, version, description, author, homepage, repository, license, keywords, metadata, schema URL.

feature: Reserved plugin names
detail: Validation errors on names that pass as Anthropic's own (claude-, anthropic- prefixes, official beside claude) and warns on whole-word use.

feature: Directory listing fields
detail: Icon, documentation, support, privacy policy and terms URLs are read by Anthropic's plugin directory on submission, ignored at load.

feature: defaultEnabled plugin flag
detail: Plugins can start disabled; marketplace entry value overrides; saved user choices persist across updates.

feature: Engines version constraint
detail: Manifest can require a Claude Code semver range (v2.1.323+); older versions reject the field.

feature: Plugin dependencies field
detail: Names plugins that must be enabled, as bare name, name@marketplace or object with version.

feature: Network hosts declaration
detail: Manifest lists hosts the plugin reaches (v2.1.328+); validate lists them but does not allow or block.

feature: Component path forms and rules
detail: Component keys take paths starting with ./ inside plugin root that must exist; escaping or missing paths error in Errors tab.

feature: Commands map with inline content and options
detail: Commands can be files, directories or a map with source or content plus description, argument hint, default model, allowed tools; run as /plugin:name.

feature: Inline and file-based hooks in plugin
detail: Hooks accept JSON files or inline event maps, merged with the default hooks file.

feature: Plugin MCP servers: json, bundle, URL or inline
detail: MCP servers via json file, .mcpb/.dxt bundle path or https URL, or inline map; later same-name entry replaces earlier.

feature: Plugin LSP servers config
detail: Language servers declared with command, extension-to-language map, args, transport, env, timeouts (request default 60s), restart-on-crash, max restarts, and diagnostics push into context.

feature: Plugin background monitors (experimental)
detail: Monitors run persistent background commands, started always or on first invocation of a named skill; shown in task panel; don't start with -p.

feature: Plugin themes, workflows, output styles, evals
detail: Plugins can ship themes, workflow scripts, output styles and eval cases; some under an experimental key whose shape may change.

feature: Plugin path replace vs add vs merge semantics
detail: Setting commands, agents, outputStyles, workflows, themes, monitors replaces the default folder; skills adds; hooks, MCP, LSP merge; a warning shows when a default folder is ignored.

feature: Plugin userConfig prompts
detail: Plugins declare options (string, number, boolean, directory, file) with title, description, required, default, fixed options picker (v2.1.271+), multiple, sensitive, min/max; prompted on enable and shown in config panel (v2.1.269+).

feature: Sensitive plugin options in secure storage
detail: Sensitive values are masked and stored in the platform credential store; others go to user settings; sensitive values are not substituted into skill or agent content.

feature: User config substitution and env export
detail: Saved values substitute into MCP, LSP, exec-form hooks and skill content, and export as plugin-option env vars to hooks; shell-form hooks, monitors and headersHelper reject them.

feature: Plugin channels
detail: Plugins can declare message channels (e.g. chat-app bridges) bound to an MCP server with their own config prompt.

feature: Plugin path variables
detail: Root, persistent data and project directory variables resolve in hooks, MCP, LSP and skill content; not present in Bash tool commands.

feature: Standard plugin layout and bin directory
detail: Defaults: skills, commands, agents, hooks, MCP, LSP, output styles, workflows, themes, monitors and bin (put on Bash PATH); claude.ai and Cowork refuse plugins with bin; a root CLAUDE.md is not loaded.

feature: Marketplace entry strict mode
detail: Strict (default) merges entry components with the manifest; non-strict plus entry components conflicts and fails to load; entry display and enabled fields override the manifest, manifest version wins.

feature: Marketplace file format
detail: A marketplace is a marketplace.json with name, owner and plugin entries, plus description, version, pluginRoot, forceRemoveDeletedPlugins, cross-marketplace dependency allowlist and renames map; one invalid entry doesn't fail the whole file.

feature: Reserved marketplace names
detail: Official, community, directory, impersonating, claudeai- prefixed, and internal names (inline, builtin, skills-dir, synced) cannot be used by third-party marketplaces; imitation names stop loading and removal uninstalls their plugins.

feature: Marketplace plugin entry fields
detail: Entries carry name, source, description, version, category, tags, strict, relevance signals, dependencies, engines, defaultEnabled, displayName, metadata and archive-download headers.

feature: Relevance signals for plugin suggestions
detail: Entries can declare relevance topic and signals that tell Claude Code when to suggest the plugin to users.

feature: Plugin source types
detail: Plugins can come from a relative path, GitHub repo, git URL, git subdirectory (sparse checkout), npm package, zip archive with sha256 pin, or a command that prints a directory.

feature: Pin plugin to ref or commit SHA
detail: GitHub, URL and git-subdir sources accept a branch/tag ref and a 40-char SHA, which wins when both are set.

feature: Marketplace submodules fetched only when needed
detail: Clones fetch only submodules holding plugin files (v2.1.295+); sparse checkout paths skip submodules.

feature: npm plugin source safeguards
detail: npm sources fetch without running install scripts and refuse git, file, alias, forge tarball and plain-http links; registry must be https unless the user's default.

feature: Archive plugin source
detail: HTTPS zip with optional sha256 check; loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata hosts are refused.

feature: Command plugin source: copy and link modes
detail: A tool-provided command prints a plugin directory; copy mode caches it (256 MiB, 20,000 entries cap), link mode loads in place; not on Windows for link; admins can disable command sources.

feature: Marketplace sources and policy lists
detail: Marketplace source types url, github, git, file, directory, settings (inline) are usable in extraKnownMarketplaces; admins allow or block via strictKnownMarketplaces/blockedMarketplaces with host and path regex patterns and owner wildcards.

feature: Pin marketplace to commit SHA
detail: A github or git marketplace source can pin ref to a full SHA (v2.1.324+) so refreshes never move off a reviewed commit; refused for reserved names.

feature: Authenticated marketplace and archive downloads
detail: Marketplace URLs and archive entries support static headers or a headersHelper command for short-lived credentials (v2.1.238+).

feature: Marketplace validation messages and Claude Desktop warnings
detail: Validate reports errors and warnings per field and flags names that Claude Desktop rejects (reserved, character set, max 128 chars).

feature: Plugin details: token cost per plugin
detail: A plugin details shell command lists component inventory and projected always-on and on-invoke tokens per skill, agent and command; hooks and MCP schemas not counted.

feature: Reduce plugin always-on token cost
detail: Always-on counts names, descriptions and when_to_use; authors shorten descriptions or split plugins; Context cost line is highlighted at 2,000 tokens or more for official plugins.

feature: Not used recently flag (14 days and 10 sessions)
detail: Installed tab moves unused user-installed marketplace plugins under a header after 14 days and 10 sessions, with last-used time; excluded for dir, managed, seed, theme/style/monitor/workflow plugins.

feature: /skill-doctor report
detail: Shows each skill's cost and usage and flags never-invoked skills, including plugin skills; opens in the plugin manager Stats tab.

feature: /doctor flags unused skills, MCP servers and plugins
detail: Checkup lists user-installed items and recommends disabling unused ones.

feature: /usage attributes usage to skills, subagents, plugins, MCP
detail: Breakdown shows share of total usage per skill, subagent, plugin and MCP server.

feature: Plugin OpenTelemetry events for fleets
detail: Admins can export plugin_installed, plugin_loaded, skill_activated, hook_plugin_metrics events and plugin-tagged cost counters to their backend.

feature: Third-party plugin names redacted in telemetry
detail: Non-official plugin names are redacted or omitted unless an OTEL tool-details env var is set to 1; plugin id hash still counts distinct plugins.

feature: Analytics API plugin usage endpoint
detail: Enterprise admins query per-plugin per-day install and invocation counts across Claude Code and Cowork grouped by user, RBAC group or product, using a read:analytics API key.

feature: Mods: plugins that run code inside Claude Code
detail: A mod is a plugin with a hooks module running with the installing user's permissions, unsandboxed; on by default from v2.1.286.

feature: Admin: block user-installed mods (allowManagedModsOnly)
detail: Managed option on the built-in guard stops every user-brought mod (plugin, plugin-dir or Claude-written) from running hooks while org mods, settings hooks, status lines and /goal keep working.

feature: Built-in sec-default guard mod
detail: A built-in guard loads ahead of user mods on managed machines or Team/Enterprise logins; it stops user mods rewriting the system prompt, managed instructions, settings reads and managed MCP tool lists; cannot be disabled.

feature: Guard keeps deny rules, ask rules and PreToolUse blocks in force
detail: With the guard loaded, a user mod's approval cannot override deny rules, ask prompts or blocked PreToolUse hooks unless allowModsToOverrideDenyRules is set.

feature: Mod calls can bypass permission checks
detail: Mod file, process and tool/MCP calls can skip permission rules and hooks; admins limit with no-user-mods policy or a policy mod.

feature: Admin: mod policy options table
detail: Policy choices range from no installed mods, only org mods, marketplace-allowlisted mods, to any mod with an org policy mod; disableAllHooks, allowManagedHooksOnly, disableSideloadFlags widen or narrow scope.

feature: disableSideloadFlags
detail: Managed setting rejects plugin-dir and plugin-url flags at startup, blocks mods Claude writes in-session, and also rejects agents and MCP-config flags.

feature: Safe mode turns off installed mods
detail: Starting with a safe-mode flag runs without installed mods, org mods included, to isolate problems.

feature: Org-owned mods with prepend and append ordering
detail: Admins install org mods via managed enabledPlugins and marketplaces (remote v2.1.324+ or admin-owned local dir) and order them with prependPlugins/appendPlugins relative to user mods.

feature: Review what a mod can do via validate
detail: Validate prints hooks and calls lines (file, process, http, env, settings, MCP, model, prompt, session calls) so admins can vet a mod before approving.

feature: Policy mod that vets other mods
detail: An org policy mod receives plugin.register for each mod, can refuse or strip hooks, and can audit tool and file-write calls; fails open unless a catch handler is added.

feature: Worker crash unloads mods for session
detail: If the hooks worker crashes three times all non-built-in mods unload until reload or new session.

feature: Hooks passed over where guard loads
detail: On managed machines user-mod hooks on classic hook events, prompt composition, skill text, attribution, telemetry log, compaction and settings read never run, noted in plugin details (v2.1.299+).

feature: Network policy covers mod http fetch
detail: Org policy disallowing WebFetch also blocks mod fetches; disabling the tool alone does not; nonessential-traffic variable only stops built-in mods and credentialed requests.

feature: Ask Claude to write a mod
detail: Describe a mod in an interactive session (or run /plugin-authoring) and Claude writes it into a per-session dev-mods folder; hot reload requires approval in default/acceptEdits modes and is automatic in auto/bypass.

feature: Mod hot-reload approval prompt
detail: First saved mod file asks to turn on hot reloading for the session (answer persists on resume) or Not now; mods load at turn end and reload when a turn changes them.

feature: Mods Claude writes are session-scoped
detail: Claude-written mods load only in their session and the folder is deleted after cleanupPeriodDays; copy elsewhere and load with plugin-dir to keep.

feature: Cases where Claude-written mods cannot load
detail: No loading in dontAsk mode, print mode in default/acceptEdits, untrusted workspaces, safe or bare mode, disableAllHooks, or org policy blocks.

feature: Mod authoring tutorial: hooks module and manifest
detail: A mod is a plugin whose hooks.json lists a modules JS/TS file exporting register(on); no build step; example adds a spinner count and /tally command.

feature: Mod hot reload while session runs
detail: A plugin-dir mod reloads automatically when its files change, rerunning register and resetting in-memory state.

feature: Generated TypeScript types for mods
detail: Interactive plugin-dir or Claude-written mods get .d.ts files for events, API, built-in tools and connected MCP tools plus a tsconfig.

feature: Mod static analysis rules
detail: Validation requires literal event names, full-form $ API calls, relative imports only, ES modules and no dynamic import or shadowed on.

feature: Plugin test command
detail: A plugin test shell command runs mod tests offline with a testing module that fires events and stubs answers.

feature: Share a mod
detail: Mods ship like plugins: directory or zip, team marketplace, org managed settings, public repo or submission to Anthropic's directory.

feature: Mods API: add slash commands
detail: A mod registers a command (name, description, argument hint, optional immediate flag) and answers it with text shown in the transcript; names of built-in commands are refused.

feature: Mod command text hidden from Claude
detail: A command can print display-only text that Claude does not read (v2.1.326+).

feature: Mods API: add tools for Claude
detail: A mod registers a tool with description and JSON schema, exposed as an mcp__plugin__name tool; optional isDeferred false to load upfront rather than via MCP tool search (v2.1.293+).

feature: Mods API: call a model (complete and fork)
detail: complete sends a standalone prompt to a chosen model; fork sends the current conversation plus a prompt with session model and context; both bill to the user's plan, key or cloud provider.

feature: Mod prompt caching breakpoints
detail: Prompt and system accept block arrays with cache flags (v2.1.292+); entries last five minutes by default (one hour via setting), up to four breakpoints; usage shows cache read/write tokens.

feature: Mods API: timers
detail: Mods schedule recurring or one-shot work with clock every/after/now; callbacks run between turns and errors go to the debug log.

feature: Mod UI feedback: status, toast, log, notify
detail: Mods show a persistent line under the prompt, a toast, a dim transcript line Claude doesn't read, or a terminal notification honoring the user's preferred notification channel.

feature: Mod notify result reasons
detail: Terminal notify resolves sent with channel or not sent with reason: disabled, no-channel, no-surface (print mode, SDK, desktop, VS Code, cloud) or refused.

feature: User Notification hooks run for mod notifications
detail: A mod notification triggers user Notification hooks with type plugin_notification even when notifications are disabled.

feature: Mod-started turns via prompt submit
detail: A background job can submit a prompt that starts a turn, attributed to the mod or sent as the user's own words; waits for idle.

feature: Interrupt handling for mod work
detail: After the user presses Esc/Stop, mod prompts, commands, subagent spawns, background tool calls are refused or dropped until next input; mods retry from a turn-complete hook (v2.1.304+).

feature: Mod calls limited in print and SDK runs
detail: In -p and Agent SDK runs mod prompts are refused at max-turns, budget limit, ended input or after interrupt; submitting every turn would never exit without a limit.

feature: Cross-session messages from mods
detail: Mods send plain-text messages to another session, subagent or agent-team teammate and observe send/receive events, consuming inbound messages before Claude reads them.

feature: Mods API: files, processes, network
detail: Mods read/write files, run or stream programs without shell (30s default timeout), fetch HTTP (five redirects, header stripping across origins), keep a JSON store, use env, settings read, MCP calls and compile WASM up to 64 MiB (v2.1.326+); no Node globals.

feature: Mod settings read by source or key
detail: Settings read returns merged settings, one source (user, project, local, flag, policy) or one top-level key (v2.1.304+).

feature: Every mod API call is a hookable event
detail: Calls like fs.read are events that earlier mods can observe, rewrite or refuse, which is how orgs restrict mods.

feature: Mod hooks: observe, rewrite or answer events
detail: Hooks form a middleware chain around events (tool call, prompt, turn, model request, session); a hook can pass through, change a copy of the event or short-circuit with its own result.

feature: Mod hook matchers and wildcards
detail: Hooks filter by value, array or regex on event fields; wildcards like classic.* and *; plugin matcher needed to hook other mods' controls (v2.1.323+).

feature: Mod tool.call hook: guard, change, retry or answer tool calls
detail: A hook can deny a call, change arguments, retry, return its own result, or withhold a result after it ran; managed PreToolUse hooks run first.

feature: Mod asks user before a tool call (ask dialog)
detail: A hook can pause a tool call and show a question dialog with numbered options, a type-your-own row and Chat about this; wait time doesn't count against the hook time limit; rejects in print mode.

feature: Mod tool.check permission decisions
detail: A hook can allow, ask or deny before the permission prompt, after PreToolUse hooks; in plan mode it can only tighten non-read-only decisions; read-only flag available (v2.1.304+).

feature: Mod prompt.submit: rewrite, add context or drop prompts
detail: Hooks can edit prompt text, add Claude-only context, or drop the prompt with a reason shown to the user.

feature: Mod turn events: start, step, complete
detail: Hooks observe turns and each model request (token and cache usage, reroute to another model, answer without calling) and can add a line under the answer; server-side tool uses visible (v2.1.290+).

feature: Mod settings.read hook
detail: Hooks can change or refuse settings reads by mods or Claude Code's own merge across plugin, user, project, local, flag and policy layers (v2.1.304+).

feature: Mod access to settings hook events
detail: Settings hook events (Stop, PostToolUse, etc.) are exposed as classic.* events but don't run for user mods on managed machines.

feature: Mod execution order
detail: Guard and org prepend mods run first, then user mods, org append mods, then other built-ins; managed PreToolUse hooks run before the first mod and other settings hooks after the last.

feature: Mod hook failure handling and catch handlers
detail: A failing hook is skipped (before next) or its result stands (after next); catch handlers let guard hooks fail closed with deny/drop/refuse.

feature: Mod UI element: Text
detail: Mods draw styled text (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, dim, inverse, colors).

feature: Mod UI element: Markdown
detail: Renders formatted Markdown the way Claude replies are formatted.

feature: Mod UI element: Link
detail: Draws a label and URL; whether click opens depends on terminal.

feature: Mod UI element: Code with syntax colors and diffs
detail: Shows source in the user's theme colors with optional line numbers, or unified diffs with word-level shading; plain text in VS Code.

feature: Mod UI element: Box layout
detail: Row/column layouts with gap, padding and borders.

feature: Mod UI controls: Button, Input, Select
detail: Buttons (hotkey, plain, dim), single or multi-line text inputs (rows v2.1.301+; one line in VS Code) and dropdown selects; Tab moves focus.

feature: Mod UI element: Raster
detail: Grid of colored character cells for heat maps or sparklines.

feature: Mod UI element: Svg
detail: Draws an SVG in Desktop app and VS Code; empty in terminal.

feature: Mod UI element: Image and Client
detail: Image draws PNG/raw pixels in kitty 0.28+, Ghostty, iTerm2 3.5+ (v2.1.305+) and tmux with prerequisites; otherwise alt text; Client lets a second file draw animation and pointer input.

feature: Mod pane and band placement
detail: Panes open as a sidebar beside the transcript in wide fullscreen terminals or a framed region above the prompt; mods can also edit the spinner, status line, toast, log and question dialog.

feature: Gallery mod with /gallery sample command
detail: Tutorial builds a gallery mod whose /gallery command opens a pane drawing sample elements; hot reload on save.

feature: Image draw env override for terminals
detail: An env var forces terminal image drawing for kitty-protocol terminals, except in screen, old tmux, popups or passthrough off.

feature: Mod pane: sidebar or framed region
detail: A mod can open a pane beside the transcript in a wide fullscreen terminal, or a framed region above the prompt in a narrow one; several panes get tabs titled by name.

feature: Mod band above the prompt
detail: A strip directly above the prompt input where each mod gets its own row, stacked in mod run order.

feature: Mod redraw of built-in render sites
detail: Mods can restyle or replace messages, tool call rows/results/groups, command output, the question dialog, spinner, tool progress, turn duration, info notices, mode labels, prompt hint and agent rows.

feature: Mod cannot change permission prompt
detail: The permission prompt is not a render site, so mods cannot alter what it shows; the AskUserQuestion dialog can be changed.

feature: Mod pane options: title, focus, closeOnEscape, holdToasts, rows, columns
detail: Opening a pane accepts a tab title, keyboard focus request, Esc-to-close, toast holding, requested height above the prompt and width beside the transcript (max 45% of terminal).

feature: Pane width remembered after user resize
detail: Once a user resizes a side pane, later panes open at that width, capped at 45% of the terminal.

feature: Mod toasts held while a dialog pane is open
detail: A pane can hold toasts (including Claude Code's own short-lived notifications) while it is showing, releasing them afterwards.

feature: Mod pane waits for a wide terminal
detail: Self-opened panes appear only at 144 columns or wider (110 after the user opened it once); user-triggered panes appear at any width.

feature: Mods in the VS Code chat panel
detail: Mod drawing appears in the VS Code chat panel from extension 2.1.299 (2.1.304 without feature flags); panes dock beside the conversation at 800px or wider, otherwise show inline with 12 rows.

feature: VS Code panel labels mod-drawn content
detail: The panel frames mod output and labels it with the plugin name such as From the X plugin or Edited by the X plugin.

feature: VS Code panel: no hotkeys, limited focus, text limits
detail: Buttons are click/Enter only; pane focus is granted only when panel focused, Claude idle and prompt empty; status lines cut at 200 chars/two rows, toasts at 500.

feature: Mod toasts and status lines stack above prompt (VS Code)
detail: Toasts and per-mod status lines share one stack above the prompt box, hidden while a permission request or dialog shows.

feature: Mod transcript row via place
detail: A mod can add a row to the transcript after the latest message (terminal, v2.1.314+); it disappears on conversation end, rewind, or compaction outside fullscreen, and Claude does not see it.

feature: Mod backdrop behind the conversation
detail: On the Desktop and mobile app, a mod can set a scene backdrop and color scheme override, removable with a clear call; the terminal draws none (v2.1.319+).

feature: One theme per session for mods
detail: Setting a theme replaces any earlier mod's backdrop and colors; clearing removes them regardless of which mod set them.

feature: Desktop Code tab colors via a mod
detail: Ask Claude to write a colors mod (e.g. cream in light, dark brown in dark) or write one with makeColors anchors; requires Claude Code v2.1.324+ in the Code tab; terminal keeps its colors.

feature: Desktop colors mod needs Claude account
detail: With a third-party provider on Desktop v5.11492.5 or earlier the Code tab keeps its own colors.

feature: Remove mod colors in Desktop settings
detail: Turn off the mod, start a new local session, then Settings > search code appearance > Remove colors if colors persist.

feature: Mod elements: Box, Text, Button, Link, Code, Markdown
detail: Core drawing elements available everywhere; Input and Select in terminal/Desktop/VS Code; Svg in Desktop/VS Code; Client in terminal/Desktop; Raster and Image terminal only.

feature: Link rules in Desktop and VS Code
detail: Links render only for https or localhost http URLs without @ and in normalized spelling; otherwise shown as plain text.

feature: Raster grid element and blit animation
detail: Terminal-only element for heat maps, sparklines and game boards drawn from packed 24-bit color cells, repainted by a blit call without re-rendering.

feature: Mod controls: Button, Input, Select callbacks
detail: Buttons take press handlers, inputs take submit/input handlers, selects take a choice handler; controls need keys so tests and other mods can identify them.

feature: Other mods can observe or alter control events
detail: Press, input and select events are fired to other mods before the callback runs, letting them see or change typed text or block the callback.

feature: Pane keyboard focus: Ctrl+X Tab, click, focus request
detail: A pane takes focus when opened with a focus request, via Ctrl+X then Tab, or by clicking in fullscreen rendering; focus is only granted when the prompt is empty.

feature: Mod pane key bindings
detail: Tab, arrows, Enter, hotkeys, Page Up/Down, Home/End scroll or navigate; Ctrl+X plus arrow resizes the pane; Ctrl+X then X closes it; Esc returns focus to prompt.

feature: Button hotkeys and autoFocus
detail: A button can have a one-digit or lowercase-letter hotkey and an autoFocus prop; hotkey display differs between terminal, Desktop (small key) and VS Code (none).

feature: Collapse the mod band to one row
detail: Click [-] in fullscreen or press Ctrl+X then Ctrl+A (rebindable via abovePrompt:toggle) to collapse; stays collapsed until user expands, reset on next start.

feature: Mod state: module variable, $.state, $.store
detail: Values last until reload, until session end or /clear /resume /branch, or persistently in a per-plugin JSON store under ~/.claude/plugins/store until cleanupPeriodDays idle.

feature: $.state reset by /clear, /resume, /branch
detail: These commands reset reactive mod state to defaults; mods should reload saved values on the SessionStart hook for clear, resume and fork.

feature: Mod redraw: invalidate, timers, throttling
detail: Mods redraw on prop or width change, on explicit invalidate, or on a clock timer; redraws are throttled per site and coalesced.

feature: Shared mod store across sessions
detail: All sessions on a machine share one store; get-then-set is not atomic so mods should use per-item keys.

feature: Mods: plugins that change Claude Code behavior and UI
detail: A mod is a plugin of JS/TS event handlers that can draw panes/bands, restyle built-in UI, intercept tool calls and requests, add /commands and share data between hooks.

feature: Install or update a mod via marketplace
detail: Install with /plugin install name@marketplace or claude plugin install; run /reload-plugins after installing from a shell during an open session.

feature: Sample mods from Anthropic
detail: token-weather draws a context-window forecast above the prompt, blast-radius holds risky shell commands with proceed/cancel buttons, replay-theater adds /replay to step through last turn's edits; shared unsupported.

feature: Mods run with full user permissions and are not sandboxed
detail: A mod can read/write files, run processes, read env vars and settings, see all prompts and tool calls, rewrite them, submit prompts, approve tool calls, and spend plan usage; sandboxing does not cover its processes.

feature: Built-in guard stops user mods overriding managed rules
detail: cc-plugin-sec-default by default prevents user mods from approving tool calls that deny/ask rules or PreToolUse hooks would stop.

feature: Preview a mod with claude plugin validate
detail: Lists the events a mod handles and the calls it makes without running it, to review before installing.

feature: Turn mods off: per mod, safe mode, disableAllHooks
detail: Disable a plugin in /plugin, run with --safe-mode for one session, or set disableAllHooks true in settings to stop all installed mods and settings hooks; managed policy still runs.

feature: Mods require Claude Code v2.1.287 (Desktop v2.1.286)
detail: Mods are on by default from those versions; the env var CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS is ignored.

feature: /plugin shows mods loaded count
detail: A dim line under the /plugin tabs lists the number and names of active mods; built-in mods are listed under Built-in on the Installed tab.

feature: Where mods run (terminal, Desktop, VS Code, SDK, remote, cloud)
detail: Mods run in terminal, Desktop Code tab (not WSL or SSH), VS Code panel, claude -p/Agent SDK (no drawing), Remote Control sessions on your machine, and cloud sessions for plugins that carry over.

feature: Admin control of mods via managed settings
detail: Administrators decide whether mods run and which ones (allowManagedModsOnly) via managed settings, with a default guard and review process.

feature: Built-in mod: /diff pane
detail: cc-plugin-diff takes over /diff and draws its pane in interactive terminal sessions; can be disabled and the built-in command then answers.

feature: Built-in: AGENTS.md loaded as project instructions
detail: cc-plugin-agents-md loads AGENTS.md in every session that can read it; can be disabled or instruction-file choice configured.

feature: Built-in: plugin-authoring skill
detail: cc-plugin-plugin-authoring gives Claude a skill for writing mods unless Anthropic turned installed mods off remotely.

feature: Built-in telemetry mod
detail: cc-plugin-telemetry sends analytics records for Claude Code; disable in /plugin or via DISABLE_TELEMETRY.

feature: You should know suggestions (built-in mod)
detail: A side agent shows a note above the prompt when it spots something you may have missed; off until turned on.

feature: Auto charts from MCP results (easel mod)
detail: cc-plugin-easel gives Claude a chart-drawing tool and automatically charts time-series MCP results such as Prometheus ranges; toggle Auto charts in /config; needs claude.ai subscription, v2.1.321+ (Team/Enterprise 2.1.326+), macOS or Linux outside WSL.

feature: Mod file layout: plugin.json, hooks.json, hooks module
detail: A mod needs a manifest, a hooks.json naming one module file (.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx/.ts/.mts/.cts/.tsx), optional types/index.d.ts and *.test.ts files.

feature: Mod userConfig options
detail: The register function receives userConfig values declared in the manifest, with defaults filled in; values stored via pluginConfigs in user or managed settings.

feature: Mod tool events: call, check, judge, run, describe
detail: Mods can deny or answer tool calls, return allow/ask/deny decisions, intercept auto mode's classifier (v2.1.326+), and rewrite tool descriptions or defer them behind tool search.

feature: Mod prompt events: submit, autocomplete, compose, context, mention
detail: Mods can rewrite or drop prompts, add autocomplete suggestions, edit system prompt sections, add context blocks, redirect @-mentioned files and rewrite skill text or commit attribution.

feature: Mod commands and /config row events
detail: Mods can run or describe slash commands, add/rename /config rows, veto or alter a config change and filter merged settings reads.

feature: Mod turn events: start, step, complete
detail: Mods follow each answer, can pick the model or effort of each request, and show a line under the answer.

feature: Mod session events
detail: Hooks for start, end, compact (can skip), message send/receive between sessions, row append, app attach/detach, per-turn usage measure and user stop (v2.1.326+).

feature: Mod subagent events: offer and spawn
detail: Mods can withhold a subagent type, choose the model of a starting subagent or agent-team teammate, or refuse a resumed run (v2.1.299+).

feature: Mod interface events
detail: Events for render, element table, press/input/select, focus/scroll, pane close, Client messages and Client faults.

feature: Mods can refuse other mods at load
detail: A plugin.register hook can refuse a plugin or only its hooks module based on the events, calls and env vars it uses.

feature: Telemetry hooks need collector filter
detail: Installed mods hooking telemetry events must filter to the collector or fail validation; records are sent only when Claude Code or a built-in mod logs.

feature: Settings hook events exposed to mods as classic.*
detail: Each settings hook event (e.g. Stop, PostToolUse) is available to mods as classic.<Event> with the stdin JSON.

feature: Mods API namespaces
detail: ui, theme, command, tool, agent, model (complete/fork/classify), prompt, turn, session (usage, compact, send), config, settings, env, fs, store, state, clock, http, process, mcp, wasm, audio, telemetry.

feature: Mods can read context and plan rate-limit usage
detail: session usage returns context tokens/window/percent, rate limits with percent used and reset time, and cost.

feature: Render sites and which apps draw them
detail: Pane, AbovePrompt, Placed, Backdrop, messages, tool rows, command output, question dialog, spinner, turn duration, info notice, session mode, prompt hint and agent rows, each marked for terminal, Desktop, VS Code or mobile.

feature: Button variants, roles, actions and digit hotkeys
detail: Buttons support primary/secondary variants, dismiss role, binding to a Claude Code keybinding action, rich children (v2.1.295+) and digit hotkeys fired from an empty prompt.

feature: Box border styles and spacing steps
detail: Ten border styles (single, double, round, bold, classic, arrow, dashed, quote and mixed) and xs-xl spacing steps (v2.1.299+).

feature: Text typography props
detail: size, weight, mono and tabular are honored by Desktop only; terminal and VS Code ignore size/mono/tabular and draw semibold/bold as bold; bold is deprecated in favor of weight.

feature: Mod execution and size limits
detail: Hooks time out at 10s (50ms for prompt.edit), process runs 30s default/10min max, http bodies 4MiB, store 4MiB, trees up to 20,000 elements, toasts 4s default, 500 placed rows per mod.

feature: Plugin env vars: CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS and DIR_WATCH
detail: Load plugin directories without a flag and control reload-on-save for mods.

feature: Managed mod settings: prependPlugins, appendPlugins
detail: Admins list plugin ids that run before or after user-installed mods in a set order.

feature: allowManagedModsOnly and allowModsToOverrideDenyRules
detail: Admin options on the built-in guard: restrict hooks to organization mods, or let user mods approve calls past deny rules.

feature: allowManagedHooksOnly, disableAllHooks, disableSideloadFlags
detail: Managed settings that block non-organization hooks and mods, disable all plugin hooks, or reject --plugin-dir and --plugin-url at startup.

feature: claude plugin validate command
detail: Checks a plugin's manifest and hooks module, reports events and calls; --strict turns warnings into errors, --json gives machine output.

feature: claude plugin test command
detail: Runs *.test.ts and *.test.tsx files in a plugin directory and exits 1 on failure; each test has a 5 second default timeout.

feature: claude --plugin-dir flag and /reload-plugins
detail: Load a plugin directory for one session with reload on save, repeatable, and reload plugins on demand.

feature: Automated mod tests with claude plugin test
detail: Runs *.test.ts files that load a mod, fire events and check hook results with no session, sign-in or network; exit status 1 on failure for CI.

feature: Test kit stubs and mocks
detail: The claude-code/testing kit offers stubs for mods API calls and ready mocks for clock, store, env and appended session rows (mock.session needs v2.1.293+).

feature: Test a drawing with ui.mount
detail: A test can draw a render site for terminal or desktop, press buttons, type into inputs, pick select values, find elements and unmount, to check drawings on several apps.

feature: Test a policy mod with tier and inline plugins
detail: Tests can load a mod as prepend/append/builtin and add inline mods to confirm an organization policy mod refuses or admits them.

feature: Debug log for mods: claude --debug / --debug-file
detail: Writes a log of every module loaded or refused and every failed hook; a loaded mod line lists the events it handles; mods can write their own lines via a log call.

feature: Mod problems shown as transcript or stderr lines
detail: Load failures, skipped hooks and refusals appear as a dim transcript line in hot-reload sessions, in the debug log for marketplace mods, or on stderr in claude -p.

feature: Check whether mods can load via claude plugin test
detail: Running it in a non-mod directory reports whether mods are enabled, blocked by disableAllHooks or policy, or turned off remotely by Anthropic.

feature: Remote rollout switch can turn installed mods off
detail: Anthropic can disable installed mods remotely, shown by a specific message; a stale saved switch value is refreshed by starting claude once.

feature: Mod refusal reasons: managed-only, --bare, name clash
detail: Mods are refused under disableAllHooks, allowManagedHooksOnly, --bare mode, allowManagedModsOnly, or when another plugin of the same name loads first.

feature: Guard blocks mods from lifting deny rules
detail: A mod's tool-check approval of a call that a deny rule refuses is ignored with a message; if rules cannot be checked the call is refused.

feature: Folder trust prompt required before mods load
detail: Mods do not load in a directory you opened for the first time until you accept the trust prompt in an interactive session.

feature: --safe-mode loads no installed plugins
detail: Starting with --safe-mode prevents every installed plugin from loading.

feature: Hot reloading prompt for Claude-written mods
detail: Claude asks whether to enable hot reloading for mods it writes; if the question times out unanswered three times it stays off, and the mod can be copied out and loaded with --plugin-dir.

feature: Mods crash isolation and automatic unloading
detail: Installed mods share one worker; a mod that crashes or blocks it is unloaded, and after three untraceable crashes all non-built-in mods are turned off for the session until /reload-plugins.

feature: Auto mode denies calls changed by hooks after review
detail: If a mod or PreToolUse hook changes a tool call's input after the auto-mode classifier reviewed it, the call is denied and Claude retries it as recorded.

feature: Stopped toast after interrupting a turn
detail: After Esc interrupts a turn, mod-initiated work is blocked and a toast says stopped, type a message to continue; some work resumes after your next message.

feature: Mod toast behavior and limits
detail: Toasts can be held by a pane, replaced by newer ones in the classic renderer, show under the prompt there, and fullscreen draws at most three at once.

feature: Reload failure keeps previous mod version loaded
detail: If a changed mod fails to reload the last working version keeps running until all plugins reload; /plugin shows whether a version is active.

feature: Plugin policy delivery: server-managed, MDM, managed file
detail: Plugin keys reach machines via claude.ai admin console (Owner role), macOS plist/Windows registry MDM, or managed-settings.json plus a managed-settings.d drop-in directory; the first source delivering a key wins unless managedSourcesBehavior is merge.

feature: Force-install plugins via extraKnownMarketplaces and enabledPlugins
detail: Admins register an organization marketplace and force-enable plugins on every machine; users cannot disable them, and a false value blocks and hides a plugin at all scopes.

feature: Require plugins per repository
detail: A repo .claude/settings.json can register marketplaces (only in trusted folders) and enable plugins, but contributors still run plugin install --scope project.

feature: Plugin rollout by surface and CI sync install
detail: Terminal, -p/CI and cloud sessions apply plugin keys differently; CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL=1 makes headless runs wait for installs.

feature: Seed directory for containers and CI
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR points to a pre-built read-only plugin cache with no cloning; multiple seeds separated by colon; auto-update is forced off and plugins still need enabling.

feature: Marketplace allowlist strictKnownMarketplaces
detail: Restricts marketplace sources by github repo (with owner wildcard), git url, url, file, directory, hostPattern, pathPattern or skills-dir; empty list locks out everything including the official marketplace.

feature: Marketplace blocklist blockedMarketplaces
detail: Blocks sources checked before the allowlist, with canonicalized git URLs and case-insensitive owner wildcards.

feature: syncClaudeAiPlugins toggle
detail: Setting false stops Claude Code downloading plugins synced from users' claude.ai accounts (v2.1.273+); a single synced plugin can be disabled via enabledPlugins.

feature: disableSideloadFlags
detail: Rejects --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, SDK plugins option, CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS folders and non-SDK --mcp-config at startup.

feature: disableCommandPluginSources
detail: Blocks plugins whose directory is produced by running a command; defaults to the allowManagedHooksOnly value.

feature: strictPluginOnlyCustomization
detail: Blocks skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from user and project sources (all four or a chosen subset); also stops skills-directory plugins.

feature: pluginTrustMessage and pluginSuggestionMarketplaces
detail: Admins can append text to the /plugin trust warning and list marketplaces whose plugins may be suggested.

feature: allowedChannelPlugins
detail: Replaces the default list of plugins allowed to push channel messages; requires channelsEnabled true.

feature: Disable auto-registering the official marketplace
detail: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_OFFICIAL_MARKETPLACE_AUTOINSTALL=1 stops interactive sessions from auto-registering claude-plugins-official.

feature: Fleet plugin auto-update policy
detail: Set autoUpdate per managed marketplace (users' toggle then refused), disable all with DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER, or keep plugin updates with FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS.

feature: Release channels per user group
detail: Stable and early-access marketplaces can be assigned per group via endpoint-managed settings, Claude apps gateway policies, or Enterprise per-group configuration.

feature: Plugin install and load OpenTelemetry events
detail: claude_code.plugin_installed and plugin_loaded events record plugin activity; third-party names are redacted unless OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1.

feature: Plugin analytics API
detail: GET /v1/organizations/analytics/plugins returns per-plugin per-day install and invocation counts across Claude Code and Cowork, groupable by user or RBAC group.

feature: claude.ai Organization settings > Plugins & skills
detail: Admin page that turns plugins on for members' claude.ai accounts; these reach Claude Code as synced plugins and do not set managed-settings keys.

feature: Managed policy troubleshooting
detail: Invalid managed-settings JSON stops startup; /status shows whether managed settings loaded; plugins a user disabled can still load when a managed entry force-enables them.

feature: Claude Code plugins bundle skills, agents, hooks, mods and MCP servers
detail: A plugin is one directory with a manifest that Claude Code installs as a unit; skills run as /plugin:skill commands, agents are delegable subagents, hooks run on lifecycle events.

feature: /plugin Discover tab and official marketplace
detail: Run /plugin in a terminal to browse and install plugins from your marketplaces; Anthropic's official marketplace is added automatically on first interactive start unless policy blocks it.

feature: Plugin marketplaces and tiers
detail: A marketplace is a catalog repo with marketplace.json; names fall into official, community (Anthropic-sourced) and third-party tiers; Claude Marketplace website is separate.

feature: Plugin install scopes: user, project, local
detail: Choose who a plugin is enabled for: you everywhere, everyone on a repository via committed settings, or you in one repository; terminal, desktop local sessions and VS Code share settings.

feature: Cloud sessions do not load local plugins
detail: A cloud session including claude.ai/code does not load plugins from local settings.

feature: Plugin context cost shown before install
detail: Official marketplace plugins show a Context cost estimate; enabled plugin skill names and descriptions count toward every turn's context and usage.

feature: Installed tab: Not used recently, disable without uninstall
detail: The Installed tab groups plugins not used recently; claude plugin disable or /plugin turns one off without uninstalling.

feature: Plugins on claude.ai and Cowork use same format
