detail: The same plugin format installs on claude.ai and Cowork where a different set of components loads.

feature: Share a plugin without a marketplace
detail: Send a folder or zip; recipients load it with --plugin-dir for one session, --plugin-url with a release zip, or by placing it under ~/.claude/skills/ for every session.

feature: Publish plugin through own marketplace
detail: Adding a .claude-plugin/marketplace.json to a git repo publishes it with no submission; private repos make the marketplace private; users add it with claude plugin marketplace add and install name@marketplace.

feature: Install and add marketplace in one command
detail: Use /plugin install name --marketplace org/repo (v2.1.275+) or claude plugin install name --marketplace org/repo from the shell (v2.1.292+).

feature: Plugin update on request and auto-update
detail: claude plugin update refreshes the marketplace and installs a changed version; auto-update is off by default for third-party marketplaces and runs in the background after start when on.

feature: Submit a plugin to Anthropic's directory
detail: Developer portal at claude.ai/directory/manage reaches claude.ai, Cowork and Claude Code via account sync; needs a paid plan (Pro, Max, Ultra, or Team/Enterprise Owner, with Directory permission via custom role on Enterprise).

feature: Plugins synced from claude.ai load as name@synced
detail: A plugin a person installs from the directory on claude.ai appears in Claude Code with the @synced suffix.

feature: Pre-release checks: validate --strict, plugin eval, tag
detail: claude plugin validate --strict fails on warnings, claude plugin eval runs plugin test cases, claude plugin tag creates name--vVersion tags (--push to send).

feature: Plugin dependencies and renames
detail: plugin.json dependencies install other plugins with optional semver range; a marketplace renames map migrates existing installs; changing name otherwise orphans installs.

feature: Plugin suggestions from relevance signals
detail: Claude Code suggests an uninstalled org-marketplace plugin when the working directory, files read, commands run, hostnames or package manifest dependencies match; it never auto-installs and matching stays local.

feature: Plugin suggestion surfaces: spinner tip, start notification, Discover pin
detail: Suggestions appear as a tip under the spinner, a one-line session-start notice for cwd matches, and a pinned entry on the /plugin Discover tab annotated with the matching signal.

feature: Suggestion frequency limits
detail: A plugin is suggested at most once every three sessions, the start notification stops after two combined showings, none after install, and the Discover pin shows only the first time.

feature: spinnerTipsEnabled turns off plugin tips
detail: Setting spinnerTipsEnabled false or overriding default tips hides spinner and start suggestions but not the Discover pin.

feature: Enable plugin suggestions via pluginSuggestionMarketplaces
detail: Admins must allowlist a marketplace name in managed settings and declare its source for suggestions to appear in the terminal.

feature: Plugins run code with user privileges
detail: Installed plugins can run hooks, background monitors, mods, MCP and LSP servers and bin/ executables outside the sandbox; permission rules cover only Claude's tool calls to them.

feature: Marketplace tiers: official, community, third-party
detail: Official and community marketplace names are accepted only from github.com/anthropics sources; claude-community entries are commit-pinned and a different commit is refused.

feature: Review a plugin before install
detail: Use claude plugin marketplace list, the /plugin details pane Will install section, Open homepage/View on GitHub, and claude plugin details for a component inventory.

feature: Trust warning before plugin install
detail: The details pane shows a standard warning that plugins can run code with access to files and shell; admins can append pluginTrustMessage.

feature: Remove an untrusted plugin
detail: claude plugin uninstall with --scope deletes persistent data by default (--keep-data to keep); cached files linger 14 days; removing the marketplace uninstalls all its plugins.

feature: Marketplace refusal and archive integrity checks
detail: Claude Code refuses marketplaces using Anthropic names from non-Anthropic sources and archive installs whose sha256 digest mismatches.

feature: Plugins default-enabled on install
detail: Installing a plugin enables it unless defaultEnabled false is set in its manifest or marketplace entry.

feature: Plugin names in telemetry by tier
detail: Official plugin names appear as-is in OpenTelemetry events; community and third-party names are replaced by third-party unless OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1; Analytics API follows the same rule.

feature: /plugin panel only in terminal sessions
detail: The /plugin panel needs a terminal session; in Desktop Code tab, VS Code panel (bare /plugin or /plugins opens Manage plugins), web and -p, install from the surface's own plugin dialog or the shell command.

feature: Plugin command aliases
detail: claude plugins aliases claude plugin, remove aliases uninstall, and /plugins and /marketplace open the same panel as /plugin.

feature: Add marketplace sources: owner/repo, URL, SSH, local path
detail: Accepted forms are GitHub owner/repo, http(s) URL, user@host:path, or a local path; a directory with marketplace.json or a .json file; --sparse limits monorepo checkout.

feature: Add a claude.ai-hosted marketplace
detail: Marketplaces named claudeai-* are added with claude plugin marketplace add --claudeai name.

feature: Official marketplace manual registration
detail: If not auto-registered (VS Code-only use, policy, env var), add it with /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official; the shell commands never register it.

feature: Git auth for marketplaces runs without prompts
detail: Clones disable prompts and askpass and use batch SSH with strict host key checking, so credentials must work non-interactively; CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_PREFER_HTTPS=1 skips SSH for GitHub sources.

feature: Marketplace clone timeout and offline handling
detail: Clones time out at 120s (CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_GIT_TIMEOUT_MS) and CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_KEEP_MARKETPLACE_ON_FAILURE=1 keeps an existing checkout when the host is unreachable.

feature: Marketplace name rules and reserved names
detail: Marketplace names may use letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen and must start with a letter or digit; JavaScript member names like constructor are reserved.

feature: Refresh a marketplace: /plugin marketplace update
detail: A stale catalog causes plugin-not-found; marketplace update refreshes it, and naming the marketplace in install refreshes it first.

feature: Plugin install safeguards
detail: Installs are refused for folder-name collisions between ids, unsupported source types, archive sha256 mismatches, malformed npm sources, and invalid or corrupt manifests, each with a specific message.

feature: Plugin dependency resolution errors
detail: Plugins with dependencies stay disabled until deps are installed, enabled and within semver ranges (tags named name--v*); cross-marketplace deps need allowlisting; claude plugin list --json reports error types.

feature: Marketplaces ignored when source is unsafe
detail: Marketplaces on network drives, with dot segments, a refused URL, or a mismatch with an extraKnownMarketplaces entry are listed as added but ignored and stop loading.

feature: Errors tab in /plugin
detail: The /plugin Errors tab lists load failures with guidance; /reload-plugins prints counts of plugins, skills, agents, hooks and servers reloaded.

feature: Reload applies automatically after install, --force for cache break
detail: After an install Claude Code runs /reload-plugins itself; a reload that adds or removes MCP servers or the LSP tool invalidates the prompt cache and requires /reload-plugins --force.

feature: Plugin settings precedence: local override of project plugins
detail: A plugin disabled in user settings may still load because project or managed settings enable it; set it false in .claude/settings.local.json to opt out, except synced plugins marked required by the org.

feature: Plugins enabled in project settings need explicit install
detail: A repository's settings enable a plugin but do not download it; each contributor runs claude plugin install name@marketplace --scope project.

feature: Plugin install records are self-healing
detail: Unreadable or invalid installed_plugins.json records are set aside or rebuilt as kept files that age out on cleanupPeriodDays; list shows notes.

feature: Plugin hook errors name the plugin
detail: A plugin hook that blocks with exit code 2 reports which plugin it came from; non-blocking failures show hook error notices; hooks need exact event names and matchers.

feature: Plugin MCP servers: user_config and /plugin configure
detail: Bundled MCP servers needing user configuration are skipped until values are set via /plugin Installed > Configure or /plugin configure; /mcp shows status and Reconnect.

feature: claude plugin install --config and claude plugin configure
detail: Shell installs never prompt for userConfig; pass --config KEY=VALUE or configure later, with unset required options reported (v2.1.285+).

feature: Code intelligence plugins use external language servers
detail: LSP plugins spawn a language server binary from PATH; failures show on the Errors tab, heavy servers can be disabled with /plugin disable.

feature: claude plugin validate messages and strict mode
detail: Validation errors cover missing manifest, bad JSON, path traversal, frontmatter, reserved names, engines range; unknown fields and missing frontmatter fail only with --strict.

feature: Marketplace validation rules
detail: Validation checks duplicate plugin names, relative path traversal, control characters in names, kebab-case, version drift vs plugin.json, and Claude Desktop-reserved or invalid marketplace names.

feature: URL-based marketplaces cannot use relative plugin paths
detail: Only marketplace.json is downloaded from a URL, so entries must use fetchable sources like a GitHub repo; git-hosted marketplaces clone everything.

feature: Policy messages users see when plugins are blocked
detail: Users get explicit refusals for blocked marketplace sources, plugins, dependencies, --plugin-dir (disableSideloadFlags), skills-dir plugins, command-sourced plugins and seed-managed marketplaces.

feature: Marketplace update skips seed-managed marketplaces
detail: Seed marketplaces are read-only; a bulk update skips them and updates the rest.

feature: Windows plugin path handling
detail: On Windows, hooks via Git Bash get CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT with forward slashes; exec-form or PowerShell hooks keep native paths; Git for Windows must be on PATH for marketplace clones.

feature: Plugin eval init scaffold
detail: claude plugin eval init writes an evals suite in a plugin root (--eval-dir to override); evals can check whether a skill is invoked.

feature: Prompt caching handled automatically
detail: Claude Code re-uses already processed conversation prefix and bills re-reads at a lower cached rate; it is on by default and can be disabled by env variables.

feature: Model switch warning before cache loss
detail: Running /model while the cache is warm asks for confirmation because each model has its own cache and the next turn is slow and uncached; a PreModelSwitch hook can require or skip it.

feature: Effort level change keeps cache on newest models
detail: Changing effort mid-session keeps the cache on current Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku generations with API key or subscription; other models and providers ask for confirmation first.

feature: Fast mode has its own cache
detail: Turning fast mode on or off uses a separate cache; the first enable in a conversation reads history uncached at fast rates, so enabling it at session start is cheaper.

feature: opusplan model setting
detail: Resolves to Opus in plan mode and Sonnet when executing, so each plan-mode toggle is a model switch with a fresh cache.

feature: Automatic model fallback on safety flag
detail: When a safety classifier flags a request in a category with a fallback model, Claude Code re-runs it on that model and the session continues there.

feature: MCP tool search defers tool definitions
detail: With tool search (default on supported models) MCP tools load on demand, so connecting or removing servers mid-session does not break the cache; without it, adding or removing tools invalidates the cache.

feature: Plugin enable/disable cache impact
detail: Skills, commands, agents, hooks, monitors and themes from plugins append without invalidating cache; plugin MCP servers follow MCP rules; disabling a just-enabled plugin restores the older cache entry.

feature: /reload-plugins applies plugin changes
detail: Runs automatically when closing the /plugin menu; warns and holds if a full re-read would result, with --force to apply anyway; also works in desktop, Agent SDK and -p sessions except plugin MCP changes.

feature: Code intelligence plugin adds LSP tool
detail: Enabling a code intelligence plugin gives Claude an LSP tool for code navigation.

feature: Deny rule for whole tool
detail: A bare tool-name deny rule (e.g. Bash, WebFetch, or mcp__*) removes the tool from the next request; scoped deny, allow and ask rules do not change tools visible to Claude.

feature: /compact summarizes history
detail: Replaces history with a summary; costs most after the cache has expired; best run at natural breaks, while /rewind returns to an earlier cached turn instead.

feature: Idle compaction setting (idleCompaction)
detail: A long idle conversation on the one-hour cache can be compacted automatically; set idleCompaction to false to turn it off.

feature: Oldest images and PDFs trimmed at request limit
detail: When a request would exceed image/PDF count or size limits, a batch of the oldest images is dropped and Claude can no longer see them; re-share if needed.

feature: Auto-update applies on next launch
detail: Updates download in the background and apply on next start; the first turn after upgrade is uncached; DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 controls timing.

feature: CLAUDE.md edits mid-session do not reload
detail: Project and user CLAUDE.md are read at session start; /clear, /compact or restart reloads them; nested CLAUDE.md and path-scoped rules load on demand.

feature: Permission mode changes are cache-safe
detail: Switching between permission modes does not change the prompt prefix, except opusplan's model change.

feature: Output style switch applies mid-session
detail: /output-style, /config or the outputStyle setting takes effect on the next message without losing cache (since v2.1.251).

feature: /recap session summary
detail: Generates a summary shown in the terminal without replacing history, so cache stays intact.

feature: /rewind truncates conversation
detail: Returns to an earlier turn, hitting the earlier cache entry; file checkpoints can be restored alongside.

feature: Resume session reuses cache if warm
detail: Resuming sends full history and reads any still-valid cached prefix; resumed conversation keeps its original system prompt until compacted.

feature: Cache TTL: one hour on subscription
detail: On a Claude subscription within plan usage, the main conversation gets a one-hour cache; API key, cloud providers or usage-credit overage get five minutes; subagents, workflows, forks, compaction get five minutes.

feature: Choose cache TTL (promptCacheTtl)
detail: promptCacheTtl and CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL set 5m or 1h for the main conversation; subagentPromptCacheTtl and its env variable do it for everything else; FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M and ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H override.

feature: Subagents have separate cache; forks share parent's
detail: A subagent starts its own cache; a fork inherits the parent's prompt and history and reads the parent cache; workflow fan-outs hold same-prefix agents up to 5 seconds to share cache.

feature: Subagent cacheTtl frontmatter
detail: A subagent can set an experimental cacheTtl in frontmatter; a 1h value is ignored while the subscription uses usage credits.

feature: Prompt cache stats in /usage
detail: /usage shows a Prompt cache (main) line with hit ratio, misses, warm status and likely cause of the last miss; a statusline script can read current_usage and prompt_cache fields.

feature: Disable prompt caching env variables
detail: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING plus per-family variables (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, Fable) turn caching off, mainly for debugging; can be set org-wide in managed settings.

feature: Cache scope per machine and directory
detail: Cache is effectively tied to one machine and directory; parallel sessions in the same directory can share; isolated between organizations.

feature: Cache policy via managed settings
detail: Admins can set caching disable or TTL env variables in the env block of managed settings.

feature: Gateway handling of cache_control markers
detail: Behind an LLM gateway or custom base URL, caching depends on whether the gateway forwards cache_control markers; Claude Code retries by moving the marker if the gateway returns a 400.

feature: Prompt library of copy-paste prompts
detail: A docs page of Claude Code prompts tagged by task and role, each with a Why this works explanation, as starting points.

feature: @ file reference in prompts
detail: Typing @ references a file so Claude reads the source directly; guidance also suggests pasting errors, logs and screenshots.

feature: /verify skill checks change against running app
detail: A bundled skill that runs the finished change against the live app to confirm it works.

feature: Output styles set default response format
detail: Output styles make a chosen answer format the default for every response.

feature: Plan mode previews file list before edits
detail: Plan mode shows which files will change before any edits happen, for larger or riskier changes.

feature: CLAUDE.md records conventions for each session
detail: CLAUDE.md stores project conventions so every session starts with that context.

feature: Save a prompt as a skill /command
detail: A working prompt can be saved as a skill and run by teammates as a slash command.

feature: Claude Code in Action course on Claude Academy
detail: Free video course and Claude Code 101 for learning the patterns.

feature: Native install script (macOS, Linux, WSL, Windows)
detail: One-line curl or PowerShell/CMD installer; auto-updates in the background; Git for Windows recommended so the Bash tool works, else PowerShell is used.

feature: Homebrew cask (stable and latest)
detail: brew install --cask claude-code tracks the stable channel (about a week behind); claude-code@latest tracks latest; no auto-update.

feature: WinGet install
detail: winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode; no auto-update.

feature: apt, dnf, apk Linux package managers
detail: Install options for Debian, Fedora, RHEL and Alpine.

feature: claude --version check
detail: Confirms the installation by printing the version.

feature: Sign in with subscription, Console, cloud provider or gateway
detail: First run prompts login in browser; accepts Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise, Claude Console, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, or a self-hosted Claude apps gateway; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY can skip login.

feature: /login to switch accounts
detail: Re-authenticate or change account inside a running session.

feature: Claude Code available on web, desktop, IDEs, Slack, CI
detail: Besides the terminal, Claude Code runs at claude.ai/code, the desktop app, VS Code, JetBrains, Slack, GitHub Actions and GitLab CI/CD.

feature: Ask questions about the codebase
detail: Claude reads project files as needed to answer what the project does, tech stack, entry points and folder structure without manual context.

feature: Edit files with approval prompt
detail: Claude finds the file, shows the change and asks for approval before editing.

feature: Shift+Tab cycles permission mode
detail: Switches the session's permission mode at any time.

feature: Conversational Git operations
detail: Ask for status, commits with messages, branches, history and merge-conflict help.

feature: Fix bugs, refactor, write tests, update docs, review changes
detail: Natural-language requests for common development tasks.

feature: claude command: interactive, with prompt, -p, -c, -r
detail: claude starts interactive; claude "task" starts with a prompt; -p runs a one-off query; -c continues the last conversation in the directory; -r resumes a previous one.

feature: /clear, /help, /exit session commands
detail: /clear starts a new conversation (resumable with /resume); /help lists commands; /exit or Ctrl+D twice exits.

feature: /resume continues a previous conversation
detail: Resumes an earlier session.

feature: Slash menu, Tab completion, history
detail: / lists commands and skills; Tab completes; up arrow recalls history.

feature: Ask Claude about its own capabilities
detail: In-session how-do-I questions, plus /help, docs, academy courses and a Discord community.

feature: Remote Control: drive a local Claude Code session from phone or browser
detail: Connects claude.ai/code or the Claude iOS/Android app to a session running on your machine; execution and files stay local; reconnects after sleep or network drops.

feature: Use local MCP servers and tools remotely
detail: Filesystem, MCP servers and project config remain available and @ autocompletes local paths from the remote device.

feature: Synchronized conversation and subagent progress
detail: Messages, subagent and dynamic workflow progress sync across terminal, browser and phone, and stopping a task from the device stops it locally.

feature: Attach images and files from phone or browser
detail: Photos reach Claude directly; other files are downloaded to the machine and passed as @ references; a note shows if an attachment did not arrive.

feature: Remote Control requirements
detail: Needs claude.ai subscription login (no API keys), not available on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, custom base URL or Claude apps gateway; Team/Enterprise Owner must enable it; workspace trust required.

feature: Admin toggle and custom role for Remote Control
detail: Owners enable Remote Control in Claude Code admin settings; Enterprise custom roles need cloud sessions plus Claude Code remote control permission; disableRemoteControl setting turns it off; unavailable with ZDR or HIPAA.

feature: claude remote-control server mode
detail: Runs a server waiting for connections, shows a URL and spacebar-toggled QR code, alias claude rc, and serves many concurrent sessions in one process.

feature: Server flag: --name and session name prefix
detail: --name sets session title; --remote-control-session-name-prefix (or env) sets prefix for auto names, defaulting to hostname.

feature: Server flags: --continue and --session-id
detail: Bring back the last session or one by ID after stopping the server; works for about four hours; unarchives archived sessions.

feature: Server flag: --spawn same-dir, worktree, session
detail: same-dir shares one directory, worktree gives each session its own git worktree, session serves exactly one session; press w at runtime to toggle and save the project default.

feature: Server flag: --capacity
detail: Maximum concurrent sessions, default 32.

feature: Server flag: --create-session-in-dir
detail: Pre-creates a session in the current directory at start (on by default); --no-create-session-in-dir leaves none and archives sessions on stop.

feature: Server flags: --permission-mode, --settings, --chrome
detail: Set starting permission mode, apply a settings file, and turn Chrome integration on or off for server-created sessions.

feature: Server flags: --debug, --debug-file, --verbose
detail: Debug logging with optional filter, log file output, and detailed connection logs.

feature: --sandbox flags removed from remote-control
detail: Passing --sandbox or --no-sandbox to the server errors since v2.1.300; sandboxing is turned on in settings instead.

feature: claude --remote-control interactive session
detail: Starts a normal interactive session with Remote Control on, optionally named; alias --rc.

feature: /remote-control (/rc) from an existing session
detail: Carries current conversation to Remote Control, with a one-time enable confirmation and a status panel showing URL and QR code and a disconnect option.

feature: Remote Control in VS Code and Desktop app
detail: Type /remote-control in the prompt; VS Code shows a footer indicator, no name argument or QR code; Desktop sessions appear at claude.ai/code.

feature: /rc active indicator and connection failure reasons
detail: Terminal shows an indicator linking to the session; failures show reasons like taken over, archived elsewhere, or deleted, with reconnect via /remote-control.

feature: Connect by URL, QR code or session list
detail: Open the URL, scan the QR, or find the session in claude.ai/code or the app's Code tab, marked by a computer icon with green dot; /mobile shows an app-store QR.

feature: Remote session title precedence
detail: Title comes from the name flag, /rename, last message, or an auto name; renaming from claude.ai or the app updates the local title.

feature: Share-link safety on /resume and /teleport
detail: Remote Control disconnects when /resume or /teleport opens another conversation if the session has a share link, so viewers do not see the new one.

feature: Diff pane for session changes
detail: A connected device shows the git diff: changes since branching from default branch including uncommitted edits, or only uncommitted on default branch.

feature: Pick model and effort from connected device
detail: Model and effort selected on a device apply to the machine's session; /model sent to an interactive session also sets the default for new sessions.

feature: Fork a session from the browser
detail: Fork the whole session or from an earlier message at claude.ai/code into a new session while the original continues; declined if busy, VS Code hosted, or in --spawn session mode.

feature: Enable Remote Control for all sessions (auto-connect)
detail: /config toggle with on, off, default; also a VS Code toggle and a Desktop Connect new sessions setting; remoteControlAtStartup in settings; project settings can only turn it off.

feature: Remote Control connection model and transcript storage
detail: Outbound HTTPS only with short-lived scoped credentials; the transcript is stored on Anthropic servers while connected to sync devices.

feature: Trusted Devices requirement
detail: Requires an enrolled device and a sign-in under 18 hours old (refreshed with Face ID, Touch ID, Windows Hello or passkey) to view or steer Remote Control and Cowork computer access; Owners enable it for Team/Enterprise, individuals for Pro/Max/Ultra.

feature: Manage trusted devices in account settings
detail: Members review enrolled devices and revoke them; credentials expire if unused; admins can Sign out everywhere; hardware keys work without a platform authenticator.

feature: Compare Remote Control, cloud, Dispatch, Channels, Slack, scheduled tasks
detail: A table of ways to work away from the terminal: Dispatch (not available to new users), Remote Control, Channels, Slack, self-hosted environments, and scheduled tasks.

feature: Dispatch: message a task from phone to Desktop
detail: Pair the Claude mobile app with Desktop to hand off a task that spawns a Desktop session.

feature: Mobile push notifications from Claude Code
detail: With Remote Control active, pushes arrive when a long task finishes or a decision is needed; toggles Push when Claude decides and Push when actions required in /config; skipped while typing in the terminal.

feature: Presence file to suppress pushes
detail: CLAUDE_CLIENT_PRESENCE_FILE marker path suppresses mobile pushes while the file exists, e.g. when the screen is unlocked.

feature: Slash commands usable from mobile and web
detail: Text commands (/compact, /clear, /context, /usage, /recap, /usage-credits), /model, /effort, /fast, /color, /rename, /mcp, /config, /autocompact, /advisor, /output-style, /focus work remotely; /plugin and /resume are local only.

feature: Re-authorize a claude.ai connector from shell
detail: claude mcp login "claude.ai Slack" --no-browser prints an auth link; then /mcp reconnect <name> works from phone or web.

feature: Limits: one remote session per interactive process, 403 and outage retry
detail: Interactive instances hold one remote session; server mode gives up after about 10 minutes offline; 403 retries up to three minutes; forwarded dialogs expire after five minutes (dialogExpiry).

feature: Remote Control troubleshooting messages
detail: Documented fixes for auth, API-key conflicts, feature-flag env variables, org policy, trusted device and reconnect errors, and claude doctor diagnostics.

feature: Cloud scheduled tasks (formerly routines)
detail: Saved Claude Code configuration of prompt, repositories and connectors that runs on Anthropic cloud (or self-hosted environment) when the laptop is closed, from schedule, API or GitHub triggers.

feature: Schedule trigger: preset, custom cron, one-off
detail: Hourly, daily, weekly presets or custom cron (not more often than hourly), or a one-time run that then shows Completed; on-the-hour runs may start minutes late; presets use local time, raw cron uses UTC unless CRON_TZ.

feature: API trigger with bearer token
detail: Each task gets a fire URL and a one-time token; POST /fire with optional text starts a session and returns its URL; text arrives wrapped as untrusted data; tokens can be regenerated or deleted.

feature: GitHub event trigger
detail: Starts a session on pull request, release or issue events with Claude GitHub App installed; each event gets an independent session; per-task and per-account hourly caps drop extra events.

feature: Pull request filters
detail: Filter by author, title, body, base branch, head branch, labels, draft, merged with operators equals, contains, starts with, is one of, is not one of, regex (whole-value match).

feature: Multiple triggers per task
detail: One task can combine schedule, API and GitHub triggers, added with + in the Trigger row or removed with a trash icon.

feature: Create task from web, Desktop or CLI
detail: New task dialog or full-page form at claude.ai/code/routines (Create with Claude or Set up manually), Desktop Code tab Scheduled, or /schedule (alias /routines); all write to the same account.

feature: /schedule list, update, run and run history
detail: CLI manages tasks conversationally, including one-off natural-language times and explaining why a run did nothing.

feature: Per-task model, effort, repositories and environment
detail: Choose model and effort, one or more GitHub repos cloned each run (pushes to claude/ branches), and a cloud environment with network access, variables and setup script.

feature: Connectors included by default in tasks
detail: All connected claude.ai connectors are attached to a task and can be removed per task; local claude mcp add servers do not appear unless added as connectors or via .mcp.json.

feature: Run now, pause/resume switch, edit and delete
detail: Task detail page lets you start immediately, toggle schedule on/off, edit all fields, or delete.

feature: Run history with Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled
detail: Each run opens as a full session to inspect, create a PR, continue or archive; history has a status filter and warning banners for last-run problems.

feature: Runs start in auto mode
detail: Cloud task sessions begin in auto mode with a classifier; they still stop for ask rules or repeated blocks and wait for an answer in the run's session.

feature: Scheduled runs can publish artifacts
detail: In auto mode a run can publish an artifact, private until shared; in Accept edits mode new artifacts publish without asking but runtime capabilities or republishing other cases ask first.

feature: Scheduled task hourly limits
detail: 100 scheduled runs per hour per account; Run now and API fires 30 per hour per task and 100 per account; usage draws subscription usage, with overage only via usage credits.

feature: Admin toggle and role permission for scheduled tasks
detail: Owners can turn tasks off org-wide at Capabilities > Remote sessions; Enterprise custom roles need the scheduled tasks permission; tasks are per-account and not shared.

feature: GitHub connection lapse behavior
detail: If GitHub access is missing, runs are skipped up to 72 hours, then the task turns off.

feature: Cloud environment network access levels
detail: Default environment uses Limited network with package managers allowed; domains can be added or Full access chosen; org-shared environments are read-only for members.

feature: Self-hosted environment routing
detail: Tasks can run in the organization's self-hosted environment instead of Anthropic cloud.

feature: Routines naming still appears
detail: Older UI, URL, API and org toggle use the name routines for the same feature.

feature: Compare cloud, Desktop and /loop scheduling
detail: Mentions Desktop scheduled tasks (local files) and /loop (in-session) as the other two options.

feature: Sandbox options comparison
detail: Compares sandboxed Bash tool, sandbox runtime, dev container, custom container, VM and cloud sessions by what is isolated, Docker need and setup effort.

feature: Sandbox runtime (srt claude)
detail: @anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime wraps the whole Claude Code process incl. file tools, MCP servers and hooks; denies network by default; config in ~/.srt-settings.json; beta research preview.

feature: Runtime blocks risky writes automatically
detail: Denies .git/hooks, .git/config, .mcp.json, .claude/commands, .claude/agents and shell startup files at the project root; Linux builds the list once at launch.

feature: Dev container with default-deny firewall
detail: Published example dev container with iptables firewall supports --dangerously-skip-permissions for unattended work and standardizes team environments.

feature: Custom container and VM isolation options
detail: Run in any Docker/OCI container or microVM such as Firecracker or Docker Sandboxes; review writable mounts, credentials and egress.

feature: --dangerously-skip-permissions needs isolation, refuses root
detail: Skips prompts; should only run inside a container, VM or sandbox runtime; refuses to start as root on Linux and macOS.

feature: Cloud sessions as isolated VM
detail: Cloud sessions run commands in an Anthropic-managed VM with a network allowlist proxy and a GitHub token proxy; need a subscription and GitHub (or --cloud with bundled local repo).

feature: Enforce isolation org-wide
detail: Only the built-in Bash sandbox can be enforced by Claude Code via managed or server-managed settings; containers and VMs rely on device management.

feature: Sandboxed Bash tool (/sandbox)
detail: OS-enforced boundary around Bash, PowerShell and Monitor commands; off by default; macOS Seatbelt, Linux and WSL2 bubblewrap; native Windows unsupported.

feature: /sandbox panel: Mode, Overrides, Config, Dependencies tabs
detail: Choose auto-allow or regular permissions, toggle unsandboxed fallback, view resolved settings, and see missing dependencies on Linux; saves to .claude/settings.local.json.

feature: Sandbox auto-allow vs regular permissions mode
detail: Auto-allow runs sandboxed commands without prompts (deny rules, critical-path rm, ask rules still apply); regular mode keeps normal prompts.

feature: Unsandboxed retry (dangerouslyDisableSandbox)
detail: Claude may retry a failed command outside the sandbox; approval depends on permission mode (prompt, classifier, denied); an ask rule can force prompting.

feature: Strict sandbox mode (allowUnsandboxedCommands false)
detail: Disables the unsandboxed retry; managed or --settings use makes the sandbox admin-required; shown as Strict sandbox mode on the Overrides tab.

feature: Sandbox filesystem allowWrite, denyWrite, denyRead, allowRead
detail: Default writes to working directory, temp and added dirs and reads most of the machine; narrower read rules win; settings merge across scopes.

feature: blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories
detail: Stops sandboxed commands reading home and other user directories outside working directories.

feature: excludedCommands run outside the sandbox
detail: Patterns like docker compose * run without restrictions but through permission flow; every command in a chained call must match.

feature: Disable filesystem isolation (filesystem.disabled)
detail: Keeps network isolation but drops read/write restrictions; only user, managed or --settings can set it.

feature: Protect credentials (sandbox.credentials deny)
detail: List credential files and env variables to block or unset for sandboxed commands; no built-in deny list.

feature: Mask credentials with sentinel substitution
detail: Mask mode shows commands a placeholder and the proxy swaps in the real secret for allowed hosts; needs TLS termination; supports extract, decode, injectHosts, AWS SigV4 re-signing; macOS blocks masked files.

feature: Protected paths inside the sandbox
detail: Sandbox denies writes to .claude settings, skills, agents, commands, hooks, .mcp.json, shell startup files, .gitconfig, .vscode, .idea, git hooks/config and ~/.claude contents.

feature: Network isolation via sandbox proxy
detail: No direct route out; a local proxy checks hostnames against allowedDomains and deniedDomains; non-proxy tools (ssh, DB drivers, UDP, ping) cannot connect.

feature: Prompt when a command needs a new host
detail: Manual and acceptEdits prompt, bypassPermissions allows, auto mode refuses unless the command lists the host, dontAsk refuses; Yes and don't ask again saves a WebFetch domain rule.

feature: Per-command allowed domains in auto mode
detail: In auto mode Claude names needed hosts on the command and the classifier reviews them; approval covers only that command.

feature: strictAllowlist and allowManagedDomainsOnly
detail: Deny any host outside the allowlist without prompting; managed variant honors only managed entries.

feature: Local-address and IPv6 domain handling
detail: Proxy refuses allowed hostnames resolving to loopback or metadata addresses unless the IP is allowed; IPv6 entries use bracket form; claude doctor flags ambiguous entries.

feature: Custom proxy ports and corporate proxy
detail: httpProxyPort and socksProxyPort send traffic to your own proxy (which then must filter); HTTPS_PROXY routes through a corporate proxy while keeping the allowlist.

feature: Managed sandbox enforcement settings
detail: Managed settings set enabled, failIfUnavailable and allowUnsandboxedCommands false; make the sandbox admin-required so repository settings cannot loosen it; allowManagedReadPathsOnly locks reads.

feature: failIfUnavailable
detail: Makes Claude Code exit at startup if the sandbox cannot run, instead of running commands unsandboxed.

feature: Weaker sandbox options (nested sandbox, Apple Events, Unix sockets, local bindin
detail: Settings like enableWeakerNestedSandbox, allowAppleEvents, allowAllUnixSockets, allowLocalBinding, allowNestedUserNamespaces trade isolation for compatibility; some cannot be set by repositories.

feature: Linux and WSL2 dependencies and AppArmor profile
detail: Needs bubblewrap and socat (optional seccomp filter); Ubuntu AppArmor user-namespace restriction needs a bwrap profile or sysctl change.

feature: Sandbox scope: what runs outside
detail: Read/Edit/WebFetch tools, hooks, local MCP servers, plugin monitors, LSP, status line, apiKeyHelper and mods run unsandboxed; subagents and background sessions inherit the sandbox.

feature: Sandbox troubleshooting guide
detail: Covers jest/watchman, Go TLS on macOS, docker, Chromium and Podman, clipboard tools, git index.lock/unlink and SSH, localhost servers, 0-byte placeholders and claude doctor checks.

feature: Sandbox deletes new HEAD, objects, refs entries
detail: After a sandboxed command, new top-level HEAD/objects/refs are deleted or quarantined to prevent bare-repo tricks.

feature: /loop repeats a prompt in the session
detail: Interval and prompt run on a cron schedule; prompt only lets Claude pick a 1-minute to 1-hour delay each iteration; bare /loop runs a maintenance prompt; skills can be the prompt.

feature: Interval units s, m, h, d
detail: Fixed intervals are converted to cron, seconds round up to a minute, and uneven intervals round to a clean step.

feature: Built-in loop maintenance prompt
detail: Continues unfinished work, tends the branch's PR (comments, CI, conflicts), then runs cleanup passes, under normal permission checks.

feature: loop.md custom default prompt
detail: Project .claude/loop.md or user ~/.claude/loop.md replaces the maintenance prompt; edits apply next iteration; truncated beyond 25,000 bytes.

feature: Stop a loop
detail: Esc on empty prompt stops a self-paced loop; fixed-interval loops need asking Claude to cancel; Claude can end its own loop via ScheduleWakeup stop; Ctrl+C twice detaches a background session without stopping it.

feature: One-time reminders in natural language
detail: Ask to be reminded at a time or after a delay; a single-fire task that deletes itself.

feature: CronCreate, CronList, CronDelete tools
detail: Create (5-field cron, recurring or once), list with next run times, and delete tasks by 8-character ID; up to 50 per session.

feature: Scheduler jitter and early one-shots
detail: Recurring tasks run late up to half the gap (max 30 minutes), except */5; one-shots on :00/:30 run up to 90 seconds early.

feature: Seven-day expiry of recurring tasks
detail: Recurring session tasks fire a last time 7 days after creation and delete themselves.

feature: Cron expression syntax
detail: Standard 5-field cron in local time with wildcards, steps, ranges, lists; no L, W, ? or name aliases; day-of-month and day-of-week match if either does.

feature: Disable scheduler (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON)
detail: Turns off CronCreate and /loop and stops scheduled tasks firing.

feature: Session-scoped task limitations and resume
detail: Tasks fire only while Claude is running and idle, no catch-up for missed fires, restored on --resume except expired ones and self-paced loops; backgrounding carries /loop tasks over.

feature: Monitor tool for event streaming
detail: In a dynamic loop Claude may use Monitor to stream a background script's output instead of polling.

feature: Scheduling options comparison table
detail: Cloud (1-hour minimum, no local files), Desktop (1-minute via Claude, local files) and /loop (1 minute, inherits session) compared on persistence and permissions.

feature: Security guidance plugin
detail: Official plugin makes Claude review its own code changes for vulnerabilities and fix them in-session; runs automatically after install.

feature: Per-edit risky pattern check
detail: After each file write, a no-model pattern match flags eval, pickle, innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, workflow file edits and similar; warns once per pattern per file per session.

feature: End-of-turn security diff review
detail: A background separate Claude reviews the turn's git diff (up to 30 files) for authz bypass, IDOR, injection, SSRF and weak crypto, and re-prompts Claude with findings, at most three times in a row.

feature: Commit and push agentic security review
detail: On git commit or push through Claude's Bash tool, a deeper agentic review reads callers and related code; capped at 20 per rolling hour; commits from your own shell are not reviewed.

feature: Custom guidance file for security reviews
detail: claude-security-guidance.md at user, project or project-local scope adds threat-model rules for model-backed reviews; additive only, combined cap 8 KB.

feature: Custom per-edit patterns file
detail: security-patterns.yaml/.yml/.json adds regex or substring rules with reminder, paths and exclude_paths; up to 50 rules.

feature: Security plugin env switches and review models
detail: ENABLE_PATTERN_RULES, ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW, ENABLE_COMMIT_REVIEW, ENABLE_CODE_SECURITY_REVIEW and SECURITY_GUIDANCE_DISABLE turn layers off; SECURITY_REVIEW_MODEL and SG_AGENTIC_MODEL pick review models (Opus by default).

feature: Install security-guidance from official marketplace
detail: /plugin install security-guidance@claude-plugins-official, or via desktop app or VS Code plugin dialogs; cloud sessions do not load user plugins; teams can enable via checked-in enabledPlugins.

feature: Org-wide plugin enablement
detail: Admins can enable the plugin through enabledPlugins in managed settings and distribute org rule files via device management; plugin then cannot be disabled by users.

feature: Security reviews consume usage
detail: End-of-turn and commit reviews spend model usage; per-edit check is free.

feature: Security tooling stack: /security-review, Claude Security, Code Review
detail: Mentions /security-review (branch changes), the Claude Security plugin (multi-agent repo scan with patches) and Code Review on pull requests for Team and Enterprise.

feature: Auto mode permission classifier
detail: Default starting mode in terminal and VS Code: a separate classifier model reviews actions and blocks unsafe ones; explicit ask and deny rules still apply; orgs can turn it off.

feature: Manual permission mode
detail: Starts read-only; asks before edits, tests and commands, with approve once or always; built-in read-only commands (ls, cat, git status) run without asking.

feature: Accept Edits mode
detail: Auto-approves file edits and filesystem Bash commands (mkdir, touch, rm, mv, cp, sed) inside the working directory; others still prompt.

feature: Working directory boundary
detail: In Manual mode file tools ask before reading or writing outside the start folder; additional directories can be added.

feature: Prompt injection safeguards
detail: Permission system, network command approval for curl/wget, command-injection detection and fail-closed matching in Manual mode.

feature: WebFetch summarized by a separate model
detail: For most fetches a separate model call reads the page and Claude gets only its answer.

feature: Workspace trust dialog and .mcp.json approval
detail: Shown when starting in an untrusted folder; home-directory trust is not persisted; -p sessions skip both prompts.

feature: Secure credential storage
detail: Keys and tokens in macOS Keychain, a 0600 file on Linux, user-profile-protected file on Windows.

feature: Data retention and training controls
detail: Limited retention and restricted access to session data; consumer users set training preferences at claude.ai/settings/privacy; Team/Enterprise/API under commercial terms.
plans: Free, Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise

feature: MCP server security and managed MCP
detail: Project .mcp.json, other scopes, claude.ai connectors and plugins can add servers; Anthropic reviews directory listings but does not audit MCP servers; managed MCP config restricts servers.

feature: Cloud session security controls
detail: Isolated VM, limited network by default, GitHub credentials held server-side via a proxy, rejected branch deletes and tag pushes, audit logging, automatic VM cleanup and session deletion.

feature: Windows WebDAV warning
detail: Recommends against enabling WebDAV or allowing \\* paths because it can bypass the permission system.

feature: Team security practices: managed settings, OpenTelemetry, ConfigChange hooks
detail: Enforce standards via managed settings, monitor with OpenTelemetry, audit or block settings changes with hooks, review permissions with /permissions.

feature: Report vulnerabilities and /feedback
detail: Vulnerability reports go through the HackerOne program; /feedback reports suspicious behavior; Trust Center provides SOC 2 and ISO 27001 material.

feature: Remote Control security model
detail: Local execution with TLS to Anthropic API and short-lived scoped credentials; transcript stored while connected; no cloud VM or sandbox.

feature: Self-hosted environments for cloud sessions
detail: Lets an organization run Claude Code cloud sessions on its own infrastructure via runners it deploys; sessions started from claude.ai, apps, terminal or scheduled tasks can be routed there instead of Anthropic hosts.

feature: Allow self-hosted environments admin toggle
detail: An Owner turns on this setting on the Cloud environments admin page; it is off by default and requires cloud sessions to be enabled for the organization.

feature: Environment picker at session start
detail: The session-start UI lists Anthropic-hosted environments next to the organization's self-hosted ones so the developer chooses where the session runs.

feature: Environment, runner, session model
detail: An environment is a named group of runners created in admin settings; runners are long-lived processes on the customer's hosts that claim queued sessions; each session runs as a child Claude Code process.

feature: Owner lock: one runner serves one account
detail: The first session a runner claims locks it to that account (or Claude Tag agent) and it serves only that owner up to its capacity, so checked-out code never mixes between owners.

feature: Anthropic-hosted vs self-hosted outbound-only networking
detail: Runners only make outbound HTTPS calls to api.anthropic.com for queue polling, event streaming and by default inference; Anthropic never connects inbound.

feature: Zero Data Retention and HIPAA exclusion
detail: Self-hosted environments are unavailable to organizations with Zero Data Retention enabled or the HIPAA configuration applied.

feature: What stays on customer infrastructure
detail: Repository checkouts, build artifacts, secrets and created files stay on customer machines, while prompts, responses and tool results go to Anthropic, which stores the transcript so sessions can be resumed from other surfaces.

feature: Surfaces that can use self-hosted environments
detail: claude.ai/code, mobile and desktop apps, cloud scheduled tasks, and terminal dispatch with --cloud or --environment can run there; Claude Tag sessions can too (without Access bundles), but Claude Security and Code Review do not route there yet.

feature: Supported repository hosts for self-hosted sessions
detail: Sessions check out from GitHub or GitHub Enterprise Server; sessions started with an --environment dispatch can use other git hosts.

feature: Self-hosted sessions use organization Claude Code usage
detail: Sessions in a self-hosted environment consume the organization's Claude Code usage the same as Anthropic-hosted environments.

feature: Model inference via Bedrock or Google Agent Platform
detail: A runner can be configured to send model requests to Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Agent Platform instead of the Anthropic API; session content still goes to Anthropic.

feature: Corporate egress proxy and mTLS support
detail: Runner and orchestrator honor HTTPS_PROXY, NO_PROXY and mTLS variables; the proxy must not buffer the server-sent-event session stream.

feature: Runner session lease and requeue behavior
detail: Each poll refreshes a lease; if a runner stops polling the lease lapses after about 60 seconds and the session is requeued to another runner after a few minutes.

feature: Runner retire time (--retire-at)
detail: For hosts killed at a known time without a signal, the runner stops taking work, releases sessions after their turn finishes and exits 0 so sessions resume on a fresh runner.

feature: Runner drain grace behavior
detail: With drain grace 0 the runner exits right after its sessions finish so the orchestrator can restart it clean; a positive value keeps polling the locked owner's queue for that many seconds.

feature: Autoscaling orchestrator option
detail: Customers can start runners themselves or host an orchestrator process that starts runners as sessions queue.

feature: Sessions resumable across surfaces
detail: Because Anthropic stores the transcript, a self-hosted session can be resumed from any supported surface.

feature: Guided setup command (self-hosted-runner setup)
detail: An interactive Claude Code session that walks an Owner through creating the environment, starts a local runner, confirms registration and writes a cheat sheet file.

feature: Create environment in Cloud environments admin page
detail: Owners select New under Self-hosted environments, name it and copy the environment key, which is shown once and expires after 365 days.

feature: Environment secret rotation and revocation
detail: A new secret can be created from the environment's Configuration tab, rolled out, then the old one revoked; runners on a revoked secret fail their poll and exit.

feature: Environment status Healthy / No runners deployed
detail: The admin page shows an environment's status and an Activity tab listing its runners.

feature: Runner host requirements
detail: Linux or macOS host or container with outbound HTTPS, git 2.24 or newer, synchronized clock and Claude Code 2.1.224 or later; Windows hosts are not supported as runners.

feature: Runner start command and base directory
detail: claude self-hosted-runner is started with an environment secret file and a dedicated base directory where it checks out repositories and per-session folders.

feature: Runner exits after one session by default
detail: Started plainly, a runner exits after serving one session and must be restarted by a supervisor; it also exits if it loses contact with Anthropic.

feature: Send follow-up to a cloud session from CLI
detail: claude -p "msg" --cloud <session-id> posts one message to a running cloud session from any logged-in machine and prints a view link.

feature: Requires GitHub connector and per-user GitHub connection
detail: Owners must turn on the GitHub connector and each developer connect GitHub so they can pick github.com repositories for sessions.

feature: Session access token (JWT) in self-hosted sessions
detail: Every session gets a signed JWT in CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ACCESS_TOKEN with prefix sk-ant-cc- that internal services can verify to learn which session, environment and creator made a request.

feature: Public JWKS endpoint for token verification
detail: Anthropic publishes ES256 verification keys at a public unauthenticated endpoint, rotated periodically and cacheable for five minutes.

feature: Token claims: issuer, audience, role, expiry
detail: Services should check prefix, ES256 signature, issuer ccr, audience containing the environment ID, role session_worker and expiry (4 hours default, 8 max).

feature: Creator identity in act claim
detail: The act claim carries user:<id> or agent:<id> and optionally email, plus the runner, environment and secret creator chain, so services can attribute actions.

feature: decode-token subcommand for wrapper scripts
detail: self-hosted-runner decode-token verifies signature and expiry and prints claims as JSON from inside a session; --no-verify allows offline inspection.

feature: Scope derived credentials guidance
detail: Tokens stay valid until expiry with no revocation feed and can be read by any code in the session, so credentials derived from them should be least-privilege, short-lived and audited by session ID.

feature: Dispatch a cloud session from CLI (--environment)
detail: claude -p with --environment <id> (and optional --ref) creates a session on a chosen environment from a git checkout and exits, printing JSON with session ID and URL.

feature: CLI dispatch flag restrictions
detail: --environment beats the default environment setting, does not support stream-json output and cannot combine with resume, continue, teleport, session-id or init-only.

feature: Stop hook capture for end-to-end tests
detail: A sample Stop hook writes each turn's final reply to a file or POSTs it to a URL so CI can assert on replies from a self-hosted runner.

feature: CI authentication for dispatch requires claude.ai OAuth
detail: --environment and --cloud need a claude.ai OAuth login (API keys not accepted); the cloud-session scope is capped at 30 days and no long-lived CI token exists yet.

feature: Create and delete environments via API
detail: An Owner OAuth token can create and delete self-hosted environments programmatically for ephemeral per-CI-run environments using the same endpoints as the admin page.

feature: Runner flag --base-dir
detail: Directory for repository checkouts and per-session working dirs; default /workspace; runner exits at startup if it cannot write there.

feature: Runner flag --capacity
detail: Maximum concurrent sessions a runner handles for its locked owner; default 1.

feature: Runner flag --client-label
detail: Label sent at registration and exposed in the runner info metric; defaults to hostname.

feature: Runner flag --configure-git
detail: At startup writes git identity, Anthropic commit signing, push negotiation and hooks adding a Co-authored-by trailer.

feature: Runner flag --confine-repo-settings
detail: Guard mode (warn, enforce, off) that flags repository settings granting access outside the workspace, setting env vars or overriding sandbox/hooks posture; default warn.

feature: Runner flag --debug-token-dir
detail: Writes live tokens to disk for inspection; debug only.

feature: Runner flag --defer-shutdown-max-min
detail: On first SIGTERM keep serving attached sessions for N minutes before releasing them and exiting; 0 disables.

feature: Runner flag --drain-grace-sec
detail: Seconds the runner keeps polling the locked owner's queue after sessions finish before exiting; 0 exits immediately.

feature: Runner flag --drain-marker-file
detail: Marker file written by the host to announce a graceful drain so exit is reported as a host drain.

feature: Runner flag --drain-wait-sec
detail: Seconds to wait for in-flight turns and background tasks before terminating session children on drain; default 0.

feature: Runner flag --environment-secret-file
detail: Path to the environment secret (or orchestrator work-order JWT); legacy pool-secret names still work with a deprecation notice.

feature: Runner flag --exec-path
detail: Binary or wrapper script spawned for each session instead of the runner's own binary.

feature: Runner flag --exit-if-unused-min
detail: Exit after N minutes of polling with no work ever assigned, for autoscaler scale-down.

feature: Runner flag --git-host-rewrite
detail: Rewrites https source hosts before clone, for split-horizon DNS; repeatable.

feature: Runner flag --git-ssh-rewrite
detail: Rewrites https remotes to SSH form for SSH-only git hosts; repeatable.

feature: Runner flag --health-port
detail: Port for /healthz and /metrics; default 8080; 0 disables.

feature: Runner flag --hold-idle-file
detail: File the host keeps touching to hold an idle session on the runner while its processes run.

feature: Runner flag --hooks-dir
detail: Directory of lifecycle hook scripts (checkout, post-session, command).

feature: Runner flag --host-config-snapshot
detail: Where the startup snapshot of the host config dir is kept: disk (digest-verified) or memory (capped at 64 MiB).

feature: Runner flag --kill-session-after-min
detail: Wall-clock limit per session as a backstop for stuck sessions; runner releases then terminates after a grace window; 0 disables.

feature: Runner flag --lock-to-account
detail: Pre-locks the runner to a specific account email or user ID; such a runner never serves Claude Tag channel sessions.

feature: Runner flag --log-file
detail: Mirrors runner logs to a 0600 file; needed for the doctor command to tail logs.

feature: Runner flag --log-level
detail: info or debug.

feature: Runner flag --max-hold-min
detail: Cap on how long a held idle session stays before release; default 1440 minutes.

feature: Runner flag --post-session-hook-timeout-sec
detail: Budget for the post-session hook on every session end; default 60.

feature: Runner flag --proxy-authorization-command
detail: Shell command whose output supplies the Proxy-Authorization header for each proxy connection.

feature: Runner flag --proxy-authorization-file
detail: File whose contents supply a rotating Proxy-Authorization header value.

feature: Runner flag --push-outcome-on-release
detail: On a runner-initiated session end, pushes session branches with new commits to origin before deleting the workspace.

feature: Runner flag --release-idle-session-min
detail: Releases a session's slot after N idle minutes so it can resume on a fresh runner; 0 disables.

feature: Runner flag --remove-session-state
detail: Deletes per-session directories when the session ends on this runner.

feature: Runner flag --repository-folder
detail: At capacity 1, uses a given folder as the clone of an owner/repo not prepared by a checkout hook.

feature: Runner flag --retire-at
detail: Retires the runner at an absolute Unix timestamp for infrastructure killed at a known time.

feature: Runner flag --server-auto-mode-lists
detail: Controls which auto-mode classifier rule lists (all, no-allow, none) from the control plane reach sessions; default no-allow.

feature: Runner flag --session-stop-grace-sec
detail: How long to wait for the Claude process to exit cleanly after a session ends; default 5.

feature: Runner flag --startup-timeout-min
detail: How long to wait on a child that has not initialized before releasing the slot; default 15; 0 disables.

feature: Runner flag --trust-workspace
detail: Seeds persisted trust so repo-committed permission allows and additional directories are honored; default on.

feature: Runner flag --use-anthropic-git-proxy
detail: Clones github.com repositories through Anthropic-managed git instead of customer credentials; needs capacity 1 and git 2.32+.

feature: Runner flag --api-url
detail: API base URL override for testing only.

feature: Orchestrator flag --hook-concurrency
detail: Max parallel spawn-runner hooks; default 4.

feature: Orchestrator flag --hook-timeout
detail: Seconds before a spawn hook's process tree is terminated; default 60.

feature: Orchestrator flag --hook-label
detail: Passes a session's metadata label to the hook as an env var with allowed values; blocks sessions with other values.

feature: Orchestrator flag --expected-spawn-seconds
detail: Expected p99 time from spawn request to runner registration; sent as the server-side lease; default 120.

feature: Orchestrator flag --min-idle
detail: Keeps at least N idle session slots free by pre-warming standby runners; 0 disables.

feature: Orchestrator flag --shutdown-drain-sec
detail: Seconds to let running spawn hooks finish after SIGTERM; max 3600.

feature: Orchestrator flag --debug-dir
detail: Writes each spawn request's work order and hook stderr to disk; debug only.

feature: SCM connector flags (not yet available)
detail: Flags for a WebSocket tunnel to a GitHub Enterprise Server host reachable only inside the network are documented but the connector is not available.

feature: Runner environment-variable-only settings
detail: Extra env vars tune background-task grace, host config dir, kill grace, post-turn settle, SIGKILL grace, renewal warning, git fetch depth, fetch progress cap, skip git verify and plugin auto-update.

feature: Disable Artifact tool in sessions (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT)
detail: Setting it on the runner disables the Artifact tool regardless of the organization admin setting and removes its egress requirement.

feature: Telemetry controls for session children
detail: Operational telemetry is sent unless disabled via DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DO_NOT_TRACK, DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING or nonessential-traffic variables; Datadog metrics are opt-in for self-hosted via a dedicated flag.

feature: Runner /healthz endpoint
detail: Returns 200 while the process is alive with JSON status, runner ID, active sessions and last poll age; orchestrator health also reports connection state and queue counts.

feature: Prometheus metrics for runners and orchestrator
detail: /metrics exposes series for capacity, active sessions, poll age and errors, session start/complete/fail/interrupt counts, init duration, idle seconds, queue depth and spawn hook outcomes.

feature: Sample alert rules and PodMonitor
detail: Documentation supplies example Prometheus alerts (stale poll, version drift, init errors, orchestrator disconnected, circuit-broken sessions, runners below floor, queue wait high) and a PodMonitor.

feature: Pass-through of session child metrics
detail: With Prometheus exporter and telemetry enabled, child counters and gauges are re-exposed on the runner's /metrics tagged with session ID and client platform.

feature: Autoscaling guidance with HPA and KEDA
detail: Recommends scaling on environment pending sessions or active-to-capacity ratio, gated on orchestrator connection, with a caution about KEDA scaling in on empty results.

feature: Wrapper scripts around the session process
detail: A script run in place of the Claude binary per session for per-session credentials, secrets, toolchains or resource limits, ending with exec of the runner's binary.

feature: Wrapper environment variables
detail: Wrappers receive session token, creator email, client platform, Claude binary path, session IDs, Slack thread/channel IDs for Claude Tag, config dir, MCP config path, base URL and OAuth token.

feature: Inference OAuth token rotation over stdin
detail: The per-session inference token lives about 30 minutes and is rotated via the child's stdin, so wrappers must keep stdin attached or calls fail with 401.

feature: System prompt flags delivered as files
detail: The control plane's system and appended prompts reach wrappers as file paths; appended file flags replace rather than add, and custom text belongs in the image CLAUDE.md or --append-system-prompt.

feature: Provision credentials scoped to session creator
detail: A wrapper can decode the session token and exchange the creator identity for short-lived cloud credentials before launching Claude.

feature: Lifecycle hook: checkout
detail: Replaces the built-in clone/fetch per repository, e.g. to use a mirror, archive or per-session git auth; failures fail the session for push repos and skip read-only repos.

feature: Lifecycle hook: post-session
detail: Runs after the child exits to snapshot uncommitted work, archive logs or emit events; exit reason is completed, failed, interrupted or abandoned; failures are logged and ignored.

feature: Lifecycle hook: command
detail: Replaces the built-in child spawn so all customization can live in the hooks directory; --exec-path takes precedence.

feature: Git configuration fixed inside lifecycle hooks
detail: Hooks run with disabled git hooks, fsmonitor, restricted protocols (https, http, ssh), ignored sshCommand/askPass from config files and runner-set gpg programs, overridable via env pairs.

feature: On-demand runners via orchestrator
detail: A stateless orchestrator polls for spawn requests and runs a spawn-runner hook that submits a Kubernetes Job, VM or similar; each runner gets a single-use work order and the secret stays off session hosts.

feature: Spawn-runner hook contract
detail: Hook must be idempotent on order ID, not retry, use exit codes (0 submitted, 1 retryable, 2+ blocks session until new message or Owner Retry) and have a spawn timeout covering p99 boot.

feature: Retry blocked sessions from Activity tab
detail: Owners can select Retry on a failed or blocked session in the environment's Activity tab to re-request a runner.

feature: Spawn reason values
detail: The hook receives why a spawn was requested (session_created, no_runner_registered, hook_failed, runner_lost, runner_reported_failure, resumed, requeued, server_retry, prewarm).

feature: Pre-warming standby runners
detail: --min-idle makes the orchestrator keep standby runners that register unbound and claim queued work; they self-exit via --exit-if-unused-min.

feature: Make on-demand runners exit when idle
detail: Hooks pass release-idle and kill-after flags so runners release idle sessions and exit, with workloads removed afterward.

feature: Orchestrator graceful stop
detail: --shutdown-drain-sec lets in-flight spawn hooks finish on SIGTERM; guidance sizes it as hook timeout plus 10 seconds with a stop timeout 15 seconds longer.

feature: Send model requests to Amazon Bedrock
detail: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK and a region on the runner routes session inference to the customer's AWS account with scoped IAM credentials.

feature: Send model requests to Google Cloud Agent Platform
detail: Setting the Vertex variables, region and project on the runner routes inference to the customer's Google Cloud account.

feature: Differences on Bedrock/Agent Platform sessions
detail: Server-managed settings and org policies, account skills and file attachments do not reach these sessions; model env vars are stripped; web search is unavailable on Bedrock and fast mode on both.

feature: MCP servers baked into the runner image
detail: claude mcp add --scope user in the image seeds MCP servers into every session; managed MCP file, managedMcpServers, repo .mcp.json and --mcp-config are other sources.

feature: claude.ai connectors delivered to self-hosted sessions
detail: When enabled, org connectors reach interactively created sessions through api.anthropic.com; CLI-dispatched sessions get none, and a same-named local server is not connected.

feature: MCP startup wait settings
detail: Sessions wait up to 5 seconds for alwaysLoad HTTP/SSE servers and 2 seconds on the first turn for stdio servers, tunable by env vars.

feature: Turn off Claude Code Remote built-in MCP server
detail: Deny rules (server-level or per tool) disable the built-in server used to create scheduled tasks, steer other sessions, add repositories and follow PRs.

feature: Stop hook that nudges Claude to commit and push
detail: Reference Stop hook for runners that prompts once per turn to commit and push, so the Create PR button activates and work survives idle release.

feature: Permission modes in self-hosted sessions
detail: Default config pre-approves routine tools and file edits; unanswered prompts stall until the user responds in the UI.

feature: Pin auto permission mode from wrapper
detail: Appending --permission-mode auto in a wrapper starts sessions in auto mode until a client sets a mode; recommended only with default-deny egress.

feature: Pre-approve tools via --allowed-tools in wrapper
detail: Allowed and disallowed tool flags accumulate on top of control-plane rules, letting operators pre-approve or deny specific tools.

feature: Session config seeded from host ~/.claude snapshot
detail: settings.json, CLAUDE.md, hooks, agents, commands and skills in the runner image apply to every session as a baseline, captured once at runner start.

feature: Skills in self-hosted sessions
detail: A person's own sessions download account-enabled skills; scheduled-task runs and Bedrock/Agent Platform sessions do not, so skills must be in the image or repo.

feature: Auto memory off by default in self-hosted sessions
detail: Outside Claude Tag, sessions run with auto memory off; persistent instructions go in the image or repository CLAUDE.md.

feature: Force remote settings refresh
detail: forceRemoteSettingsRefresh in managed-settings.json blocks session start when server-managed settings cannot be fetched; not usable for Claude Tag channel sessions.

feature: Repository settings in multi-repo sessions
detail: Only one repository's settings and .mcp.json apply depending on capacity and checkout hook; project threads load none; every repo's CLAUDE.md loads.

feature: Repo-committed permission rule restrictions
detail: Bare Edit/Write/NotebookEdit allow rules in a repository are flagged by the confine guard; defaultMode auto is honored only from image or user-level settings.

feature: Control-plane supplied hooks for Claude Tag
detail: The runner installs hooks from Anthropic (needing python3, v2.1.229+) alongside customer config, e.g. one that has Claude post its Slack reply.

feature: Production hardening checklist
detail: Ephemeral per-session containers, no broad credentials in the image, host GitHub creds kept from sessions, secret off session hosts, default-deny egress, least-privilege IAM, metadata endpoint blocked, per-runner filesystem isolation and repo-settings guard enforced.

feature: Revoke token on a suspect session
detail: Owners can select Revoke token in a session's Activity-tab menu so no runner can resume it, before rotating the environment secret.

feature: Dispatch has no per-environment access control
detail: Any organization member can dispatch to any environment; lock-to-account only bounds execution, and Owners can hide Anthropic-hosted environments so self-hosted is the only picker option.

feature: Hide Anthropic-hosted environments for the org
detail: An Owner can hide Anthropic-hosted environments from the Cloud environments page so self-hosted environments are the only choice.

feature: Network egress requirements list
detail: Required hosts are api.anthropic.com and the git host; conditional hosts include api.github.com, downloads.claude.ai, storage.googleapis.com, registries, frame.claudeusercontent.com for Artifacts and cloud provider endpoints.

feature: Authenticate to an egress proxy
detail: A local listener on the runner adds a rotating Proxy-Authorization header for the runner, hooks and sessions; runner refuses to start with conflicting or missing proxy settings.

feature: IP allowlisting for self-hosted runners
detail: Orgs with IP allowlisting must add runner, session container and orchestrator public egress addresses, though it should not replace network egress control.

feature: Runner-configured git identity and signing
detail: --configure-git sets user Claude, SSH commit signing via Anthropic's service verifiable on GitHub, push negotiation and a Co-authored-by trailer hook.

feature: Claude-Session trailer in commits and PR descriptions
detail: Claude Code adds a session-URL trailer to commits and PR descriptions; attribution.sessionUrl false in runner settings removes it.

feature: Anthropic-managed git proxy
detail: For github.com repositories Anthropic serves git using the creator's GitHub OAuth token (or the org GitHub App for bot sessions); limits include github.com only, branch pushes only, capacity 1 and replaced global git config.

feature: Built-in gh api command
detail: On runners using Anthropic-managed git, a built-in gh supports only gh api for REST calls such as opening PRs; absent if the image includes the GitHub CLI.

feature: GitHub CLI with per-session GH_TOKEN
detail: If the image includes gh, a wrapper should mint a short-lived least-scoped GH_TOKEN per session and api.github.com egress is needed.

feature: Private CA trust with Anthropic-managed git
detail: GIT_SSL_CAINFO and system CA stores are supported with a per-session certificate bundle; GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY does not bypass checks for the runner's own clone.

feature: Add github.com repos to Claude Tag channel sessions
detail: Requires the Claude GitHub App installed, the GitHub org linked under Git providers, and the repository granted to the channel in Claude Tag admin settings.

feature: Start a session on non-GitHub repositories
detail: From a terminal checkout, claude -p --environment <id> runs a session on another git host if the origin is owner/name on a domain and runner credentials work.

feature: Build your own runner image
detail: Anthropic publishes no runner image; customers build one around the claude binary (Linux x64/arm64/musl) with git, jq, python3 and toolchains, and pin versions via build args.

feature: Sizing CPU, memory and process limits
detail: Guidance starts at 4 GiB memory and 2-4 CPUs per session, one session per container for memory isolation, and process/thread limit sizing with measurement steps.

feature: Kubernetes runner Deployment recipe
detail: Example Deployment with secret volume, health probes on /healthz and a 90-second termination grace period.

feature: Docker Compose runner recipe
detail: Example Compose service with restart always and 90-second stop grace, intended for evaluation rather than production isolation.

feature: Shutdown timing and graceful drain
detail: On SIGTERM the runner stops accepting sessions, waits for turns, terminates session trees and runs post-session hooks; the stop timeout must cover the logged time (80 seconds default).

feature: Post a status message on an environment
detail: Owners can post a message (with expiry) from the Cloud environments page that members see in their claude.ai/code sessions before a restart.

feature: Defer drain past first signal
detail: --defer-shutdown-max-min keeps serving sessions after the first signal, then releases and drains in stages; requires a longer stop timeout.

feature: Consistent base directory and capacity across runners
detail: All runners in an environment should share --base-dir and --capacity so resumed sessions keep the same working paths.

feature: Reuse a pre-warmed checkout
detail: A clone baked into the image or on a persistent volume (for account-locked runners) skips cold clones; capacity 1 resets hard while higher capacity uses worktrees.

feature: Pin and upgrade runner version
detail: Sessions run the runner's own binary with auto-update off; fleets pin versions in the image, check model-required versions, and plugins auto-update only with FORCE_AUTOUPDATE_PLUGINS.

feature: Scale the fleet: fixed vs on-demand
detail: Minimum replicas equal concurrently active owners; a fixed fleet scales on metrics, on-demand uses the orchestrator; idle sessions can hold slots, so release-idle and kill-after flags help.

feature: Hold an idle session while processes run
detail: --hold-idle-file keeps an idle session on the runner while a host-touched file stays fresh (under three minutes) up to a cap.

feature: Connector traffic leaves the network
detail: Claude.ai connector tools are called from Anthropic infrastructure through api.anthropic.com; allow/deny MCP server policies can filter them.

feature: Idle detection exceptions
detail: Sessions with running background tasks, non-MCP tool approvals or MCP elicitation requests do not count as idle, so kill-after-min is the backstop.

feature: Resumed sessions lose unpushed work
detail: A session resuming on a fresh runner re-clones, losing unpushed work unless --push-outcome-on-release is set; uncommitted changes and hook-checked repos are not saved.

feature: Known limitations of self-hosted sessions
detail: Interrupted commands can rerun on resume, repos added mid-session may fail to clone without credentials, and unconnected connectors do not appear in self-hosted sessions.

feature: runner doctor subcommand
detail: claude self-hosted-runner doctor starts an interactive session with runner logs and state attached to diagnose problems; fuller with claude auth login.

feature: Troubleshooting guide for runners
detail: Covers base directory errors, TLS inspection proxies, queued sessions due to owner locks, git auth failures, SSE stream buffering, missing branches, 401 token refresh, stale model versions and pod kills mid-drain.

feature: Runner restart-with-backoff guidance
detail: Supervisors should restart runners on exit with growing waits and alert on rapid failures; failed-start log lines use [runner:fatal] or error prefixes.

feature: Session event stream proxy requirements
detail: Proxies must pass the /worker/events/stream SSE response unbuffered and keep idle timeouts well above 15 seconds or the first message never arrives.

feature: Archive a stuck session
