feature: CODEX_HOME for alternate profile
detail: Environment variable points Codex at a different home directory, e.g. for an automation user.

feature: Audit loaded instructions via log_dir
detail: Plaintext TUI log or session JSONL shows which instruction files were loaded.

feature: Rules files (.rules) to control commands outside sandbox
detail: Starlark rules under a rules/ folder in any config layer decide which commands may run outside the sandbox. Marked experimental.

feature: prefix_rule decisions: allow, prompt, forbidden
detail: Rule matches a command prefix with optional alternatives; the strictest of forbidden, prompt, allow wins; optional justification shown in prompts and inline match/not_match tests.

feature: Compound shell commands split before rule check
detail: Simple bash -c chains joined by && || ; | are split and each part checked; scripts with redirection, substitution, variables, wildcards or control flow are treated as one command.

feature: codex execpolicy check
detail: CLI command that tests how a rules file applies to a given command and prints the strictest decision as JSON.

feature: Smart approvals propose prefix rules
detail: On escalation requests Codex may suggest a prefix rule; allowing a command in the TUI saves it to the user rules file.

feature: Project-local rules load only when trusted
detail: Rules in a repo .codex folder apply only when that project layer is trusted; admins can enforce prefix rules via requirements.

feature: Speed picker: Standard, Fast, Ultrafast
detail: Lightning-bolt control in the composer model/effort picker in ChatGPT Work and Codex app (mobile via model picker); faster modes consume more allowance or credits.

feature: Fast mode (about 1.5x on (model name) Astra)
detail: Supported on several (model name) models; also usable in the CLI and IDE extension with ChatGPT sign-in.

feature: Ultrafast mode (up to 4.5x on (model name))
detail: Available on (model name) Astra and Sol, and on some (model name) models (up to 8x for (model name) in Codex); on Pro $500 and eligible Enterprise/Edu plans.

feature: Ultrafast admin permission and spend limits
detail: Enterprise needs credit- or usage-based agreement, Edu a credit plan; owners enable models and Ultrafast separately (off by default) per user or workspace; per-user spend controls apply.

feature: Ultrafast inference residency limits
detail: Ultrafast supports US residency only for (model name) models and (model name); (model name) also supports Europe (EEA and Switzerland).

feature: /fast and /ultrafast slash commands
detail: Choose speed in the CLI; repeating the active command returns to Standard; selection is saved; /statusline shows Fast in footer.

feature: API-key sign-in bills at API rates
detail: With an API key, token rates apply instead of ChatGPT credit multipliers.

feature: (model name) retired from Codex
detail: Retired for ChatGPT-signed-in users on October 14, 2026.

feature: Subagent workflows (parallel agents)
detail: Spawn specialized agents in parallel and merge results in one reply; enabled by default in current Codex; uses more tokens than a single agent.

feature: Subagents in ChatGPT Work hosted environment
detail: Ask ChatGPT to delegate; agents run in the hosted environment and the chat shows their activity and results.

feature: Ultra intelligence level proactively delegates
detail: Ultra uses maximum reasoning and lets ChatGPT delegate to subagents on its own; only eligible accounts and supported models.

feature: Intelligence levels: Light, Medium, High, Extra High, Max
detail: Composer picker in ChatGPT Work offers these levels depending on the selected model.

feature: Subagents panel in ChatGPT Work (read-only)
detail: Active and Done lists let you inspect results but not stop or steer an individual subagent.

feature: Subagent threads in desktop app
detail: Open each subagent thread to inspect work and its summary; ask Codex to steer, stop or close them; panel lists completed ones.

feature: /subagents command and approval source label
detail: Switch between running agent threads; approvals from inactive threads show a source label and key o opens that thread.

feature: IDE background-agent panel
detail: Active subagents appear above the composer; expand to see status, stop all, or open a thread.

feature: Subagents inherit sandbox and permission mode
detail: They use the parent's sandbox, approval settings and MCP servers; custom agent files cannot override these.

feature: Built-in agents: default, worker, explorer
detail: General fallback, implementation-focused and read-heavy exploration agents ship with Codex.

feature: Custom agent TOML files
detail: Personal (~/.codex/agents) or project (.codex/agents) files with name, description, developer instructions and optional model, reasoning effort, verbosity; can disable shell, apps, plugins, memories or skills.

feature: [agents] global settings
detail: Enable/disable multi-agent tools, cap concurrent threads, default subagent model and reasoning effort, interrupt message toggle.

feature: Per-subagent model and reasoning effort
detail: Subagents inherit parent model unless set via prompt, [agents] defaults or agent file; efforts range low to ultra; Luna suggested for light work, Sol for everyday.

feature: Use Amazon Bedrock as model provider
detail: Local ChatGPT Work and Codex clients can send model requests to OpenAI models on Bedrock with AWS auth instead of ChatGPT sign-in; hosted web Work and Codex cloud are unavailable in this mode.

feature: Bedrock sign-in options
detail: Sign in another way offers Use Amazon Bedrock: AWS profile, access keys, environment variables, Bedrock API key, SSO, console login or federated credential_process.

feature: Bedrock Runtime (cross-Region) vs Mantle (in-Region)
detail: Runtime uses Global or US Geo inference profiles; Mantle serves in-Region inference and is required for hosted web search; models include (model name), Sol, Luna.

feature: Daybreak Blue and Red cyber models on Bedrock
detail: Approved customers can use Daybreak Blue and Daybreak Red ((model name) Cyber) through Mantle in a US Ohio Region after access approval.

feature: Bedrock mode limits: no Fast mode, no Runtime web search
detail: Fast mode, image generation, hosted web search on Runtime and cloud features are unavailable; feature matrix lists local features such as scheduled tasks, worktrees, Appshots, browser, Skills, plugins, MCP, memories.

feature: ~/.codex/.env for desktop and IDE credentials
detail: Desktop and IDE may not inherit shell variables, so required environment values go in a .env file in Codex home.

feature: /status confirms provider
detail: Shows which model provider (amazon-bedrock or amazon-bedrock-runtime) is active.

feature: Computer History (customization)
detail: Customization feature listed in the Codex capability matrix; no detail on this page.

feature: Linear and Slack cloud integrations, Sites, Daybreak Defense Factory
detail: Named in the capability matrix as cloud and security features; unavailable under Bedrock.

feature: Browser annotations on any site
detail: In the built-in browser people select part of a page, add a comment and send it as context to Codex or ChatGPT Work with no site changes.

feature: Browser Annotation API for site developers
detail: Sites can customize selection targets, text selection, hidden metadata, annotation requests from their own buttons, editor default mode, custom preview controls, canvas objects and mode toggling via document.oai.annotation.

feature: Annotation selection container, text selection and metadata attributes
detail: HTML attributes make a card selectable as one named object, enable drag text selection, and attach small JSON context (max six properties, 2,048 bytes).

feature: Site-opened annotation with suggested comment
detail: A site button can open an annotation with an editable prefilled comment (up to 240 units), advanced mode or screenshot omitted; only the user can send it.

feature: Custom annotation controls: color, range, select, toggle
detail: Up to 12 controls per registration let people preview changes (e.g. spacing) and compare original, then reset; manual Adjust controls only on localhost or in Codex.

feature: Canvas annotation surfaces via hitTest
detail: Apps can expose individual canvas-drawn objects with id, name and role, plus custom selection drawing and controls.

feature: Hold Space to use page controls in Annotation mode
detail: Annotation mode captures page clicks; holding Space temporarily lets you use the page; Escape cancels a selection.

feature: Site tools > Annotation features permission
detail: Users can re-enable annotation features blocked for a site; per-site setting must be on for text selection containers to work.

feature: Admin policy: Site annotation customizations
detail: Enterprise and Edu admins must allow site annotation customizations in workspace policy.

feature: Open page in ChatGPT's browser via deeplink
detail: A deeplink opens a URL in the app's built-in browser; Annotations Extensibility plugin helps add support.

feature: ChatGPT desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
detail: Installable desktop app with chat, Work and Codex modes; sign in with ChatGPT account, then start a chat, create a project or open a folder.

feature: Chat / Work toggle and Quick chat
detail: Toggle above the composer switches between Chat and Work; a Quick chat icon next to New chat starts a fast question.

feature: Run projects in parallel in one workspace
detail: Move between projects and long-running chats without losing context.

feature: Schedule a task inside a chat
detail: Create a standalone scheduled task or schedule a task within an existing chat.

feature: Appshots: send frontmost app window to chat
detail: Captures an image and available text of the frontmost window and attaches it to a chat; macOS and Windows desktop app only.

feature: Appshot hotkey: both Command (Mac) or both Alt (Windows)
detail: Default shortcut; a custom hotkey can be set in settings.

feature: Appshot destination: Automatic, Current chat, New chat
detail: Automatic starts a new chat unless a chat was used in the last 60 seconds, and consecutive appshots stay in one chat.

feature: Appshots from floating pet controls / Mini
detail: On macOS, with floating controls open and main window in background, an appshot starts a new chat from them; on Windows it opens in main app.

feature: Appshot permissions and storage
detail: macOS needs Screen & System Audio Recording and Accessibility; appshots are stored locally in the session file like attachments; orgs can disallow them.

feature: Appshot limits: Google Docs apps and CLI
detail: Some web apps give only a visible screenshot; plugins may supply full content in Work or Codex; the CLI can resume chats with appshots but cannot take new ones.

feature: Preview generated documents, slides, spreadsheets and PDFs
detail: Desktop app previews files beside the chat and can auto-open a generated file when a task finishes.

feature: Interactive HTML preview with source toggle
detail: Generated .html/.htm files open as interactive previews with rendered and source views.

feature: LaTeX editing with PDF preview
detail: Open a .tex file to edit source beside a compiled PDF; failed compile keeps last good PDF and your edits.

feature: Annotations on previews for focused revisions
detail: Point to part of a document, spreadsheet, slide, code, Markdown or site and request a targeted change.

feature: Chat sidebar: plan, sources, generated files, summary
detail: Lets you steer work while a task runs and inspect outputs.

feature: Create and download files in ChatGPT Work on web
detail: Attach sources or request documents, presentations, spreadsheets or PDFs, review in chat and download.

feature: CLI and IDE file creation without visual preview
detail: CLI has no preview or annotations; IDE edits workspace files and opens documents in compatible viewers.

feature: /theme picker and custom .tmTheme themes
detail: Preview and save a syntax-highlighting theme; add custom themes in the themes folder.

feature: Shell completions for Bash, Zsh, Fish, PowerShell
detail: codex completion <shell> generates a completion script.

feature: Ctrl+G opens external editor for prompt
detail: Opens VISUAL or EDITOR to write long prompts and returns text to composer.

feature: Codex Cloud tasks
detail: Run coding tasks remotely in their own workspace, even while your computer sleeps; review changed files, request follow-ups, commit or open a pull request; available on web, mobile and desktop.

feature: Cloud environments: default and published
detail: Start without a repository in the default environment, or select a published reusable environment (Enterprise limited to those you can access).

feature: Check out repos from GitHub or GitLab in cloud
detail: Ask Codex to use any repository available through your connected GitHub or GitLab account.

feature: Start and list cloud tasks from the CLI
detail: Begin a cloud task from the terminal and list recent cloud chats with status.

feature: Cloud environment variables, network secrets, internet settings
detail: Environment settings configure allowed network destinations and credentials for HTTPS services; saved state is reused per environment.

feature: Legacy cloud: agent internet access off by default
detail: Per environment: Off blocks the internet during the agent phase; setup scripts still have network.

feature: Legacy cloud domain allowlist presets
detail: None, Common dependencies (package registries, source hosts) or All (unrestricted), with extra domains addable.

feature: Legacy cloud allowed HTTP methods
detail: Optionally limit requests to GET, HEAD and OPTIONS; other methods blocked.

feature: Sign in with ChatGPT or an API key
detail: ChatGPT sign-in uses subscription access and workspace policies; API key uses usage-based billing and API-org data settings; cloud tasks need ChatGPT sign-in.

feature: Desktop sign-in: Continue to sign in / Sign in another way
detail: Browser flow for ChatGPT; separate path to enter an API key.

feature: codex login, login status, logout
detail: Browser login by default; pipe API key or access token via flags; status shows active method.

feature: IDE sign-in: Sign in with ChatGPT / Use API Key
detail: Signed-out screen offers both methods; profile menu shows account and Log out.

feature: ChatGPT web workspace selection and Log out
detail: Sign in at chatgpt.com, choose workspace, profile menu confirms account and logs out.

feature: Local computer access with Work Cloud requires ChatGPT sign-in
detail: Needs eligible workspace with owner enabling Work Cloud and Allow local computer access; API keys and access tokens do not enable it.

feature: Device code login (beta)
detail: codex login --device-auth for headless machines or blocked localhost callback; must be enabled in security settings or workspace permissions.

feature: Headless login fallbacks
detail: Copy auth cache to another machine or forward the localhost callback port over SSH.

feature: Codex access tokens for enterprise automation
detail: Enterprise admins can let members create tokens for non-interactive workflows needing workspace access.

feature: MFA required for Codex cloud
detail: Email/password accounts must set up MFA; social logins can rely on provider MFA; SSO admins enforce it.

feature: Login caching and credential store options
detail: Cached login shared by CLI and extension in file, OS keyring, auto or in-memory (ephemeral); tokens refresh automatically.

feature: Admin-enforced login method and workspace
detail: Managed settings can force ChatGPT-only or API-only login and a specific workspace ID; mismatched credentials are logged out.

feature: Custom CA bundle for corporate TLS proxy
detail: CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE (or SSL_CERT_FILE) applies to login, HTTPS and WebSocket traffic.

feature: Login diagnostics log
detail: Direct login writes a dedicated log file for debugging.

feature: Alternative model providers and auth methods
detail: Custom providers can use OpenAI auth, env-var key, gateway OAuth, command-backed token helper, or no auth for local models.

feature: Scheduled tasks and Scheduled inbox
detail: Recurring background tasks; a Scheduled view lists active, paused and completed tasks and recent runs, with unread indicator for runs needing attention.

feature: Web scheduled tasks use uploads, connectors, skills and plugins
detail: Created from Chat or Work; cannot access a local folder or worktree between runs, so durable instructions go in the prompt or skill.

feature: Event-triggered tasks: Gmail, Slack, GitHub
detail: Run when new Gmail mail, Slack channel messages or GitHub pull request activity occurs, with filters; cannot combine with a time schedule; related events may be batched; Run now processes pending events.

feature: Admin permission: Allow event-triggered scheduled tasks
detail: Managed workspaces control event triggers through this permission; Team Tasks run in cloud via the team service account.

feature: Desktop scheduled tasks on local projects
detail: Run in the project directory or an isolated worktree; computer and app must stay on; same task can cover multiple projects; non-git projects run in place.

feature: Custom schedule and RRULE editing
detail: Custom schedule controls plus advanced editing of an RFC 5545 recurrence rule.

feature: Schedule a task inside a chat
detail: Return to an existing chat with its context on minute-based, daily or weekly cadence, e.g. to watch a long operation or PR review loop.

feature: Ask ChatGPT to create or update scheduled tasks
detail: Describe work and timing in chat and it drafts the prompt and destination; skills can also create tasks.

feature: Invoke a skill in a task prompt with $skill-name
detail: Explicitly triggers a skill within scheduled task prompts.

feature: Scheduled task sandbox and approval behavior
detail: Runs unattended with default sandbox and approval never when policy allows, otherwise follows selected permission mode; admins can restrict.

feature: Worktree cleanup for scheduled tasks
detail: Frequent worktree runs accumulate; archive old runs and avoid pinning them to free worktrees.

feature: CLI and IDE have no Scheduled interface
detail: Use web or desktop to create and manage tasks; CLI and IDE help prepare and test prompts.

feature: Scheduled tasks on retired model need update
detail: (model name) retired in Codex Oct 14 2026; tasks using it should move to a current model.

feature: Browser: ChatGPT opens sites and acts on them
detail: Opens websites, gathers current info and takes multi-step actions while you stay in control; (model name) Astra suggested for visual judgment; not in CLI or IDE.

feature: Built-in browser in desktop app
detail: Shared view of websites and local web apps inside a chat, with its own profile separate from your regular browser; sign in directly when needed.

feature: Browser tabs: New tab, Cmd/Ctrl+T, split and full view
detail: Open tabs from the chat or shortcut; Enter full view or split view; Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B toggles tabs beside chat.

feature: Address bar search from history or Google
detail: Typing searches the built-in browser's own history, falling back to Google.

feature: Settings > Browser: history, clear data, downloads
detail: Search and remove history (if org allows), Clear browsing data by time range and type, choose download folder or Ask where to save downloads, profile import.

feature: ChatGPT can request to search browsing history
detail: With permission, may look up your built-in browser history for task context; review each request.

feature: Computer Use in the built-in browser / @Browser
detail: ChatGPT Work or Codex opens pages, clicks, types, screenshots and verifies results; reference with @Browser; cannot automate file uploads.

feature: Agent permissions for browsing, downloads, uploads
detail: Default permissions with per-site exceptions; confirmation required for submitting data, purchases, permission changes or deletion; org can restrict.

feature: Preview a local page and review beside code diff
detail: Run dev server, open local route, compare rendered state with the diff and leave comments.

feature: Annotate button: comments on elements or areas
detail: Enter Annotation mode in the toolbar, click or drag to select, save comment, then ask ChatGPT to address comments.

feature: Adjust style controls in annotations
detail: Change font, text, spacing and color values, preview on the page and send as a clearer target.

feature: Developer mode: full Chrome DevTools Protocol access
detail: Setting lets ChatGPT profile JS, read console and network, inspect DOM and styles in built-in browser or Chrome via @Chrome; needs per-site approval and admins can disable.

feature: Cloud browser inspection of web app in Codex Cloud
detail: A cloud task with browser access can start your app, reproduce a bug and verify a fix with screenshots.

feature: ChatGPT Work cloud browser (own computer)
detail: Work uses its own browser on a separate cloud computer to read, click and type on sites, keeps working when you close your device, and may combine with plugins.

feature: Take over the cloud computer
detail: If blocked, you can take control of Work's computer on mobile and desktop.

feature: Website sign-in in Work with secure form
detail: Pauses for you to enter credentials and 2FA in a secure form unseen by the model, or sign in on the page and press I'm done; iOS supports password managers; sessions persist.

feature: Cloud browser website permissions: Always ask, Auto approve, Always allow
detail: Settings > Cloud browser sets default and per-site allow/block; asks confirmation before consequential actions like payment; phishing review before sign-in.

feature: Cloud browser data: clear all or per site
detail: Settings > Cloud browser > Browser data clears cookies and signs you out; it ignores your personal browser's tabs, history and passwords.

feature: Cloud browsing availability and limits
detail: Paid plans except Free and Go, all regions; Enterprise admins must enable; website sign-in not for Enterprise or Edu; CAPTCHA sites may block.

feature: Managed browser controls
detail: Admins restrict origins, uploads, downloads and developer access on managed desktops.

feature: Plugins: reusable packages of apps and skills
detail: A plugin bundles apps (service connections), skills (task instructions), or both; named after a service or a workflow.

feature: Plugin Creator: build a plugin by conversation
detail: Mention Plugin Creator in Chat or Work and describe purpose, inputs, output and rules; attach templates; needs Use plugins permission and Plugin Creator enabled; no code.

feature: @ mention to select a plugin or skill
detail: Typing @ in Chat or Work lists matching plugins and skills to pick for a task.

feature: Edit Plugin via conversation
detail: Open Plugins, choose Edit Plugin, describe changes or replace reference files; creator and workspace admins can edit.

feature: Private-by-default workspace plugins and sharing
detail: New plugins start private; sharing to people or groups needs Share plugins permission, directory listing needs Publish plugins to workspace; recipients must install it.

feature: Plugins directory with app status
detail: Browse Plugins or Apps, see included apps, Connect prompts, and states like Disabled by admin or Admin approval required.

feature: Custom MCP server plugins
detail: Connect your own system through a custom MCP server, built with Plugin Creator and Sites.

feature: Custom GPTs retiring into plugins (Enterprise)
detail: Enterprise custom GPTs are being retired; migration guide moves workflows to plugins.

feature: Plugins GitHub import and sync
detail: Distribute workspace plugins through GitHub.

feature: Agent skills (SKILL.md folders)
detail: A skill packages instructions, optional scripts, references and assets; follows the open agent skills standard; standalone in desktop, CLI and IDE, and bundled-in-plugin skills work in Chat and Work on web, desktop and mobile.

feature: Skills sidebar section in desktop app
detail: Open Skills in the sidebar to view and explore skills from your projects.

feature: Explicit skill invocation: @ in ChatGPT, $ or /skills in Codex
detail: Mention a skill directly in the prompt.

feature: Implicit skill invocation by description match
detail: The agent can choose a skill when the task fits its description; allow_implicit_invocation can disable it.

feature: skill-creator and Record & Replay
detail: Create skills by describing them with @skill-creator / $skill-creator, or record a workflow demonstration and draft a skill from it.

feature: Skill locations: repo, user, admin, system
detail: Scans .agents/skills up to repo root, home folder, /etc/codex/skills and bundled system skills; symlinks supported; same-named skills are not merged.

feature: $skill-installer for curated skills
detail: Installs curated skills such as Linear or from other repositories.

feature: Enable or disable skills in config
detail: [[skills.config]] entries disable by path or name; bundled system skills can be turned off per project.

feature: Skills list context budget
detail: Initial skills list capped at about 2% of context (or 8,000 chars), shortening descriptions first; skills.max_context_tokens up to 10,000.

feature: agents/openai.yaml skill metadata
detail: Sets display name, icons, brand color, default prompt, implicit invocation policy and MCP tool dependencies.

feature: ChatGPT browser extension (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi)
detail: Lets ChatGPT read and act in your regular browser tabs and signed-in sites from the desktop app; all five support tab mentions and browser control.

feature: Side chat beside the current page
detail: Chrome, Edge, Brave and Vivaldi (not Opera) open ChatGPT in a panel tied to the tab, shareable with open tabs, files and connected apps; Cmd+Shift+. on macOS; chats sync with the app.

feature: Right-click Ask ChatGPT and highlighted text
detail: Send selected text or page context into side chat without copying the page.

feature: Ask about a YouTube video using its transcript
detail: With captions available, side chat uses the timestamped transcript to explain or summarize.

feature: Mention a browser or open tab with @
detail: In Work or Codex, @Chrome/@Edge/@Brave/@Opera/@Vivaldi picks the browser; open tabs can be mentioned as context.

feature: Settings > Computer Use browser setup
detail: Install button opens the extension store; Manage appears when connected; per-browser toggle controls presence in the @ menu; More browsers expander.

feature: Website access prompts: Allow once, this site, all sites, Decline
detail: Asks per website host by default; Allow for all sites removes confirmations and is marked elevated risk.

feature: Allowlist and blocklist of domains
detail: Manage next to a browser edits allowed and blocked domains shared across supported browsers.

feature: Browser history access with per-request ask
detail: ChatGPT asks when it wants history, scoped to the request, with no always-allow option.

feature: Browser extension data handling and Memories
detail: OpenAI stores browser content only when it enters chat context; Computer Use uses memories only if Memories setting is on.

feature: Chrome file uploads need Allow access to file URLs
detail: Extension setting in Chrome must be enabled for tasks that upload local files.

feature: /feedback with chat ID for browser connection problems
detail: Troubleshooting steps end with sending feedback including chat ID.

feature: Code Review plugin for pull requests
detail: Shows PR description, changed files, comments and checks in Summary and Changes tabs; connect a source account; GitHub GA, GitLab merge requests in preview.

feature: Code Review inbox: Assigned to me, my team, Authored by me
detail: Personal inbox of GitHub pull requests across repos with review status; pin PRs to the sidebar.

feature: Mark files as viewed and Stack view
detail: Per-revision viewed markers; Stack section opens related dependent PRs.

feature: Automatic cloud PR reviews and @codex review
detail: With the connector and repo permissions, Codex reviews GitHub PRs before you open them; comments show on GitHub and in Code Review; needs no cloud environment.

feature: Review with Codex and customizable review instructions
detail: Starts a review in a new chat; Review instructions gear or Settings > Code Review set cross-repo criteria; optional Comic book, Visualization or PDF explanation formats.

feature: Submit review: Comment, Approve, Request changes
detail: Chat review posts nothing until you post comments or submit; drafts stay in chat; posting sends to the provider immediately.

feature: Fix failing checks from the PR Checks section
detail: Fix attaches failing CI output to a chat message for Codex to investigate, prepared but not sent.

feature: /review for local changes in app
detail: Choose review against a base branch or uncommitted changes; reports prioritized findings without altering the working tree; requires a Git project.

feature: /review presets in CLI
detail: Base branch, uncommitted changes, a specific commit, or custom instructions; review_model config can use another model.

feature: /review in IDE with chatgpt.reviewDelivery
detail: Base branch or uncommitted changes; setting detached starts a separate review chat.

feature: Review pane scopes: Unstaged, Staged, Commit, Branch, Last turn
detail: Pane reflects the whole Git repo state, with a repository selector and All repos for multi-repo projects.

feature: Inline diff comments
detail: Hover a line and press + to attach feedback, then message the chat to address it.

feature: Stage, unstage or revert by diff, file or hunk
detail: Git actions in the review header and per file or hunk.

feature: Detached code review chats setting
detail: Settings > General > Code review: choose Detached for separate review chat.

feature: Review pane navigation shortcuts
detail: Click file name to open in editor, background to collapse diff, Command-click a line to open it.

feature: Code review in ChatGPT Work on web
detail: Upload code or use a source plugin and name the PR, branch or files; findings appear in chat.

feature: Codex SDK (TypeScript and Python)
detail: Libraries to start, continue and resume Codex threads from CI or your own app; set model, reasoning effort, sandbox, config overrides.

feature: SDK ExternalMessage, resume without history, per-turn service tier
detail: Pass tool-supplied content at lower priority, resume or fork without loading turns, and set speed tier per turn.

feature: SDK sandbox presets: read_only, workspace_write, full_access
detail: Applied when creating a thread or changing access for later turns.

feature: codex mcp-server removed in favor of app server
detail: The standalone MCP server command and binary no longer exist.

feature: Codex app-server for custom clients
detail: Open JSON-RPC interface that powers rich clients such as the VS Code extension: auth, thread history, approvals and streamed events; stdio, Unix socket and experimental WebSocket transports with auth tokens.

feature: Remote terminal UI: run CLI against a remote app-server
detail: Connect the CLI terminal UI to an app-server on another machine over ws, wss or unix endpoints with bearer-token auth; remote Code Mode host option.

feature: Thread fork, resume, archive, unarchive, delete, rename
detail: Fork a conversation from any turn (or ephemerally), reopen stored threads, archive with spawned descendants, restore, or permanently delete.

feature: Revert thread history to before a turn
detail: Removes a turn and later turns from conversation history without undoing local file changes.

feature: Steer an active turn and interrupt
detail: Append input to the running turn without starting a new one, or cancel it.

feature: Manual conversation compaction
detail: Trigger history compaction on demand; progress appears as a context compaction item.

feature: Thread goal (/goal)
detail: Set, read or clear a persisted objective of up to 4,000 characters with optional token budget and usage tracking.

feature: Thread sections and Pinned section
detail: Create named sections, move and order threads inside them; pinning moves a thread into the built-in Pinned section.

feature: Thread attachments (e.g. pull requests)
detail: Associate resources such as pull requests with a thread and find threads that reference one.

feature: Thread list filters and search
detail: Filter by section, source, archived state, working directory, title search; sort by created, updated, recency or section position.

feature: Run shell command in a thread (outside sandbox)
detail: User-initiated shell commands run with full access, default one-hour timeout, only for explicit user actions.

feature: Background terminals list and clean
detail: Experimental controls to list, stop one or stop all background terminals for a thread.

feature: Turn inputs: text, image URL, local image
detail: Per-turn overrides for model, effort, working directory, sandbox and summary persist to later turns; structured output schema per turn.

feature: Model list with reasoning efforts and input modalities
detail: Picker data includes supported efforts, default, upgrade suggestions, hidden models and text/image input support; personality selection no longer supported.

feature: Model rerouting, safety buffering and verification notices
detail: Events tell clients when a request is moved to another model, enters transient safety buffering, or needs extra account verification.

feature: Plan updates and aggregated turn diff
detail: Streams the agent's plan steps (pending, in progress, completed) and a combined diff for the turn; plan mode yields a plan item.

feature: Collaboration mode presets
detail: Experimental presets that select built-in instructions for modes such as planning.

feature: Approval decisions: accept, accept for session, decline, cancel, rule amendment
detail: Command and file-change approvals, network approvals grouped by host and port, and grantable permission requests scoped to turn or session.

feature: Agent asks the user questions (1-3 short, free-form option)
detail: Experimental tool request prompting the user, with optional auto-resolve timeout; MCP servers can send form or URL elicitation requests.

feature: Apps picker (/apps) and per-app approval settings
detail: List accessible and enabled apps; invoke with $app-slug mention; defaults and per-tool approval modes and reviewer set in config.

feature: Plugin marketplaces: add, remove, upgrade
detail: Add remote or Git plugin marketplaces and refresh them; plugin list, read, install and uninstall methods are under development.

feature: MCP server management: status, OAuth login, reload, resources
detail: List servers, tools and auth status, start OAuth, read resources, call tools, reload config; required servers block thread start if they fail.

feature: Import config from other agents
detail: Detect and import external-agent AGENTS.md, config, skills, plugins, MCP config, subagents, hooks, commands and sessions, including from Claude settings marketplaces.

feature: Lifecycle hooks list
detail: Discovers hooks per working directory; hook started/completed events for synchronous hooks.

feature: Feedback upload
detail: Submit classified feedback with logs and conversation id from clients.

feature: Rate limits, usage and earned reset credits
detail: Read ChatGPT rate-limit buckets (used percent, window, reset time, credits), token activity by day, consume earned rate-limit resets, and email a workspace owner about depleted credits or limits.

feature: Workspace messages and headlines
detail: Clients can fetch active workspace messages with notification headlines.

feature: Auth modes: API key, ChatGPT, device code, tokens, Bedrock
detail: Account state reports auth mode and plan type; device-code and gateway device sign-in supported.

feature: Windows sandbox readiness and setup
detail: Check readiness and run elevated or unelevated setup for the Windows sandbox.

feature: Filesystem API with watch
detail: Read, write, copy, remove and watch absolute paths so clients refresh UI on change.

feature: Web search items: search, open page, find in page
detail: Agent web actions are surfaced as items in the turn stream.

feature: Read admin requirements (requirements.toml/MDM)
detail: Clients read allowlists, pinned features and independent fast and ultrafast mode requirements.

feature: Codex CLI: terminal coding agent
detail: Inspect, edit and run code from a terminal inside a local repository, steering the active turn and inspecting commands and diffs as they appear; usable interactively or via codex exec in scripts and CI.

feature: Codex CLI install methods (installer script, PowerShell, npm, Homebrew)
detail: Install via a curl script on macOS/Linux, a PowerShell script on Windows, npm global package, or Homebrew cask; updating reruns the same command.

feature: Codex CLI sign in with ChatGPT
detail: On first run in a project directory, choose Sign in with ChatGPT or another available sign-in method.

feature: codex resume: reopen saved chats
detail: Reopen a recent chat from the current repository or search across local chats to return to older work.

feature: Codex CLI image input (--image or paste)
detail: Pass screenshots, diagrams or design references with the first prompt via --image, or paste an image into the interactive composer.

feature: Codex subagents for splitting investigations
detail: Codex can delegate focused work to specialized agents and bring their findings back into the main terminal session.

feature: Codex CLI live web search (--search)
detail: Switch a run to live web search for current docs or releases; search activity remains visible in the transcript.

feature: codex cloud: hand work to Codex cloud from the CLI
detail: Browse active and completed cloud chats, submit work to a configured environment, and apply results to the local repository.

feature: codex mcp: add and inspect MCP servers
detail: Add local or remote MCP servers, authenticate, and inspect the tools available in the session before use.

feature: Codex skills and plugins in the CLI
detail: Package repeatable instructions as skills and add plugins to connect Codex to team tools and data.

feature: /permissions: per-run approval and sandbox boundaries
detail: Choose when Codex may edit files or run commands without asking and inspect the active sandbox and writable roots.

feature: Dedicated code review of changes
detail: Run a review against uncommitted changes, a commit or a base branch; reports prioritized findings without modifying the working tree.

feature: Codex CLI shell completions, syntax theme, external editor
detail: codex completion generates shell completions; pick a syntax theme; open long prompts in the editor set by VISUAL or EDITOR.

feature: Choose model, reasoning effort and permissions per task
detail: CLI users select the model, reasoning effort, permissions and commands that fit each task.

feature: Codex IDE extension
detail: Work with Codex beside code in the editor, with open files and selections and recent chats attachable from the composer; review summary and focused diff in place and keep wanted edits.

feature: Supported IDEs: VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code Insiders, Xcode, JetBrains
detail: VS Code and compatible editors use the Codex extension; Xcode (coding assistant) and JetBrains (AI Chat) provide their own Codex integrations.

feature: Open Codex sidebar via icon or Command Palette
detail: In VS Code, Cursor or Windsurf choose the Codex icon or run Codex: Open Codex Sidebar; in Xcode start a new chat and pick Codex; in JetBrains select Codex in AI Chat.

feature: Delegate IDE tasks to Codex web (cloud)
detail: Keep quick work local or connect Codex web to run longer tasks, then return to review the result from the same chat.

feature: Computer Use in ChatGPT desktop app
detail: ChatGPT can see and operate graphical interfaces on macOS or Windows, for tasks like testing desktop apps, using a browser, changing app settings or reproducing GUI-only bugs; available in supported regions with Work and Codex.

feature: Settings > Computer use: Any App switch and Always-allowed apps
detail: Turn on Any App control (install prompt if needed) and manage apps approved for future tasks; separate browser or per-app controls do not grant access to other apps.

feature: Computer Use macOS permissions: Screen Recording and Accessibility
detail: macOS needs Screen Recording to see the target app and Accessibility to click, type and navigate; checked under Privacy & Security for Codex Computer Use.

feature: Computer Use runs in background on macOS, foreground on Windows
detail: On macOS a scoped task can run in the background while you work; on Windows it takes over the active desktop, so use a VM, remote control from phone, or step away with the device unlocked.

feature: Start Computer Use with @Computer or @AppName
detail: Mention @Computer or @AppName (for example @Chrome) in a prompt, or ask to use Computer Use, naming the app, window or flow to operate.

feature: Computer Use per-app permission prompts and Always allow
detail: ChatGPT asks before using an app and may ask again before sensitive actions; Always allow remembers the app and can be revoked in settings; you can stop or take over any time.

feature: Windows Computer Use always_allowed_app_ids in config.toml
detail: Persistent Windows app approvals are stored under [computer_use.windows] by executable name or app user model ID; older allow-list entries migrate, the denied list is not part of current schema.

feature: Computer Use locked use on macOS
detail: Optional setting installs an Apple authorization plug-in so a task from a connected device can use apps after the Mac locks; unlock is short-lived, screens are covered, and local input relocks the Mac.

feature: Admin controls for Computer Use
detail: Workspace admins can restrict which apps Computer Use reaches, whether approvals can be saved, and disable it via requirements.toml [features].computer_use=false.

feature: Computer Use limits: no terminal apps, no ChatGPT itself, no admin prompts
detail: It cannot automate terminal apps or ChatGPT, authenticate as administrator or approve security permission prompts; screenshots fall under ChatGPT data controls and file edits still follow sandbox rules.

feature: (model name) Astra suggested for visual Computer Use tasks
detail: Choose this model in the picker for screenshot-heavy or visual-judgment Computer Use tasks.

feature: Codex config.toml user and project layers
detail: User config at ~/.codex/config.toml plus project .codex/config.toml files, shared by CLI and IDE; project layers load only for trusted projects, and the IDE gear menu opens the file.

feature: Codex configuration precedence order
detail: Highest to lowest: CLI flags, project configs (closest wins), profile files, user config, cloud-managed defaults, system config, built-in defaults; admin requirements constrain values.

feature: Default model setting (model)
detail: Set the default model Codex uses in CLI and IDE.

feature: approval_policy setting (on-request, never; untrusted retired)
detail: Controls when Codex pauses to ask before running commands; the older untrusted value is retired with a migration path.

feature: sandbox_mode setting (e.g. workspace-write)
detail: Adjusts filesystem and network access for executed commands; .git, .agents, .codex and .aws paths are protected in writable roots.

feature: Named permission profiles (:read-only, :workspace, :danger-full-access)
detail: Reusable filesystem and network policies; three built-ins plus custom [permissions.<name>] tables chosen with default_permissions.

feature: Windows sandbox mode (MXC preferred, elevated or unelevated legacy)
detail: Prefer MXC when device and policy allow via features.prefer_mxc; legacy elevated fallback, unelevated only when elevated setup is unavailable and policy permits.

feature: web_search modes: cached, indexed, live, disabled
detail: Cached (default) serves an OpenAI-maintained index; indexed gates external access via the index; live fetches fresh pages (same as --search, default under full access); disabled turns the tool off.

feature: model_reasoning_effort setting
detail: Tune the reasoning effort the model applies when supported, for example medium.

feature: personality = none; /personality command removed
detail: Setting none drops the built-in personality instructions; friendly and pragmatic values no longer select a style and the /personality command is gone.

feature: TUI keymap customization (global, composer, chat)
detail: Rebind terminal shortcuts such as open_transcript, submit and interrupt_turn under tui.keymap; empty list unbinds; composer actions fall back to global bindings.

feature: shell_environment_policy for spawned commands
detail: Control which environment variables are forwarded to commands with include filters; optional automatic filtering of names containing KEY, SECRET or TOKEN when ignore_default_excludes is false.

feature: log_dir override and codex-tui.log
detail: Set where local logs are written; setting it also enables an opt-in plaintext TUI log; can be set per run with -c log_dir.

feature: Feature flags: apps, goals, hooks, fast_mode, memories, multi_agent, remote_plugin, shell_snapshot, shell_tool, unified_exec
detail: Stable toggles under [features]: apps, goals, hooks, fast_mode, multi_agent, remote_plugin, shell_snapshot, shell_tool, unified_exec on by default; memories off by default; enable via --enable flag or config.

feature: Deprecated web_search feature flags
detail: Legacy features.web_search, web_search_cached and web_search_request map to the top-level web_search setting and should not be used.

feature: CODEX_HOME and CODEX_SQLITE_HOME state locations
detail: CODEX_HOME relocates config, auth, logs, sessions and skills (directory must exist); CODEX_SQLITE_HOME relocates SQLite state, overridden by the sqlite_home option.

feature: Installer variables CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE and CODEX_INSTALL_DIR
detail: Skip installer prompts for scripted installs and choose where the codex command is installed (default ~/.local/bin or %LOCALAPPDATA% path).

feature: CODEX_API_KEY and CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN for automation
detail: API key for non-interactive exec/review/SDK runs, and ChatGPT or Codex access token for trusted automation, persistable via codex login --with-access-token.

feature: Workload identity variables (federation rule, identity token file, context)
detail: OPENAI_FEDERATION_RULE_ID, OPENAI_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE (OIDC or SPIFFE token) and OPENAI_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_CONTEXT (audit attribution only) support workload identity auth.

feature: Custom CA bundle via CODEX_CA_CERTIFICATE or SSL_CERT_FILE
detail: Point HTTPS, login and WebSocket clients to a PEM bundle for corporate TLS interception or private roots; the Codex variable wins.

feature: RUST_LOG diagnostics and plaintext TUI log
detail: RUST_LOG sets log verbosity (error to trace or targeted filters); codex exec defaults to error output and prints inline; codex-tui.log appears only when log_dir is set.

feature: Configuration hub: config file, AGENTS.md, subagents, speed, rules, Record and Replay, MCP
detail: Landing page listing configuration areas: customization, memories, computer history, config files, agent guidance (AGENTS.md, subagents, speed, rules), Record & Replay and MCP extension.

feature: Record & Replay: turn a demonstrated workflow into a skill
detail: Show ChatGPT or Codex a workflow and convert it into a reusable skill.

feature: ChatGPT desktop app on Linux (preview)
detail: Linux preview for Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora or Arch Linux.

feature: ChatGPT desktop app on Windows with PowerShell or WSL, Windows sandbox
detail: Use the Windows desktop app with PowerShell or WSL workflows; a native Windows sandbox provides filesystem and command isolation.

feature: Custom prompts as slash commands (deprecated)
detail: Markdown files in ~/.codex/prompts become /prompts:name commands with description and argument-hint front matter; replaced by skills.

feature: Custom prompt placeholders ($1-$9, $ARGUMENTS, named KEY=value, $$)
detail: Positional and named argument placeholders expand when invoking a custom prompt; prompts are local to the Codex home, not shared via repo, and need explicit invocation.

feature: Computer History: activity timeline turned into memories
detail: macOS desktop feature that turns activity across allowed apps and websites into summaries and a timeline ChatGPT and Codex can reference to resume work, find recent items and suggest skills or automations; replaces the Chronicle research preview.

feature: Computer History availability and requirements
detail: Off by default; macOS only, needs Memories, unavailable with an API key or Amazon Bedrock, available in supported regions including EEA, Switzerland and UK; Business and Enterprise need admin grant first.

feature: Admin: Enable Computer History permission and per-user opt-in
detail: Admins grant access to workspace roles under Workspace Settings > Permissions & roles; granting only allows members to opt in individually.

feature: Computer History data captured: interaction events, no screenshots or audio
detail: Uses clicks, typing, shortcuts, app switches and macOS accessibility text; excludes screenshots, microphone and system audio, and never includes private-mode browsing; needs no Screen Recording permission.

feature: Settings > Computer history > History timeline
detail: Timeline grouped by day and time with title, summary, contributing apps, suggested skill or automation, reveal-in-Finder and delete actions, and an Ask about your history chat entry.

feature: Computer history Permissions: exclude or include-only apps and websites
detail: Choose Exclude these apps/websites or Include only these apps/websites; app icon on a timeline item excludes that app; changes affect future history only.

feature: Computer History menu bar pause and resume
detail: The macOS menu bar ChatGPT icon shows what is captured and offers Pause and Resume; an in-flight summary may finish after pausing; turning it off stops future collection.

feature: Clear Computer History: last 10 minutes, hour, day, all, or single item
detail: Clearing deletes interaction events and derived memories irreversibly; the menu bar can clear the last session for a recent app.

feature: Computer History local storage and 48-hour event retention
detail: Event files live in the ChatGPT App Group and are deleted after 48 hours; summaries are plain Markdown files under the Codex memories extensions folder, unencrypted; OpenAI processes events transiently, does not retain or train on them.

feature: Computer History prompt injection risk and token usage notice
detail: Content from visited sites and apps can carry malicious instructions, and summarization consumes tokens; users are advised to pause around communications needing consent.

feature: Computer History troubleshooting (Finish setup, Resume, Try again)
detail: Confirm Memories is on, use the status button in settings, then restart the desktop app.

feature: Local Codex memories (separate from ChatGPT memory)
detail: Codex turns eligible prior chats into local memory files, skipping active or short sessions and redacting secrets, updated in the background after idle; off by default; ChatGPT web/Work uses account memory under Settings > Personalization instead.

feature: /memories per-chat control
detail: In the desktop app and Codex TUI, choose whether the current chat can use existing memories and whether it can feed future memories, without changing global settings.

feature: Personalization: Enable Codex memories, tool-assisted chats, Delete Codex memories
detail: Toggle memories per machine, choose whether chats using MCP tools or web search may contribute, and reset the machine's memory store (also clears Computer History).

feature: Memory config keys (generate, use, external context, rate-limit threshold, models, version)
detail: memories.generate_memories, use_memories, disable_on_external_context, min_rate_limit_remaining_percent, extract_model, consolidation_model, version and dual_write tune local memory; v2 store used on fresh homes.

feature: AGENTS.md project guidance (global and repo, closest wins)
detail: Durable instructions loaded before work from ~/.codex/AGENTS.md and repo or nested AGENTS.md files; nearer files take precedence; agent can be asked to update it after corrections.

feature: Skills: SKILL.md folders with scripts, references, assets
detail: Reusable workflows with progressive disclosure (metadata first, body when chosen), invoked explicitly or chosen implicitly; global in ~/.agents/skills or repo-level in .agents/skills.

feature: Plugins as distribution unit for skills and connectors
detail: Skills are the authoring format; plugins package skills with connectors/MCP servers for sharing across teams; skills can declare MCP dependencies in agents/openai.yaml.

feature: MCP servers: tools, resources, prompts
detail: Connect Codex to external systems such as Figma, Linear, GitHub or internal docs; servers can expose actions, readable data and prompt templates.

feature: Scheduled tasks for recurring checks
detail: Automations can run recurring checks such as daily scans for guidance gaps to suggest AGENTS.md updates.

feature: Subagents with distinct roles and tools
detail: Create agents with different prompts and tool sets, for example one for test commands and another with MCP servers for production logs.

feature: OpenAI Daybreak: GPT-Daybreak-Blue defensive cyber model
detail: Flagship model with reduced refusals for approved defensive security work like vulnerability triage, secure code review, detection engineering, malware analysis in controlled environments and patch validation.

feature: GPT-Daybreak-Red specialist cyber model
detail: Separately approved model for authorized exploit validation, penetration testing and red teaming; not default, not available on every surface, and Blue approval does not grant it.

feature: Trusted Access for Cyber application
detail: Individuals apply via an individual form and organizations via an enterprise request; access is tied to identity, workspace or API org, model and surface and is not guaranteed; it does not grant Zero Data Retention.

feature: Report cyber safeguard false positives via /feedback
detail: When a legitimate request is blocked, rerouted or limited, inspect client notices and logs and report Codex false positives with /feedback.

feature: Integrated terminal in the desktop app
detail: Run commands and inspect output inside the ChatGPT desktop app.

feature: Hooks: custom commands on lifecycle events
detail: Run custom commands when Codex emits lifecycle events.

feature: Site tools (WebMCP) and browser Annotations extensibility
detail: WebMCP lets sites expose direct tools to AI agents; annotations extensibility customizes website selection, context and controls for browser annotations.

feature: Local environments, Git worktrees and cloud environments
detail: Choose local, worktree-isolated or cloud runs; configure setup scripts and actions; create and share reusable cloud environments.

feature: Codex SDK, App Server, GitHub Action, non-interactive mode
detail: Control Codex programmatically, integrate with the client protocol, run in GitHub Actions workflows, or run from scripts.

feature: Third-party integrations: GitHub, GitLab (Beta), Slack, Linear
detail: Assign work and review changes via GitHub, connect projects and review merge requests in GitLab, start ChatGPT requests in Slack delegating repo work to Codex Cloud, assign Linear issues to Codex.

feature: Developer commands reference for app, CLI and IDE
detail: Slash commands and commands available across the desktop app, Codex CLI and IDE extension.

feature: Cyber workflow: isolated lab environment guidance
detail: For higher-risk security work, use a fresh strongly isolated sandbox per attempt without unrestricted internet or production access, and destroy it afterward.

feature: Custom permission profile with filesystem deny globs and network domain allowlist
detail: A [permissions.<name>] profile extending :workspace can deny files like .env or *.pem and allow named domains; network_proxy feature is required to enforce the domain allowlist; private addresses blocked unless allow_local_binding.

feature: Auto-review (approvals_reviewer = auto_review)
detail: Routes eligible approval requests to a separate reviewer before the action runs; requires an interactive approval policy, auto_review reviewer and an enforceable sandbox; org can replace the reviewer policy.

feature: Approve for me permission mode and Full Access warning
detail: Selecting an approved Daybreak model auto-switches permissions to Approve for me when available; enabling Full Access for such models shows a warning recommending Approve for me; managed policy is never overridden.

feature: Command rules: prefix_rule with decision prompt under ~/.codex/rules
detail: Starlark rules force review of specific commands (for example curl) even when allowlisted; per-MCP-tool approval_mode = prompt does the same.

feature: Managed organizations can exclude danger-full-access and --yolo and require Auto-review
detail: Enterprise-managed configuration can restrict approval policies, exclude full-access modes and enforce the reviewer.

feature: Desktop app general Settings coverage
detail: Settings page covers profile, keyboard shortcuts, notifications, appearance, personalization, memories and archived chats.

feature: Project and terminal behavior settings
detail: Choose where files open, how much command output appears in chats, and where terminal tabs open by default.

feature: Review delivery: Inline or Detached
detail: Under Settings > Git (app) or chatgpt.reviewDelivery (IDE), run /review in the current chat or start a separate review chat.

feature: IDE extension sync and IDE context toggle
detail: Desktop app and IDE extension in the same project share active chats and editor context; IDE context in the composer lets Codex use open editor files; chats can continue across both.

feature: Git settings: branch naming, force-push, commit and PR prompts
detail: Standardize branch names, decide whether Codex may force push, and set prompts used to generate commit messages and pull request descriptions.

feature: Integrations and MCP settings with recommended servers and OAuth
detail: Enable recommended MCP servers or add your own; OAuth flows start from the app; config shared by CLI and IDE via config.toml.

feature: Browser Developer mode: Enable full CDP access
detail: Lets ChatGPT use the Chrome DevTools Protocol for performance profiling and deeper debugging; cannot be enabled locally if the organization disabled it.

feature: ChatGPT Work uses managed environment, not local Codex config
detail: Work chats on the web run in a managed environment and do not read local config files; preferences live in ChatGPT settings and may be admin managed.

feature: /status, /debug-config and --strict-config
detail: /status shows model, approval policy, writable roots and token usage; /debug-config lists config layers and managed policy sources; --strict-config errors on unknown keys.

feature: Per-run flags: --model, --sandbox, --ask-for-approval, --profile, --search, -c
detail: Dedicated flags or -c/--config override any key for one run and have highest precedence; model availability varies by plan.

feature: TUI slash commands: /tui, /model, /permissions, /experimental, /memories, /keymap, /statusline, /title, /theme, /vim, /raw
detail: Pickers for terminal mode, model, permissions, optional tools, UI customization and editing defaults; some choices can be saved to config.

feature: Collapse turn details in full-screen transcript
detail: Under /config > Sessions, folding completed activity under each prompt; final answers stay visible and search includes folded output; off by default.

feature: IDE Codex Settings panel and Open config.toml
detail: Gear icon in the Codex sidebar opens Codex Settings for shared agent controls, with a link to edit config.toml directly.

feature: chatgpt.commentCodeLensEnabled (TODO CodeLens)
detail: Shows CodeLens above TODO comments so Codex can address them; default on.

feature: chatgpt.openOnStartup
detail: Focus the Codex sidebar when the extension finishes starting; default off.

feature: chatgpt.followUpQueueMode: queue or steer, with shortcut to invert
detail: Messages sent during a run either wait for the next run (queue, default) or steer the current run (steer); Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Enter inverts for one message; interrupt is treated as steer.

feature: chatgpt.composerEnterBehavior: enter, cmdIfMultiline, cmdAlways
detail: Choose whether Enter always sends, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends only multiline prompts, or the modifier is always required.

feature: chatgpt.localeOverride UI language
detail: Set the preferred Codex UI language; empty means automatic detection.

feature: Run Codex in WSL from VS Code on Windows
detail: chatgpt.runCodexInWindowsSubsystemForLinux runs Codex in WSL when available; changing it reloads VS Code.

feature: Chat font size settings honored (chat.fontSize, chat.editor.fontSize)
detail: Controls text size of Codex chat and composer, and of code snippets and diffs in chats.

feature: chatgpt.cliExecutable (development only)
detail: Override the bundled Codex CLI executable path; only for CLI developers and may break the extension.

feature: Dots: always-on cloud agent
detail: A persistent agent that keeps work moving across tools and projects, follows up between conversations, uses background agents in parallel and reaches out with results or decisions; runs in the cloud even when your computer is off.
plans: Pro 100/200/500, Business Premium, Enterprise, Edu, Healthcare

feature: Dots access by plan and region; usage limits
detail: Pro tiers for ages 18+ outside EEA, UK and Switzerland; Business Premium in supported regions; Enterprise/Edu/Healthcare default-on from 2026-11-18 unless opted out; dot chats do not count toward usage limits, delegated Work or Codex tasks do.
plans: Pro 100, Pro 200, Pro 500, Business Premium, Enterprise, Edu, Healthcare

feature: Create a dot on mobile, desktop app or desktop browser
detail: Setup flow: intro, name and appearance, connect plugins (skippable); same dot continues across devices; mobile web unsupported; mobile app can be set to open directly to the dot.

feature: Customize dot name, shape, color, eyes, glasses, accessories and handle
detail: Appearance is changeable anytime; the dot gets a handle like @yourname-dot that updates when you rename it; several characters to choose from.

feature: Dots draw on multiple frontier models including (model name) Terra
detail: A dot can use different models for different parts of its work.

feature: Call your dot with the phone button (type while talking)
detail: Start a voice call from the dot conversation or Call in the desktop profile; typing during a call is allowed; ending the call does not stop assigned work; dot-initiated calls planned after launch.

feature: Dot in Slack: DM, channel mention, monitoring
detail: Connect Slack in the dot profile; DM it or mention it in channels it was added to; replies to you by default, engages others if instructed; monitoring must be requested explicitly; can privately ask what you will allow shared.

feature: Dot update routing and where to be notified
detail: Tell the dot which updates stay in ChatGPT and which decisions go to Slack or another channel, and what counts as needing attention; it can message with progress or questions.

feature: Reply to dot notification inline on iOS
detail: Touch and hold the notification, type a reply and tap Send.

feature: Share photos or content to your dot via iOS share sheet
detail: Share a photo or other content from any app to the dot, review it in the composer, optionally add a message and send.

feature: Your dot iOS Home Screen widget with optional shortcut buttons
detail: Small widget shows the dot's name and look and opens its conversation; Show shortcut buttons (off by default) adds message and call buttons; needs ChatGPT iOS 1.2026.279 and dot access.

feature: Apple Shortcuts action Open your dot (Messaging, Dictation, Call)
detail: One Shortcuts action with three modes; usable from the Action button or Shortcuts widget; Dictation unavailable during a call; requires authentication.

feature: Texting your dot via iMessage or RCS
detail: Verify a phone number, save the dot's contact card and chat one-to-one with text, photos and voice messages; approval requests arrive as links; no group chats, phone calls or FaceTime; the dot can only text you.

feature: Dot memory: ChatGPT memory plus its own saved notes
detail: Carries preferences, decisions and ongoing work across conversations and channels; checks with you before sharing private-conversation information with others.

feature: Dot proactive read-only research of connected information
detail: The dot researches connected apps and keeps private notes to suggest next steps; the research tools cannot send messages, change content or control browser or computer; OpenAI does not train directly on those notes.

feature: Dot cloud computer and browser with Take over and Return control
detail: Each dot has its own cloud computer, files, software and browser sessions that persist between uses; open it from the profile under Computers, Take over to use mouse and keyboard, Return control to resume.

feature: Connect one or more of your computers to a dot
detail: Allow access from the dot profile in the desktop app on each computer; gives local files, code, apps and local Codex tasks; computer must be online with the app open; Offline status does not revoke; Revoke access removes it; separate from Codex connection and Work Sync.

feature: Private website sign-in requests and Take over to sign in
detail: When a site needs login the dot sends a private form whose credentials go to the browser outside the conversation, or you take over; Done returns control; cloud browser sessions are separate from yours and may be blocked by some sites.

feature: Save to Passwords for dot logins, confirmation required on reuse
detail: Optionally save a login; reusing a saved login for a new sign-in always needs your confirmation; an active session is distinct from a saved login.

feature: Annotate browser pages and files for your dot
detail: Use the in-app browser toolbar annotation tool, or select a region of a PDF, document, presentation or spreadsheet, add a comment and Send it to the dot.

feature: Dot cloud threads and delegated Work or Codex tasks
detail: Dot starts separate cloud threads visible as conversations in all apps, creates local Work or Codex tasks, continues local Codex tasks, and can use a Codex cloud environment for repo coding; each thread uses one computer.

feature: Dot profile Activity and Scheduled views
detail: Activity shows delegated tasks with progress, files and requests for decision, approval or sign-in; Scheduled lists recurring tasks with instructions, timing and destination.

feature: Dot scheduled check-ins and event-triggered actions
detail: Ask for a time-zone-aware schedule with a duration, or for actions when an event occurs such as a new Slack bug report; the dot confirms what it set up and the dot may also decide its own follow-ups.

feature: Dot uses plugins with existing permissions (Gmail, Drive, GitHub)
detail: Installed and connected plugins give access within their permissions, e.g. read but not send email; expired connections prompt reconnect; local skills need a connected computer; messaging channel does not grant app access.

feature: Gmail links from dot open in Gmail app on iOS
detail: Supported Gmail message links from the dot open the email in the Gmail app when available, otherwise in the browser.

feature: Dot automatic action review before sensitive actions
detail: Actions affecting accounts or sharing information are checked against instructions, permissions, custom rules and safety rules, and either proceed, need approval, or are handed to you (e.g. password changes); drafting permission does not imply sending.

feature: Wallet payments need biometric approval per payment
detail: If you use Wallet, each dot payment must be approved with biometrics.

feature: Dot custom instructions (Customize > Behavior on mobile)
detail: Dot-specific instructions separate from ChatGPT custom instructions, set by telling the dot in chat or editing under How [name] handles tasks on mobile.

feature: Dot custom rules: four handling modes
detail: Under Settings > Personalization > Permissions > Custom rules (or Customize > Custom rules on mobile): take action without asking, when you say so, ask before, or hand off to you; they do not grant app access or override safety.

feature: Admin can disable custom rules for dots; dots admin guide
detail: If the workspace disables custom rules, saved rules cannot be edited and no longer apply; admins configure dots permissions, setup, governance and Enterprise billing in a dedicated guide.

feature: Data controls apply to dot conversations
detail: ChatGPT data controls cover eligible dot conversations and work; proactive research and private notes are not trained on directly.

feature: Pause, stop delegated tasks and cancel schedules separately
detail: Pause halts only the main task (Resume continues); delegated tasks are stopped in Activity and recurring ones in Scheduled; stopping does not undo completed actions.

feature: Delete your dot (irreversible)
detail: Delete removes the dot with confirmation explaining effect on conversations, memories and scheduled tasks; cannot be undone and does not reverse actions in connected apps or sent messages.

feature: Chat vs Work vs Codex vs dot experiences
detail: Chat for answers, Work for delegated or scheduled tasks and files, Codex for software work, dot for ongoing responsibilities that can delegate to Work or Codex and report via ChatGPT or Slack.

feature: Profiles: ~/.codex/<name>.config.toml with --profile
detail: Named config layers overlay the base user config for CLI runs; the old [profiles.x] table and top-level profile selector were removed in Codex 0.134.0.

feature: One-off overrides with -c / --config (TOML dot notation)
detail: Override any key for a single run, e.g. nested keys like mcp_servers.x.enabled; values parse as TOML, falling back to string.

feature: openai_base_url for proxies and data residency
detail: Repoints the built-in OpenAI provider to a proxy, router or residency-enabled endpoint without defining a new provider.

feature: Project config ignores credential-redirecting keys
detail: Project-local .codex/config.toml cannot set openai_base_url, model_provider(s), notify, profile(s), otel and similar; a startup warning is printed.

feature: Lifecycle hooks via hooks.json or inline [hooks] (PreToolUse etc.)
detail: Command hooks with matcher, timeout and status message load from user and trusted project layers; both forms in one layer load with a warning.

feature: Enterprise MCP hooks on the cloud orchestrator for Work with local access and do
detail: Admin-defined MCP hooks run on the cloud coordinator for supported events; command, local-config and plugin hooks are unsupported there; not a complete audit trail.

feature: project_root_markers
detail: Define what marks a project root (default .git; e.g. .hg, .sl); empty list treats the working directory as root.

feature: Custom model providers (base URL, env_key, headers, wire API)
detail: Define providers beyond built-in openai, ollama, lmstudio, amazon-bedrock, gcp; static or env-sourced HTTP headers; optional standalone web search capability flag (off by default).

feature: Native gateway OAuth and command-backed provider auth
detail: Sign in through an org identity provider (with device-code for SSH) or have Codex fetch bearer tokens from an external helper with timeout and refresh interval.

feature: Amazon Bedrock provider (Mantle and Runtime endpoints)
detail: Select amazon-bedrock or amazon-bedrock-runtime with AWS profile and region; uses standard AWS credential chain if profile omitted.

feature: Google Cloud Vertex AI provider
detail: Built-in gcp provider with project_id, location (default global), gcloud ADC or credential_file auth.

feature: OSS mode: --oss with Ollama or LM Studio
detail: Run against local providers via --oss, --local-provider or oss_provider; interactive CLI prompts when unset, exec errors.

feature: Azure provider and per-provider retry and idle-timeout tuning
detail: Azure OpenAI configuration with query params, request/stream retries and stream idle timeout.

feature: Data residency API organizations
detail: Use a residency base URL prefix for API orgs; ChatGPT workspaces with residency need no custom provider.

feature: model_reasoning_summary, model_verbosity, model_context_window
detail: Disable reasoning summaries, shorten responses (Responses API only) and set context window size.

feature: Granular approval policy
detail: approval_policy can be a granular table toggling prompt categories such as sandbox_approval, rules, mcp_elicitations, request_permissions and skill_approval so others fail closed.

feature: approvals_reviewer user or auto_review; allow_login_shell hardening
detail: Route eligible approvals to Auto-review, and optionally disallow login shells for shell tools.

feature: sandbox_workspace_write options
detail: Control writable roots, TMPDIR and /tmp access and outbound network access in workspace-write mode; .git, .agents, .codex, .aws stay read-only.

feature: approval_policy untrusted is no longer supported
detail: Codex and ChatGPT Work retired the untrusted value; migration guidance points to supported settings.

feature: sandbox_mode danger-full-access
detail: Disables sandboxing entirely; intended only when the environment already isolates processes.

feature: shell_environment_policy inherit none or core, set, filters
detail: Start from empty or trimmed environment, set values, include/exclude by case-insensitive glob; legacy exclude/include_only arrays cannot be combined with filters.

feature: OpenTelemetry log and metric export (otlp-http or otlp-grpc)
detail: Opt-in export of conversation starts, API requests, tool decisions and results, with prompt text redacted unless log_user_prompt is on; admins can enforce settings.

feature: Anonymous usage analytics toggle ([analytics] enabled)
detail: Codex sends small anonymous usage and health data by default; disable analytics and the built-in metrics exporter with enabled=false.

feature: Feedback upload toggle and local diagnostic ZIP
detail: [feedback] enabled=false disables /feedback uploads in desktop, CLI and IDE; Ctrl+S in the CLI feedback editor saves a diagnostic ZIP locally.

feature: hide_agent_reasoning and show_raw_agent_reasoning
detail: Suppress reasoning events in noisy output or surface raw reasoning for models that emit it.

feature: notify external program on agent-turn-complete
detail: Run a script for desktop toasts, webhooks or CI updates when a turn completes (macOS example uses terminal-notifier).

feature: TUI notifications: method auto/osc9/bel and condition unfocused/always
detail: Choose terminal notification mechanism and whether to fire only when the terminal is unfocused.

feature: History persistence none and history.max_bytes
detail: Disable saving session transcripts to history.jsonl or cap its size, dropping oldest entries.

feature: Clickable citations via file_opener
detail: Render file citations as links using vscode, cursor, windsurf, vscode-insiders or none.

feature: AGENTS.md discovery knobs: project_doc_max_bytes and project_doc_fallback_filena
detail: Limit bytes read per AGENTS.md and name fallback filenames per directory.

feature: Desktop custom file handlers (Open in menu)
detail: Add editors under desktop.custom_file_handlers with label, icon, command, args and input mode (path, json_argument, json_stdin); IDs get a custom: prefix and can be set as preferred editor.

feature: TUI options: animations, alternate_screen, show_tooltips, notifications
detail: Toggle ASCII animations, keep scrollback by disabling alternate screen, hide onboarding tooltips, restrict notification types.

feature: review_model: separate model for /review
detail: Optional model override used only by the review command; defaults to the session model.

feature: Auto-compaction thresholds (token limit, scope, post-turn percent, compact_promp
detail: Control when history compacts automatically (by token threshold counting total or only new growth, or after a final response at a context percentage) and override the compaction prompt.

feature: model_catalog_json custom model catalog
detail: Load a JSON model catalog at startup, overridable per profile.

feature: Reasoning effort levels low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra; plan_mode_reasonin
detail: Effort levels depend on the selected model; Plan mode can have its own effort override.

feature: service_tier fast and Fast/Ultrafast mode toggles
detail: Prefer the fast tier for new turns (maps to priority); features.fast_mode and features.ultrafast_mode enable independent speed controls subject to model and account.

feature: Granular approval categories (sandbox, rules, MCP elicitations, request_permissi
detail: Each category can be allowed to surface or be auto-rejected.

feature: auto_review.policy: custom Auto-review policy text
detail: Markdown policy replacing the default reviewer policy; managed policy takes precedence.

feature: browser_use origin policies (access, uploads, downloads, full CDP)
detail: Per-origin and default allow/deny for agent browser use, including history access restriction.

feature: computer_use app rules for macOS bundle IDs and Windows AUMIDs or signed executa
detail: Allow or deny native app access by identity; default app access fallback; local config cannot relax managed rules.

feature: check_for_update_on_startup
detail: Toggle update checks; disable only when updates are centrally managed.

feature: developer_instructions, model_instructions_file
detail: Inject extra developer instructions or replace built-in instructions from a file.

feature: tool_output_token_limit, thread_unload_delay_secs, background_terminal_max_timeo
detail: Tune stored tool output size, idle thread unload delay and background terminal polling window.

feature: skills config: bundled skills, instruction inclusion, token budget, enable/disab
detail: Toggle bundled system skills, whether skill instructions enter context, a catalog token budget (default 2% of window, max 10000) and per-skill enablement.

feature: Per-app controls: enabled, destructive and open-world tool gating, approval mode
detail: Set defaults and per-app or per-tool settings for connectors, including blocking destructive or open-world tools.

feature: tool_suggest discoverables and disabled tools
detail: Allow or suppress suggestions of additional connectors or plugins.

feature: MCP server config: stdio and streamable HTTP, env, headers, OAuth
detail: Per server: command/args/env/cwd or URL, bearer token env var, headers, OAuth client and callback, scopes, resource parameter, environment id.

feature: MCP server controls: enabled, required, startup timeout, tool timeout, allow/den
