detail: Disable without removing, require readiness at startup, timeouts (10s startup, 60s tool default), tool allow and deny lists, parallel-call flag, schema compaction and per-tool output limits.

feature: Multi-agent settings: enabled, max concurrent threads, default subagent model an
detail: Configure subagent limits, defaults, interrupt message and named roles with descriptions and role config files.

feature: Persisted goals with token budget (features.goals, goals.max_goal_token_budget)
detail: Goals persist with automatic continuation; a default and maximum token budget can be configured.

feature: Rollout budget tracking (under development)
detail: Token-limit tracking with reminder thresholds and sampling/prefill weights; off by default.

feature: Code mode and context management feature flags (under development)
detail: Code mode with namespace controls is off by default; experimental context management is not available.

feature: Hook events and options (PreModelRequest, PostModelRequest, PreToolUse, Permissi
detail: Command and MCP-tool hooks per event with async mode, context size limit and Windows command override; prompt and agent hooks are skipped.

feature: Memory generation tuning keys
detail: Limits for raw memories, unused days, rollout age, rollouts per startup, minimum idle hours, rate-limit floor (default 25%), plus extract and consolidation model and tier overrides.

feature: Misc stable feature flags: unified_exec, view_image, shell_snapshot, request com
detail: Built-in tools and behaviors toggled under [features]; defaults mostly on.

feature: prevent_idle_sleep (experimental)
detail: Keep the machine awake while a turn is running; off by default.

feature: Sandboxed network proxy (features.network_proxy) with domain and Unix socket rul
detail: Experimental proxy enforcing domain allowlists for sandboxed commands, with listener URLs, upstream proxy chaining and dangerous overrides.

feature: Provider capabilities: websockets transport, remote compaction, external web acc
detail: Per-provider flags and retry, stream retry and idle timeout tuning for custom providers.

feature: tui.auto_recap, status_line, terminal_title, theme, show_server_version_notice
detail: Automatic recaps while unfocused, configurable footer status line and terminal title items, syntax theme.

feature: tui presets for ten saved prompts or slash commands (/presets)
detail: Save up to ten prompts or commands in slots 0-9 with optional labels, up to 8,000 bytes each.

feature: tui vim_mode_default, raw_output_mode, disable_paste_burst, resume_cwd
detail: Start in Vim normal mode, raw scrollback mode for copying, disable burst-paste detection, and choose resume directory.

feature: TUI keymap contexts (global, chat, composer, editor, vim...)
detail: Bind or unbind actions with normalized key names per context.

feature: Plugin marketplaces and plugin enablement config
detail: Define marketplaces from git or local sources with ref and sparse paths, default plugin activation, and per-plugin MCP server and tool approval settings.

feature: cli_auth_credentials_store, forced_login_method, forced_chatgpt_workspace_id, ch
detail: Choose credential storage (file or keyring), restrict login method or workspace, override login base URL.

feature: MCP OAuth credential store and callback port or URL settings
detail: Choose where MCP OAuth credentials are stored and fix callback port or base URL.

feature: tools.web_search object configuration
detail: Set search context size, allowed domains and approximate user location for the web search tool.

feature: projects.<path>.trust_level and notice acknowledgements
detail: Mark projects trusted or untrusted in user config; stored flags track dismissed warnings and model migration prompts.

feature: requirements.toml: admin-enforced configuration
detail: Admins pin allowed approval policies, reviewers, sandbox modes, web search modes, permission profiles, login methods, workspaces, residency (us), providers and feedback.

feature: Config server enrollment with company OAuth sign-in
detail: Local requirements can enroll Codex with an HTTPS configuration server that supplies a policy bundle.

feature: Managed per-model defaults for new threads and Auto-review required models
detail: Set default model, effort and tier for new threads, and require automatic review on named models.

feature: Admin toggles for desktop features (in-app browser, chat, dictation, voice, loca
detail: Requirements can disable the built-in browser, ChatGPT chat screens, dictation, real-time voice, local scheduled tasks, in-app updates, Appshots and device remote control.

feature: Admin toggles for Browser Use, site tools (WebMCP), Computer Use, locked use, pe
detail: Disable agent browsing and external browsers, full CDP, history access, auto-review and Always allow approvals; add request headers; block Locked Use.

feature: Managed desktop storage locations and application network allowlist
detail: Pin parent directory for new local projects and root for projectless chats; restrict desktop app HTTPS/WSS destinations to allowed domains.

feature: Managed network proxy requirements for sandboxed commands
detail: Admins set allowed and denied domains, review domains, managed-only domain mode, ports and Unix sockets.

feature: Managed hooks, MCP server identity allowlists, plugin allowlists, marketplace so
detail: Admin hooks from a managed directory, allowlists matching MCP servers by command or URL, and limits to allowed marketplace sources.

feature: Admin command rules and filesystem deny_read
detail: Enforced prefix rules that can only prompt or forbid, plus read denials users cannot weaken.

feature: Windows sandbox requirements (allowed implementations, allow or require MXC) and
detail: Constrain native Windows sandbox implementation and apply sandbox modes by hostname pattern.

feature: Local computer access with Work Cloud: policy scopes and compatibility limits
detail: With Work using local access and dots, Global policy governs the cloud orchestrator while local requirements govern the computer; enforce_residency disables Allow local computer access; some keys are rejected or partial.

feature: Agent Security UI exposes approval policies and web search modes
detail: Admins set allowed approval policies and web search modes in the UI; other requirements are TOML-only.

feature: Annotated sample config.toml covering all main keys
detail: Complete example file showing defaults for model, reasoning, approvals, sandbox, auth, history, TUI, features, MCP, providers, apps, projects, OTel and Windows.

feature: TUI notifications filter by event type (agent-turn-complete, approval-requested)
detail: tui.notifications accepts true/false or a list of event types to notify on.

feature: Terminal title and status line item IDs; custom .tmTheme themes
detail: Choose items such as app-name, project, spinner, status, thread, git-branch, model; add custom .tmTheme files under $CODEX_HOME/themes and preview with /theme.

feature: tui.resume_cwd: current or session
detail: Choose whether resumed or forked sessions use the current or saved directory.

feature: cli_auth_credentials_store: file, keyring or auto
detail: Where CLI login credentials persist; MCP OAuth store supports auto, file, keyring.

feature: AGENTS.md first-turn embedding limit (default 32768 bytes)
detail: project_doc_max_bytes caps how much AGENTS.md is embedded into first-turn instructions.

feature: Model reasoning summary values auto, concise, detailed, none; verbosity low, med
detail: Controls summary detail and text verbosity for Responses API models.

feature: Dot handles several responsibilities and keeps working between chats
detail: A dot tracks multiple tasks at once, lets you switch or reprioritize in one conversation, and decides itself when to pause and resume without fixed schedules. You can name a time or supported event to trigger work and say which results need an update.

feature: Dot delegates to parallel background agents
detail: A dot splits work among background agents that run in parallel and report back, while you keep chatting. It can also create separate visible threads and send them follow-up instructions.

feature: Dot creates local Work or Codex tasks on a connected computer
detail: A dot can start a new local Work or Codex task, or continue an existing local Codex task, on a computer connected to it; the computer must stay online with the ChatGPT app open.

feature: Dot creates cloud coding tasks in a Codex cloud environment
detail: A dot can start cloud coding tasks in a Codex cloud environment you have already set up with repository and setup config; your computer can be offline. Changing the dot's selected computer does not move existing tasks.

feature: Dot profile Activity view to inspect and steer tasks
detail: In the desktop app, a dot's profile has an Activity tab where you open a task to see progress, files, results or input requests and give instructions directly.

feature: Each dot task gets its own conversation and scoped context
detail: A new task receives instructions and context from the dot but not every past conversation; connecting a computer does not expose all existing ChatGPT or Codex conversations.

feature: Dot recurring tasks with saved schedule and Scheduled list
detail: Fixed-time work needs a saved schedule stating what to check, when (time zone, end date), what warrants notification and where to deliver. The Scheduled view lists recurring work, and the dot can list, change or cancel schedules.

feature: Dot reads and edits existing ChatGPT Work automations
detail: A dot can review what Work automations are scheduled and change a recurring task's instructions or timing when you identify it and ask for confirmation.

feature: Stopping active work is separate from canceling a schedule
detail: Halting a running task and canceling its recurring schedule are distinct actions in dots.

feature: Dot event monitoring on connected services
detail: When a connected service supports it, a dot can respond to specific events, e.g. new bug reports in a Slack channel, and prepare fixes for review. Connecting the source alone does not create monitoring; you must say which events and when to notify.

feature: Dot searches past ChatGPT conversations for context
detail: A dot can look up earlier conversations and reuse decisions from them; retrieved content is context for the task, not persistent memory.

feature: Dot keeps its own persistent notes separate from ChatGPT memory
detail: A dot starts from relevant ChatGPT memory and also maintains its own notes on preferences, decisions and ongoing work. Those notes are separate from saved memory and are not changed automatically by memory settings.

feature: Same dot reachable in ChatGPT and Slack with shared notes
detail: Messaging the dot in ChatGPT or Slack reaches one dot with the same notes; visible conversations stay separate and having information does not permit disclosing it to another audience.

feature: Dot proactive background research
detail: A dot can research sources it has permission to read and keep private notes, then surface a suggestion or question (e.g. a conflict with a draft). Proactive research does not send messages, change apps or control a browser; follow-up actions need normal permissions.

feature: Codex access tokens for non-interactive workspace-scoped runs
detail: ChatGPT workspace credentials scoped to Codex let scripts, scheduled jobs, CI and app-server automation run Codex CLI under a workspace identity without browser sign-in. Runs appear in workspace governance data.

feature: Admin Access tokens page: create, list and revoke
detail: Tokens are created at the admin Access tokens page with a name and finite validity (e.g. 7, 30, 60, 90 days, minimum one day); the secret shows once. Owners/admins can list and revoke any token; members only their own.

feature: Access token scopes: Codex and Workspace Agents
detail: When shown, a Scopes selector chooses Codex for automation and Workspace Agents to trigger published workspace agents; a Codex-only token cannot trigger agents.

feature: Workspace permission to allow personal access token creation
detail: An owner enables token creation for members in workspace Permissions and roles; it does not grant desktop app, CLI or IDE access and also requires the local Codex permission. Disabling local Codex access suspends, not revokes, tokens.

feature: Access token expiration limit
detail: A workspace owner sets the longest validity members can choose for new tokens; existing tokens keep their window. An older Codex-only dialog may offer no expiration, which is discouraged.

feature: Codex CLI login with access token or CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN
detail: Use the CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable for ephemeral runs or pipe the token to codex login --with-access-token for a stored agent-identity credential; codex app-server accepts the same credential.

feature: Token permission matrix across owners, admins and members
detail: Owners/admins see all tokens and who created them; members with permission see and revoke only their own; only the workspace owner grants or removes the permission; tokens are created for one's own identity.

feature: Admin plugin in ChatGPT Work for conversational administration
detail: Admins describe goals in plain language and the plugin reads workspace state via selected admin APIs, explains findings with sources and unverified items, and pauses for review before a supported change, then re-reads to confirm.

feature: Admin plugin: list and review workspace roles
detail: Read-only lists of built-in and custom roles, their feature permissions and assigned users or groups, plus a single-role review flagging overly broad permissions.

feature: Admin plugin: explain a user's or group's access
detail: Shows assigned roles, what access they give, overlaps and gaps, and marks unverifiable items as unknown.

feature: Admin plugin: assign an existing role to an existing group
detail: After showing current roles and the change and getting explicit approval, it assigns the role and verifies the group afterward. It cannot create roles or edit role permissions.

feature: Admin plugin: general connector permission check
detail: Checks whether a user has general connector access through roles; it cannot confirm access to a specific connector or item.

feature: Admin plugin: troubleshoot an approved change
detail: Compares an approved change record with the current workspace, checks workspace and role, confirms record owner and suggests a safe next step.

feature: Admin plugin analytics: cost and model mix, usage and adoption
detail: Read-only analyses of token use and cost by use case, model and reasoning mode, and usage and adoption by team, skills and plugins; needs connected approved data sources and reports only available fields.

feature: Admin plugin analytics: business value and Codex ROI
detail: Combines verified usage and cost with approved outcomes to estimate value and ROI by team, repository and workflow, stating formulas and limits and not claiming causation.

feature: Bulk migration of custom GPTs (admin)
detail: Admins can inventory custom GPTs, migrate eligible batches and coordinate owner testing and access checks, per the linked migration guide.

feature: Workspace permission layouts: Codex and Work Local vs separate sections
detail: Workspaces expose either a combined Allow members to use Codex and Work Locally permission or independent Codex Local and Work Local toggles; enabling one does not enable the other.

feature: Local runtime requirements via requirements.toml
detail: Admins deliver requirements.toml through cloud, device or system channels to constrain approvals, permission profiles, filesystem and network access in the desktop app, CLI and IDE extension, separate from roles and groups.

feature: Allowed permission profiles and default permissions policy
detail: requirements.toml can set a default permission profile and allow only chosen profiles such as read-only or workspace, replacing legacy sandbox-mode restrictions.

feature: Admin disable of Computer Use and browser use via feature keys
detail: Set browser_use, browser_use_full_cdp_access, browser_use_external, in_app_browser and computer_use to false in managed requirements to turn off Computer Use across surfaces.

feature: Repository-scoped config, rules and skills for teams
detail: Checked-in .codex or .agents config, rules and skills share defaults and workflows; they cannot grant workspace, model, API or connected-system access.

feature: Codex cloud admin permissions and environment management
detail: Codex cloud is off by default for Enterprise; admins grant Use Codex in the cloud and, separately, Manage workspace environments; setup covers repo connection, environments, secrets, internet access and optional code review.

feature: Plugin availability across surfaces and admin review steps
detail: Plugins work in Chat and Work on web, desktop and mobile, in Codex in the desktop app and the CLI plugin browser, but not the IDE extension; ChatGPT and Codex share one public directory filtered by workspace controls.

feature: Governance surfaces: analytics, Analytics API, Compliance API, spend limits
detail: Interactive workspace and Codex analytics, an aggregated Analytics API, a Compliance API for audit records, and usage limits and spend controls for credit consumption.

feature: Allow local computer access with Work Cloud toggle
detail: An owner enables Work Cloud then Allow local computer access so Work and dots can use a connected computer; it is disabled if any cloud policy enforces residency, gives no strict zero data retention, and turning it off interrupts running turns.

feature: ChatGPT Enterprise on AWS Marketplace data residency note
detail: Enterprise bought via AWS Marketplace has residency requirements documented in the Help Center that should be reviewed before rollout.

feature: Agent Security admin console replaces Policies and Configuration
detail: Admin Console Agent Security manages agent policies with a Global baseline plus Local and Codex Cloud environment overrides; eligible legacy cloud policies migrate into Global keeping assignments and ordering.

feature: Requirements vs Defaults in agent policies
detail: Requirements are limits users cannot override; Defaults set starting values within those limits and never override an enforced requirement.

feature: Orchestrator controls: approval policies, reviewers and web search modes
detail: Global policy sets allowed approval policies, approval reviewers/auto review and allowed web search modes; only approval policies and web search modes have dedicated UI, the rest via TOML.

feature: Admin control of apps, MCP servers, plugins, command rules and managed hooks
detail: Global TOML can restrict available apps, MCP servers and plugins, define which commands are allowed, need approval or are forbidden, and set admin hooks at task and tool events.

feature: Execution controls: shell, sandbox modes, permission profiles, Windows
detail: Per-environment settings govern login shell use, allowed sandbox modes, permission profiles and defaults, host-specific remote sandbox config, and Windows execution options.

feature: Managed networking with allow/deny domains and admin-only allowlist
detail: Manage Networking lets admins add domains as Allow or Deny and optionally restrict to admin-added domains so users cannot expand the proxy allowlist; deny-only does not allow the rest of the internet.

feature: Policy precedence across and within agent policies
detail: Across policies the higher-priority one wins; within a policy OS-specific override beats all-OS override beats Global; MDM ranks above Agent Security and the device requirements file below.

feature: Cloud browser use and Cloud network access capability permissions
detail: Under Permissions and roles, Cloud computer capabilities toggles for browser use and code/shell network access apply to Work Cloud and dots and are managed separately from each other and from Work access.

feature: Policy API and Terraform for Global settings
detail: Global agent policy settings can be managed by API and Terraform; Local and Codex Cloud settings only through the UI.

feature: Daily Usage Analytics API for ChatGPT, Codex and Work
detail: Aggregated daily workspace usage metrics for programmatic reporting, using a workspace-scoped Admin key with the analytics usage read scope; not an audit log, and must be enabled for the workspace.

feature: Plugins bundle skills and apps
detail: A plugin can contain skills (instructions, templates, reference material) and apps (tools connected to services like Google Drive or Slack); admins can read skills in a preview but cannot edit them or pick individual skills.

feature: Member plugin permissions (use, upload, share, publish, create with MCP)
detail: RBAC permissions let members use plugins, upload ZIP plugins, upload plugins with custom MCP servers, share owned plugins by person, group or link, publish to the workspace directory, and create custom app connections in developer mode.

feature: Plugin installation settings (available, installed, by role, disabled)
detail: Admin console bulk edit sets a plugin as available to install, installed by default, customized per custom role, or disabled; several plugins can be edited at once.

feature: Per-app access, tool allowlists and ask-before-use permissions
detail: Admins choose who can use each app, which read/write tools are allowed, whether newly added tools are auto-allowed, and when ChatGPT asks before using the app; a Manage Legacy Apps link opens older settings.

feature: Content restrictions (Safety and Security Controls) for apps
detail: Supported apps offer workspace limits on which content ChatGPT can access, applied on top of the connected service's own permissions.

feature: Troubleshooting Disabled by admin plugin state
detail: Checks include plugin availability, role and group permissions (Use plugins, Use apps in FedRAMP), app access, Lockdown Mode roles, and a five-minute propagation delay for role changes.

feature: Lockdown Mode restricts plugin and app use
detail: Lockdown Mode roles (and a Security setting on self-serve Business) can block plugin actions even if ordinary roles allow them; it does not affect Codex network access.

feature: Export public plugin catalog to CSV for security review
detail: Enterprise owners and admins can export public-plugin metadata (name, developer, verified flag, MCP servers, skills) from Plugins > Public; data can be 48 hours old and not available in FedRAMP workspaces.

feature: Verified-domain restriction on company app accounts
detail: When activated, employees using company-domain accounts can connect apps only in authorized workspaces; verification alone does not turn it on and existing connections stay.

feature: Workspace connections (shared accounts) for plugins
detail: Plugins can use a shared workspace account when members have permission to use it; installing a plugin for everyone does not create one.

feature: Plugins in Sites use each visitor's connected accounts
detail: Plugins in Sites run with the visitor's own connected accounts and need a separate Sites permission.

feature: Import and sync workspace plugins from GitHub
detail: Admins can manage workspace plugins from a repository via a GitHub import-and-sync flow.

feature: @ChatGPT in Slack: summarize, draft and use approved tools
detail: People ask @ChatGPT in supported Slack conversations; it uses a service account's configured plugins and workspace connections plus conversation context, not each person's private access.

feature: @ChatGPT in Microsoft Teams
detail: Same assistant available in Teams chats where an admin enables it, assigns users and grants Microsoft consent; features and conversation types can differ from Slack.

feature: Surfaces: per-workspace or tenant scope with Selected channels only
detail: Admins create one surface per Slack workspace (including each Enterprise Grid workspace) or Teams tenant, name it, choose plugins and connections, and can limit to selected channels; direct messages are not blocked.

feature: @ChatGPT in Slack and Teams excludes memory
detail: At launch the assistant neither includes memory nor uses a person's ChatGPT memories.

feature: Delegate Codex Cloud coding tasks from Slack
detail: With Codex Cloud enabled, RBAC for the service account and users, and a shared published environment, a Slack request starts a coding task that runs as the requesting user.

feature: Shared replies visible to conversation participants
detail: Responses in Slack or Teams are visible to participants, and shared company plugins use the company account's permissions rather than each member authenticating.

feature: ChatGPT Space (formerly Library) for pages, slides and files
detail: A shared workspace of pages, slide decks, uploaded files and shared content where people and agents collaborate, draft documents, edit pages and request revisions.

feature: Share pages with people or teams with view or edit access
detail: Users share a page with individuals or workspace teams at view or edit level; private chats and memory stay private but content added to the page is visible to collaborators.

feature: ChatGPT Slides: collaborative decks with comments
detail: Members create and edit decks with ChatGPT, share with view or edit access, and discuss changes in shared comments; the Windows desktop app may instead produce a PowerPoint file, so use cloud mode or web for collaborative decks.

feature: Admin Library sharing controls by workspace and role
detail: Sharing of Library files and folders can be disabled per workspace or role, blocking new shares and permission changes while existing access stays; private content remains usable.

feature: Compliance API permissions needed to export or delete Library files
detail: Admin role alone does not grant sensitive compliance access; Compliance API permission is required to export or delete eligible saved Library files.

feature: Deleting pages or Spaces moves them to Trash
detail: Deleted pages or Spaces and nested pages go to Trash; files saved separately remain when a chat or project is deleted.

feature: Sharing a project removes personal Space files from sources
detail: Files uploaded directly to the project remain; personal Space files are removed from its sources without deleting originals.

feature: Work Cloud runs tasks in OpenAI-managed VM sandboxes
detail: Cloud tasks execute on shared hosted infrastructure using the Codex harness; environments can be reused or replaced with eligible state kept, and cloud containers do not inherit local files, apps, browser sessions or private network access.

feature: App action control and confirmation levels
detail: Where supported, admins allow read-only, all or custom actions per app, and app permissions choose when ChatGPT asks: Always ask, Any changes, Important actions or Never ask; some high-risk actions can still be blocked.

feature: Personal, shared and agent-owned app connections
detail: A personal connection uses the employee's permissions; a shared or agent-owned connection uses its own account's permissions, which may exceed the requester's, so admins should scope it and limit who can use it.

feature: Cloud browser for Work tasks with separate hosted sign-in
detail: A hosted browser lets Work tasks use websites, including public forms, without the user's local profile, tabs, passwords or history; users can sign in via a secure hosted flow where supported.

feature: Website permission levels: Always ask, Auto approve, Always allow
detail: Where available, cloud browser site access can ask each time, auto-approve after automated risk checks, or always allow; none grants app permissions and consequential actions can still need confirmation.

feature: Cloud computer capability toggles: browser, network, computer use, passwords
detail: Admin Permissions > Workspace default > Let agents use cloud computers has independent toggles for browser, code/shell network access and computer use shared by dots, Work Cloud and team automations; Use password manager is a separate permission.

feature: Code and shell networking policy with managed destination allowlist
detail: Public internet access for code or shell runs can be turned off while required ChatGPT Work destinations stay reachable via an allowlist; changes apply after the current run finishes.

feature: Work Cloud retention by data category
detail: Conversations follow workspace retention (deleted chats generally purged within 30 days), execution snapshots have a separate lifecycle, Library and project files persist independently, transient Enterprise uploads can expire after 48 hours, and Compliance Logs Platform records last 30 days.

feature: Users can remove saved cloud browser cookies
detail: Hosted browser data is separate from local data and saved cookies can be cleared via settings.

feature: Enterprise Key Management for stored content and execution snapshots
detail: Eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces can use customer-managed keys for supported stored content, including hosted execution snapshots; rotating a key does not delete data and revoking access can disrupt workflows.

feature: Local computer access with Work Cloud has no strict zero data retention
detail: Cloud coordination stores task data under normal retention; organizations requiring ZDR should not enable it, and enforce_residency in any cloud policy disables Allow local computer access.

feature: Work Cloud and Work Local permissions govern cross-device sync
detail: Work Cloud and Work Local can be separate role permissions; cloud-only Work enables Cloud and disables Local, while Sync needs both and turning either off disables Sync. Role permissions have Default, On, Off states that combine additively.

feature: Compliance Logs Platform covers supported Work prompts and responses
detail: Eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces get supported Work prompts and responses and eligible Library files via compliance endpoints; connected-app calls have separate logs and not every shell command or browser action is exported.

feature: ChatGPT Work: multi-step tasks with authorized files, apps and tools
detail: Work completes multi-step tasks using a member's authorized files, apps and tools, running locally on the computer or in the cloud, sharing Codex's execution and isolation mechanisms.

feature: Local computer access with Work Cloud (cross-device continuation)
detail: Cloud coordinates a Work task and calls an online connected computer for steps needing local files or tools; users must update the desktop app, and a turn started while the computer is offline runs in a cloud container without local access.

feature: Save Work files to Library and attach authorized files
detail: Eligible uploaded or generated Work files can be saved to Library where available, and users can explicitly attach files they are authorized to use.

feature: Work network access setting: Allow public internet access
detail: Under Settings > Data controls > Work network access, users toggle public internet for code and shell commands; it cannot override an admin restriction, and turning it off leaves a managed allowlist and keeps apps, web search and cloud browser working.

feature: Cloud browser: public sites, forms, replay and screenshots
detail: Work's remote browser navigates public websites, fills supported public forms and combines app data with web tasks, and users can inspect page screenshots and browser replay in the conversation; it is separate from the desktop in-app browser.

feature: Per-site approvals in cloud browser
detail: By default ChatGPT asks before visiting a new website; users can choose Always ask, Auto approve or Always allow and allow or block individual sites, and admins can disable options such as Always allow workspace-wide.

feature: Confirmation before consequential website actions
detail: Even on allowed sites ChatGPT can ask separately before actions creating a financial, legal or account commitment.

feature: Workspace IP allowlisting limits incoming access
detail: IP access restrictions limit incoming access to the ChatGPT workspace or Compliance API, separate from outgoing agent network controls.

feature: Synced apps and disconnect behavior
detail: Changes to source content or permissions in synced apps can take time to appear, and disconnecting an app does not remove information already saved in a conversation, file or record.

feature: Work usage draws from shared workspace credits
detail: On credit-based agreements Work activity consumes credits from the same pool as other eligible ChatGPT features, varying by model, environment, reasoning or speed settings, task complexity and frequency; USD-billed Enterprise uses a separate rate card.

feature: Overage behavior and workspace overage limit
detail: With no credits left, usage pauses, or continues within a configured workspace overage limit at the contracted rate if allowed; a limit of zero blocks overage while No limit is not a spend cap.

feature: User usage limits: workspace defaults, group limits, individual overrides
detail: Admins set monthly per-user limits at workspace, group or individual level; individual overrides win, the highest group limit applies, and limits do not add credits or control Work access.

feature: Billing usage alerts with thresholds and recipients
detail: Alerts notify at configured thresholds to chosen recipients but do not stop spending.

feature: Billing credit balance, usage reports and invoices
detail: Billing shows remaining credits, downloadable usage reports and issued invoices depending on role; reports may lag and estimates are not invoices.

feature: Admin default Work and Codex model, reasoning level, speed and Fast Mode
detail: Workspace settings > Models sets the starting model, reasoning level, speed and whether Fast Mode is available; Fast Mode can use more credits on supported models.

feature: Usage Insights for workspace activity
detail: An Insights overview with category details helps admins see what activity drives usage.

feature: Work Local runs tasks on the user's computer via the desktop app
detail: Local tasks use approved files, apps and browser sessions through the desktop app; with Local computer access with Work Cloud, cloud coordinates and calls the online connected computer, and file excerpts or screenshots may still be sent to OpenAI services.

feature: Computer Use operates approved native applications
detail: Computer Use acts through native apps under their permissions; admins can restrict which apps it may operate and whether approvals are saved. It cannot approve OS security prompts, authenticate as admin, or automate terminals or ChatGPT itself, and users can stop a task any time.

feature: macOS Computer Use needs Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions
detail: On macOS Screen Recording lets it see app content and Accessibility lets it click and type, with supported tasks running in the background; on Windows it uses the active visible desktop and cannot run in the background.

feature: Locked Use continues Computer Use after the Mac locks
detail: Optional macOS setting installs an authorization plugin that temporarily unlocks the Mac for a trusted Computer Use turn across all displays, relocking and pausing if local input is detected; admins can prevent enabling it.

feature: Desktop in-app browser with separate profile and no file uploads
detail: The built-in browser uses its own profile where users can sign in; managed Browser Use policies can restrict sites and capabilities, and it cannot automate file uploads.

feature: Chrome extension acts in existing tabs and signed-in accounts
detail: With extension and website access approved, agents can interact with existing tabs and signed-in accounts; managed Browser Use policies apply, and OpenAI keeps no complete record of extension actions.

feature: Managed Browser Use policies: sites, uploads, downloads, history, CDP
detail: Admins can restrict site access, uploads, downloads, browser history access, full Chrome DevTools Protocol access, auto-approval review, saved approvals and approval duration; a user approval cannot override an admin denial.

feature: Cloud browser website sign-in unavailable in Enterprise and Edu
detail: The hosted browser does not inherit local sign-ins and its website sign-in flow is not offered in Enterprise or Edu workspaces.

feature: Plugin and app defaults by plan
detail: New Enterprise and Edu workspaces start with a selected app set enabled (not Healthcare) and new plugins and apps are disabled by default; Business apps are enabled by default; admins can change availability.

feature: Managed feature flags to disable Computer Use, browser, apps and plugins
detail: requirements.toml keys such as features.computer_use, allow_appshots, features.in_app_browser, browser_use, browser_use_external, apps and plugins can be set false, plus computer_use.allow_locked_computer_use.

feature: Appshots capture of frontmost window
detail: Appshots capture the frontmost window screenshot and accessible app text as task context, and admins can prevent them via allow_appshots.

feature: Managed network requirements via experimental_network proxy
detail: Domain rules need experimental_network.enabled=true and do not override a sandbox that disables networking; experimental, limited on Windows, and separate from Browser Use origin policies.

feature: Managed requirements delivery via workspace config, system file or macOS MDM
detail: Enforced requirements load at config load, MDM changes at next client launch, users cannot override them, and managed defaults are changeable starting values.

feature: OpenTelemetry export and Browser Use capability events
detail: Local executors export execution events to a customer OTel collector; with Local computer access cloud orchestration events do not reach it. Browser Use can emit site-access, upload and download decision events.

feature: Voice and Appshots local data handling
detail: Microphone input, frontmost-window screenshots and app text are stored locally in sessions and may be sent as task context.

feature: Continue Work across devices by choosing Cloud in the desktop composer
detail: With local computer access enabled, selecting Cloud makes new Work conversations cloud-coordinated and continuable on other devices, while Local keeps coordination and execution on the computer.

feature: Dots use a connected computer for local engineering work
detail: A dot can investigate bugs, implement changes and run builds in permitted local repos, create local Work or Codex threads, control existing local Codex threads, and use desktop apps or the local browser when cloud sign-in cannot.

feature: Connect a computer to a dot: Allow, Revoke access, offline vs disconnected
detail: In the dot's details choose Computers, Allow and confirm; offline keeps the grant but pauses local work, Revoke access removes it, and running local tasks do not move to the cloud.

feature: Separate admin opt-ins for Work and dots local computer access
detail: Owners enable Work Cloud then Allow local computer access, and dots then Allow local computer access under Use dots; both need desktop app 26.929 or higher and ChatGPT sign-in (API keys and Codex access tokens cannot enable it).

feature: Admin hook compatibility checks for cloud orchestration
detail: Cloud orchestration supports only some hooks; a failed PreToolUse hook can let the tool run and hooks do not cover every subagent path, so local-only hook workflows should stay local.

feature: Audit records for local computer access: Compliance API plus local OTel
detail: Cloud records appear as conversation_message and codex_log events, local execution emits OpenTelemetry events to a customer collector, and neither is a complete record of every local action.

feature: Local requirements precedence: MDM, legacy config, Agent Security, system file
detail: Local requirements layer from macOS MDM down through legacy managed_config.toml, cloud Agent Security requirements and system requirements.toml, with field-specific merge rules.

feature: Compliance API append-only log stream for audit and eDiscovery
detail: Enterprise Compliance API exposes immutable compliance events and files for SIEM, legal hold and investigations; not a productivity dashboard.

feature: Download compliance log files via Bash or PowerShell scripts
detail: Provided scripts list and download log files after a given timestamp with pagination, output JSONL, using a Compliance API key and workspace or org ID.

feature: Self-hosted Codex configuration server via config_server in requirements.toml
detail: For users not signing in with ChatGPT, admins point Codex CLI and the desktop app to an HTTPS server that returns a JSON bundle of enterprise-managed defaults and requirements, optionally behind OAuth with PKCE.

feature: /debug-config command inspects config layers and requirements
detail: In the Codex CLI, /debug-config shows the config layer stack and the source of enforced requirements, useful for verifying served policy.

feature: Desktop app cannot prompt for config server sign-in
detail: If the configuration server needs new sign-in, run codex login in a terminal and reopen the app; startup pauses if required settings cannot load.

feature: Connect Codex to an organization model gateway
detail: Codex can route model requests through a company gateway (e.g. in front of Amazon Bedrock) configured in config.toml with base URL, model name and wire_api responses; custom provider added via /config Sessions > Model providers in the CLI or Settings > Model Providers in the desktop app.

feature: CLI gateway setup wizard and codex doctor/status checks
detail: An optional sign-in wizard enabled by --enable gateway_setup_wizard offers a custom provider path; codex doctor and /status confirm the active provider and model.

feature: Gateway authentication: OAuth, API key, custom header, credential helper
detail: Gateway auth options include native OAuth with browser or device-code sign-in and refresh, an API key from an environment variable, a custom header, or an admin-installed credential command, with credentials delivered as bearer, cookie or header.

feature: Use ChatGPT workspace sign-in alongside a gateway
detail: With requires_openai_auth set, users sign into their ChatGPT workspace for first-party plugins and workspace controls while the gateway handles model requests with its own credential in a separate header or cookie.

feature: Model catalog for gateway: built-in name, catalog URL or local file
detail: Custom aliases need Codex-compatible metadata via a catalog endpoint, a model_catalog_json file, or a built-in recognized model name.

feature: Voice sessions use a separate route from the model gateway
detail: Only model-provider requests go through the gateway; voice, workspace sign-in, MCP servers and plugins can use other network paths.

feature: Connect Codex to Google Cloud Vertex AI
detail: Sign in another way > Use Google Cloud with project ID, location (default global) and ADC or a credential file lets Codex call OpenAI models on Vertex; needs CLI 0.167.0+ or a recent desktop app, and the model must be enabled for the project.

feature: MDM policies for the desktop in-app browser (Chrome Enterprise policies)
detail: Admins can deploy 244 supported Chrome Enterprise policies (cookies, password manager, URL allow/blocklists, downloads, extensions, printing, proxy and more) to the built-in browser via Windows registry, macOS managed preferences or Linux JSON; cloud management is not yet available.

feature: Verify browser policies at chrome://policy in the desktop app
detail: Opening chrome://policy inside the in-app browser and reloading policies shows each policy's value, source, scope, level and errors after an app restart.

feature: Gateway compatibility: Responses API, SSE streaming, tool loop, headers
detail: A gateway for Codex must accept POST /v1/responses, stream SSE incrementally to response.completed, replay conversation input and function call outputs, route model aliases correctly, support token or header auth and return distinct errors; a qualification checklist is provided.

feature: Dots: personal agent for ongoing work
detail: A dot is a personal ChatGPT agent that takes on ongoing work, uses connected apps and delegates tasks to Work or Codex; members choose whether to create their own dot.

feature: Dots enterprise preview: free preview, default access from Nov 18, 2026
detail: In eligible workspaces admins can enable dots for selected roles; from November 18, 2026 members get access by default unless the workspace opts out. Preview is free, delegated Work and Codex tasks bill at standard rates, with flat-rate or consumption billing later.

feature: Dots admin permissions: use, Slack, local computer, custom rules
detail: Admin Permissions has toggles for Use dots, connecting dots to Slack, Allow local computer access and Use custom rules for dots (when off, saved rules stop applying); grant via workspace default or custom roles.

feature: Wallet permission for dots (off by default)
detail: Admins can give eligible members Use Wallet; each Wallet payment must be approved by the member with biometrics.

feature: Dot Slack options: member's Slack connection or own Slack identity
detail: A dot can use the member's Slack plugin connection from ChatGPT, or have its own Slack identity so the owner can message or mention it and its posts are visible; turning off its identity does not remove access through the member's account.

feature: Admin Console Dots inventory with pause, resume and delete
detail: Admins see all personal dots with owner, status, identity and Slack connection; they can pause (member cannot resume, billing stops), resume to prior state, or delete (removes the dot's context but not files, Codex threads or chats it created).

feature: Revoking dots permission hides and pauses the dot
detail: Removing every Use dots grant hides the dot from the member, pauses it and stops billing; restoring returns it to its prior state.

feature: Enterprise model controls do not apply to the main dot
detail: Workspace model defaults and controls do not govern the main dot; delegated Work and Codex tasks must be reviewed separately.

feature: Dots usage analytics and audit logs
detail: Workspace analytics report enabled-dot counts and active users; the daily usage endpoint tags dots with client_id DOTS; audit logs record admin pause, resume, delete and manage actions; the Compliance API holds prompts, tool calls and MCP calls.

feature: Admin keys for analytics and compliance (Credentials > Admin keys)
detail: Owners or admins create admin keys with enterprise.analytics.usage.read or CODEX_LOG access to export dots records; broad compliance access is owner-granted.

feature: Dynamic groups driven by SCIM attributes
detail: Admins define membership rules on attributes sent by the identity provider such as department, title, manager, costCenter, division, organization, userType, country, isAdmin and location; all conditions must match and membership updates as attributes change.

feature: Dynamic group editor: rules, Save changes, Re-sync and Cancel sync
detail: In Groups & roles, create a group with Dynamic group on and add attribute/operator/value conditions; Save stores rules, Re-sync re-evaluates members with a status panel and Cancel sync (which can leave partial updates).

feature: Member profile card shows SCIM attributes
detail: Admins can open a member in Identity and access > Members to see their SCIM attribute table and debug dynamic group matching.

feature: ChatGPT Edu with credit-based pricing
detail: Institutional workspace plan including file uploads, data analysis, web browsing, custom GPTs and admin controls; eligible metered usage draws on workspace credits.

feature: Edu Plus and Edu Pro workspaces
detail: Institution plans whose included usage aligns with ChatGPT Plus or Pro rate limits, with extra credits purchasable as needed.

feature: ChatGPT for Teachers (US K-12 educators)
detail: Self-serve after eligibility verification; educators create or join a school or district workspace with writing, file analysis and research tools, collaboration and admin controls.

feature: ChatGPT for Academic Researchers
detail: Verified researchers get a dedicated workspace with Pro-level rate limits and business data protections, no institutional contract; a verified email can join only one researcher workspace and new applications are closed with a waitlist.

feature: Switch between workspaces
detail: Each workspace has one plan type with its own members, settings and content; switch from the web profile menu or mobile sidebar, and switching does not move content, models or features between workspaces.

feature: Workspace analytics and Codex analytics dashboards
detail: Interactive admin dashboards report workspace-wide adoption and Codex activity; they are not raw audit logs and their fields may change.

feature: ChatGPT workspace credits and usage limits can pause eligible features
detail: On some plans Codex activity draws on workspace credits and exhausted limits can pause access to eligible features; these controls are separate from analytics and Platform API billing.

feature: Hook-based auditing with admin MCP hooks on the cloud orchestrator
detail: Where enabled, admin-defined MCP hooks run on the cloud coordinator for lifecycle and tool events, separate from Compliance API coverage.

feature: Admin controls for who can create and share GPTs
detail: Admins control who can create GPTs and whether they can be shared with specific people, groups or the whole workspace.

feature: GPT builders use approved apps or custom actions, not both
detail: Builders can use workspace-approved apps or configure actions to permitted third-party APIs, but not both in one GPT, subject to policies.

feature: Approved domains for GPT custom actions
detail: Admins restrict actions to approved external domains; with no domains allowed, custom actions cannot run, and domain approval does not replace authentication.

feature: GPT management view
detail: Admins review workspace GPTs by assigned or unassigned ownership with name, builder, custom actions, access, chat count, created and updated dates, manage sharing and ownership, and delete GPTs.

feature: Group types: manual, identity-provider managed (SCIM), dynamic
detail: Owners and admins create groups that carry custom roles; membership comes from ChatGPT admin, from the identity provider via SCIM (which can overwrite workspace-side edits), or from SCIM-attribute rules.

feature: Roles assigned to groups; permissions combine across roles
detail: Custom roles can be assigned to groups or directly to members and ordinary role permissions combine, while Lockdown Mode, seat type and eligibility still apply; group membership alone grants no feature permission.

feature: SCIM provisioning for joiners, movers and leavers
detail: SCIM provisions workspace membership and group assignments but not permissions in connected systems; leavers must be removed at the identity provider or a later sync can restore access.

feature: Dot runs on its own cloud computer with persistent snapshots
detail: A dot works from a cloud computer built on Work's infrastructure, can preserve snapshots across sessions, and can still draft, organize and use permitted apps even if browser, network and desktop capabilities are off.

feature: Owner can view the dot's cloud computer, Take over, then Return control
detail: From the dot's profile the owner opens the cloud computer to watch, takes over to do a step (for example SSO and MFA sign-in) and returns control so the dot continues; the cloud browser cannot use the laptop's VPN or device status.

feature: Private sign-in form sends website credentials past the model
detail: For supported sites the dot offers a private form whose username, password and codes go straight to the cloud browser outside the model's view; using a saved password needs confirmation.

feature: Clear cloud browser cookies in Settings > Cloud browser > Browser data
detail: The cloud browser keeps its own cookies and session tokens separate from the device; signing out or clearing a site's cookies there ends the saved session.

feature: Auto-review checks write actions before they run
detail: Auto-review reviews tool calls labelled write, such as sending an email, against the owner's instructions, Custom Rules and safety requirements, and can block or ask the owner; the dot cannot disable required checks and owner approval cannot override safety requirements.

feature: Safety monitoring can pause or stop a dot's task
detail: Monitoring watches for attempts to bypass safeguards or act outside the owner's instructions and can pause a task with a warning or stop it.

feature: Prompt injection resistance for hidden instructions in documents and emails
detail: Models behind dots are trained to refuse harmful requests and ignore instructions embedded in emails, files or web pages; only the owner or an authorized automation can direct the dot.

feature: Only the owner can direct a personal dot
detail: Messages from others, including Slack mentions, do not start work or give them control of the dot.

feature: Custom Rules: owner standing instructions such as ask before sending
detail: Owners can add rules (when admins allow them) that add approval steps, but cannot grant permissions the connected account lacks or bypass required safety checks; disabling custom rules does not force asking for everything.

feature: Standing authorization needs named action, recipients and schedule
detail: An owner can pre-approve a recurring action; changes to audience, content or timing need fresh approval, and permission to draft does not cover sending.

feature: Computer Use app approval with Always allow on delegated local work
detail: On a connected computer, approving an app with Always allow lets the dot use it without asking again; Computer Use asks separately for desktop app permission.

feature: Wallet payments require biometric approval per payment
detail: Even with Wallet enabled and a standing instruction, the member must review and approve every Wallet payment with biometrics.

feature: Dots data residency and inference residency regions
detail: Personal dots support storage in Australia, Canada, EEA and Switzerland, India, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, UAE, UK and US; inference residency covers US and Europe but not UAE; dots made in beta migrate to the workspace region within 30 days of GA on November 4, 2026.

feature: Dots eligibility: EKM, HIPAA, no ZDR, not in FedRAMP
detail: Dots support Enterprise Key Management and HIPAA for eligible workspaces, offer no strict zero data retention and are unavailable in FedRAMP workspaces.

feature: Dot memory is separate; individual dot memories cannot be deleted
detail: Dot notes and research notes persist for the dot's lifetime and cannot be removed individually; Reset or admin deletion removes the dot's chats, memory, notes and schedules, with dot-owned copies purged within 30 days.

feature: Dot conversations can contribute to ChatGPT Memory
detail: Memories created from dot chats are managed in ChatGPT Memory settings; turning off sharing does not remove context the dot already received and deleting a chat may leave a saved memory.

feature: Dot data retention by category with 30-day deletion windows
detail: Space files, pages, cached Outputs, cloud snapshots, backups, delegated Work and Codex threads and compliance logs each follow separate retention clocks; compliance logs last 30 days and Space pages are purged after 30 days in Trash.

feature: Dot Slack posts visible to channel; recommended for internal channels only
detail: Anyone who can read the channel sees the dot's posts, so OpenAI recommends internal channels and not Slack Connect channels shared with customers or partners.

feature: Admin offboarding: pause, resume, revoke dots access, delete dot
detail: Admins can find a user's agents, pause a dot (stops new and scheduled runs, not already delegated tasks), revoke Use dots, or delete it irreversibly; connected accounts, website sessions and computers need separate revocation.

feature: Compliance API records for dots: TOOL_CALL_SUGGESTED and APP_MCP_CALL/RESULT
detail: Exports tag dots with client_id DOTS and include prompts, replies, cloud browser/computer tool suggestions and connected-app MCP calls and results, though outputs may be missing; more detailed cloud audit logs are in development.

feature: Agent Security site rules for the dot's cloud browser (in development)
detail: Planned admin rules to allow or block domains in a dot's cloud browser and control per-site uploads and downloads.

feature: Messaging channels can start tasks on the member's connected computer
detail: A request sent from another device through a messaging channel can make the dot start a thread with the connected computer attached if it is available; camera, microphone and screen access depend on device permissions.

feature: Edu recommended custom roles (Core, Plus, Advanced, Power, TEST)
detail: Guidance suggests five custom roles for campus access, each with a permission matrix; built-in roles Owner, Admin, Analytics viewer and Member stay separate. Custom roles never confer Owner or Admin authority.

feature: Permissions admin: Workspace default plus per-role overrides
detail: Admin Console Policy & security > Permissions sets a workspace baseline and per-role On/Off overrides; grants from multiple roles combine, and a Test view shows effective access (updates take up to five minutes).

feature: Admin Console Roles and role groups
detail: Owners create custom roles (name, description) and assign groups to them; SCIM-synced membership is managed in the identity provider.

feature: Admin plugin: review roles and assign a role to a group
detail: An Admin plugin can compare workspace permissions to a matrix and, after confirmation, assign an existing role to an existing group; it cannot create roles or edit their permissions.

feature: Permission: search the web
detail: Role-level toggle controlling web search in chat.

feature: Permission: run deep research
detail: Role-level toggle controlling deep research.

feature: Permissions: create/manage projects and share projects
detail: Separate toggles for creating and managing projects, sharing projects, and sharing projects via workspace links.

feature: Permissions for workspace agents (browse, build, share, publish)
detail: Separate toggles to browse and run, build, share, publish workspace agents, and share agents that use agent-owned connections.

feature: Custom GPT permissions and retirement
detail: Toggles for creating GPTs, publishing to workspace or externally, allowing OpenAI GPTs, third-party GPTs or owner-approved GPTs only. Custom GPTs are scheduled to retire December 11, 2026 and migration drops custom actions and sharing settings.

feature: Permission: image generation models
detail: Role toggle for using image generation.

feature: Permissions: Voice and screen/video sharing in Voice
detail: Separate toggles for using Voice and for sharing screen and video within Voice.

feature: Permission: reference Space files automatically
detail: Role toggle letting chats automatically reference files in Spaces.

feature: ChatGPT Record and past notes/transcripts permissions
detail: Toggles for using ChatGPT Record and for referencing past notes and transcripts.

feature: Permission: run code and internet access in Canvas and code blocks
detail: Two toggles: running code in Canvas/code blocks, and allowing internet access from them.

feature: Permission: share chats and scheduled tasks in workspace
detail: Role toggle for sharing chats and scheduled tasks within the workspace.

feature: Permissions for ChatGPT in PowerPoint, Excel/Sheets, Word
detail: Three separate role toggles for the Office add-in style products.

feature: Work permissions: local, cloud, event-triggered tasks, local computer access
detail: Toggles for using Work, running it locally on the desktop app or in the cloud on web/mobile/desktop, event-triggered scheduled tasks, and local computer access.

feature: Codex permissions list
detail: Toggles for local Codex on desktop, cloud Codex, Computer History, remote device discovery/control, Windows computer-use, device-code sign-in (Codex, Excel, PowerPoint, Word), workspace environments, Codex Security, and Codex and Security administration.

feature: Cloud computer controls: browser, network, computer use
detail: Workspace capabilities let agents use cloud computers through three separate toggles: use a browser, allow network access, allow computer use; they affect Work Cloud, dots and team automations.

feature: dots permissions (Beta)
detail: Toggles for using dots, adding dots to Slack and Teams, dots local computer access, and custom rules for dots; dots is labeled Beta.

feature: Plugin and skill permissions
detail: Toggles to use, upload, share and publish plugins and skills, upload plugins with custom MCP servers, create plugins with MCPs, and install skills for others.

feature: Sites permissions
detail: Toggles for using Sites, publishing publicly, publishing with private tunnels, inviting external visitors and attaching private tunnels; new Sites in US/EU residency workspaces store and host in that region.

feature: Permissions: teams, team tasks, password manager, memory, tokens
detail: Toggles for creating teams and team tasks, password manager, shared memory, improved memory, personal access tokens, and viewing workspace members and groups.

feature: Permission: members export their own data
detail: Role toggle allowing members to export their data; Edu workspaces with data residency are not eligible for member export.

feature: Teen content filter permission
detail: Role toggle to apply teen content filters for under-18 users.

feature: Space sharing permissions
detail: Toggles for sharing Space files, pages, folders and spaces, and for workspace links; disabling does not remove access already granted.

feature: Per-role model access and effort/speed permissions
detail: Admin Console Models lets each role enable specific models, medium/high/extra-high effort, Pro models, fast mode and Ultra Fast mode; Chat effort/Pro apply to Chat while fast modes apply to Work and Codex. A Models Test checks a member.

feature: Default model, effort, speed by product
detail: Workspace defaults can differ for Chat and for Work & Codex (model, effort, speed, new chats); a default does not grant access.

feature: Credit-based usage limits by group and user
detail: Billing > Usage limits sets member limits via workspace default, group defaults and user overrides; user overrides win, otherwise the highest group limit. Alerts do not stop usage and workspace overage can be set to 0.

feature: Disable desktop in-app updates via managed policy
detail: Admins set in_app_updates=false in requirements.toml of a managed policy so the ChatGPT desktop app stops self-updating; it must be in requirements.toml, not config.toml, and users must fully quit and reopen.

feature: Settings shows Managed In-app updates row
detail: With the policy applied, Settings > General shows In-app updates as Managed; Check for Updates menu may still appear.

feature: Deploy approved versions via MDM/Intune
detail: With in-app updates off, orgs deliver pinned app versions using Intune, MDM or other tools; macOS uses a .dmg installer. No OpenAI-managed pinning or separate channel; applies to macOS and Windows desktop only.

feature: Policy targets: groups, users, platforms
detail: Managed policies for the desktop app can target Groups, Users or Platforms, edited in Raw TOML or a policy list editor, by Codex administrators.

feature: Agent security policies (Requirements, Defaults, Overrides)
detail: Admin Console Agent security holds a Workspace default policy plus per-user, group or role overrides; Requirements are enforced limits, Defaults are starting values members may change. Replaces Policies & Configuration.

feature: Agent security: Edit as TOML and copy policy
detail: Every policy can be switched between a visual editor and raw requirements.toml/config.toml text for Global or environment scopes, so settings can be copied between policies; Test policies shows which policy matches a member, group or role.

feature: Environment overrides: Local Environments and Codex Cloud Environments
detail: Policies can add environment-specific settings (optionally OS-specific) that override Global; order is OS-specific environment, all-OS environment, then Global, and higher-priority policies win over specificity.

feature: Desktop feature availability: force off browser, external browser, computer use
detail: Admins can force off the in-app browser, Browser use, External browser use and Computer use in the desktop app, and block user opt-in to Full CDP access.

feature: Browser site rules (access, downloads, uploads, debug/CDP, auto-review)
detail: Per-origin rules set access, downloads, uploads, Debug/CDP, auto-review, always-allow and approval duration (this turn or this thread); most restrictive match wins and a default row can block all sites.

feature: Browser history, saved site approvals, auto-approve admin controls
detail: Requirements can block agent access to browser history, persistent global approvals and saved site approvals, and can disable auto-review for browser actions.

feature: Site tools (WebMCP) in the built-in browser
detail: On eligible managed plans a workspace policy flag allows or turns off site tools in the desktop built-in browser.

feature: Native-app Computer Use app rules
detail: Admins allow or deny Computer Use per app by macOS bundle ID, Windows AUMID or Windows executable (publisher/product name), with a default block-all option and a toggle for saving app approvals.

feature: Allow use while locked (Locked Use) control
detail: A requirement can stop users enabling Locked Use of Computer Use on managed Macs; it does not turn it off where already enabled.

feature: Appshots and their admin disable
detail: Appshots let supported clients include application snapshots; admins can disable them with allow_appshots=false.

feature: Device remote control and admin disable
detail: Users can pick up work from another device by remote control; admins can disable it with allow_remote_control=false, which does not disable SSH remote connections.

feature: Approval policy and reviewer guardrails
detail: Admins limit approval styles (Ask when needed, Never ask, Ask for untrusted commands) and the approval reviewer, and can require Auto-review; the untrusted approval_policy setting is retired.

feature: Sandbox modes and permission profiles
detail: Admins restrict sandbox modes (Read-only, Workspace write, Full access) or allowed permission profiles with a managed default and custom profiles that extend built-ins; profiles need Codex 0.138.0 or later.

feature: Deny-read filesystem requirements
detail: Admins can block reads of exact paths or globs (such as env files or ~/.ssh) that users cannot weaken; full-access is rejected when present, and on native Windows it covers file tools only.

feature: Host-specific sandbox overrides
detail: remote_sandbox_config entries match hostname patterns so dev boxes or CI runners can allow different sandbox modes than laptops.

feature: Command rules and MCP server allowlist
detail: Requirements rules can force prompt or forbid commands by prefix pattern, and an mcp_servers allowlist enables only servers matching approved command or URL identity; an empty list disables all MCP servers.

feature: Web search mode guardrails and defaults
detail: Admins can allow only Cached or Disabled web search, set default web search mode and context; Disabled is always implicitly allowed.

feature: Defaults for apps and tools (connectors, open-world, destructive)
detail: Defaults card sets starting behavior for Apps/connectors, Open-world tools and Destructive tools for supported app tools.

feature: Managed command networking with domain rules
detail: Network use controls turn on a managed proxy with allow/deny domain rules (wildcards), an admin-only allowlist option and local network access toggle; covers command traffic only, not web search, MCP or apps.

feature: Desktop app network destination allowlist
detail: application.network requires HTTPS/WSS to exact allowed domains for the desktop app's external requests; separate from command and browser rules and not applied to Work Cloud.

feature: Use system proxy for native client requests (experimental)
detail: The experimental respect_system_proxy feature lets desktop/Codex runtime use OS proxy or PAC settings; a sign-in fallback through system proxy is on by default.

feature: Disable plugins and restrict plugin marketplace sources
detail: Admins can turn off plugins, define local or Git marketplaces, and restrict allowed marketplace sources (including the OpenAI curated one); applies to desktop and CLI, not web, mobile or IDE.

feature: Managed hooks via requirements
detail: Hook scripts can be distributed by device management and pinned on with features.hooks, and Work/dots can use managed mcp_tool hook handlers whose callback timeouts should be tested.

feature: Restrict login methods and workspaces locally
detail: Local system requirements or macOS MDM can limit login to ChatGPT, API or both, allow only approved workspace IDs, and force OS keyring credential storage; ignored in cloud-managed policy.

feature: Enforce OpenTelemetry export settings
detail: Requirements can set OTLP log, trace and metrics exporters and whether prompts, agent responses or approval assessments are logged; needs a recent desktop build.

feature: Cloud-managed requirements delivery and cache
detail: Signed-in ChatGPT users on supported plans fetch workspace policy at launch with a signed cache; load failure errors rather than silently skipping, and some changes need a restart.

feature: macOS MDM managed preferences (Jamf, Fleet, Kandji)
detail: Device profiles under com.openai.codex deliver base64 TOML for managed defaults and requirements; managed defaults override local config at startup.

feature: Legacy managed_config.toml defaults
detail: Device-managed starting defaults at /etc/codex/managed_config.toml (or ~/.codex on Windows) reapplied every launch; retained for legacy deployments.

feature: Model retirement: (model name) in Codex with ChatGPT sign-in
detail: (model name) retires from Codex with ChatGPT sign-in on October 14, 2026; pinned defaults must move to an available model and (model name) pins need migration; API-key sessions are unaffected.

feature: Policy API and Terraform for Global settings
detail: Global Agent security settings can be managed by the policy API and Terraform; Local and Codex Cloud environment settings need the UI.

feature: Local computer access with Work Cloud policy interplay
detail: Work and dots with local computer access use Global orchestrator policy plus local requirements; enforce_residency in any cloud policy disables local computer access for both.

feature: Import plugin marketplace from GitHub
detail: Workspace admins import a GitHub-hosted marketplace (repo, optional path, branch/tag/commit) via Admin > Plugins; public and private repos work, and new marketplaces sync daily.

feature: Supported marketplace formats (Codex and Claude-compatible)
detail: Import accepts Codex marketplace.json, Claude-compatible marketplace.json or a standalone Claude plugin.json; entries may be native plugins, Agent Plugins 1.0 or skill packages.

feature: Plugin installation policy per role
detail: After import admins set each plugin to Available or Installed by default for eligible roles, and enable required apps; repo settings are not applied automatically.

feature: Sync now, sync report and No longer in source
detail: Admins can force a marketplace sync; invalid updates keep the last working version, removed entries are marked No longer in source, and deleting a marketplace deletes its imported plugins.

feature: Move existing plugin to GitHub management (pluginId)
detail: Adding pluginId to a marketplace entry moves a workspace plugin to GitHub management, keeping ID and sharing; archive upload replacement then stops working.

feature: Desktop-only plugins label
detail: Imported plugins that declare MCP servers can be labeled Desktop only and cannot run in ChatGPT on the web.

feature: Plugins reference existing apps via .app.json
detail: A plugin can reference existing apps (IDs starting asdk_app_, connector_, templated_apps_) and mark them required; this grants no member access by itself.

feature: Reconnect or change GitHub owner of marketplace sync
detail: Sync uses the importing admin's GitHub connection; another admin can re-import with the same source to take over.

feature: Prisma AIRS external guardrail for Codex prompts
detail: Admins connect Palo Alto Prisma AIRS (API key, security profile, endpoint) under Policy & security > External guardrails to scan newly submitted Codex prompts for DLP, prompt injection and malicious URLs; access requires contacting OpenAI.

feature: AIRS enforcement mode and failure behavior
detail: Choose Block (default) or Alert only on flagged prompts, and Allow (default) or Block prompts when AIRS is unavailable.

feature: AIRS regional endpoints and manage actions
detail: US (default), Germany, India or Singapore endpoints; admins can test the connection, rotate the key, disable scanning or disconnect; responses, tool calls, files and images are not scanned.

feature: Service accounts for headless Codex
detail: Owners and admins create non-human workspace identities for CI or scheduled jobs, with their own roles, groups, plugins and audit attribution; available only on pay-as-you-go plans.

feature: Service-account access tokens (Codex scope)
detail: Tokens created per service account with a name, Codex scope and expiration are shown once; Codex CLI 0.142.0+ uses CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN or codex login --with-access-token.

feature: Shared-account roles: User, Configure, Manager
detail: Sharing a service account grants User (create tokens), Configure (configure plugins, enable/disable) or Manager (both); only owners/admins create, delete or share.

feature: SCIM provisioning and Admin API for service accounts
detail: Identity providers can provision service accounts with userType ServiceAccount, and the Admin API lists, creates, enables/disables, deletes accounts and manages tokens and sharing.

feature: Disable or delete service account revokes tokens
detail: Disabling or deleting an account revokes all active tokens; disabled accounts can be re-enabled, deletion cannot be undone.

feature: Workspace credit usage limits and spend controls
detail: Workspace limits apply to eligible chat and some Codex activity under credit agreements, not to API Platform billing; exhausted limits can pause eligible features.

feature: Ultrafast mode off by default in Enterprise
detail: (model name) Ultrafast is off by default; owners enable it via permissions, and per-user spend limits apply at its higher usage rates.

feature: Seat types and built-in roles (Owner, Admin, Member, Analytics Viewer)
detail: Seats decide product access (ChatGPT, Codex seats by plan); built-in roles set admin authority, with Analytics Viewer limited to workspace analytics; custom roles add feature permissions only.

feature: Custom roles via RBAC, groups and SCIM
detail: Owners create custom roles with Default/On/Off per permission, assign by group (manual or SCIM) or directly; multiple roles combine additively.

feature: Work Local vs Work Cloud permissions
detail: Workspaces show Work Local and Work Cloud (or a combined Codex and Work Local) permissions; Work Local allows desktop-app work without cloud tasks, and role cannot exceed seat.

feature: Cloud browser use and cloud network access capabilities
detail: Shared Cloud computer capabilities (browser, network) used by Work Cloud and dots are configured independently; browser and code/shell network are separate.

feature: Codex Cloud access and workspace environment management
detail: Use Codex in the cloud runs cloud tasks; Manage workspace environments (off by default) creates shared environments, while members can create personal environments.

feature: Allow local computer access with Work Cloud
detail: Owners can let Work Cloud tasks reach the user's own computer; nested under Work Cloud, requires ChatGPT sign-in, and is disabled if enforce_residency is on.

feature: Computer History (off by default, role grant, user opt-in)
detail: Computer History is off for Business/Enterprise until owners grant a role access; each member must still opt in on macOS desktop and choose which apps and websites contribute.

feature: Control boundaries: workspace, local, Codex cloud, API, plugins, connected syste
detail: A request must pass each applicable boundary; workspace access, local permission profiles, plugin availability and source-system permissions are independent.

feature: Skill distribution models: workspace skill, filesystem skill, plugin
detail: Skills can be shared as ChatGPT workspace Skills, loaded from local filesystem locations, or packaged in plugins; each has separate administration and ownership does not transfer.

feature: Plugin surfaces and universal directory
detail: Plugins work in Chat and Work on web, desktop and mobile, in Codex in the desktop app and the Codex CLI plugin browser (not the IDE extension), drawing public plugins from one shared directory.

feature: Teams in ChatGPT
detail: Teams are shared places for colleagues to organize work, created from Settings > Teams with name and optional description; team membership is separate from workspace groups and cannot sync from SCIM, Slack or Teams.

feature: Team invites, join links and ownership
detail: Members can invite coworkers and remove non-owner members, same-workspace join links need no owner approval, only the owner can delete the team, and owners must transfer ownership before leaving.

feature: Team Tasks (scheduled or event-triggered)
detail: Teams can create tasks from Scheduled > New Task with the Team toggle, a schedule or supported event trigger, instructions, plugins and model; tasks run in the cloud with the team's service account and connections, and have Run now and Previous runs.

feature: Team Task instructions do not inherit personal context
detail: Team tasks do not use the creator's memories, custom instructions or chat history, may link a team Space for shared instructions, and can use a different model than the creator's account.

feature: Team and workspace connections for Team Tasks
detail: Team tasks use company-managed workspace connections or an individually connected team connection; unattended runs cannot complete a new sign-in and can write to systems if allowed.

feature: Team activity view, pause and billing
detail: Teams have an Activity view of changes, pausing stops future runs but not active ones, admins audit via Compliance API, and tasks use workspace credits with separate team spending limits.

feature: Permissions: Create teams and Create and manage team automations
detail: Two workspace permissions govern who can create teams and who can create or edit team tasks across every entry point.

feature: Workspace connections (company-managed app accounts)
