detail: Admins authorize app accounts once under Admin Console > Workspace connections so Team Tasks and @ChatGPT surfaces use a shared account without each person connecting; connections get a nickname and per-user, team or service-account access.

feature: Workspace connection auth: Google Drive, Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Linear, Slack
detail: Supported setups include Google OAuth or Cloud service account JSON key (optionally domain-wide delegation), Gmail mailbox OAuth, GitHub user-account sign-in (app sign-in unavailable at launch), Notion via MCP, Linear via guest account, and the shared Slack connection.

feature: Connection roles: owner, availability and use vs manage permissions
detail: Use and manage permissions are reviewed separately; enabling @ChatGPT in Slack/Teams for a connection also enables its team and service-account access; disabling a connection does not revoke provider authorization.

feature: Sites: pages, forms, trackers and dashboards
detail: Sites let members build and publish pages, forms, trackers and interactive dashboards from chat; workspace admins govern creation and publishing, site owners govern audience and editors, and app code governs record access.

feature: Site audience: invitations, groups, workspace, public
detail: Owners choose visitors via individual invites, groups, workspace-wide or public access; public publishing is off by default in Enterprise and external invites can be allowed separately (Business has no separate setting).

feature: Site editors, saved versions and publish updates
detail: Editors can publish updates after the owner's first publication without owner approval; versions are saved and explicitly published, and review is organizational only.

feature: Remix an existing site
detail: Teams can adapt an existing site with Remix to reuse its layout with their own content, versus co-editing a shared site.

feature: Sites with connected apps and visitor-chosen connections
detail: Connected sites stay private to the workspace and each visitor uses their own connected account permissions; creating a site does not authorize app access.

feature: Admin Insights: use cases and tasks for Work and Codex
detail: Admin Console Analytics > Insights classifies Work and Codex usage into categories and tasks, with Use cases/Tasks toggle, messages, share of credits and active users per category; may use sampling.

feature: Insights category details: model, reasoning, speed, plugin and skill breakdowns
detail: Category drawers show credits by task, model, reasoning and speed share, and plugin and skill invocation counts across Work and Codex.

feature: Code review analytics: PRs reviewed, issues found, priority and reactions
detail: A Code review view shows pull-request review counts, issues found, issues by priority and reaction sentiment for engineering reviews.

feature: Usage analytics views (usage, tokens, filters)
detail: Admin Console offers Usage for activity and consumption (including token measures) with workspace, date and group filters; history begins when classification started.

feature: Provisioning methods: manual invite, Automatic Account Creation, SCIM
detail: Workspaces add members by manual invitation, auto account creation for eligible email domains, or SCIM directory sync (Enterprise, Edu, Healthcare); auto creation and SCIM should not be combined.

feature: SCIM-synced groups with SCIM badge and role assignment
detail: Synced identity-provider groups appear with a SCIM badge, take over matching workspace groups, and receive custom roles; syncs run roughly every 30-40 minutes and cannot be forced.

feature: Seat types and Change seat type (ChatGPT vs Codex-only)
detail: Workspaces may offer ChatGPT and Codex-only seats; SCIM users get a default seat from Identity & access; converting to Codex-only hides chats, memories and projects without deleting data; new Business Codex-only seats are restricted after June 24, 2026.

feature: Custom roles availability by plan
detail: Custom roles and RBAC are available on Enterprise, Edu, Healthcare and Teachers workspaces; Codex access tokens on Business and Enterprise.

feature: Access tokens page: view creators, revoke, scopes, expiration
detail: Admins list Codex access tokens with creator and status and can revoke any; members with permission revoke only their own; removing local Codex permission suspends but does not revoke tokens.

feature: Member removal: project and GPT ownership reassigned, retention rules
detail: When a member leaves, projects and custom GPTs go to a workspace owner (returned if they rejoin) without exposing private chats; Enterprise and Edu follow the retention policy while Business keeps chats and files indefinitely.

feature: Direct roles review on member profile
detail: Owners can see and remove a member's direct roles and review effective permissions across direct and group roles when changing teams.

feature: Windows desktop app deploy via Intune Microsoft Store
detail: Admins deploy the ChatGPT Windows app as a Microsoft Store app in Intune with System install behavior, Required or Available in Company Portal assignment.

feature: Windows app offline MSIX (x64 and Arm64) and SCCM
detail: An offline MSIX plus license supports Intune line-of-business, Win32 packaging, SCCM or other tools via provisioned install for all users; no standalone MSI or EXE exists.

feature: Windows self-install via web installer or winget
detail: Users with admin approval can install from a web installer or the winget command, with automatic updates through the installer.

feature: Windows desktop auto-update endpoint and uninstall data retention
detail: The app checks for updates by default from persistent.oaistatic.com; uninstall keeps local chats and settings in CODEX_HOME unless uninstall_codex_home is set true.

feature: Deploy Codex CLI on Windows (standalone installer or npm)
detail: CLI is installed by a PowerShell installer or npm with a pinned release, defaulting to per-user profile and PATH; device-wide packaging requires custom design; verify with codex --version.

feature: Windows managed requirements file location
detail: Admin requirements go in %ProgramData%\OpenAI\Codex\requirements.toml (overridable by registry RequirementsPath); /status and /debug-config show effective policy.

feature: Windows sandbox: MXC preference and elevated legacy fallback
detail: Windows command execution can prefer Microsoft Execution Containers (prefer_mxc) with legacy elevated or unelevated fallback, restrictable via allowed_sandbox_implementations; unelevated has weaker network isolation.

feature: Route Codex through an enterprise LLM gateway
detail: Admins can point Codex CLI and the desktop app at an HTTPS gateway serving the Responses API (POST /v1/responses with SSE streaming, continuation and tool calls) via a custom model provider block.

feature: Gateway authentication: native OAuth, scoped API keys, credential helper
detail: Developers sign in to a gateway by OAuth with PKCE (optionally device-code for remote CLI), per-developer scoped API keys via env_key, or a command-backed token resolver; can be combined with ChatGPT sign-in.

feature: Custom model aliases with model catalog (local JSON or remote URL)
detail: Gateway model names unknown to Codex need a model catalog supplying instructions, reasoning levels, context limits and tools, loaded by model_catalog_json or model_catalog_url; entries appear in the model picker.

feature: Distribute gateway config via config.toml, requirements.toml and routing headers
detail: Provider settings can be pushed through system config.toml, enforced provider definitions in requirements.toml, MDM and custom HTTP headers for gateway routing; /status and /debug-config verify.

feature: Reuse existing Claude Code gateway for Codex
detail: Orgs with a Claude Code gateway can keep network, logging and Bedrock access but must add a Responses route; apiKeyHelper and Claude settings are not supported by Codex.

feature: Restrict Codex sign-in to company workspace
detail: Local requirements can allow only ChatGPT login to an approved workspace UUID, rejecting personal accounts and API-key login on managed devices; existing sessions are not invalidated.

feature: Restrict permission profiles and block Full Access/--yolo
detail: Admins allowlist read-only or workspace profiles and approval policies so users cannot pick danger-full-access, never-ask approvals or the bypass flag.

feature: Approved-MCP-server allowlist by URL or stdio executable and args
detail: Admins enable only MCP servers matching approved name and identity (exact URL or executable with argument matchers, including plugin-bundled servers); stdio launch context is not constrained.

feature: Monitor Codex activity with OpenTelemetry, hooks, proxy logs, Compliance API
detail: Four evidence sources: OTel run/tool events (prompt redaction), managed lifecycle hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd), proxy logs, and Compliance API into a SIEM.

feature: Restrict network destinations for local Codex and Codex Cloud
detail: Local profiles with managed proxy allow only approved domains; current Codex Cloud environments can turn off public internet and package domains with additional allowed domains and HTTP secrets; Legacy Cloud adds HTTP-method limits.

feature: Protect secrets: deny-read globs and shell environment filters
detail: Workspace profiles can deny reads of .env, keys and cloud config, and shell_environment_policy excludes credential variables; Cloud HTTP secrets substitute real values only for approved destinations.

feature: Prefix rules requiring approval or forbidding commands
detail: Admin rules make commands like git push, terraform apply or kubectl delete prompt, or forbid rm; rules cannot allow, and shell-wrapper rules are noisy.

feature: Managed-only hooks and login shell/shell snapshot restrictions
detail: Admins install hook scripts in a root-managed directory and set allow_managed_hooks_only so user, project and plugin hooks are ignored; allow_login_shell and shell_snapshot can be disabled.

feature: Local computer access with Work Cloud
detail: Lets members continue an eligible cloud Work conversation across devices and use approved files or tools on a connected computer.

feature: Admin toggle: Allow local computer access
detail: Workspace owners enable it under Permissions & roles, nested under Work Cloud; it needs policy review and consent steps and is separate from using Codex locally in the desktop app.

feature: Residency policy disables local computer access
detail: If enforce_residency is set in any cloud policy, local computer access is turned off for both Work and dots.

feature: Agent Security admin console
detail: Replaces Policies and Configuration as the place for the global cloud policy baseline for Work and Codex; existing policies, assignments and ordering carry over, and a policy API manages Global settings.

feature: Policy precedence order
detail: Within a policy: OS-specific override, then all-OS override, then Global; for local runs MDM and legacy managed-device requirements outrank Agent Security, which outranks the device requirements file.

feature: MDM-delivered requirements for local execution
detail: Enterprise requirements delivered through MDM govern local execution only; Work cloud containers keep using their own Work Cloud policies.

feature: Global MCP hooks and local command hooks with Work
detail: With managed policy and remote hooks on, Work with local access and dots support Global MCP hooks; a command hook on the connected computer runs only in local-only workflows.

feature: Cloud fallback when local computer is offline
detail: An eligible new turn can run in a cloud container with its own requirements, without local files, tools or device policy.

feature: Turning local computer access off interrupts turns
detail: Disabling it stops running turns; existing tasks keep their original mode and members must start a new cloud task to use local access again.

feature: Local-access conversations hidden from Codex history
detail: Chats using local computer access with Work Cloud do not appear in Codex history and do not change Codex configuration behavior.

feature: Local computer access is not zero data retention
detail: Running a step on a connected computer does not make the workflow ZDR-compliant; residency coverage must be checked in the help center.

feature: Separate permissions for Work Cloud, Work Local and Codex Local
detail: Owners and admins manage hosted Work, local desktop Work and local Codex (desktop, CLI, IDE) as distinct permissions; Enterprise and Edu default role includes Work unless turned off.

feature: Identity controls: SSO, domain verification, SCIM, groups
detail: Enterprise supports SSO, domain verification, SCIM provisioning and identity-group sync; Business lacks SCIM and group sync; no workspace-wide MFA enforcement, so enforce MFA via the IdP.

feature: Built-in workspace roles
detail: Enterprise roles are Owner, Admin, Member and Analytics Viewer; custom roles and member RBAC gate Work, plugins and other capabilities on supported plans.

feature: Seat type must include ChatGPT for Work
detail: A Codex-only seat does not grant access to Work.

feature: Plugin and app action controls
detail: For apps that support action control, admins allow all actions, read-only or a custom set and choose how newly added actions are handled; app permissions separately decide when ChatGPT asks first.

feature: Workspace Agents controls
detail: Separate controls decide who can build, publish, share, schedule or configure reusable agents and shared connections.

feature: Individual vs agent-owned shared connections
detail: Individual connections use that person's source access; agent-owned or shared connections give agent users the connected account's access, so scopes, actions and audience should be limited.

feature: Monthly per-user credit limits with group defaults and overrides
detail: Admins set a workspace default monthly credit limit, group defaults and individual overrides; users see their usage and can request increases if allowed, and approval creates an override.

feature: Workspace credit alerts and overage limit
detail: Configured in the Global Admin Console: alerts notify recipients and the overage limit caps usage after the committed credit pool is used up.

feature: Cost API for credit-usage export
detail: Eligible Enterprise admins can pull credit-usage data through a unified Cost API for internal reporting.

feature: Work and Codex share pricing, credits and limits
detail: Chat, Work and Codex usage draw from the same credit allocation; consumption depends on model, reasoning or speed settings, tokens and tools. Business has a separate credit and spend-control model.

feature: Compliance Logs Platform and Compliance API for Work
detail: Eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces get Work prompts and agent responses, connected app calls and active Library files via compliance endpoints; not a complete audit of every action.

feature: Compliance log retention of 30 days
detail: Compliance Logs Platform keeps data 30 days, so records should be exported to eDiscovery, DLP, SIEM or a data lake for longer retention.

feature: OpenTelemetry export changes with local access
detail: Enabling local computer access keeps local executor events flowing to an OTel collector but cloud orchestration events no longer reach it; Compliance API covers cloud records.

feature: Codex local OpenTelemetry opt-in
detail: Local Codex clients can export events such as API requests, errors, tool approvals and results; prompt contents stay redacted unless otel.log_user_prompt is explicitly enabled; no OTel export for Work on web.

feature: Workspace analytics in Global Admin Console
detail: Shows adoption and credit-usage views for ChatGPT and Codex, with user, product, agent and model breakdowns depending on the surface.

feature: Locked chats cannot be disabled or reset by admins
detail: Admins cannot turn off locked chats, unlock them or reset a user's PIN; retention policies still apply and message logs stay available through the Compliance Platform.

feature: Work action categories: read, draft, write, share, schedule, execute
detail: Actions are grouped by risk, from reading and drafting up to writing, sharing, scheduling and executing code or browser automation, with review and approvals for higher-impact ones.

feature: Incident revocation paths
detail: Admins can remove user or group access, disable plugins, revoke shared connections, unpublish Workspace Agents, disable scheduled tasks or API triggers, and revoke Codex access tokens and repo or cloud-environment access.

feature: Enterprise no-training and encryption commitments for Work
detail: Work inherits workspace commitments including no training on business data by default, encryption in transit and at rest, access controls and audit logging.

feature: Browser and network controls restrict Work Cloud
detail: Cloud browser and shell network permissions further limit hosted Work on web, mobile and desktop.

feature: Library access for Work context
detail: Work can use earlier files via the current chat, projects, authorized Library access or automatic Library references.

feature: ChatGPT workspace analytics dashboard
detail: Interactive workspace-wide view of adoption and engagement; exports are identifiable organizational data and should be handled under access and retention policy.

feature: Codex analytics dashboard
detail: Interactive Codex-focused reporting in the admin console, including Usage Insights with Use cases and Tasks compared against consumption and reach.

feature: Codex Analytics API
detail: Programmatic aggregated Codex adoption and activity reporting for automation.

feature: Compliance API for audit records
detail: Separate from analytics, it provides auditable records for security, legal and investigation use.

feature: Model access depends on surface and sign-in
detail: Workspace model settings do not carry over to Codex desktop, CLI, IDE, Codex cloud or the API; API-key sign-in follows the API org and project, ChatGPT sign-in follows the identity's access.

feature: Workspace starting defaults for Chat and Work/Codex
detail: Owners and admins set separate default model, reasoning level, speed and new-chat behavior for Chat and for Work and local Codex; these are defaults, not permissions.

feature: Codex cloud default model cannot be changed
detail: The default model for hosted Codex cloud tasks is not adjustable.

feature: Fast mode pinned via requirements.toml
detail: A features.fast_mode requirement can force Fast mode on or off for managed local Codex clients but cannot override workspace or product availability.

feature: Maximum reasoning level and speed per model and role
detail: Enterprise admins cap reasoning level and speed per supported model for the workspace or a custom role under Workspace settings > Models, limiting cost without disabling the model.

feature: Preview and Launch model access with sync
detail: Where visible, Preview and Launch access are saved separately; a Sync preview and launch access option copies Preview choices to Launch only at save time.

feature: New frontier models off by default in Enterprise and Edu
detail: Newly launched models (the (model name) and 6.1 and 6.2 families named on the page) start disabled until an admin enables them; members also need Work or Codex access to pick them there.

feature: Ultrafast speed option enabled separately
detail: Eligible workspaces can separately enable an Ultrafast speed option for the newest model generation.

feature: Early Model Access setting does not grant newest model
detail: Existing early-access settings do not enable the latest model; owners enable it per workspace or role across Chat, Work and Codex.

feature: (model name) retirement from Codex with ChatGPT sign-in
detail: Retires October 14, 2026; API and API-key sessions are unaffected, and defaults, managed configs, custom agents and scheduled tasks should move to a replacement.

feature: (model name) and (model name) mini retired from Codex
detail: Retired August 31, 2026 for ChatGPT sign-in; replacements are the newer Sol and Luna models, with Luna needing admin enablement in Enterprise and Edu.

feature: Safety monitoring can pause tasks for review
detail: Tasks on the newest model can pause for review under safety monitoring.

feature: Codex Cloud (Legacy) environments
detail: Legacy environment experience that still backs Code Review and the Linear and GitHub integrations; planned for deprecation in favor of the new cloud environments.

feature: Universal default container image
detail: Cloud tasks run in a prebuilt universal image with common languages and tools, and runtime versions such as Python and Node can be pinned via Set package versions.

feature: Environment variables vs secrets in cloud tasks
detail: Variables last the whole task; secrets are extra-encrypted, available only to setup scripts, and removed before the agent phase.

feature: Automatic dependency setup for common package managers
detail: Codex installs dependencies automatically for npm, yarn, pnpm, pip, pipenv and poetry projects.

feature: Custom setup script and maintenance script
detail: Optional Bash setup script runs in its own session with internet access; an optional maintenance script runs when a cached container resumes.

feature: Container caching for up to 12 hours with Reset cache
detail: Cached container state speeds up new tasks, is invalidated when scripts, variables or secrets change, can be reset manually, and is shared across users in Business and Enterprise.

feature: Agent internet access off by default (legacy)
detail: Setup scripts have internet; the agent phase is offline unless limited or unrestricted access is enabled, with all traffic going through an HTTP/HTTPS proxy.

feature: AGENTS.md used for lint and test commands
detail: In cloud tasks the agent reads AGENTS.md in the repo to find project-specific lint and test commands.

feature: Cloud task result: answer, diff and open PR
detail: When finished the agent shows its answer and a diff, and the user can open a pull request or ask follow-ups.

feature: Codex Cloud tasks run while computer is asleep
detail: Cloud tasks run on hosted workspaces from web, mobile or desktop so work continues when your machine is off.

feature: Start a cloud task: Work in > Cloud
detail: On web or desktop pick Work in then Cloud; on mobile open Codex; a default environment lets you start without choosing a repo.

feature: Cloud task without a repository
detail: A task can start with no repo (for example script on sample data) and later be told which repository to clone.

feature: Desktop project auto-uses GitHub repos in default environment
detail: Projects in the desktop app automatically use associated GitHub.com repos if GitHub is connected; GitLab is excluded from automatic setup.

feature: Create and publish a reusable cloud environment
detail: Choose repos, let Codex inspect, install and test, review the setup report, then Publish; Save keeps config, Publish captures the filesystem, Share controls who can use it.

feature: GitLab.com repositories in the repository picker
detail: GitLab.com repos can be checked out through the picker after creating a reusable environment on web or desktop.

feature: Install script and Start skill fields
detail: Codex records the tested setup as an Install script for dependencies and a Start skill that starts services and checks readiness.

feature: Edit and Republish an environment
detail: Editing via the environment menu, describing the change, testing and republishing affects new tasks only; existing tasks keep their own saved files and state.

feature: Environment variables and network secrets
detail: Variables go straight to programs; network secrets give programs a placeholder that the proxy swaps for the real value on allowed HTTPS port 443 domains, and saving them adds their domains to restricted access.

feature: Personal vault for personal variables and secrets
detail: Settings > Codex Cloud > Personal vault stores your own variables and network secrets, applied to all or selected environments, with environment-specific values taking precedence.

feature: Share environment with workspace or keep Only me
detail: Privacy > Who can use sets workspace or private sharing; shared environments request per-user personal values and tasks keep separate working files.

feature: Use Codex in the cloud and Manage workspace environments permissions
detail: Two admin permissions: one controls task access, the other controls creating and editing workspace-shared environments.

feature: Agent Security network requirements for environments
detail: Admin workspace requirements for agent behavior, managed networking and tools apply alongside each environment's own domain settings.

feature: Enable all public internet access toggle
detail: Turning it on grants full public internet; turning it off allows only package-manager presets and additional allowed domains.

feature: Package managers allowlist preset
detail: Preset allows registries and download hosts for npm, Yarn, PyPI, PyTorch, Rust, Go, Maven, Gradle, Bazel, Buf, CPAN, apt repos, vendor repos and GitHub, plus www variants of root domains.

feature: Additional allowed domains
detail: Users add specific hosts beyond the preset; subdomains need their own entries.

feature: Published agent egress IP feed
detail: A public JSON feed of shared egress IP ranges lets services allowlist cloud agent traffic.

feature: Private networking via Tailscale VPN
detail: Cloud tasks reach private services over Tailscale (reusable ephemeral auth key, private DNS, subnet routes, split DNS/MagicDNS); other VPN providers are planned.

feature: TCP service access through VPN and proxy
detail: Databases or SSH over IPv4 Tailscale routes via the environment's HTTP CONNECT proxy at proxy:8088; TLS and credentials are the client's job.

feature: OIDC short-lived cloud credentials
detail: Advanced > OIDC attaches a connection so tasks get short-lived credentials from a cloud provider; trust uses the displayed issuer, audience and subject.

feature: OIDC support for AWS
detail: Supported for AWS CLI/boto3, S3, ECR, CodeArtifact, EKS, ECS and Bedrock Nova Micro; RDS IAM database login not yet supported.

feature: OIDC support for Google Cloud
detail: Supported for gcloud, Cloud Storage, Artifact Registry containers and packages (10 MiB upload limit), GKE, IAM, Secret Manager and KMS; Cloud SQL IAM login not yet supported.

feature: OIDC support for Azure
detail: Only Azure CLI and identity profiles work; Resource Manager, Blob and ADLS, and Container Registry pull and push are not yet supported.

feature: Continue cloud task across web and mobile
detail: Reopening the same task continues it on another device; new environments must be created on web or desktop.

feature: Start cloud tasks from Slack or Microsoft Teams
detail: With Cloud delegation enabled, asking @ChatGPT to work on a repo picks a shared environment; follow-ups must come from the same connected account.

feature: Cloud VM size by plan
detail: Plus and Edu Plus get 2 vCPU, 8 GiB RAM, 8 GiB disk; Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu and Edu Pro get 4 vCPU, 16 GiB, 32 GiB; larger VMs on request for Enterprise.

feature: Cloud task VM state recoverable for seven days
detail: Saved VM state can be recovered up to seven days after the last turn or resume.

feature: Cloud limitations: no computer use, no GitHub Enterprise Server
detail: Computer use and self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server are not yet supported in cloud environments; repo skills work but local personal skills do not sync.

feature: Environment Unpublished badge
detail: Environments not yet published show an Unpublished badge and cannot be used for tasks until published.

feature: Worktrees for parallel Codex chats
detail: Git worktrees let several independent chats run in one project without interfering; requires a Git repository and stays on the computer or remote dev environment holding the repo.

feature: Mobile app controls worktree chats on a connected computer
detail: From the ChatGPT mobile app you start, guide, approve and review worktree chats; worktrees never run on the phone.

feature: Worktree selector and starting branch
detail: Under the composer choose Worktree and a base branch (main, a feature branch, or current branch with unstaged changes); Codex works in detached HEAD by default.

feature: Optional local environment for worktree setup
detail: A local environment can be picked to run setup scripts when a worktree is created.

feature: Create branch here from worktree
detail: Chat header button turns the detached worktree into a branch so you can commit, push and open a PR; the branch then cannot be checked out elsewhere.

feature: Hand off chat between Local and Worktree
detail: Hand off in the chat header moves chat and code between checkouts, handling Git steps; a chat returns to its same worktree later; ignored files do not move unless included.

feature: Scheduled tasks on background worktrees
detail: In Git repos scheduled tasks run on dedicated background worktrees; in non-Git projects they run in the project directory.

feature: .worktreeinclude to copy ignored files
detail: A repo-root file lists ignored paths or patterns (like .env) copied into new local managed worktrees; AGENTS.override.md is copied automatically; symlinks and existing files are skipped.

feature: Codex-managed worktrees in CODEX_HOME
detail: Default lightweight disposable worktrees live under CODEX_HOME/worktrees, start at the selected branch HEAD plus uncommitted changes, and are detached.

feature: Automatic cleanup keeps latest 15 worktrees
detail: Default limit of 15 managed worktrees, adjustable or disableable in settings; pinned or in-progress chats are protected, archiving a chat deletes its worktree.

feature: Worktree snapshot and restore before deletion
detail: Codex saves a snapshot before deleting a managed worktree and offers restore when the chat is reopened.

feature: Settings > Worktrees: Worktree root
detail: Lets users choose where managed worktrees are created.

feature: Permanent worktrees retired
detail: Earlier permanent worktrees stay protected from cleanup but new ones can no longer be created from the project menu.

feature: Local environments with setup scripts
detail: Desktop-only config in the project .codex folder; setup scripts run when a new worktree starts, with per-OS overrides for macOS, Windows and Linux, and can be committed to share.

feature: Project actions in the top bar
detail: Named actions (such as Run or tests) with chosen icons and per-platform scripts appear in the top bar and run in the integrated terminal.

feature: Built-in Git tools and diff pane
detail: Diff pane shows checkout changes with inline comments for Codex, stage or revert hunks or files, commit, push and create a PR without leaving the app.

feature: Choose where Codex runs: Local, Worktree or Cloud
detail: In the desktop app pick Codex, then Work in This computer or Cloud, with a separate Worktree control for local Git projects.

feature: Cloud tasks keep own files and do not alter published environment
detail: File changes in a task do not update the published environment, and local files, processes, browser sign-ins and VPN are not transferred to the cloud task.

feature: Shared environment access is use-only
detail: In Enterprise, shared access lets you use an environment but not edit it.

feature: NFS home directory support via codex migrate-nfs-db
detail: On Linux, shared Codex homes over NFS use rollback-journal SQLite mode; the migrate-nfs-db command converts existing WAL databases once, with all clients stopped.

feature: Codex daemon mode and daemon_auto_start setting
detail: CLI can use a background server; app-server daemon stop halts it, daemon_auto_start=false stops auto launch, and --no-daemon bypasses it for one session.

feature: log_dir setting for local diagnostic logs
detail: Config option moves diagnostic logs to a host-local directory to cut NFS traffic.

feature: unsafe_enforce_sqlite_journal_mode managed requirement
detail: Fleet-wide requirements.toml setting makes Codex migrate WAL databases automatically when opened on NFS.

feature: CODEX_SQLITE_HOME for independent batch jobs
detail: Per-job local SQLite directory with a durable CODEX_HOME keeps rollouts on NFS without database contention; managed sqlite_home takes precedence.

feature: codex exec --ephemeral and -o output
detail: Ephemeral runs skip saving a resumable session; -o writes the final reply to a file and --json streams events to a job runner.

feature: codex --no-daemon resume
detail: Resumes a prior conversation from the CLI without using the background daemon.

feature: Record and Replay: turn a demonstrated workflow into a skill
detail: On Mac you record a workflow after approving permission, and ChatGPT or Codex drafts a reusable skill with when-to-use, inputs, steps and verification, replayable in a new chat with new inputs.

feature: Record a skill menu entry
detail: Plugins > + menu > Record a skill starts it from ChatGPT with Work on or from Codex; stop from the menu bar, overlay or by telling the chat.

feature: Record and Replay needs Computer Use
detail: Requires macOS and Computer Use enabled; the requirements.toml computer_use=false setting disables both.

feature: Feature maturity labels
detail: Features are labeled under development, experimental, beta, stable or deprecated, indicating reliability and support; experimental may be removed, deprecated should be migrated away from.

feature: Projects and chats
detail: Keeps related chats, context and work together in projects.

feature: Codex on mobile
detail: Start tasks, approve actions and review work from the phone.

feature: Build plugins in conversation
detail: Create and refine reusable workflows by talking to ChatGPT.

feature: Visualizations
detail: Turn ideas and information into interactive visual explanations.

feature: Scheduled tasks
detail: Schedule recurring work and review completed results.

feature: Long-running work
detail: ChatGPT keeps working while the user steps away.

feature: Notification preferences
detail: Choose how ChatGPT signals that work needs attention.

feature: Pets
detail: Pick a companion, start chats and follow activity through it.

feature: Codex Micro keyboard
detail: Monitor and control chats from a Work Louder keyboard.

feature: Browser
detail: Lets ChatGPT browse websites and act while the user stays in control.

feature: Computer use
detail: Lets ChatGPT operate apps through their visual interface.

feature: ChatGPT Voice in Chat, Work and Codex
detail: Voice is available across Chat, Work and Codex in the desktop app.

feature: Composer Predictions
detail: Suggests your next message in Codex.

feature: Plugins
detail: Install reusable workflows, connected tools and shared context.

feature: Sign in with ChatGPT in other apps
detail: Use a ChatGPT account in third-party apps and choose how they use the plan.

feature: Web search
detail: Finds current information and brings sources into a task.

feature: Image generation
detail: Create and edit images as part of work.

feature: Image inputs
detail: Use screenshots and images as context.

feature: Appshots
detail: Capture app state for visual inspection and debugging.

feature: Browser extension for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi
detail: ChatGPT works with several Chromium browsers via an extension.

feature: Work with files and artifacts viewer
detail: Create, preview and refine documents and generated files.

feature: Sites: build, publish and manage websites
detail: Build a website in ChatGPT, save records, connect apps, add sign-in, choose audience, invite editors, view analytics and manage versions.

feature: ChatGPT dots
detail: A persistent dot is created with a responsibility, reachable in ChatGPT and connected channels, with scheduled tasks, memory, computers, apps and controls to review activity and stop work.

feature: ChatGPT Space and Pages
detail: Shared workspace for files and Pages developed with the agent, with view, comment and edit permissions for collaborators.

feature: Commands, slash commands and deep links reference
detail: Desktop app has app commands, keyboard shortcuts, deep links and slash commands for interactive actions.

feature: Desktop app settings and troubleshooting references
detail: Reference pages for desktop preferences and common issue resolution.

feature: Codex Micro keyboard with ChatGPT desktop
detail: Limited-run Work Louder keyboard that checks chats, switches between them, adds voice input and triggers actions or skills; also works with Creator Micro 2.

feature: Micro connection: USB-C or three Bluetooth channels
detail: Connect by cable or pair on one of three Bluetooth channels; macOS requires Input Monitoring permission.

feature: Agent Keys show chat status lights
detail: Six keys follow chats with colors for idle, thinking, complete unread, needs input, error and unassigned; single press switches, double press also focuses ChatGPT.

feature: Agent key modes
detail: Follow most recent chats, pinned chats, priority chats, or custom assignments of chat, shortcut or skill per key.

feature: Default Command Keys
detail: Fast mode toggle, Approve, Decline, Fork chat, Mic push-to-talk and Send for the composer, all remappable with keycap swap and Reset layout.

feature: Micro Mic key: push-to-talk, hands-free, Voice Chat
detail: Uses the computer microphone; hold to talk, double press for hands-free, or map to start Voice Chat; separate mic keys can be mapped independently.

feature: Micro analog stick actions
detail: Four directions default to Plan mode toggle, forward, sidebar toggle and back, and can be set to any desktop command or skill.

feature: Micro dial modes
detail: Composer navigation, reasoning only, conversation scrolling or custom assignments; press and hold opens device settings.

feature: Micro lighting, auto-dim and battery
detail: Brightness, auto-dim from 30 seconds to one hour or off (default three minutes), and battery status in settings and sidebar.

feature: Micro extra layers via Work Louder Input
detail: Up to five more layers for other apps; ChatGPT uses layer 1.

feature: Composer predictions with Tab to accept
detail: After a reply, a suggested next message appears; Tab inserts it as an editable draft without sending; it does not appear after every response.

feature: Predictions use current thread context and memory in thread
detail: Suggestions draw only on the current conversation, including memory or connected-app context already in it; they work with memory off.

feature: ChatGPT Voice in Chat, Work and Codex
detail: Voice conversation powered by GPT-Live to start work, check progress and change direction in the desktop app; Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, Enterprise, with Enterprise and Edu getting two-week early access first.

feature: Voice through Codex on iOS
detail: After pairing the phone with a desktop host, voice works from Codex on iOS.

feature: Start voice chat in existing or new task
detail: Select Start voice chat in a task or Start new voice chat; first use asks for microphone access, voice choice and screen context on macOS; existing-task voice is rolling out.

feature: Voice chat hotkey
detail: Settings > Voice > Voice chat hotkey sets a shortcut to start voice.

feature: Interrupt and steer during voice response
detail: Natural turn-taking lets users interrupt, follow up or change direction while work runs.

feature: Voice delegates and checks tasks
detail: Voice can start separate tasks, check existing ones, send follow-ups and report progress and blockers back; it follows the same permissions as the tasks.

feature: Switch voice between tasks
detail: User can ask to talk to another task and return; the target task must support voice and be on a connected host.

feature: Screen context via appshot
detail: On macOS, Settings > Voice > Screen context lets voice capture the front window image and accessible text on request; needs Screen Recording and Accessibility permission; admins can disable.

feature: Voice vs voice dictation
detail: Voice is a live conversation; dictation only turns speech into prompt text.

feature: Only one voice chat active at a time
detail: One active voice chat is allowed across the desktop app; resuming an earlier voice chat is by opening it and starting voice.

feature: ChatGPT Work for delegated multi-step tasks
detail: Work completes tasks with a clear outcome such as decks, analyses, recurring updates and files using files, plugins and approved tools, with user progress follow, questions and approvals; Chat is for quick answers.

feature: Work uses local files, apps and browser on desktop
detail: On the desktop app, Work can use local files, apps and the browser when available.

feature: Continue Work across devices with Cloud selector
detail: With Work Cloud and local computer access, a Cloud Work task started on desktop continues on mobile or web; laptop must stay online for steps needing its files; Enterprise keeps Local/Cloud selector.

feature: Local vs Cloud choice for Work tasks
detail: Without local access, Local suits tasks needing the computer and Cloud suits ones like scheduled website checks.

feature: Create presentation, spreadsheet or recurring update in Work
detail: Example outcomes include an eight-slide deck from source materials, a scored comparison spreadsheet with summary tab and a Monday recurring agenda refresh drafted for approval.

feature: Plugins library under Customize > Plugins
detail: Left navigation Customize > Plugins lists plugins like Slack, Google Drive, SharePoint, email, calendars, CRM and trackers; type @ and a plugin name to point Work at a tool.

feature: Model picker guidance for Work
detail: Pick the top model for demanding reasoning and polished files, the middle model for everyday coding and writing, and the smallest for simple tasks; longer tasks use more credits.

feature: Safety monitoring pauses tasks for review
detail: A task may pause for safety review and show findings to review before continuing.

feature: Codex GitHub Action (openai/codex-action)
detail: Runs Codex in GitHub Actions jobs to review PRs, apply patches or run repeatable tasks by installing the CLI and running codex exec; needs an OpenAI API key secret and Linux or macOS runner.

feature: Action inputs: prompt, prompt-file, model, effort, sandbox, codex-args
detail: Choose inline or file prompt, model and effort, sandbox mode (read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access), extra CLI flags, pinned codex-version and shared codex-home.

feature: Action outputs: final-message and output-file
detail: Last message is exposed as an output and can be saved to a file; --output-schema via codex-args enforces structured JSON.

feature: Action safety-strategy and unprivileged user
detail: Default drop-sudo removes sudo irreversibly; an unprivileged-user strategy runs Codex as a named account; Windows requires unsafe.

feature: Action allow-users and allow-bots trigger limits
detail: By default only write-access users can trigger runs; extra trusted accounts or bots must be listed.

feature: Automatic approval review
detail: A model reviews eligible approval requests before they proceed.

feature: Approval policy
detail: Rules deciding when Codex must ask before acting.

feature: Computer History opt-in on macOS
detail: Opt-in feature building memories and a timeline from interaction events across allowed apps and websites.

feature: Scheduled tasks: standalone, in-chat and Heartbeat
detail: Standalone tasks start a new chat per run and report findings in Triage; in-chat tasks reuse a chat's context and return results there; Heartbeat is a recurring task that returns to the same chat.

feature: Findings and scheduled run history
detail: Each scheduled run has status and surfaced findings managed per task.

feature: Compaction of older context
detail: Older context is summarized so long-running work can continue.

feature: Custom agents and subagents
detail: User-defined agent roles with own instructions, and child agents run in parallel on parts of a task with results combined.

feature: Deny-read rules
detail: Filesystem permission rules blocking reads of sensitive paths or globs.

feature: Permission profiles
detail: Named least-privilege policies combining filesystem and network rules for local command execution.

feature: Prefix rules
detail: Command rules that allow, prompt for or forbid matching command prefixes.

feature: Profiles (named config presets)
detail: Named configuration presets for Codex selectable in CLI and IDE.

feature: Full access, read-only and sandbox modes
detail: Sandbox modes include read-only inspect, workspace-write and full access without normal sandbox restrictions.

feature: Network policy domain allow and deny rules
detail: Domain-based rules constrain sandboxed outbound traffic.

feature: Writable roots
detail: Directories Codex is allowed to modify.

feature: Fast mode
detail: Speed setting that makes supported models respond faster at higher credit cost.

feature: Live web search vs cached search
detail: Live lookup for current information, or pre-indexed cached results without live browsing, set by web search mode.

feature: Local Memories reusable across sessions
detail: Locally stored context Codex can reuse across sessions.

feature: Hooks lifecycle handlers
detail: Handlers run when events match such as tool use, permission requests or turn stop.

feature: MCP servers: STDIO and streamable HTTP
detail: STDIO servers run as local processes; streamable HTTP servers use optional bearer token or OAuth; MCP exposes tools and resources.

feature: Plugins bundle skills, connectors and tools
detail: Installable bundles distributed through a universal directory shared by ChatGPT and Codex, with a manifest naming skills, connector mappings, MCP servers and hooks.

feature: Skills with progressive disclosure
detail: Reusable workflow packages whose details load only when needed, invoked explicitly or implicitly.

feature: Codex app-server and SDK
detail: Local JSON-RPC server and SDK for embedding Codex threads, turns, approvals and streamed events in custom clients, with thread fork.

feature: Codex IDE extension for VS Code, JetBrains, Cursor, Windsurf
detail: Editor integration across several IDEs.

feature: Review pane with diffs, hunks and inline comments
detail: Desktop view to inspect diffs, comment on lines, stage or revert hunks, and review pull requests.

feature: Plan mode and plan steps
detail: Codex proposes or tracks steps for a task.

feature: Quick chat
detail: Starts a ChatGPT chat from within Codex.

feature: ChatGPT sign-in vs API key sign-in with auth cache
detail: Codex can authenticate with a ChatGPT account and workspace permissions or an OpenAI API key, with login credentials cached locally.

feature: Remote connections to a connected host
detail: Access chats on another device through a host computer or dev environment that supplies files, tools and shell.

feature: Computer Use in the built-in browser
detail: Lets ChatGPT operate the built-in browser directly.

feature: Appshot of frontmost window
detail: Snapshot of the frontmost app window sent into a chat.

feature: Hooks framework for Codex
detail: Run scripts or MCP tools at lifecycle points for logging, prompt scanning for secrets, memory creation or validation on stop; matching hooks from all sources run, concurrently for the same event.

feature: Hook events list
detail: Events: PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStop, Stop, PreModelRequest, PostModelRequest, Interrupt, SessionStart, SubagentStart and SessionEnd.

feature: Hook file locations by scope
detail: hooks.json at system (/etc/codex or ProgramData), user CODEX_HOME, or trusted project .codex, or inline under [hooks] in config.toml; plugins can bundle hooks.

feature: Hook review and trust via /hooks
detail: Non-managed hooks must be reviewed and trusted by hash before running; /hooks in CLI (or Review hooks / Settings > Hooks in desktop) inspects, trusts or disables them; managed hooks cannot be disabled.

feature: --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust flag
detail: Runs enabled hooks without persisted trust for a single invocation, for pre-vetted automation.

feature: Hook handler types: command and mcp_tool
detail: Command hooks run scripts with JSON on stdin; mcp_tool hooks call a tool on an already-connected MCP server with templated arguments; prompt and agent handlers are parsed but skipped.

feature: Hook matchers by regex
detail: Matcher filters tool name, compaction trigger (manual or auto), session start source (startup, resume, clear, compact, fork) or subagent type; some events ignore it.

feature: PreToolUse hook can block, rewrite or add context
detail: Can deny a call, rewrite input via updatedInput with allow, or add model-visible context; covers Bash, apply_patch, MCP and local function tools but not hosted tools like web search.

feature: PermissionRequest hook can auto-allow or deny approvals
detail: Runs when approval would be requested; any deny wins, an allow skips the prompt, otherwise the normal approval flow continues.

feature: PostToolUse hook feedback
detail: Runs after tools including failed Bash, can replace the result with feedback or stop processing but cannot undo side effects.

feature: UserPromptSubmit hook can add context or block a prompt
detail: Receives the prompt about to be sent and can inject developer context or block it.

feature: Stop hook continues a turn
detail: Returning block makes Codex continue with the reason as a new prompt; continue false takes precedence.

feature: SubagentStart and SubagentStop hooks
detail: Add context to a subagent at start, and ask it to do another pass at stop.

feature: SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks
detail: Start hooks add developer context (also after compaction); SessionEnd runs when a conversation is archived, deleted, closed or idle 30 minutes, always synchronous and advisory.

feature: Interrupt hook
detail: Runs when a user interrupts an active main-thread turn with a 1 to 3 second timeout; cannot prevent the interruption.

feature: PreModelRequest and PostModelRequest hooks
detail: Diagnostic logging per model attempt including retries, with status, error and token usage; cannot change context or block.

feature: Pre/PostCompact hooks
detail: Run before and after compaction with manual or auto trigger; continue false stops around compaction.

feature: Async background hooks
detail: async true runs a command hook in the background, up to eight concurrently per session, delivering informational output at the next safe point; cannot block or approve.

feature: Hook output spilling and additionalContextLimit
detail: Hook output over about 2,500 tokens is saved to disk with a preview; additionalContextLimit changes the threshold per handler.

feature: Hook timeouts
detail: Default 600 seconds; SessionEnd and Interrupt default to 1 second and max 3; status messages can be shown while running.

feature: Disable hooks via features.hooks=false
detail: Hooks are on by default and can be turned off in config.toml, or forced off by admins in requirements.toml.

feature: Managed hooks in requirements.toml
detail: Admins declare hooks with managed_dir, can pin hooks on, and set allow_managed_hooks_only to ignore user, project, session and plugin hooks.

feature: Cloud-orchestrated Global MCP hooks
detail: Work Cloud with local access and dots can call admin-configured MCP hooks at task and tool events; command, prompt, agent, plugin and SessionEnd hooks are unsupported; errors may let a tool run.

feature: Plugin-bundled hooks
detail: Enabled plugins can supply lifecycle hooks via hooks/hooks.json or manifest, with PLUGIN_ROOT and PLUGIN_DATA env vars; plugin script updates require re-review.

feature: Generate and edit images from the composer
detail: Ask in app, web, CLI or IDE chat to create or edit images such as UI assets, banners, illustrations and sprite sheets; add a reference image to transform or guide.

feature: Expanded image viewer: Focused view and Canvas view
detail: Selecting a generated image opens a viewer; Focused shows one image and Canvas shows all images from the chat.

feature: Canvas Comment and Multi-select for image feedback
detail: Add precise comments to one or several images and send them with edit instructions in the same chat.

feature: $imagegen skill and image usage limits
detail: Include $imagegen to invoke explicitly in app, CLI or IDE; built-in generation uses (model name) and consumes included limits 3 to 5 times faster, with an API-key option for large batches.

feature: Web image availability depends on plan and workspace
detail: Image generation limits in ChatGPT web vary by plan and workspace settings.

feature: Edit a selected area of an image
detail: Select a specific region and describe the change for that area; multiple reference images can be ordered and described.

feature: IDE reference image by Shift-drag
detail: In the IDE extension, hold Shift while dragging an image into the composer so it is accepted.

feature: CLI image generation with -i flag
detail: Describe the image or use $imagegen and attach a guiding image with -i or --image.

feature: Image inputs as prompt context
detail: Add error screenshots, designs or diagrams to a prompt: drag with Shift in desktop or IDE, attach, paste or drag on web.

feature: CLI image input: -i and --image flags
detail: Pass one or more PNG or JPEG files by comma or repeated flag, or paste into the interactive composer.

feature: Import from another agent in desktop app
detail: Settings > Import brings instructions, settings, skills, plugins, projects and recent chats from Claude Code, Claude Cowork or Cursor, leaving the original setup unchanged.

feature: Automatic sync and import history
detail: Settings > Import can keep imported work in sync with the source agent and shows import history.

feature: Codex CLI /import from Claude Code or Cursor
detail: Imports setup, project files and up to 50 chats from the last 30 days.

feature: What import maps over
detail: Instruction files become AGENTS.md, settings.json becomes config.toml, plus skills, plugins, project folders, Claude Code project memories, 30 days of chats, MCP config, hooks, slash commands as skills and subagents.

feature: Finish setup status card after import
detail: A lower-left card flags plugins or connections needing authorization, with a Finish action.

feature: Integrated terminal per chat
detail: Each desktop chat has a terminal scoped to its project or worktree, opened via New tab > Terminal or Ctrl+backtick, and ChatGPT can read its output.

feature: Terminal shortcuts and actions
detail: Ctrl+L clears the terminal, Cmd+K opens the command palette, and local-environment actions run in it.

feature: ChatGPT desktop app for Linux (preview)
detail: Preview app for Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Debian 13, Fedora 43 and 44 and current Arch, on x64 and ARM64, with projects, local files and Codex after ChatGPT sign-in.

feature: Linux installation: deb, rpm and Arch script
detail: Install with apt for .deb, dnf for .rpm, or an install script for Arch; packages configure a signed OpenAI repository so updates come through the distro package manager.

feature: Linux limitation: no Computer Use yet
detail: Computer Use works on macOS and Windows but not yet in the Linux preview.

feature: Experimental native Wayland
detail: App uses XWayland by default; chatgpt --ozone-platform=wayland selects native Wayland, with possible gaps in floating windows, positioning, focus and shortcuts.

feature: Goal mode with /goal
detail: Typing /goal in desktop, CLI or IDE starts a goal whose text is both first prompt and completion criteria; /plan can first interview to refine it.

feature: Goal progress row: pause, resume, edit, clear
detail: Desktop shows a progress row above the composer for controlling a running goal, with follow-ups and a side chat for recaps without interrupting.

feature: Goals keep same sandbox and approvals
detail: Starting a goal grants no extra access; it pauses for decisions and can use automatic approval reviews.

feature: Parallel goals per chat with worktrees
detail: Each chat keeps its own context and goal; worktrees give parallel coding chats separate checkouts.

feature: Prevent sleep while running setting
detail: Desktop setting keeps the Mac awake during local long-running work.

feature: Hosted long-running work through Work on web
detail: On web, long tasks use ChatGPT Work with outcome, constraints and review criteria in the prompt; separate chats run in parallel.

feature: codex mcp-server removed
detail: The command and standalone binary that hosted Codex as an MCP server are gone; integrations should use the experimental app-server JSON-RPC protocol, while codex mcp still manages external MCP servers.

feature: Codex on mobile
detail: In the ChatGPT mobile app, start tasks on Cloud or a connected Mac or Windows PC, follow progress, send instructions, approve commands and review changed files, diffs and test results.

feature: Connect a computer via Settings > Connections > Control this Mac or PC
detail: Set up on desktop, approve remote access, scan the QR code on the phone with the same account and workspace; the computer must stay awake and online.

feature: Mobile task list across Cloud and connected hosts
detail: Shows active tasks in Cloud and on connected computers and when input is needed.

feature: Custom GPTs being retired in favor of plugins
detail: Custom GPTs are transitioning to plugins; at retirement GPTs stop running and leave the directory, new GPT creation stops, and migration remains possible afterward.

feature: Migrate to plugin from My GPTs
detail: Creators or workspace admins convert a published GPT via Created by me > Migrate to plugin; instructions become a skill, knowledge files and apps carry over, the original becomes read-only and the replacement starts private.

feature: GPT custom actions do not transfer
detail: Actions must be rebuilt with a supported app connector or a custom MCP server; selected model, conversation starters and past chats also do not carry over.

feature: Plugin = skills plus apps package
detail: A plugin packages reusable skills (instructions and reference files) and apps (service connections); skills-only plugins need no app connection and plugin use respects existing app access.

feature: Invoke plugins with @ mention or + > More
detail: Users pick a plugin or skill via @ or the + menu, and ChatGPT may automatically use a relevant installed skill when its description matches.

feature: Plugin permissions: Use, Share, Publish to workspace, Upload
detail: RBAC permissions separately govern using plugins, sharing with people or groups, publishing to workspace directory, and uploading plugins or ones with custom MCP servers.

feature: Plugin install policy: Available vs Installed
detail: Admins either let eligible users install a plugin or install it automatically for eligible users or roles; sharing and installing are separate; shows a Disabled by admin label when off.

feature: ChatGPT Admin plugin GPT report and bulk migration
detail: Admins use the ChatGPT Admin plugin in Work to report GPT owners, 30-day usage, migration status, actions and knowledge files, export to Excel, CSV or Sheets, schedule the report, and bulk migrate with confirmation; sharing does not copy.

feature: Plugin conversion costs no credits; editing does
detail: Converting a GPT consumes none, while editing or updating a plugin uses credits under credit pricing; Instant Chat is generally unlimited but reasoning or tool features can use credits.

feature: Migrated plugins work in Chat and Work
detail: Plugins can be used in Chat where enabled and in Work; creation and editing experience needs separate access.

feature: Model lineup guidance: Astra, Sol, Terra, Luna
detail: Sol is the default for most Work and Codex tasks, Astra for complex projects, Terra for visual reasoning and app navigation, and Luna for small repeatable automations.

feature: Model and reasoning effort pairing recommendations
detail: Page maps eight model and effort combos (for example Luna Low for small edits, Astra Extra high for open-ended problems) and ranks models by fit across six work types.

feature: Interactive model recommender
detail: A page widget suggests a model and reasoning effort from a chosen task and priority.

feature: Model and reasoning control under composer
detail: Work and Codex show a control beneath the composer to pick model and reasoning effort; a Power slider (Faster to Smarter) has an Advanced option to pick a specific model.

feature: Default Work model and effort by plan
detail: New Work chats start with the mid-tier model at Light on consumer plans or Medium in Enterprise workspaces where it is enabled.

feature: Reasoning effort levels: Light/Low, Medium, High, Extra High
detail: Higher effort improves hard tasks but costs time and tokens; Light is called Low in the CLI; defaults vary by model, with Luna starting at High.

feature: Max reasoning mode
detail: Gives the selected model more time to reason on one task; Luna supports up to Max; may need to be enabled in app settings.

feature: Ultra mode with subagents
detail: Uses subagents to split complex work in parallel; not supported on Luna; enable via Settings > Configuration > Ultra in model picker slider; in CLI via /model > More reasoning.

feature: Model context windows in Codex
detail: Astra default 272k tokens, Sol default 500k, both up to 1 million via model_context_window in config.toml.

feature: Terra needs Codex CLI 0.159.0 or later
detail: Selecting the visual-reasoning model from the CLI requires a recent version, with codex -m or /model.

feature: CLI model switching with /model and --model
detail: Use /model in a session or --model/-m at launch, also for codex exec.

feature: Default local model in config.toml
detail: Desktop, CLI and IDE share config.toml; a model entry sets the default, otherwise a recommended model is used.

feature: Custom model providers via Responses API
detail: Codex can use a gateway or custom provider with a compatible Responses API endpoint; Chat Completions-only endpoints are unsupported.

feature: (model name) retirement from Codex (Oct 14, 2026)
detail: Replacement is the 6.1 Sol model on paid plans or the Luna model on Free and Go in the desktop app; API-key sessions unaffected.
plans: Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu

feature: Retired Codex models: (model name), (model name), 5.4 mini, 5.2, 5.3-codex
detail: Spark retired September 14, 2026, 5.4 and 5.4 mini August 31, 2026, and 5.2 and 5.3-codex already deprecated for ChatGPT sign-in.

feature: Model availability on Free and Go in the desktop app
detail: Free and Go plans can use the smallest model in the desktop app where available.

feature: codex exec non-interactive mode
detail: Runs Codex from scripts or CI without the TUI; progress goes to stderr and only the final message to stdout so it can be piped.

feature: Piped stdin as context or as full prompt
detail: With a prompt argument, piped input is extra context; omitting the prompt or using codex exec - reads the whole prompt from stdin.

feature: codex exec default read-only sandbox and --sandbox
detail: Defaults to read-only; --sandbox workspace-write allows edits and danger-full-access broader access for isolated runners.

feature: --approve-for-me automatic review in exec
detail: Replaces unsupported --full-auto, routing approvals through automatic review with a workspace-write sandbox.

feature: --trust, --ignore-user-config and --ignore-rules flags
detail: Project config and project MCP servers load only for trusted projects; --trust saves trust, and the other flags skip user config or execpolicy rules.

feature: Required MCP server failure aborts run
detail: An MCP server with required=true that fails to initialize makes codex exec exit with an error.

feature: --json JSONL event stream
detail: Streams every event (thread, turn and item events covering messages, reasoning, commands, file changes, MCP calls, web searches, plans) as JSON lines with token usage.

feature: -o / --output-last-message and --output-schema
detail: Writes the final message to a file and optionally constrains it to a JSON Schema for structured results.

feature: CODEX_API_KEY for automation auth
detail: Set per invocation for exec, review, the TypeScript SDK and exec-server remote; avoid job-level env vars in jobs running repo code.

feature: ChatGPT-managed auth in CI (advanced)
detail: Runs CI with a Codex account via a seeded auth.json refreshed in place; not for public repos and the file must be protected like a password.

feature: codex exec resume
detail: Continues a prior non-interactive session with --last or a session ID.

feature: Git repository required, --skip-git-repo-check
detail: Codex insists on running inside a Git repo to avoid destructive changes unless the check is skipped.

feature: CI autofix pattern with Codex action
detail: Example two-job workflow: read-only job runs Codex and emits a patch artifact, separate write job applies it and opens a PR without the API key.

feature: Desktop turn-completion alert setting
detail: Settings choose whether turn-completion alerts appear never, only when ChatGPT is in the background, or always; OS notification permission may be requested.

feature: Permission and question notifications toggles
detail: Separate desktop controls turn permission requests and question prompts on or off.

feature: Activity view bell
detail: Sidebar bell lists unread, running or awaiting-response chats, filterable by Work, Chat, Pinned and Scheduled, with Mark all as read and shortcut Cmd/Ctrl+Option/Alt+U.

feature: Floating pet shows chat status
detail: A pet shows Running, Needs input, Ready or Blocked for chats while using other apps.

feature: Web Settings > Notifications with push, email, SMS channels
detail: Categories and channels depend on account; Manage tasks opens Scheduled.

feature: CLI notification config and notify program
detail: TUI notification timing and an external program run at turn completion are set in advanced config; the IDE has no separate controls but can use notify on the host.

feature: Open-source Codex components
detail: CLI, SDK, Security CLI and SDK, app-server, skills, plugins and universal cloud image are open on GitHub; IDE extension and Codex cloud are not.

feature: Codex for OSS program
detail: Maintainers of widely used open-source projects can apply for API credits, ChatGPT Pro with Codex and selective Codex Security access.

feature: Issue reporting on GitHub, no external PRs
detail: Bugs and requests go to the openai/codex issue tracker or discussions; community issues are welcome but external code contributions are not accepted.

feature: Permission modes: Ask for approval, Approve for me, Full access
detail: Control beneath the composer sets what the app can do alone; Ask for approval is the default start, Approve for me routes eligible requests to automatic review, Full access removes sandbox limits; managed requirements can restrict modes.

feature: Sandbox vs approvals
detail: Sandbox limits files and network; approvals decide when to pause; changing the reviewer never widens the sandbox. CLI uses /permissions.

feature: Plugin Creator builds MCP plugins hosted on Sites
detail: In a Work task, @Plugin Creator with API docs creates a plugin and an MCP server hosted on Sites; the Site owner publishes, then users Install and Connect from Plugins > Personal > Created by you.

feature: Enterprise permissions for MCP plugin creation
detail: Use plugins (on by default), Sites access, and off-by-default Upload plugins and Create plugins with MCPs are needed; sharing needs Share plugins and directory listing needs Publish plugins to workspace.

feature: Desktop only plugin label
detail: Plugins marked Desktop only need a supported desktop app; a remote MCP server alone does not make them web-compatible.

feature: ChatGPT web uses MCP via plugins only
detail: Web does not read local Codex config; remote MCP tools arrive through installed plugins in the Plugins tab, available to both Chat and Work.

feature: Add MCP server in desktop Settings > MCP servers
detail: Add server with name, STDIO or Streamable HTTP, command or URL, save and Restart; list shows enabled and OAuth-needed servers with Authenticate; /mcp in composer lists connected servers.

feature: IDE MCP servers via gear menu
detail: Same add-server flow with Restart extension, sharing config with desktop and CLI.

feature: codex mcp add, list, login commands
detail: CLI adds servers with env vars, lists them, and logs in via OAuth, with --no-browser for headless terminals and /mcp in the TUI.

feature: Shared MCP config in config.toml, global or project-scoped
detail: One mcp_servers table shared by desktop, CLI and IDE; project .codex/config.toml works for trusted projects only.

feature: STDIO MCP server options
detail: command, args, env, env_vars with local or remote source, and cwd.

feature: Streamable HTTP MCP auth options
detail: Bearer token env var, static or env-based headers, header helper command, OAuth default, or ChatGPT session auth for trusted first-party servers.

feature: MCP OAuth with CIMD, DCR and pre-registered clients
detail: Auto chooses Client ID Metadata Documents or Dynamic Client Registration, or a configured client ID with --oauth-client-id and secret; callback URL and port are configurable and issuer is validated.

feature: MCP OAuth scopes control
detail: Set scopes in config or per login with --scopes; otherwise requested from the server challenge or resource metadata.

feature: MCP server tuning: timeouts, required, startup_readiness
detail: Startup default 10s, tool default 60s, enabled flag, required servers fail startup, catalog readiness mode, and optional startup grace of 1 second.

feature: MCP tool allow, deny lists and approval modes
detail: enabled_tools and disabled_tools, default approval mode auto, prompt, writes or approve, per-tool override and output token limit.

feature: MCP server instructions field
detail: Codex reads the server-provided instructions as server-wide guidance; first 512 characters should stand alone.

feature: Plugin-provided MCP servers with user policy
detail: Plugins bundle MCP servers launched from the manifest; users can still toggle them and set tool policy, and plugins can declare OAuth client settings.

feature: Replace a GPT custom action with a Sites MCP plugin
detail: Ask the old GPT for a rebuild prompt, save the action schema, and have Plugin Creator build a separate Sites-hosted plugin; Sites plugins cannot yet edit skills or reference files.

feature: Enterprise mcp_servers requirement applies to local executors
detail: In local computer access with Work Cloud, admin mcp_servers policy governs local executors while cloud containers keep Work Cloud policies; local MCP servers may be unavailable in cloud.

feature: Codex permission profiles (named least-privilege policies)
detail: A profile combines filesystem rules and network rules to bound what local commands Codex runs can read, write and reach. Under active development.

feature: Built-in profile: read-only
detail: The :read-only profile keeps local command execution read-only so Codex can inspect a project without editing it.

feature: Built-in profile: workspace
detail: The :workspace profile allows writes inside active workspace roots and system temp directories; .git, .agents, .codex and .aws stay read-only by default.

feature: Built-in profile: danger-full-access
detail: Removes local sandbox restrictions entirely; meant only when broad access is deliberate. Cannot be extended by custom profiles.

feature: Custom profiles with default_permissions
detail: Define a named profile under [permissions.<name>] in config and select it with default_permissions; higher config layers can extend the same profile name.

feature: Profile inheritance with extends
detail: A custom profile can extend :read-only, :workspace or another profile and override only differing rules; unknown parents and cycles are rejected.

feature: Profile-defined workspace roots
detail: Extra directories can be declared as workspace roots for a profile so the same filesystem rules apply to them alongside the session root.

feature: Filesystem access levels: read, write, deny
detail: Paths get read, write or deny; more specific entries win, and deny beats write beats read. A narrower path can reopen a subtree inside a broader deny.

feature: Filesystem path forms and scoped subpaths
detail: Rules can target :root, :minimal, :workspace_roots, :tmpdir, :slash_tmp, absolute paths or home-relative paths; some allow nested subpath rules, none allow parent traversal.

feature: Deny-read globs for secrets (e.g. env files)
detail: Glob deny rules block reads of matching files in every workspace root; on Linux, WSL and Windows matches are snapshotted per sandboxed process, so files created later stay readable to a running process.

feature: glob_scan_max_depth setting
detail: Bounds pre-expansion of unbounded deny glob patterns on Linux, WSL and Windows; must be at least 1, deeper values add startup scanning.

feature: Network permissions per profile: enabled flag
detail: network.enabled lets sandboxed commands reach the network; off means no access. It does not by itself start the filtering proxy.

feature: Network domain allow/deny rules via network proxy
detail: With features.network_proxy on, domain patterns (exact, subdomain wildcard, apex plus subdomains, global allow wildcard) allow or deny destinations; deny wins and an empty allowlist blocks all external hosts.

feature: Network proxy feature switch
detail: Setting features.network_proxy turns on enforcement of domain rules; without it, enabled network means direct unrestricted access. Admins can start it via managed experimental_network requirements.

feature: Local/private network guard and allow_local_binding
detail: The active proxy blocks local and private targets by default; literal localhost or IPs must be allowlisted, and allow_local_binding opens hostnames resolving to private addresses.

feature: Unix socket allowlist (for tools like Docker)
detail: Absolute socket paths can be allowed or denied in the profile; denied entries are dropped from the effective list. A dangerous allow-all flag also exists.

feature: Network proxy listener settings (HTTP, SOCKS5, UDP, upstream proxy)
detail: Configurable proxy URL, SOCKS5 listener and URL, SOCKS5 UDP, whether to honor upstream proxy variables, and a dangerous option to bind non-loopback addresses.

feature: Migrating from sandbox_mode to permission profiles
detail: Profiles do not mix with older sandbox_mode and sandbox_workspace_write; if any older setting or --sandbox flag is present, the old system is used. Pick one system per session.

feature: Managed allowed_permission_profiles allowlist
detail: Enterprise admins define profiles and restrict selectable ones through requirements.toml; once present, omitted profiles (including future built-ins) are denied.

feature: Managed allowed_sandbox_modes compatibility constraint
detail: For mixed-version rollouts admins may keep the older sandbox-modes requirement until all clients run Codex 0.138.0 or later.

feature: Policy precedence for Work with local access and dots
detail: Shared cloud orchestrator follows supported Global policy; local requirements govern the connected computer, with MDM above Agent Security above the device requirements file; higher priority always wins.

feature: Sandbox enforcement per OS
detail: macOS uses Seatbelt, Linux and WSL use bubblewrap plus seccomp, Windows uses MXC process isolation with legacy elevated and unelevated fallbacks; unenforceable policies are refused, not run unsandboxed.

feature: Controls outside the network proxy scope
detail: Web search, apps and connectors, MCP servers, browser and Computer Use, Codex service traffic and cloud tasks are governed by their own settings, not the profile domain list.

feature: Example profiles: read-only with allowlist, workspace-only, write without networ
detail: The page gives ready recipes, including a workspace-only profile that denies reads outside the workspace except a minimal system set.

feature: Choose a personality (base style and tone)
detail: On web, Settings > Personalization > Base style and tone changes response style and tone without changing capabilities.

feature: Custom instructions (global AGENTS.md in Codex)
detail: Personal preferences applied across chats; in Codex they live in a global AGENTS.md, and projects or repos can add their own instructions.

feature: Writing style in Work
detail: Uses your writing from connected email, messaging or document apps so drafts sound like you; needs connecting apps and explicitly selecting Use writing style.

feature: Turn off writing style reference
detail: Settings > Personalization > Writing > Reference my writing style toggles it off and lets you return to setup.

feature: Memories carry context across chats
detail: Preferences, workflows and conventions from earlier chats carry into future work; must-always rules belong in AGENTS.md instead.

feature: Computer History (opt-in, macOS)
detail: Turns activity across allowed apps and sites into memories and a timeline using interaction events and accessibility text; no screenshots or audio. Pause, exclude apps/sites, inspect, delete items, clear recent or all.

feature: Floating pet companion (desktop)
detail: Optional animated pet floating above other windows on macOS and Windows with controls to start a chat by typing or voice and follow activity; changes looks only.

feature: Choose built-in or custom pet, or Mini mode
detail: Pick from Settings > Pets or profile menu; Mini shows the chat controls without a pet; selected custom pet also shows in Profile.

feature: Show or hide pet with /pet, command menu or right-click
detail: Toggle via the /pet command, Show pet command, right-click Hide, or Settings; selection and position persist.

feature: Pet size setting
detail: Settings > Pets > Customize adjusts Pet size, with Reset to default.

feature: Global shortcut to show pet and focus Quick Chat
detail: Default Option+Space on macOS and Windows+Alt+P on Windows; rebindable under Keyboard shortcuts.

feature: Chat from pet controls with @ context and $ skills
detail: Pencil icon opens a quick request box; @ adds context, $ picks a skill; these chats are outside any project.

feature: Voice from pet controls
detail: A voice icon on the pet controls starts a spoken chat.

feature: Pet activity tray and status (Running, Needs input, Ready, Blocked)
detail: Bell icon lists threads with status; priority is needs input, blocked, ready, then running; separate from system notifications.

feature: Send Appshots to pet (macOS)
detail: Pressing both Command keys takes an Appshot and, if the pet is visible and main window is in background, starts a new chat with it; needs Appshot destination Automatic and permissions. Windows opens it in the main app.

feature: Computer Use picture-in-picture attaches to pet (macOS)
detail: The Computer Use PiP window follows the pet; sending it to a hidden pet shows the pet.
