feature: Create a custom pet with hatch-pet skill
detail: Settings > Pets > Create pet installs a skill and opens a chat to describe the pet; stored locally, not synced to web.

feature: Pets respect reduced motion
detail: With OS reduced motion enabled the pet shows a still frame instead of sprite animation.

feature: Web pet in Work chats
detail: Settings > Personalization > Pet > Select pet shows a pet inside supported Work chats, with Default for none; no floating overlay, tray or /pet command.

feature: Upload custom pet sprite sheet (web)
detail: Transparent PNG or WebP exactly 1536x1872 pixels, up to 20 MiB; uploaded pets can be edited, downloaded, refreshed or deleted.

feature: Terminal pets in Codex CLI
detail: /pets or /pet opens a picker, /pets <name> selects, /pets off disables; shows four states; needs iTerm2 3.6+ or Kitty/Sixel graphics, not in tmux or Zellij.

feature: No pets in the IDE extension
detail: The Codex IDE extension has no pet picker or overlay.

feature: Plugins bundle skills and MCP servers into reusable workflows
detail: One universal plugin directory serves ChatGPT Chat and Work (web, desktop, mobile) and Codex; Codex CLI has its own browser; the IDE extension does not support plugins.

feature: Plugins tab and Plugin Directory tabs
detail: Browse OpenAI, workspace-provided and Personal (Created by me, Shared with me) plugins, with a separate Installed row.

feature: Install a plugin with the plus button
detail: Open details, press plus, connect any required MCP service (at install or first use), then start a new chat to use it.

feature: Invoke a plugin or skill with @
detail: Describe the outcome and let ChatGPT pick tools, or type @ to name a specific plugin or bundled skill.

feature: Desktop-only plugins
detail: Some plugins can be found on web but must be installed and used in the desktop app; not on mobile.

feature: Sign in with ChatGPT for partner plugins
detail: Beta account creation or linking with partners such as Airtable, GitLab, HubSpot, Notion, Supabase and Vercel, sharing only name, email and photo; data access still needs separate approval.

feature: Plugin parts: skills, MCP servers, browser extensions, hooks
detail: A plugin may include any mix; hooks run at Codex lifecycle points and are unsupported in cloud-orchestrated Work, where only admin-defined MCP hooks apply.

feature: Example plugins (Codex Security, Gmail, Google Drive, Slack, SVG and 3D Design)
detail: Listed examples extend ChatGPT for scanning code, working in mail, Drive files, Slack channels and creating editable SVG or 3D scenes.

feature: Plugins in Sites using visitors' own accounts
detail: A Site can use plugins so each visitor's own connected accounts and permissions supply data.

feature: Apple Messages plugin (macOS, Apple Silicon build)
detail: Lets Codex and Work read, search and send iMessage, SMS and RCS on your Mac, on all plans; not for remote ChatGPT use, regular chats, web, mobile, CLI or IDE.

feature: Apple Messages send approval: Allow once or Always allow per chat
detail: Sends need approval of message and recipients by default; persistent per-chat approval can be revoked in Settings > Computer use > Manage > Messages; Full access mode may block the prompt.

feature: Admins can disable Apple Messages via Computer Use control
detail: Managed workspaces can switch the plugin off with the existing Computer Use setting.

feature: /plugins browser in Codex CLI
detail: Groups plugins by marketplace tabs, installs or uninstalls, and Space toggles an installed plugin; new session needed to use its skills.

feature: Plugins when signed in with an API key
detail: Curated OpenAI plugins can be browsed and managed with API-key Codex sign-in, but some are unavailable because of unsupported OAuth flows; usage appears on the Platform page.

feature: Admins import and sync a GitHub marketplace
detail: Workspace admins can sync a GitHub plugin marketplace for their team; plugin workspace connections are admin-controlled.

feature: Uninstall a plugin
detail: Uninstall removes the bundle but leaves connected MCP integrations connected until disconnected separately; workspace-installed plugins are admin-controlled.

feature: Build and submit your own plugin (Plugin Creator)
detail: Create plugins by conversation where Plugin Creator is available, or via developer guides, repo marketplaces and a submission review flow.

feature: Record and Replay guide
detail: Show a workflow once and turn it into a reusable skill.

feature: Work and Codex share pricing, credits and usage limits
detail: Included plan allowance can be extended with credits or USD usage-based billing; API-key sessions are billed separately at API rates.

feature: Free plan Codex access
detail: Free ($0) lets you try quick coding tasks with (model name) at Standard speed in the desktop app, subject to rollout.

feature: Go plan Codex access
detail: Go ($8/month) offers lightweight coding use with (model name) at Standard speed in the desktop app, subject to rollout.

feature: Plus plan Codex access
detail: Plus ($20/month) adds Codex on web, CLI, IDE and iOS, cloud integrations such as automatic code review and Slack, (model name) and (model name), and credits.

feature: Pro tiers at $100, $200 and $500
detail: Pro starts at $100 with everything in Plus; Ultrafast mode is limited to Pro $500.

feature: API-key sign-in for Codex
detail: Use Codex in CLI, SDK or IDE with API billing; no cloud features such as GitHub review or Slack; models follow what the key can access.

feature: Business plan Codex access
detail: About $20 per user per month billed annually (2+ users), $25 monthly; adds larger cloud VMs, credits, dedicated workspace, SAML SSO, MFA and no training on data by default.

feature: Enterprise and Edu plan additions
detail: Priority processing, SCIM, EKM, user analytics, domain verification, RBAC, audit logs via Compliance API, retention and residency controls.

feature: Included usage estimates per five-hour window
detail: Local-message estimates per model for Plus and Standard Business (ranges such as 17-180 for (model name) Sol); Pro has no five-hour limit; weekly limits may apply and cloud tasks cost more.

feature: Enterprise flexible pricing has no fixed rate limits
detail: Enterprise or Edu with flexible pricing scales with credits; without it, per-seat limits match Plus for most features.

feature: Fast mode speed multiplier
detail: Fast costs about 2x to 2.5x included usage and 2x credits versus Standard, depending on model.

feature: Ultrafast mode speed multiplier
detail: Ultrafast uses 6x to 8x included usage and 3x to 6x credits; one model family is 3x credits through Feb 28 2027, then 6x.

feature: Credits and token rates
detail: Credits pay for usage beyond included limits; rates are quoted per million input, cached input and output tokens per model, with no separate cache-write charge.

feature: USD usage-based billing for Enterprise
detail: Enterprise agreements may bill per token in dollars instead of credits; a small subset stays on a legacy rate card.

feature: Invite a friend or coworker referrals
detail: Profile menu offers Invite a friend (personal plans) or Invite a coworker (Business) by email; dialog shows reward, limits and expiry; not available on Enterprise.

feature: Sites included during public beta
detail: Sites is included with eligible plans, subject to plan, region and workspace settings.

feature: Desktop Voice priced per minute
detail: Voice uses existing usage at $0.05 per minute (1.25 credits per minute on credit plans), plus separate model token costs; unavailable with API key.

feature: Behavior at usage limit
detail: A turn already in progress may continue under fair use; Plus and Pro can buy credits; flexible-pricing workspaces buy workspace credits; API key allowed for extra local chats.

feature: Image generation counts against usage
detail: Image generation drains limits 3-5x faster than similar turns without it, then draws credits; not on Free.

feature: Usage dashboard and /status
detail: Current limits and reset times show in a usage dashboard; /status shows remaining limits in a CLI session.

feature: Code Review usage counts only via GitHub
detail: Reviews triggered by tagging in a pull request or automatic repo reviews count as Code Review; local reviews count as general usage.

feature: Tips to stretch usage
detail: Shrink prompts, limit sources, define output format, trim nested AGENTS.md and disable unused MCP servers.

feature: (model name) Astra and Sol availability
detail: On Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, Edu in Work and Codex; off by default in Enterprise and Edu until an admin enables.

feature: (model name) and Terra only in Work and Codex
detail: Both are unavailable in Chat; Enterprise and Edu keep Sol off until enabled; Terra does not support UAE inference residency.

feature: Plan matrix: Codex cloud, Work web, desktop, CLI, IDE, SDK
detail: All available on Plus through Enterprise; web and cloud features unavailable for API key.

feature: Plan matrix: automation access tokens
detail: Codex access tokens for trusted automation are Business and Enterprise only.

feature: Plan matrix: ChatGPT for Excel
detail: Available on Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise; shares usage limits with Codex.

feature: Plan matrix: voice dictation and ChatGPT Voice
detail: Both available on all paid plans, not on API key.

feature: Plan matrix: composer predictions (beta)
detail: Limited to Pro only.

feature: Plan matrix: Appshots
detail: Available on Plus, Pro and Business but not Enterprise.

feature: Plan matrix: Computer Use, Chrome, Record and Replay, browser Computer Use
detail: Marked limited (region or rollout restrictions) on all plans.

feature: Plan matrix: SSH, mobile remote control, browser in web
detail: SSH remote connections available everywhere; mobile remote control and ChatGPT web browser unavailable with API key.

feature: Plan matrix: Memories and Computer History
detail: Memories limited on all plans; Computer History not on Plus.

feature: Plan matrix: plugin sharing, connectors, Sites, Slack, Linear, GitHub review
detail: Available on Plus through Enterprise, unavailable with API key.

feature: Plan matrix: admin and security entitlements
detail: SAML SSO, MFA, cloud-managed config, no-training default: Business and up; RBAC, SCIM, EKM, retention, analytics, Compliance API, Codex Security: Enterprise.

feature: Projects group chats, files, instructions and sources
detail: A project holds related chats (Chat or Work), uploaded files, connected sources and shared instructions; web projects have Chats and Sources sections and no direct folder access.

feature: Projects view with local projects
detail: Desktop Projects view combines ChatGPT projects and local projects attached to folders on your computer.

feature: Attach multiple folders and set a primary folder
detail: Edit project > Add folder attaches several folders; Make primary sets the working directory used for Git, AGENTS.md, skills and config discovery; remote projects allow one folder.

feature: Review pane and worktrees across project folders
detail: Review pane shows changes across attached repos; PR and worktree actions target the primary repo; other folders stay attached in a worktree chat.

feature: Chats without a project
detail: Start a standalone chat from Home or New chat for self-contained work needing no shared context.

feature: Pin projects and chats
detail: Pinning keeps items near the top of the sidebar without changing context or access.

feature: Rename chats
detail: Give a chat a short outcome title.

feature: Search projects and past chats
detail: Projects view searches projects; web searches chats with Cmd/Ctrl+K; desktop has a Search chats item whose shortcut can be assigned.

feature: Archive chats and archive all chats in a project
detail: Archive finished chats, or use a project menu to archive them together; restore from Settings (Archived chats, under Data Controls on web).

feature: Locked chats protected by account PIN
detail: Lock Chat to hide it from history and search; open under Projects > Locked chats with a PIN and Lock now when done; cloud Chat and Work only, not local; locking removes it from its project; PIN reset deletes locked chats.

feature: Unlock chat
detail: Unlock chat restores a chat to normal history.

feature: Continue Work across devices with local folders
detail: After a workspace enables local computer access, start a cloud task using a local project; the folder's computer must stay online; syncing a conversation does not upload the folder.

feature: Quick chat shortcut
detail: Quick chat icon beside New chat or Cmd+Option+N (macOS) / Ctrl+Alt+N opens an ordinary ChatGPT chat outside the Codex sidebar; an existing chat can be added to a Codex chat.

feature: CLI treats start directory as the project
detail: Run codex in a directory or pass --cd/-C; /new starts a chat, /resume or codex resume continues a saved one; no Projects view.

feature: IDE treats open workspace as project
detail: Multi-root workspace lets you pick a root; Recent chats resumes chats; selection and open files add context; no Projects view.

feature: Attach files or images to one chat vs project Sources
detail: Per-chat attachments apply to a single request; files added to project Sources are shared across its chats.

feature: Type @ in composer to pick a plugin
detail: In ChatGPT the composer lets you choose a specific plugin or skill with @.

feature: Steer or queue a message while a run is active
detail: Steer injects the message into the current run; Queue holds it for the next run; desktop Settings > General > Follow-up behavior sets the default and shows a one-message override shortcut.

feature: Queued messages can be edited, reordered, sent or deleted
detail: Queued follow-ups show above the composer with edit, reorder, send and delete controls.

feature: CLI Enter to steer, Tab to queue
detail: While Codex works, Enter steers the current turn and Tab queues for the next turn.

feature: Dictate button in the composer
detail: Select Dictate to transcribe speech into the composer for review and editing before sending.

feature: Schedule a task inside a chat vs standalone scheduled task
detail: Refine a prompt in a normal chat then schedule it in that chat; a standalone scheduled task starts a new chat on each run.

feature: /plan to propose an approach before editing
detail: In the app composer /plan makes Codex investigate and propose a plan first.

feature: /goal sets a persistent goal (Goal mode)
detail: When Goal mode is available, /goal after a plan sets a persistent goal for long-running work.

feature: Attach files with @ path autocomplete and /mention
detail: CLI and app composers insert workspace paths with @ or attach a file via /mention; the IDE includes open files automatically.

feature: Add to Codex Thread command
detail: Selecting lines and running Add to Codex Thread from the command palette adds that scope to the chat context.

feature: Drag an image into the terminal to attach
detail: Dragging an image file into the CLI attaches it to the prompt; the IDE accepts drag-and-drop or paste.

feature: Delegate a plan to a cloud chat from the IDE
detail: Cloud icon under the composer picks a cloud environment; the next prompt starts a cloud chat carrying context and local changes; review the diff and open a PR; internet is off unless enabled.

feature: /review for local code review
detail: Reviews the working tree, optionally with custom focus text; rerun after fixes.

feature: @codex review on GitHub pull requests
detail: Tag Codex in a PR comment with optional focus areas after enabling Code review on the repo.

feature: $plan skill
detail: Invoking $plan yields a step-by-step refactor plan that can be revised before delegating.

feature: Work mode for multi-step deliverables vs Chat for quick tasks
detail: Work suits tasks with several sources, steps, changes or larger deliverables; Chat is for quick questions and drafts; ask for a plan and approval before external sends.

feature: ChatGPT desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux
detail: Desktop app for projects, local files, longer tasks and quick chats; sign in with a ChatGPT account or use Codex with an API key with fewer features.

feature: Switch between Chat, Work and Codex
detail: New chat page offers Chat (conversation), Work (research and finished deliverables like documents, slides, spreadsheets, Sites) and Codex (software development) from the ChatGPT dropdown.

feature: Work in Cloud with a default or published environment
detail: Choose Work in > Cloud on web or desktop, or open Codex on mobile; submit a task with the default environment without picking a repo, or select a published environment.

feature: Create and publish a reusable cloud environment
detail: Prepare repositories and tools for future cloud tasks on web or desktop.

feature: Import your setup
detail: Bring supported setup, projects and recent work into ChatGPT from other tools.

feature: Settings shortcut Cmd+, or Ctrl+,
detail: Settings opens from the app menu or this shortcut.

feature: Choose whether Enter or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends
detail: Enter can send, or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter can be required for multiline prompts or every prompt.

feature: Prevent sleep while running (macOS, Linux)
detail: Keeps local chats running while you step away.

feature: Follow-up behavior setting
detail: Chooses whether a message sent during a run steers it or waits for the next run.

feature: Profile with activity insights and profile card
detail: Shows lifetime and peak tokens, streaks, longest task and token activity; edit picture, display name, username; save a usage profile card, shareable on consumer plans.

feature: Keyboard Shortcuts editor with search
detail: Review, rebind and reset shortcuts; search by command name or by pressing a key combination.

feature: Turn-completion notification settings
detail: Choose when completion notifications appear and whether the app prompts for notification permission.

feature: Appearance: theme, colors, fonts, share theme
detail: Pick base theme, adjust accent, background and foreground colors, set UI and code fonts, and share a custom theme with friends.

feature: Pets settings
detail: Choose built-in or custom pet, Show or Hide pet, or Mini mode.

feature: Browser settings with per-site Agent permissions
detail: Install the bundled Browser plugin and extension, set default Browse, Download and Upload permissions (Requires approval, Always allow, Block) with per-site exceptions; org can restrict.

feature: Computer Use settings and macOS permission revocation
detail: Review desktop access; revoke via macOS Screen Recording or Accessibility permissions.

feature: Edit personal AGENTS.md instructions in Personalization
detail: Personal instructions are per selected machine; repository instructions can also apply.

feature: Suggested prompts
detail: Context-aware suggestions surface follow-ups and tasks to resume when starting or returning.

feature: Enable Codex memories toggle
detail: Where available, turns on carrying context from past chats into future work.

feature: Archived chats section with Unarchive
detail: Lists archived chats with dates and project context and restores them.

feature: Pop out a chat into its own window with Always on top
detail: An active chat can detach to a separate window and stay above other apps.

feature: Shortcut: Open command menu
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+P or ⌘+K; Windows Ctrl+Shift+P or Ctrl+K.

feature: Shortcut: Open settings
detail: macOS ⌘+,; Windows Ctrl+,.

feature: Shortcut: Open keyboard shortcuts
detail: macOS ⌘+/; Windows Ctrl+/.

feature: Shortcut: Open folder
detail: macOS ⌘+O; Windows Ctrl+O. Condition: Codex and Work only.

feature: Shortcut: Navigate back
detail: macOS ⌘+[ or Mouse Back; Windows Ctrl+[ or Mouse Back.

feature: Shortcut: Navigate forward
detail: macOS ⌘+] or Mouse Forward; Windows Ctrl+] or Mouse Forward.

feature: Shortcut: Increase font size
detail: macOS ⌘++ or ⌘+Numpad +; Windows Ctrl++ or Ctrl+= or Ctrl+Numpad +.

feature: Shortcut: Decrease font size
detail: macOS ⌘+- or ⌘+Numpad −; Windows Ctrl+- or Ctrl+Numpad −.

feature: Shortcut: Reset font size
detail: macOS ⌘+0 or ⌘+Numpad 0; Windows Ctrl+0 or Ctrl+Numpad 0.

feature: Shortcut: Toggle sidebar
detail: macOS ⌘+B or ⌘+⇧+S; Windows Ctrl+B or Ctrl+Shift+S.

feature: Shortcut: Toggle bottom panel
detail: macOS ⌘+J; Windows Ctrl+J. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Toggle terminal
detail: macOS ⌃+`; Windows Ctrl+`. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Clear terminal
detail: macOS ⌃+L or ⌘+K; Windows Ctrl+L or Ctrl+K. Condition: When the terminal is focused.

feature: Shortcut: Clear all unread indicators
detail: macOS ⇧+Esc; Windows Shift+Esc. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Undo last app action
detail: macOS ⌘+Z; Windows Ctrl+Z.

feature: Shortcut: Redo last app action
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+Z; Windows Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z.

feature: Shortcut: Close current tab or window
detail: macOS ⌘+W; Windows Ctrl+W or Ctrl+F4.

feature: Shortcut: Reopen closed tab
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+T; Windows Ctrl+Shift+T.

feature: Shortcut: Close other tabs
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+W; Windows Ctrl+Alt+W.

feature: Shortcut: Toggle full screen
detail: macOS ⌘+⌃+F; Windows F11.

feature: Shortcut: Quit the app
detail: macOS ⌘+Q; Windows Ctrl+Q.

feature: Shortcut: New chat
detail: macOS ⌘+N or ⌘+⇧+O; Windows Ctrl+N or Ctrl+Shift+O.

feature: Shortcut: New standalone chat
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+O; Windows Ctrl+Alt+O. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Quick chat
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+N; Windows Ctrl+Alt+N. Condition: ChatGPT only.

feature: Shortcut: New temporary chat
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+N; Windows Ctrl+Shift+N. Condition: ChatGPT only.

feature: Shortcut: Archive chat
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+A; Windows Ctrl+Shift+A.

feature: Shortcut: Mark chat as unread
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+U; Windows Ctrl+Shift+U.

feature: Shortcut: Pin or unpin chat
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+P; Windows Ctrl+Alt+P.

feature: Shortcut: Rename chat
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+R; Windows Ctrl+Alt+R.

feature: Shortcut: Open side chat
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+S; Windows Ctrl+Alt+S. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Search chats
detail: macOS Not assigned by default; Windows Not assigned by default. Condition: Assign one in Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts.

feature: Shortcut: Find in chat
detail: macOS ⌘+F; Windows Ctrl+F.

feature: Shortcut: Find next match
detail: macOS ⌘+G; Windows Ctrl+G.

feature: Shortcut: Find previous match
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+G; Windows Shift+F3.

feature: Shortcut: Previous chat or tab
detail: macOS ⌃+⇧+Tab or ⌘+⇧+[ or ⌘+⌥+←; Windows Ctrl+Shift+Tab or Ctrl+Shift+[ or Ctrl+Page Up.

feature: Shortcut: Next chat or tab
detail: macOS ⌃+Tab or ⌘+⇧+] or ⌘+⌥+→; Windows Ctrl+Tab or Ctrl+Shift+] or Ctrl+Page Down.

feature: Shortcut: Next chat needing attention
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+A; Windows Ctrl+Alt+A. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Open recent chat 1–6
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+1–6; Windows Ctrl+Alt+1–6.

feature: Shortcut: Go to chat 1–9
detail: macOS ⌘+1–9; Windows Ctrl+1–9.

feature: Shortcut: Open model picker
detail: macOS ⌃+⇧+M; Windows Ctrl+Shift+M.

feature: Shortcut: Open recent models
detail: macOS ⌃+⌘+M; Windows Alt+M.

feature: Shortcut: Open project picker
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+⇧+O; Windows Ctrl+Alt+Shift+O.

feature: Shortcut: Start voice chat
detail: macOS ⌃+⇧+V; Windows n/a. Condition: When voice chat is available.

feature: Shortcut: Restore previous composer prompt
detail: macOS ↑; Windows ↑. Condition: When the composer is empty.

feature: Shortcut: Approve request
detail: macOS ⏎; Windows ⏎. Condition: When an approval request is open.

feature: Shortcut: Decline request
detail: macOS Esc; Windows Esc. Condition: When an approval request is open.

feature: Shortcut: Switch to Chat, Work, or Codex
detail: macOS ⌃+1 or ⌃+2 or ⌃+3; Windows Alt+1 or Alt+2 or Alt+3. Condition: In the order shown.

feature: Shortcut: Toggle Activity view
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+U; Windows Ctrl+Alt+U. Condition: When Activity is available.

feature: Shortcut: Run environment action 1
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+D; Windows Win+Shift+D; Linux Super+Shift+D. Condition: When the environment defines a primary action.

feature: Shortcut: Search files
detail: macOS ⌘+P; Windows Ctrl+P. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Toggle file tree
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+E; Windows Ctrl+Shift+E. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Open review tab
detail: macOS ⌃+⇧+G; Windows Ctrl+Shift+G. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Switch between chat and tabs
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+B; Windows Ctrl+Alt+B. Condition: In full view; shows or hides tabs in split view.

feature: Shortcut: Open browser tab
detail: macOS ⌘+T; Windows Ctrl+T. Condition: When the built-in browser is available.

feature: Shortcut: Cycle workspace layout
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+B; Windows Ctrl+Shift+B. Condition: Full view, split view, or hidden tabs.

feature: Shortcut: Enter or exit full view
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+F; Windows Ctrl+Shift+F.

feature: Shortcut: Go to line or focus browser address bar
detail: macOS ⌘+L; Windows Ctrl+L. Condition: Depends on the focused view.

feature: Shortcut: Browser back
detail: macOS ⌘+←; Windows Alt+←. Condition: When the built-in browser is focused.

feature: Shortcut: Browser forward
detail: macOS ⌘+→; Windows Alt+→. Condition: When the built-in browser is focused.

feature: Shortcut: Reload browser page
detail: macOS ⌘+R; Windows Ctrl+R. Condition: When the built-in browser is focused.

feature: Shortcut: Reload browser page without cache
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+R; Windows Ctrl+Shift+R. Condition: When the built-in browser is focused.

feature: Shortcut: Copy browser URL
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+C; Windows Ctrl+Shift+C. Condition: When the built-in browser is focused.

feature: Shortcut: Toggle browser browse or comment mode
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+.; Windows Ctrl+Shift+.. Condition: When browser commenting is available.

feature: Shortcut: Copy conversation path
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+⇧+C; Windows Ctrl+Alt+Shift+C. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Copy chat deep link
detail: macOS ⌘+⌥+L; Windows Ctrl+Alt+L.

feature: Shortcut: Copy working directory
detail: macOS ⌘+⇧+C; Windows Ctrl+Shift+C; Linux Ctrl+Shift+C |To find, customize, or reset app shortcuts, open Settings > Keyboard. Condition: Codex only.

feature: Shortcut: Take an Appshot
detail: macOS ⌘+⌘; Windows n/a. Condition: press both keys simultaneously.

feature: Keyboard shortcut customization and Appshot global shortcut
detail: Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts lets you find by name or keystroke, rebind and reset; Appshots have a separate global shortcut under Settings > Appshots; Linux native Wayland can limit shortcuts.

feature: Search chats matches content and Git branch names
detail: Search chats has no default shortcut; with expanded matching it finds phrases in chat content and branch names.

feature: Find in chat
detail: Searches text within the open chat only.

feature: codex:// deep links for chats
detail: codex://threads/new, threads/<id> and new?prompt/path/originUrl open a new or existing local chat, optionally prefilled and in a workspace; does not auto-send.

feature: codex:// deep links to start a plugin-backed chat
detail: A prompt containing a plugin mention opens a chat; if the plugin is uninstalled the user is asked to install and connect, then Continue.

feature: codex:// deep links to Settings pages
detail: Open Settings, Browser, Computer Use for Chrome, Remote connections, computer, devices and SSH pages, including adding an SSH config host.

feature: codex:// deep links to Skills and Scheduled
detail: codex://skills opens Skills; codex://automations opens Scheduled with the create flow.

feature: codex:// deep links for plugin install, detail and local plugin
detail: Open install flow from a marketplace, plugin detail, or a local marketplace plugin with optional share mode.

feature: codex:// deep link to install a pet
detail: Opens pet install with name, image URL, optional description and sprite version 1 or 2.

feature: Review pane shows all Git changes, with staged, unstaged, branch vs main and Las
detail: The review panel reflects repo Git state, including edits Codex did not make; switch views to isolate only the last turn.

feature: Remove a project from the sidebar and re-add it
detail: Hover menu > Remove; restore with Add new project or Cmd/Ctrl+O.

feature: Sidebar filter with Chronological view
detail: The filter icon beside Chats changes which chats show; Chronological reveals chats hidden by project state.

feature: Work conversations sync by account and workspace, separate from Codex history
detail: Look in Work history on each device; requires workspace owner to enable Work Cloud and Allow local computer access; enforce_residency policy blocks it.

feature: Offline host falls back to cloud container
detail: If the computer is offline, a synced turn may run in a cloud container without local files; turning off local access lets new turns use Work Cloud only.

feature: Policy API for Global settings, Agent Security UI for Local and Cloud
detail: Automation of Global policies uses the policy API; Local or Codex Cloud settings are managed in the Agent Security UI.

feature: Worktree setup via local environment or .worktreeinclude
detail: Worktrees inherit only Git-tracked files; use setup scripts or .worktreeinclude to copy ignored files.

feature: Shared local environment in project .codex folder
detail: Teammates pick up a local environment only when its config is in the project root .codex folder.

feature: Scheduled runs create worktrees; archive old runs
detail: Frequent scheduled tasks accumulate worktrees; archiving runs and not pinning them cleans up.

feature: Up arrow restores prompt after wrong target
detail: Cancelling a run started on the wrong target (Local, Worktree, Cloud) and pressing Up in the composer recovers the prompt.

feature: Approve for me automatic review mode
detail: Permissions control below the composer offers Approve for me; may be disabled by guardian_approval config or managed policy; options differ between local and cloud.

feature: Desktop app and CLI can ship different Codex versions
detail: Features can reach one surface first; version checks via codex --version or the bundled binary.

feature: Feedback via / in composer with optional session share
detail: Typing / offers feedback, optionally sharing the existing session, and returns a session ID; bugs can go to the public GitHub repo.

feature: Log and transcript locations
detail: App logs on macOS, session transcripts and archived sessions live under the Codex home directory.

feature: Integrated terminal toggle and code font setting
detail: Ctrl+backtick reopens a stuck terminal; Code font in Settings controls review pane and terminal font.

feature: Network policy priority across layers
detail: Higher-priority policy wins even if less specific; OS-specific overrides beat all-OS then Global; managed listener ports and non-loopback proxies are unsupported in cloud runtime.

feature: macOS asks approval for protected folders (Music, Downloads, Desktop)
detail: Codex reading the home directory triggers macOS prompts for protected folders.

feature: Remote connections to a Mac or Windows host
detail: Codex tab (or Remote) in the ChatGPT mobile app, or another desktop app, drives chats on a connected host using that host's projects, files, plugins, Computer Use and sandbox.

feature: What you can do remotely
detail: Start or continue chats, steer, answer questions, approve commands, review outputs, diffs and screenshots, get notified, and switch hosts.

feature: Pair a phone by QR code
detail: On the host, Settings > Connections > Control this Mac or PC > Set up shows a QR code; pair each phone or device with each host; connections unused since June 8 2026 need re-pairing.

feature: Control other devices from a desktop
detail: Settings > Connections > Control other devices adds another host; a device can both allow control and control others.

feature: Keep host awake setting and lid behavior
detail: Host can stay awake; Mac laptop needs lid open with power or external display; Sleep stops access; Windows host must stay unlocked for Computer Use.

feature: Dedicated always-on computer or remote dev environment as host
detail: Use a persistent Mac/Windows PC or SSH/remote environment so ChatGPT stays reachable for long tasks.

feature: Secure relay for reaching hosts
detail: A relay layer connects authorized devices without exposing hosts to the public internet.

feature: SSH remote projects
detail: Add hosts from SSH config; chats run commands and edit files on the remote host, which needs Codex installed and on PATH; pattern-only hosts are ignored.

feature: Hand off a chat between hosts
detail: From the chat footer choose a destination host and Hand off; Git state moves via a worktree; requires a matching saved project; interrupts a running response; cloud handoff unsupported.

feature: Admin must enable Remote Control for workspaces
detail: Workspace admins may need to allow Remote Control before phones can connect; MFA, SSO or passkey may be required.

feature: Signing out turns off Remote Control but keeps pairings
detail: After sign-in, toggle Remote Control on to restore the prior connection state.

feature: Sandbox for local agent commands
detail: Spawned commands run in an enforced boundary limiting files and network so routine work proceeds without constant confirmation; sandbox sets limits, approval policy sets when to ask.

feature: Platform sandbox prerequisites
detail: macOS works out of the box; Windows uses native sandbox in PowerShell or Linux sandbox in WSL2; Linux/WSL2 need bubblewrap installed, with AppArmor setup on Ubuntu 24.04.

feature: Permissions control beneath composer
detail: Menu can offer Ask for approval, Approve for me, Full access and named or custom permission profiles; choose narrowest approval scope (once or session).

feature: /permissions picker in the CLI
detail: Opens a picker to change the active permissions profile.

feature: Sandbox modes: read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access
detail: read-only inspects only; workspace-write edits within the workspace and runs routine commands (default low-friction); danger-full-access removes boundaries.

feature: Approval policies: on-request and never
detail: on-request asks only when leaving the sandbox; never suppresses prompts; the older untrusted policy is retired.

feature: Writable roots for extra directories
detail: sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots extends where the agent may write without removing the sandbox.

feature: Rules to allow, prompt or forbid command prefixes
detail: Command-prefix rules grant exceptions outside the sandbox more narrowly than widening access.

feature: approvals_reviewer: user or auto_review
detail: Chooses whether eligible approval prompts go to the user (default) or a reviewer agent.

feature: Work network access setting for code and shell commands
detail: Settings > Data controls > Work network access with Allow public internet access; when off only a managed hostname allowlist is reachable; separate controls for web search, plugins and remote browser.

feature: Local computer access with Work Cloud policy layers
detail: Cloud containers follow Work Cloud policies, local steps follow local requirements; desktop browser site rules do not apply to cloud browsers; test each environment separately.

feature: Auto-review (Approve for me) reviewer agent
detail: A separate reviewer agent decides eligible approval requests and returns a rationale; only applies when approvals are interactive and sandbox boundaries exist.

feature: Daybreak model auto-switches to Approve for me
detail: Picking an approved Daybreak model (also via /model) switches permissions to Approve for me when allowed; Full Access shows a warning for those models.

feature: What triggers an auto-review
detail: Escalated shell calls, prompt-rule commands, approval-requiring network destinations, edits outside writable roots, and MCP or app tool calls needing approval.

feature: What auto-review blocks
detail: Sending secrets to untrusted places, probing for credentials, broad security weakening and destructive irreversible actions.

feature: Reviewer sees compact transcript, no hidden reasoning
detail: Reviewer reads messages, tool calls and outputs plus the request and can run read-only checks; chain-of-thought is excluded.

feature: Denial handling and turn interruption
detail: Denied actions tell the agent to find a safer path or ask; CLI stops a turn after 3 consecutive or 10 of 50 denials, or the first denial for cybersecurity models; timeouts are not proof of risk.

feature: /approve override for a denied action
detail: Opens an Auto-review Denials picker (up to 10 recent) to approve one exact action for a single retry that is still reviewed.

feature: Custom reviewer policy and admin-required auto-review
detail: Replace the policy via [auto_review].policy or managed guardian_policy_config (managed wins); admins can require auto-review and restrict approval policies and reviewers.

feature: Cybersecurity engagement configuration
detail: Combine auto-review with a least-privilege permission profile and written scope; prefix allow rules are ignored for cyber models.

feature: Security documentation hub
detail: Groups permissions, sandboxing, auto-review, approvals, internet access controls for cloud chats, Codex Security (plugin, CLI, SDK, Daybreak setup, Security Review, threat model) and cyber-safety guidance on approved models and Trusted Access.

feature: Codex Security vulnerability scanning
detail: Scans code for vulnerabilities and reports findings with evidence; runs in Daybreak Defense Factory, Codex, a terminal CLI or an SDK.

feature: Daybreak Defense Factory overview of open and fixed findings
detail: Overview shows proposed fixes, open findings by severity and daily trend across repositories.

feature: Security scan workflows: scan, deep scan, code changes, backlog triage, fix, exp
detail: Guides cover focused scans, repeated deep scans, checking a PR, commit or diff, triaging other scanners' findings, patch generation and verification, and exporting findings.

feature: Codex Security standalone CLI (codex-security / cs)
detail: npm package that runs standard scans of local repositories and saves a report; needs Node 22.13+/24/26 and Python 3.10+; runs with your OS permissions and does not pause for approval.

feature: Security CLI login with ChatGPT, device auth or API key
detail: login uses ChatGPT, --device-auth for headless machines if the workspace allows, or API keys and Amazon Bedrock credentials.

feature: Scan dry run and private output directory
detail: --dry-run validates target and output location without starting; --output-dir keeps results (which may include source excerpts) outside the repo.

feature: Daybreak Blue model and cyber access program flags
detail: Workspaces with Daybreak Blue access can pass model and cyber-access-program options to the scan.

feature: Scan dashboard, headless mode, JSON output
detail: Interactive terminals show a live dashboard; --headless gives progress lines; --json yields machine-readable stdout.

feature: Scan exit codes and severity policy
detail: Exit 0 on completion, 1 when findings meet a severity threshold, 2 on input or execution failures; severity does not fail scans by default.

feature: Scan artifacts: report.md, scan-manifest.json, findings.json
detail: Results dir holds a readable report, manifest with status and scope, findings and supporting artifacts; keep together when sharing.

feature: Export saved threat model as Markdown
detail: export --artifact threat-model works offline for Standard, Deep and Diff scans.

feature: scans list and show, finding browser
detail: List scans for a repo, show one by ID; interactive scans offer a finding browser plus validate and patch commands.

feature: Scan variants: paths or diff, component scans, custom validation, deep scan limi
detail: CLI options select targets, parallel components, validation scripts, deep scan runtime, architecture context, model and effort, and an estimated cost cap.

feature: Cloud scans billed by token usage, not plan allowance
detail: Repository scans and continuous monitoring bill in credits or USD from one shared workspace balance; free scanning credits do not expire.

feature: Usage page: Scan cost and Billable remainder per repository
detail: Compare cost by repo over a date range before and after credits and exemptions.

feature: Repository scan, continuous monitoring, scheduled scan, PR reviews
detail: Different scan types for existing issues, new default-branch commits, recurring reviews and pre-merge checks.

feature: Pause continuous monitoring per repository
detail: Repositories > Continuous scanning settings toggle Continuous monitoring off and on.

feature: Editable threat model per monitored repository
detail: Edit the Threat model when architecture or assumptions change; edits apply to future scans.

feature: Cloud scans need GitHub; GitLab via local or CI
detail: Cloud scans use connected GitHub repos; GitLab code can use a local checkout or CLI in GitLab CI.

feature: Fix with Codex and Create PR for proposed patches
detail: Daybreak saves a patch for review; Fix with Codex refines it and Create PR opens a draft GitHub pull request; patches are never auto-applied.

feature: Findings page with severity/status chart, owners, scanner, search and repo filte
detail: Table lists owner, reporting scanner and detection date; detail shows summary, root cause, evidence, exploit path and status.

feature: Import findings from other scanners
detail: Settings > Integrations or report upload; confirming a shared destination authorizes assessment and publication of Reportable results; private ones stay in My recent imports; Observations lists per-scanner evidence.

feature: Generate fixes in bulk and review with Patch checker
detail: Fix on one or many findings prepares patches under Fixes; diff plus Patch checker show what was verified; mark Fixed only after verifying on the merged revision.

feature: Workspace webhook for scan events
detail: Settings > Notifications > Add takes a name and public HTTPS endpoint on 443 and sends scan.finished or scan.updated events across the workspace.

feature: Webhook signing secret shown once, test event
detail: HMAC-SHA256 signed requests per the Standard Webhooks spec; Send test notification sends a sample with is_test true; 10 second delivery window.

feature: Edit, pause and rotate webhook secret
detail: Change URL or events, disable Enabled to pause, rotate the secret with optional 24-hour overlap where both secrets sign.

feature: Codex Security plugin install
detail: Install from Plugins (desktop, then Security appears in sidebar) or /plugins in CLI; may show Disabled by admin in managed workspaces; separate Daybreak Defense Factory (Preview) plugin handles cloud GitHub scans.

feature: Security workbench: Scans, Findings, Repositories
detail: + Scan picks a codebase or folder, Deep scan toggle, model and effort, optional Additional context, Start scan, View activity.

feature: Ask Codex to run a Codex Security scan
detail: Prompting a scan in the terminal runs without a setup workspace and writes report.md plus manifest, findings and coverage files.

feature: Plugin and Codex versions tracked separately
detail: codex plugin list --json shows installed versions; the standalone npm package bundles its own plugin copy.

feature: Security CLI bulk-scan campaigns
detail: bulk-scan reviews many repositories in one campaign, saves progress, keeps per-repo results and resumes after interruption.

feature: Bulk scan GitHub discovery
detail: Interactive picker over personal or org repos active in 90 days (excludes archived and forks), pins default-branch commits, supports GitHub Enterprise Server via GH_HOST.

feature: Bulk scan CSV inventory with pinned revisions
detail: CSV columns id, repository, revision (full SHA), scope, mode (standard or deep) and per-repo prompt give repeatable campaigns.

feature: Bulk scan workers, knowledge base and prompt files
detail: --workers (default 4) parallelism, repeatable --knowledge-base files, shared scan prompt and post-scan follow-up prompt files.

feature: Bulk scan model, effort and provider options
detail: Defaults to a Sol model at xhigh effort; --model and --effort override; OpenRouter, Fireworks or Amazon Bedrock supported via provider settings.

feature: Bulk scan results, SARIF export, resume and retries
detail: Output dir holds manifest, results.jsonl and per-attempt reports; export to SARIF; rerun same command to resume; --max-attempts retries transient errors; exit codes 0, 1, 2, 130, 143.

feature: Bulk scans in hardened Docker Compose
detail: Linux Docker setup with mounted CSV, output and sign-in state for automated campaigns.

feature: Security scans in CI
detail: Run scans on pull or merge requests, default branch and schedules using an API key stored as a CI secret; scans use runner permissions and do not pause for approval.

feature: Daybreak Blue model via Trusted Access for Cyber in CI
detail: Action inputs or CLI flags select the Sol model and daybreak_blue program, but access must be granted to the API project.

feature: Severity policy for blocking merges
detail: Start advisory, then enforce a threshold on findings of the current scan only; check completeness separately.

feature: GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD or other CI integration
detail: A GitHub Action adds summary and annotations; a GitLab pipeline supports merge-request, default-branch and scheduled scans; other CI runs the npm CLI with --auth api-key.

feature: Scan auth selection: --auth chatgpt vs api-key
detail: Environment API keys win by default for non-interactive and JSON scans even after login; pick explicitly or unset the key variables.

feature: scans list, show, logs and CODEX_SECURITY_STATE_DIR
detail: Browse saved scans and view unredacted logs; set a writable private state directory if the default is unwritable.

feature: findings list and scans compare
detail: Lists open findings across scans and compares two scans, matching by root cause into new, persisting, reopened, not observed, resolved and unknown.

feature: findings false-positive feedback
detail: Recording a reason gives future scans context without suppressing a rule, path or class.

feature: scans rerun and validate to recheck fixes
detail: Rerun keeps original config and plugin version; validate rechecks a finding against a changed checkout.

feature: Deep scan --max-time and --max-cost
detail: Deadline up to 96 hours (default) and an estimated, non-hard cost cap in USD; budget-limited deep scans may still save a report with a warning.

feature: install-hook pre-commit check
detail: The CLI can install a hook to scan before each commit.

feature: Codex Security GitHub Action for scheduled repository scans
detail: Workflow scans the default branch on a cron or manual dispatch, with optional folder paths, model and effort inputs, and report-only findings by default.

feature: GitHub Action pull-request scans
detail: Scans PR changes from same-repo branches, verifies head and base freshness, skips fork PRs, reads SECURITY.md, and reports a check named for the target branch.

feature: GitHub Action Daybreak Blue/Red and standard safeguards
detail: cyber-access-program input selects daybreak_blue, daybreak_red or standard; a refusal that aborts the scan fails the Action even when fail-on-severity is none.

feature: GitHub Action cost threshold input
detail: max-cost sets an estimated USD limit (PR template uses $5); in-flight requests may exceed it.

feature: GitHub Action report artifacts and SARIF upload
detail: upload-artifacts saves downloadable reports (default 7-day retention); optional SARIF upload to GitHub Code Security needs security-events write permission.

feature: GitHub Action fail-on-severity and completed-scan gate
detail: Set a severity threshold to fail the check and optionally add a gate job requiring a completed scan, which also blocks fork PRs and empty diffs.

feature: GitLab CI/CD pipeline for Codex Security
detail: Scans committed changes and protected branches, publishes SARIF to GitLab Security (needs GitLab Ultimate 19.2+), keeps scan credentials apart from repo write access; scan-only reporting first.

feature: GitLab scan profiles by trigger
detail: Protected merge request gets a standard low-effort diff scan; opt-in default-branch push gets a high-effort full scan; opt-in schedule gets a deep xhigh scan.

feature: GitLab exit-code gate separate from reporting
detail: A report job exports SARIF and a separate gate restores the scanner exit status; --fail-on-severity high blocks on high and critical findings.

feature: GitLab verified remediation and draft merge requests
detail: Optional on protected default branch: needs a failing-then-passing regression test, rejects protected-file edits, uses verify-fix, and a Developer-role token opens a never-auto-merged draft MR.

feature: GitLab pipeline variables for budgets and opt-ins
detail: Variables control version pin, default-branch scans, scheduled deep scan time and cost limits, remediation, patch size (1-20 files), MR creation and test commands.

feature: Security CLI command set
detail: Commands cover scan, scan import, import continuum and github, policy, init, install-hook, bulk-scan, scan-components, scans, findings, export, publish, classify-severity, suggest-owners, dedupe, validate, patch, verify-fix, feedback, login, logout, info.

feature: Security CLI discoverability: --llms manifest, --schema, completions, --update
detail: Prints an agent-readable command manifest and JSON scan schema, generates Bash/zsh/fish completions and updates itself.

feature: Security CLI mcp add and skills add
detail: Registers the CLI as an MCP server exposing only read-only info, and syncs Security skills to agents.

feature: Scan targets: paths, diff, working tree, exclusions
detail: Choose repository, --path, --diff base/head or --working-tree (mutually exclusive) plus --exclude-path; deep mode supports repository and path targets.

feature: Scan mode standard vs deep and deep tuning flags
detail: Deep adds --workers, --subagents, --stop-after-no-new, --max-discovery-runs and --max-time controls.

feature: Project configuration file (init, --config)
detail: init creates YAML or JSON config selected explicitly with --config; never auto-discovered, and untrusted repo configs must not be used.

feature: Knowledge base documents for scans
detail: --knowledge-base accepts text, JSON, SARIF, PDF and DOCX files or directories to supply architecture, threat models or policies.

feature: Custom validation prompt and --validate source assessment
detail: --validation-prompt-file replaces the final validation step with your test procedure; --validate adds a source-only assessment report.

feature: Custom severity rubric
detail: --rubric FILE swaps the bundled severity policy for your Markdown rubric.

feature: scan --patch, --patch-severity and --create-pr
detail: Fixes and verifies findings after a scan and can open a draft GitHub PR or GitLab MR with verified patches.

feature: Scan output options: archive-existing, mock, workflow-id, show-cost, formats
detail: Archive prior results, synthetic mock findings, reuse workflow work, show estimated cost, print results as toon, json, yaml or jsonl.

feature: Security CLI provider, model and effort selection
detail: Providers openai, openrouter, fireworks, amazon-bedrock; default Sol model at xhigh effort; --codex overrides config values; review.config.toml profile supported.

feature: Amazon Bedrock Daybreak Blue and Red model IDs
detail: Bedrock scans use AWS credentials and region us-east-2 with specific Blue and Red model IDs after OpenAI and AWS provisioning approval.

feature: Attribute scans with --safety-identifier
detail: Hashed stable user identifier for API-key scans, needing a Codex build that forwards it.

feature: scan import from CSV or JSON
detail: Saves existing findings as a completed scan without model calls; duplicates preserved and input retained.

feature: import continuum and import github
detail: Collect AWS Continuum findings or GitHub code scanning alerts (by number, ref, state) for validation.

feature: install-hook pre-commit scan
detail: Scans staged and unstaged changes and blocks commits on high or critical findings; threshold configurable; local hook optional.

feature: policy command drafts SECURITY.md
detail: Drafts a security policy outside the repo for review without altering files.

feature: scan-components per-component scans
detail: Scans each service separately, optionally from a reviewed plan file, combines and matches findings, and retries only failed components.

feature: scans rerun, logs, match and compare
detail: Rerun with saved settings (same plugin version), view unredacted logs, match findings by root cause and compare scans.

feature: export formats: SARIF, JSON, CSV, Markdown, ServiceNow AVIT
detail: Exports findings or a saved threat model; ServiceNow format needs a template CSV and Ethical Hacker role.

feature: publish scan to Linear or a custom findings service
detail: Creates Linear issues (via connected app or API key, with team, project, assignee, dry-run, skip-existing) or posts sealed findings to a custom HTTPS service.

feature: publish findings: local report or Daybreak Cloud import
detail: Previews and saves third-party findings (Dependabot, CrowdStrike) locally then publishes to private Cloud inbox; imported findings start not_assessed.

feature: classify-severity, suggest-owners, dedupe, verify-fix
detail: Reassess severity by rubric, suggest owners from CODEOWNERS and Git history, find duplicates, and check fixes in a read-only sandbox.

feature: security CLI feedback command
detail: Sends a problem description to OpenAI and returns an ID for support.

feature: validate and patch commands
detail: validate assesses candidate findings against current source; patch generates a verified fix, can resume PR creation and patch Linear issues selected by ID, project or filter.

feature: Security CLI login, logout, device auth, API key and enterprise token
detail: Interactive or device login, stdin API key, enterprise access token, status check and logout.

feature: Scan completion summary, verbose diagnostics and exit codes
detail: stderr summary with severity breakdown; --verbose or CODEX_SECURITY_LOG_LEVEL=debug for diagnostics; exit codes include 0, 1, 2, 130, 143.

feature: Codex Security plugin: standard repository scan
detail: Scans a whole repo or one folder (monorepo service) for vulnerabilities via threat modeling, discovery, validation, attack-path analysis and a report. Started from Security > Scans > + Scan > Codebase or with the security-scan skill.

feature: Security scan setup: model, reasoning effort, additional context
detail: Scan setup lets you pick the model and reasoning effort (docs recommend the top model at xhigh) and add free-text context on attacker inputs, trust boundaries and priorities. Repo shows current branch and revision.

feature: SECURITY.md policy files guide scans
detail: Root and nested SECURITY.md files hold threat model, invariants, reportable criteria, exclusions and severity context; the closest file wins. A define-security-policy skill reviews or updates them.

feature: Security change review (diff scan)
detail: Reviews uncommitted changes, a single commit, or a base-to-head range for security regressions, limited to changed files and direct support code. Deep scan is not offered for change scans; it does not switch branches.

feature: Run Codex Security in CI via codex exec
detail: Install the Codex CLI and plugin, pass an API key as an env var, and run the diff-scan skill in GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines or Jenkins; forked PRs are skipped and outputs archived as artifacts.

feature: Scan output directory: report, findings JSON, manifest, coverage
detail: Each scan writes report.md, findings.json with stable IDs and severity/confidence, a sealed scan-manifest.json, coverage.json, plus optional per-finding writeups and hardening proposals.

feature: Deep security scan
detail: Runs several independent standard scans over the same repo or folder and merges findings; for repeated review at higher time and token cost. Toggle Deep scan in setup or use the deep-security-scan skill.

feature: Deep scan runtime config (workers, subagents, stop rules, time cap)
detail: config.toml [deep_scan] sets workers (default 4), subagents per worker (3), stop after 4 scans with no new findings, stop after 3 consecutive errors, max 40 runs, max_time_hours up to 96.

feature: Deep scan interruption handling and partial coverage
detail: A scan keeps running if a wait times out and can be continued; failed or canceled scans keep saved findings separate from unconfirmed candidates, and coverage is marked partial. Policy-blocked worker requests stop without retry.

feature: Export findings as JSON, CSV or SARIF
detail: Completed scans export structured findings for tools, spreadsheets or code-scanning integrations; plugin CSV includes triage status, close reasons and notes while CLI export does not. Markdown report opens in the configured editor.

feature: Track findings in Linear, GitHub Issues, Jira or draft Security Advisory
detail: The track-findings skill drafts an issue for validated findings (one destination per run) or a private draft GitHub Security Advisory for one finding; it shows a preview, needs approval, and verifies the result after creation.

feature: Generate, apply and verify a security patch for a finding
detail: Finding Patch tab: Generate patch (no checkout change), review diff, Apply patch, Verify fix (reruns reproducer, regression test, nearby bypasses, repo tests). Verification does not auto-close the finding; fix-finding skill does it in chat.

feature: Verify-fix skill returns fixed, still_vulnerable or inconclusive
detail: Checks whether an existing patch resolves a reported finding without changing files or trackers, giving a verdict with evidence and limits; run only on explicit request.

feature: Assess patch risk skill
detail: Reviews a proposed change against exact revisions and gives an advisory merge, revise or no-change recommendation, weighing impact, likelihood and recovery difficulty; it does not merge code.

feature: Recover findings from failed scans
detail: Valid saved findings can be recovered from a selected failed scan on request without rerunning; not available for running, completed or canceled scans. Findings are saved as workers progress.

feature: Daybreak / Trusted Access advisory before scans
detail: Before scans the plugin checks Daybreak access for ChatGPT-signed-in sessions and shows an enrollment link or warning; it is advisory and never blocks the scan. API-key-only sessions cannot verify access.

feature: Scan model providers: OpenAI, Bedrock, OpenRouter, Fireworks
detail: Scans can run on Amazon Bedrock (tokens, profiles, web identity), and credentials for OpenRouter and Fireworks or OPENAI_API_KEY pass to deep-scan workers.

feature: Live scan progress and token usage
detail: Shows phase, elapsed time, active workers, reviewed files and total/input/cached/output token usage across the scan and workers; scans can be cancelled, resumed or rerun with saved settings.

feature: Security workbench: scan history, findings filters, compare scans
detail: Security > Scans and Findings list repos, scans and findings with filters, sorting by confidence, reruns, and comparison labelling findings new, persisting, resolved or not rescanned.

feature: False-positive close reasons carried to later scans
detail: Closing a finding as false positive records a reason that suppresses the recurrence in later scans of the same target only while the reason still holds.

feature: Vulnerability write-up and security hardening skills
detail: vulnerability-writeup turns rough findings or PoCs into polished reports; propose-security-hardening produces evidence-backed structural options from scans or incident documents.

feature: Triage existing findings from scanners, advisories, Jira, Linear, GitHub
detail: Triage skill checks external findings against current code and returns an evidence-backed verdict with a ranked action queue; asks before importing Linear sub-issues.

feature: Security workbench in the desktop app (Scans, Findings, Repositories)
detail: Under Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app, a Security sidebar entry lists scans, cross-repo findings with search/filter (Summary and Patch tabs) and per-repo scan history; View activity opens the underlying Codex task and Stop scan cancels it.

feature: Security hardening proposal workflow
detail: Compares structural fixes for recurring vulnerability patterns with tradeoffs, before/after diagrams, migration and rollback plans; read-only until you pick an option. Output goes to a hardening folder linked from report.md.

feature: Backlog triage with confirmed / not_actionable / needs_review verdicts
detail: Read-only static analysis of pasted SARIF/CVE/advisories or imported Jira, Linear or GitHub (code scanning, Dependabot, advisories) findings, one verdict per input with separate ranking; dynamic validation skill follows for needs_review.

feature: Vulnerability report writer
detail: Produces one self-contained report per distinct vulnerability (grouped by root cause) with source excerpts, PoC files and safe-run notes, verified against source; works without running a scan.

feature: Daybreak: import scanner findings (Wiz, Snyk, Endor Labs)
detail: Connect a scanner or upload a report (Wiz JSON, Snyk CSV, Endor JSON; 32 MiB, 10,000 rows) so Daybreak assesses findings against the code; results stay private or are published to a shared destination as Reportable, Deferred, Suppressed or Not applicable.

feature: Import scanner reports via CLI publish findings
detail: The codex-security CLI previews and publishes saved scanner exports locally or to the cloud, with dry-run previews and receipts; also supports AWS Continuum and CrowdStrike IaC reports.

feature: Codex Security TypeScript SDK
detail: npm package to run scans (repo, folder, diff, deep), preflight, component scans, validation, cost cap, progress callbacks and export from your own tooling; needs Node 22.13+ and Python 3.10+.

feature: SDK scan controls: prompts, cost cap, abort, providers
detail: SDK options include extra scan/validation prompts, knowledge-base paths, a max dollar cost, abort signals, archiving existing output, and swapping to Bedrock, OpenRouter or other model providers.

feature: Security Review of GitHub pull requests
detail: Automatic or manual (@codex security review comment) review of a PR diff for vulnerabilities, posting findings above a severity threshold; full report in the Codex task Security Report tab. Not on Plus; uses Codex allowance or credits.

feature: Auto security review: Review policy and Trigger options
detail: Per repository, Review chooses personal preferences, All PRs or Team PRs; Trigger chooses On PR open, On every push, or alongside Code Review. Threat-model file source and per-path severity thresholds are configurable (default auto High+Critical, manual Medium+).

feature: Daybreak Defense Factory: cloud and local scanning
detail: A ChatGPT plugin (preview) that scans a connected GitHub repo or folder in Codex cloud as one-off, continuous monitoring of new commits, or scheduled scans; local scans in the desktop app with optional Deep scan. Requires a personal GitHub connection.

feature: Daybreak editable repository threat model and validation context
detail: Each monitored repo has a generated threat model you can edit, plus validation context and SECURITY.md view; changes apply to future scans.

feature: Sign in with ChatGPT for third-party apps
detail: Continue with ChatGPT signs you into partner apps sharing name, email and picture, and links to an existing account by matching email.

feature: Use your ChatGPT plan inside partner apps
detail: A separate consent lets partner apps (coding tools, Notion, Vercel etc.) spend your plan's Codex/work usage, without access to chats or memories and with no extra allowance; Go, Plus, Pro, Business eligible.

feature: Per-app weekly usage limits and disconnect
detail: Settings > Usage shows connected-app usage and lets you cap each app at a percentage of weekly plan usage; Security and login > Sign in with ChatGPT lets you disconnect an app.

feature: Admin control of external apps and plan usage
detail: Business admins allow Use ChatGPT plan per app under Tenant settings > External access, and set a workspace-wide percent of each member allowance external services may use.

feature: Sites: build, host and share a website from ChatGPT or Codex
detail: Describe a site (resource hub, dashboard, tracker, request form, calculator, guided process) or host an existing web app; supports HTTP, HTTPS, WebSockets but not raw TCP, and Remix of a coworker's site.

feature: Sites hosting allowance and pricing
detail: Monthly hosting credits: Plus 125, Pro 375, Business 125 per seat, Enterprise from contract pool. Free through Dec 31 2026; from Jan 1 2027 overage is billed (traffic 16 credits per 100k requests, DB 150 and files 3.75 per GiB, custom domain 25, private tunnel 125).

feature: Sites storage limits and prohibited uses
detail: D1 database capped at 10 GB per site, R2 file storage uncapped; payments only via third-party processors; no PHI, child-targeting, malware or impersonation. Per-site usage view arrives Dec 1 2026.

feature: Start a site via the word website or @Sites mention
detail: Including website in a prompt or mentioning @Sites starts the sites workflow; plugins can be mentioned with @ to feed data. Enterprise workspaces need an admin to enable Sites.

feature: Sites list and in-preview Edit
detail: Sites are found under More > sites on web or the sites view in desktop; the preview has an Edit mode to describe changes with Screenshot or Add files attachments. CLI and IDE have no sites management view.

feature: Remix an existing site
detail: A Remix button in the site toolbar opens a ChatGPT composer with the source site attached so you can adapt a coworker's site to a new purpose.

feature: Save a site version without deploying
detail: Publishing has two stages, save a reviewable version then deploy it; every deployment URL is production, so ask to save without deploying to review first. Saved versions can be listed.

feature: Deploy an existing local project as a site
detail: Ask ChatGPT to check a local project for compatibility and prepare it; linkage stored in .openai/hosting.json. Sites are separate from ChatGPT Projects.

feature: Site storage: D1 database and R2 file storage
detail: Sites can use D1 relational storage for records, R2 object storage for uploads, or both; server-side access rules are recommended since hiding buttons does not protect records.

feature: Sign in with ChatGPT inside a site
detail: Public sites can offer optional ChatGPT sign-in/sign-out paths; the server receives the visitor email and optional full name in headers. Workspace-restricted sites already use ChatGPT identity.

feature: SIWC bypass token for service-to-site calls
detail: The site owner can ask the agent to generate a bearer token so a script can call a sign-in-protected site; generating a new one replaces the old, which may stay valid up to five minutes.

feature: Sites that load each visitor's own connected-app data
detail: A workspace-private site can read data through plugins using each visitor's own connection and permissions, with a Load more cursor action; needs workspace plugin use enabled and visitor consent.

feature: Sites analytics
detail: Built-in traffic analytics without an SDK: unique visitors and page views over time with date range and granularity; not available for Enterprise-owned sites.

feature: Site custom domain
detail: Connect an apex domain or subdomain you own by adding provided DNS records and refreshing status; no domain registration, and not in Enterprise at launch.

feature: Site environment variables and secrets; rename URL
detail: Site settings let owners add, update or remove hosted env variables and secrets and manage the site name and URL.

feature: Take down or permanently delete a site
detail: Restrict sharing to yourself to take a site offline, or Delete site (type slug to confirm); deletion is permanent and cannot be restored.

feature: Site audience options
detail: New sites are limited to the owner and admins; options include selected users or groups, invited external viewers, anyone in the workspace, or anyone on the internet (public publishing is off by default in Enterprise).

feature: Invite external viewers to a private site
detail: Share > Only those invited lets you add outside email addresses as Viewers who sign in with the invited account; they cannot edit or publish.

feature: Site co-editing (Can edit role)
detail: Owners can promote workspace members from Can view to Can edit; editors save versions and publish updates but cannot change audience, invite others, manage settings/analytics, transfer ownership, or do the first publish. Sites appear under Shared with you.

feature: Skills: reusable workflows invoked with @ in ChatGPT or $ in Codex
detail: A skill bundles instructions and resources for a task; it is chosen automatically when relevant or explicitly via @ mention in ChatGPT and $ in Codex, and can be shared if workspace settings allow.

feature: Skill creator (@skill-creator / $skill-creator)
detail: A built-in helper that drafts a skill from a described task, with review, test and install steps.

feature: Plugins: shared directory bundling skills, MCP servers and hooks
detail: One universal plugin directory serves ChatGPT and Codex; a plugin can include skills, MCP servers (optionally with custom UI) and lifecycle hooks for the Codex runtime. Build plugins by conversation or migrate custom GPTs.

feature: Record and Replay turns a demonstrated workflow into a skill
detail: Recording a workflow produces a reusable skill.

feature: ChatGPT Space: pages, slides, spreadsheets, sites and files in one place
detail: Space is a hub where you and ChatGPT co-edit pages, slides and spreadsheets, and find sites, images and files; a space groups pages by topic or team and can be shared.

feature: Space sources from connected apps keep original permissions
detail: Linked files from apps like Google Drive keep their own permissions; copied or summarized content is visible to anyone with page access; sharing a page does not share chats or memory.

feature: Ask ChatGPT or a dot inline in a page
detail: Type @ChatGPT or @dot in a page or comment, use Ask for change on selected text, or the side conversation; proposed edits are reviewed before accepting.

feature: Page slash menu: Generate, Visualize, Image
detail: Typing / in a page opens an insert menu to generate text inline, create an interactive visualization (calculator, diagram, app, screen, widget), or generate/upload an image block.

feature: Keep Updated recurring page refresh (not at launch)
detail: A feature to keep pages updated automatically is unavailable at launch; recurring work must be set up via chat scheduled tasks and verified.

feature: Share a page or space with View, Comment or Edit roles
detail: Share to people or Teams with view, comment or edit access (Team invites may omit comment); access to a space applies to its pages and a page to its child pages, and removing a direct invite does not remove inherited access.

feature: Collaborative slides editing and Request edits
detail: Decks support view and edit roles only (no comment-only); editors co-edit in real time, use shared comments with @ mentions of people, ChatGPT or a dot, and select an element then Request edits.

feature: ChatGPT Slides: create, edit, present and export
detail: Create a deck from a conversation, outline, files or a style-reference deck; edit text, images, shapes, tables and charts; present with speaker notes; export to PPTX, PDF or Google Slides on web, open in PowerPoint/Keynote on desktop.

feature: Slides on mobile: create by chat and view only
detail: On mobile you can generate slides through conversation and view decks; direct element editing is on web or desktop.

feature: Windows app may create a local PowerPoint instead of a collaborative deck
detail: If the Windows desktop app produces a PowerPoint file, switch to cloud mode or use web to build editable slides in Space.

feature: Space views: All, Suggested, Favorites, Your items, Shared with you
detail: The All view aggregates saved work with tabs for suggested items, favorites, your items and items shared with you, plus search and a New menu (page, space).

feature: Create a page from a conversation or notes
detail: New page in the sidebar, or ask ChatGPT to turn an existing chat into a page; add files or links and ask ChatGPT alongside to organize and revise.

feature: Page block types and insert menu
detail: Blocks include headings, lists, checklists, tables, code, highlight, image, file attachment, subpage, link to page, references to files/pages/chats, Visualize, Prompt, Task and Agent Instructions.

feature: Page floating toolbar for selected text
detail: Selecting text shows Ask for change, Comment, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inline code, link and block-style (heading, list, checklist, quote).

feature: Drag blocks and table width/fit options
detail: Block handles drag blocks or whole heading sections; tables have Width (Normal, Flexible, Full width) and Fit (for readability, distribute columns evenly).

feature: Prompt blocks readers can run (Chat about this)
detail: A Prompt block stores a reusable request that readers run to start a chat about the page.

feature: Mention people, agents, files and chats; show attribution
detail: Typing @ mentions people, your agents, Space files and ChatGPT chats as references; real-time co-editing, comment threads and Show attribution reveal who contributed.

feature: Codex code review on GitHub pull requests (@codex review)
detail: Mention @codex review or enable Automatic review; Codex posts a standard GitHub review flagging P0 and P1 issues, with an eyes reaction while running. A focus can be added to the comment.

feature: Codex review settings: Automatic review and Review trigger
detail: Per-repo and personal settings at the code-review settings page turn on automatic review and choose when reviews run.

feature: AGENTS.md Code Review Rules guide Codex reviews
detail: A Code Review Rules section in root or nested AGENTS.md files defines repo-specific checks; the closest applicable files apply per changed file.

feature: Codex code review on GitLab merge requests
detail: Beta for all ChatGPT plans running in Codex cloud; @codex review posts GitLab notes (manual up to P2, automatic P0/P1) and triggers are On MR open, On every push or Smart Trigger (Experimental).

feature: GitLab service account and webhook setup for Codex
detail: Self-managed or Dedicated GitLab needs an admin-created or existing service account with an api-scope token (Developer access), project or group webhooks (GitLab 19.0+), and a project environment for coding tasks.

feature: Ask Codex to fix findings or do tasks from a merge request comment
detail: With a configured project environment, commenting @codex fix the P1 issue or any other task starts a cloud chat with the MR as context and can push to the branch.

feature: Codex for Linear: assign issues or mention @Codex
detail: Install the Codex for Linear connector, then assign an issue to Codex or mention it in a comment to start a cloud chat; progress shows in issue Activity and the result links to a chat to create a PR. Enterprise needs admin enablement.

feature: Linear triage rules can auto-delegate new issues to Codex
detail: In Linear team Triage rules, a Delegate > Codex rule assigns issues entering triage to Codex, which then runs under the issue creator's account. Repo is chosen from Linear's suggestion, else the most recent environment.

feature: Linear MCP server for local Codex
detail: Add the Linear MCP server via codex mcp add or config.toml and log in to read Linear issues from the desktop app, CLI or IDE.

feature: @ChatGPT in Slack channels
detail: Mention @ChatGPT in an enabled public/private channel (not Slack Connect) to ask questions or delegate repo work to a Codex Cloud task, with threaded follow-ups; replaces the earlier @Codex mention.

feature: Slack approval card, Follow along and Cancel for cloud tasks
detail: ChatGPT can show a private Allow/Deny card before starting repo work; the requester gets Follow along and Cancel controls, and results post back to the thread, readable by channel members.

feature: Chat, Work and Codex modes
detail: Chat is for questions and back-and-forth, Work carries a larger task to a reviewable result, and Codex adds developer views; Quick chat appears in Codex when available.

feature: ChatGPT Work capabilities overview
detail: Work plans tasks, researches the web, uses files, projects, memory, Library and plugins, creates documents/decks/spreadsheets/PDFs, images and visualizations, uses browser, extension, Computer Use and appshots, runs code, delegates to subagents, runs long tasks and scheduled tasks.

feature: Work in cloud or locally
detail: Web Work runs in a managed cloud environment that continues after closing the app and is reachable from web or mobile; desktop may also offer local Work using your files, apps and browser when enabled.

feature: ChatGPT vs Codex views in the desktop app
detail: ChatGPT view hides Git/shell details, shows web/mobile chats and Work chats, no PR pane or Quick chat; Codex view shows developer diff/review views, PR pane when enabled, and Quick chat to reach ChatGPT chats.

feature: Projects keep related chats, files and instructions together
detail: A project groups chats, files and instructions for continuing work.

feature: Attach documents, decks, spreadsheets, PDFs, images and data exports
detail: Uploaded files can be summarized, compared, cleaned or used as source for new files; generated files open in a preview where you request changes.

feature: Read-only snapshot link of a Codex thread
detail: On macOS desktop, Share or /share uploads a snapshot (messages, reasoning summaries, images, file diffs; no tool calls or shell output) with secret redaction; workspace accounts choose everyone or invited people/groups, and links are managed under Data controls > Shared links.

feature: Visualizations: interactive charts, diagrams, maps, calculators
detail: Tag @Visualize (Plugins) in the composer or let ChatGPT choose; produces explorable visuals in chat that are snapshots, not live dashboards. Rolling out on web, desktop and mobile; not rendered in Codex CLI/IDE.

feature: Accessibility refinements for visualizations
detail: Ask follow-ups for keyboard-operable controls, visible focus, labels beyond color, no looping motion, plus a text summary and data table.

feature: Web search with citations in chat
detail: ChatGPT has a first-party web search tool; results and citations appear in chat on web, search calls log in the desktop transcript, and workspace settings can restrict search.

feature: Deep research in Work
detail: Pick Deep research from the + menu (web) or Plugins (desktop) to investigate across sources and get a sourced report with follow-ups; availability depends on account and workspace.
